actions.alignment.alignHorizontally: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Moves the selected marchers (performers) onto one common X position, lining them up in a vertical column on the field. The sibling "Align vertically" lines them up in a row. Keep the two clearly distinct.
actions.alignment.alignVertically: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Moves the selected marchers (performers) onto one common Y position, lining them up in a horizontal row across the field. The sibling "Align horizontally" lines them up in a column. Keep the two clearly distinct.
actions.alignment.cancelUpdates: Name of the Escape-key action in the command palette and shortcut settings. In the field editor it cancels what is in progress (such as a half-drawn shape) or clears the current selection.
actions.alignment.distributeHorizontally: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Spaces the selected marchers (performers) evenly from left to right across the field, between the outermost two.
actions.alignment.distributeVertically: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Spaces the selected marchers (performers) evenly from top to bottom on the field view, between the outermost two.
actions.alignment.flipHorizontal: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Mirrors the selected marchers' positions left to right, like flipping a formation sideways. While a shape editor is open it flips the shape instead.
actions.alignment.flipVertical: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. Mirrors the selected marchers' positions top to bottom on the field view, like flipping a formation upside down. While a shape editor is open it flips the shape instead.
actions.alignment.lockX: Name of the Lock X action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A toggle: while on, dragging or nudging marchers can't change their X (side-to-side) position. X is the left-right axis of the field.
actions.alignment.lockXOff: Tooltip of the Lock X toggle button in the toolbar, shown while the lock is on, so pressing the button turns it off. X is the side-to-side axis of the field; "movement" is moving marchers. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.lockXOn: Tooltip of the Lock X toggle button in the toolbar, shown while the lock is off, so pressing the button turns it on and marchers can then only move up and down. X is the side-to-side axis of the field. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.lockY: Name of the Lock Y action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A toggle: while on, dragging or nudging marchers can't change their Y (up-down) position. Y is the up-down axis of the field view.
actions.alignment.lockYOff: Tooltip of the Lock Y toggle button in the toolbar, shown while the lock is on, so pressing the button turns it off. Y is the up-down axis of the field view; "movement" is moving marchers. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.lockYOn: Tooltip of the Lock Y toggle button in the toolbar, shown while the lock is off, so pressing the button turns it on and marchers can then only move side to side. Y is the up-down axis of the field view. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.snapOff: Tooltip of the Snap toggle button in the toolbar, shown while Snap is on, so pressing the button turns it off. Snap makes dragged marchers jump to the grid steps instead of moving freely. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.snapOn: Tooltip of the Snap toggle button in the toolbar, shown while Snap is off (the text first states the current state, "Snap off", then says pressing the button turns it back on). Snap makes dragged marchers jump to the grid steps. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.alignment.snapToCustomFraction: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Rounds the selected marchers' positions to the nearest grid step, using the step sizes set in the toolbar's coordinate rounding settings. A one-time rounding, not a toggle.
actions.alignment.toggleSnap: Name of the Snap toggle in the command palette and shortcut settings. Snap makes dragged marchers jump to the grid steps instead of moving freely. This is the neutral name; the button tooltips use the "Snap off" and "Turn Snap off" texts.
actions.alignment.toggleSnapKeywords: Search words for the Snap toggle in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (snap, magnet, grid, free).
actions.batchEdit.clearPage: Label of the "Clear this page" command in the field's right-click menu and the command palette, naming the page it clears. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". Clearing a page takes the marchers' positions off it, so they have no position of their own there (Not defined).
actions.batchEdit.clearPageAndLater: Label of the clear command when later pages showed the cleared positions: clearing this page also makes those pages go back to the position before it. {page} is the cleared page's name, such as "3". {count} is how many later pages move back; {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "4" and "6" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
actions.batchEdit.clearThisPageAll: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus: the "Clear this page" command for every marcher, not only the selected ones. {clearThisPage} is the command's name ("Clear this page"), filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder.
actions.batchEdit.clearThisPageAllAndFol: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus: "Clear this page" for every marcher, where later pages that showed the cleared positions also go back to the position before it. {clearThisPage} is the command's name, filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder.
actions.batchEdit.clearThisPageHoldsToo: Note in the toast after "Clear this page", when the marchers' holds on later pages were removed with it. A hold keeps a marcher where the previous page left it. {count} is how many marchers; {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language; {pages} names the pages, such as "Page 4" or "Pages 4 and 6". Add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) if it needs them.
actions.batchEdit.clearThisPageSelected: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus: the "Clear this page" command for the selected marchers only. {clearThisPage} is the command's name ("Clear this page"), filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder.
actions.batchEdit.clearThisPageSelectedA: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus: "Clear this page" for the selected marchers, where later pages that showed the cleared positions also go back to the position before it. {clearThisPage} is the command's name, filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder.
actions.batchEdit.defineAsShown: Name of the "Define as shown" action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus. {defineAsShown} is the command's name, filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder. The command gives the selected marchers a position of their own on the current page, where they are shown now (Defined).
actions.batchEdit.forAllMarchers: A command's name with a note that it acts on every marcher. {label} is the command's name, such as "Clear Page 3".
actions.batchEdit.forSelected: A command's name with a note that it acts on the selected marchers only. {label} is the command's name, such as "Clear Page 3".
actions.batchEdit.holdFromPrevious: Name of the "Hold from last keyframe" action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus. {holdFromPrevious} is the command's name, filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder. The command makes the selected marchers stay on the current page where the previous page left them (Held).
actions.batchEdit.holdKeywords: Search keywords for the hold commands in the command palette, never shown as a sentence. Translate each word people might type to find them (hold, held, defined, keep, stay, keyframe, page, state, previous); separate them with spaces.
actions.batchEdit.moveAllToNextSpots: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus. Moves every marcher on the current page to the spot it stands on at the next page. It is an edit to positions, like dragging the marchers there: on a page where a marcher holds its spot from an earlier page, the whole hold moves. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation); a spot is a marcher's position on the field. The sibling action is limited to the selected marchers.
actions.batchEdit.moveSelectedToNextSpot: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and the field's right-click menu. Moves only the selected marchers on the current page to the spots they stand on at the next page. It is an edit to positions, like dragging the marchers there: on a page where a marcher holds its spot from an earlier page, the whole hold moves. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation); a spot is a marcher's position on the field.
actions.batchEdit.movedAllToNextSpots: Success toast after moving every marcher on the current page to its spot on the next page. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is the number of marchers, such as 1 or 24; translate both forms. {currentPage} and {nextPage} are page names, such as "3" and "4". Pages are sections of the show; a spot is a marcher's position on the field.
actions.batchEdit.movedSelectedToNextSpo: Success toast after moving the selected marchers on the current page to their spots on the next page. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is the number of marchers, such as 1 or 24; translate both forms. {currentPage} and {nextPage} are page names, such as "3" and "4". Pages are sections of the show; a spot is a marcher's position on the field.
actions.batchEdit.noNextPage: Error toast shown when the user tries to copy marcher positions from the next page but the current page is the last one. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation); "coordinates" are the marchers' positions on the field.
actions.batchEdit.noPreviousPage: Error toast shown when the user tries to copy marcher positions from the previous page but the current page is the first one. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation); "coordinates" are the marchers' positions on the field.
actions.batchEdit.setAllToPreviousDone: Success toast after copying all marchers' positions from the previous page onto the current page. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is the number of marchers, such as 1 or 24; translate both forms. {currentPage} and {previousPage} are page names, such as "4" and "3". Pages are sections of the show; coordinates are field positions.
actions.batchEdit.setSelectedToPreviousD: Success toast after copying the selected marchers' positions from the previous page onto the current page. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is the number of marchers, such as 1 or 24; translate both forms. {currentPage} and {previousPage} are page names, such as "4" and "3". Pages are sections of the show; coordinates are field positions.
actions.edit.noRedoAvailable: Toast shown when the user presses Redo but there is nothing that was undone to bring back.
actions.edit.noUndoAvailable: Toast shown when the user presses Undo but there is nothing left to undo.
actions.edit.redo: Name of the Redo action in the command palette, shortcut settings and the title bar button's screen-reader label. Brings back the change the user last undid. Verb.
actions.edit.redoFailed: Error toast shown when the user chooses Redo but the app couldn't apply the edit again. The show is left exactly as it was.
actions.edit.undo: Name of the Undo action in the command palette, shortcut settings and title bar tooltip. Also the label of the Undo button inside a toast after an automatic change. Reverses the last edit. Verb.
actions.edit.undoFailed: Error toast shown when the user chooses Undo but the app couldn't reverse the last edit. The show is left exactly as it was.
actions.file.closeFile: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and the File menu. Closes the open show file and returns to the start screen.
actions.file.exportCoordinateSheets: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens the dialog for exporting coordinate sheets, printable PDF pages listing where each marcher stands at each set. The ellipsis means a dialog opens next. Keep the ellipsis.
actions.file.exportCoordinateSheetsKeywo: Search words for the Export coordinate sheets action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (print, pdf, dot sheets). "Dot sheets" are the marching band name for coordinate sheets.
actions.file.exportDrillCharts: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens the dialog for exporting drill charts, printable PDF pages that draw the formations on the field. The ellipsis means a dialog opens next. Keep the ellipsis.
actions.file.exportDrillChartsKeywords: Search words for the Export drill charts action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (print, pdf).
actions.file.exportToMobile: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Uploads the show for viewing in the OpenMarch Mobile app (a companion phone app). "OpenMarch Mobile" is a product name. The ellipsis means a dialog opens next. Keep the ellipsis.
actions.file.exportToMobileKeywords: Search words for the Export to OpenMarch Mobile action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (phone, app, upload).
actions.file.exportVideo: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens the dialog for rendering the show's animation as a video file. The ellipsis means a dialog opens next. Keep the ellipsis.
actions.file.exportVideoKeywords: Search words for the Export video action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (mp4, movie, render).
actions.file.importMusicXml: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens a file picker to import a MusicXML score file (a standard music notation format) so the show's measures and tempo follow the score. "MusicXML" is a file format name; keep it. Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.file.insertAudio: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens a file picker to add an audio file (the show's music) to the show. Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.file.loadDialogue: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens a file picker to open an existing OpenMarch show file. Verb. Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.file.newDialogue: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens the dialog for creating a new, empty OpenMarch show file. Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.file.openExport: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens the Export dialog, where the user picks what to export (coordinate sheets, drill charts, video and so on). Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.file.saveDialogue: Name of an action in the command palette and File menu. Opens a file dialog to save a copy of the current show under a new name or place (the show itself saves automatically). Keep the ellipsis (a dialog opens next).
actions.labelWithVariant: Name of an action that comes in several variants, shown in the command palette, shortcut settings and button tooltips. {label} is the action's base name (such as "Move up") and {variant} says how this variant differs (such as "¼ step, no snap"). Keep both arguments; change the brackets or order if your language words this differently.
actions.movement.moveDown: Name of the nudge-down action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Moves the selected marchers a small step down on the field view. A variant text such as "4 steps" or "no snap" is appended in parentheses, for example "Nudge down (no snap)".
actions.movement.moveLeft: Name of the nudge-left action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Moves the selected marchers a small step to the left. A variant text such as "4 steps" or "no snap" is appended in parentheses, for example "Nudge left (no snap)".
actions.movement.moveRight: Name of the nudge-right action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Moves the selected marchers a small step to the right. A variant text such as "4 steps" or "no snap" is appended in parentheses, for example "Nudge right (no snap)".
actions.movement.moveUp: Name of the nudge-up action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Moves the selected marchers a small step up on the field view. A variant text such as "4 steps" or "no snap" is appended in parentheses, for example "Nudge up (no snap)".
actions.movement.variants.coarse: Variant text added in parentheses after a nudge action's name, for example "Nudge left (4 steps)". This variant moves marchers four steps at a time. A step is the field's grid unit.
actions.movement.variants.coarseFree: Variant text added in parentheses after a nudge action's name, for example "Nudge left (4 steps, no snap)". Moves marchers four steps at a time without snapping to the grid. A step is the field's grid unit.
actions.movement.variants.fine: Variant text added in parentheses after a nudge action's name, for example "Nudge left (¼ step, no snap)". Moves marchers a quarter of a step, without snapping to the grid. A step is the field's grid unit. Keep the fraction sign.
actions.movement.variants.free: Variant text added in parentheses after a nudge action's name, for example "Nudge left (no snap)". Moves marchers one grid step without snapping their position to the grid. Lowercase on purpose.
actions.movement.variants.tenth: Variant text added in parentheses after a nudge action's name, for example "Nudge left (⅒ step, no snap)". Moves marchers a tenth of a step, without snapping to the grid. A step is the field's grid unit. Keep the fraction sign.
actions.navigation.firstPage: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Jumps to the first page of the show. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
actions.navigation.lastPage: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Jumps to the last page of the show. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
actions.navigation.nextBeat: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Moves the playhead forward by one beat (one count of the music).
actions.navigation.nextPage: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Goes to the next page of the show. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
actions.navigation.previousBeat: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Moves the playhead back by one beat (one count of the music).
actions.navigation.previousPage: Name of an action in the command palette, shortcut settings and transport tooltips. Goes to the previous page of the show. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
actions.playback.holdFaster: Name of an action in shortcut settings. While the key is held down, the show plays at double speed; releasing it returns to the normal speed. Not shown in the command palette.
actions.playback.holdSlower: Name of an action in shortcut settings. While the key is held down, the show plays at half speed; releasing it returns to the normal speed. Not shown in the command palette.
actions.playback.nextSpeed: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Steps the playback speed up to the next preset (for example from 1x to 1.5x).
actions.playback.pause: Tooltip of the play/pause button while the show is playing, so pressing it pauses. Verb. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.playback.play: Tooltip of the play/pause button while the show is stopped, so pressing it starts playback. Verb. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.playback.playOn: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Plays the show starting at the start flag (the marker where the editing window and playback begin on the timeline) and continues on past the playhead instead of stopping at the end of the window.
actions.playback.playPage: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Starts playing from the playhead (the current position on the timeline), or pauses if it is already playing.
actions.playback.playPause: Name of the main play action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Starts playback and, pressed again, stops it. The tooltip of the play button uses "Play" and "Pause" instead.
actions.playback.previousSpeed: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Steps the playback speed down to the previous preset (for example from 1.5x to 1x).
actions.playback.resetSpeed: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Sets the playback speed back to normal (1x).
actions.playback.speedKeywords: Search words shared by the playback speed actions in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find them (speed, rate, slow, fast, tempo, playback).
actions.playback.toggleLoop: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Turns looping on or off: when on, playback repeats over the loop region (the page being edited) instead of continuing.
actions.playback.toggleMetronome: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Turns the metronome (an audible click on each beat during playback) on or off.
actions.select.selectAll: Name of the Select all action in the command palette and shortcut settings, and the label of the button in the toolbar's Select tab. Selects every marcher in the show. Verb.
actions.shape.apply: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Once a shape (a box, circle or other outline) has been drawn on the field, this moves the selected marchers onto it so they stand along the shape.
actions.shape.block: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Starts the shape tool with a box (rectangular block) shape, which the selected marchers fill. "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.circle: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Starts the shape tool with a circle shape for the selected marchers to stand on. "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.curve: Name of a shape action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Text: "Shape: Curve".
actions.shape.evenOut: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Spaces the marchers evenly again along the open shape's outline so the gaps between them are equal. "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.expand: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Makes the open or selected shape larger without changing its proportions (its width-to-height ratio). "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.group: Name of the Group selection action: the first item in the field's right-click menu while two or more marchers are selected, and its name in the command palette and shortcut settings. It makes the selected marchers one shape where they stand: nobody moves, and from then on they move, turn and scale together.
actions.shape.groupKeywords: Search words for the Group action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Not shown; translate as words people might type to find it.
actions.shape.hideMarchers: Name of a shape action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Text: "Shape: Hide the marchers (hold to peek, tap to keep hidden)".
actions.shape.hideMarchersKeywords: Search keywords (space separated, not shown) for a shape action in the command palette. Text: "hide show marchers spots walks alone peek eye".
actions.shape.keywords: Search words shared by the shape actions in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find them (shape, form, formation, set, place).
actions.shape.line: Name of a shape action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Text: "Shape: Line".
actions.shape.noMarchersSelected: Warning toast shown when the user runs an action that changes the selected marchers' positions while no marchers are selected.
actions.shape.quarterTurn: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Rotates the open or selected shape by a quarter turn (90 degrees) clockwise. "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.recalculate: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Works out again which marcher stands at which spot of the shape (for example after the shape was changed). "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.removeLastPoint: Name of a shape action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Text: "Shape: Remove the last point while drawing".
actions.shape.ring: Name of an action in shortcut settings. The favorites ring is a circular menu of the user's favorite shapes: holding the key opens it so the user can aim at a shape and let go to pick it, while a quick tap opens it and keeps it open.
actions.shape.shrink: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Makes the open or selected shape smaller without changing its proportions (its width-to-height ratio). "Shape:" is a prefix that groups shape actions together; keep a similar prefix and the colon.
actions.shape.ungroup: Name of the Ungroup action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Ungroup turns a placed shape (a box of marchers) back into plain marchers: they stay where they are and stop moving as one shape from that page on.
actions.shape.ungroupKeywords: Search words for the Ungroup action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Not shown; translate as words people might type to find it.
actions.swap.mustSelectTwo: Error toast shown when the user runs Swap two marchers without exactly two marchers selected.
actions.swap.swap: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. With exactly two marchers selected, each takes the other's position on the current page.
actions.timeline.createPageAtPlayhead: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Creates a new page that ends at the playhead (the current position on the timeline), by placing a page flag there. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
actions.timeline.createSubsetAtPlayhead: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Like creating a page at the playhead, but the new page is a subset: a short page inside a larger one that keeps the later pages' numbers (for example a page 2A between pages 2 and 3). A page is a section of the show that ends in a set.
actions.timeline.goTo: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Opens a small box where the user types a page number, a measure (such as "m23") or a rehearsal mark (such as "A") and the playhead jumps there.
actions.timeline.mergeMoveIntoPage: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A move is one marcher group's travel between two points on the timeline. This folds a move that was split off back into the move of the page it belongs to. Only in the Expert timeline.
actions.timeline.splitMoveAtPlayhead: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A move is one marcher group's travel between two points on the timeline. This cuts the move under the playhead (the current position) in two, which meet at the playhead. Only in the Expert timeline.
actions.timeline.splitSelectedIntoNewMov: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A move is one marcher group's travel between two points on the timeline. This takes the selected marchers out of the current move and gives them a move of their own. Only in the Expert timeline.
actions.timeline.unsetHere: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. A keyframe is a position stored for a marcher at a certain count (shown as a diamond on the timeline). This removes the keyframe of the selected marchers at the playhead, so they go back to the keyframe before it. {removeKeyframe} is the command's name ("Remove keyframe"), filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder.
actions.timeline.unsetHereAndFollowing: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Removes the keyframe (a stored marcher position at a count) at the playhead, and the later pages that showed that position move back to the keyframe before it too. {removeKeyframe} is the command's name ("Remove keyframe"), filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder. The pages are named in the actions.timeline.unsetHereAndPagesMoveBack variant.
actions.timeline.unsetHereAndPagesMoveBa: Label of the "Remove keyframe" menu and palette entry when later pages showed the removed position, so they move back to the keyframe before it too. A keyframe is a stored marcher position at a count. {removeKeyframe} is the command's name ("Remove keyframe"), filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder. {count} is how many pages. {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "4" and "6" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
actions.timeline.unsetHereKeywords: Search words for the Remove keyframe actions in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find them. A keyframe is a stored marcher position at a count, shown as a diamond on the timeline. "Defined" and "not defined" are the app's state words for whether a marcher has its own position on a page.
actions.ui.hideNextPaths: Tooltip of the next page paths toggle in its on state, so pressing it hides the lines that preview where marchers go on the next page. Verb. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.ui.hideStartFlagPositions: Tooltip of the start flag positions toggle, so pressing it hides the dots and paths showing where marchers were at the start flag (the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins). Verb.
actions.ui.openCommandBar: Name of an action in shortcut settings. Opens the command palette (a searchable list of every action) with a different key, the slash. Same meaning as "Command palette".
actions.ui.openCommandPalette: Name of an action in shortcut settings, and the screen-reader label of the title bar button that opens it. The command palette is a searchable list of every action in the app, opened with a keyboard shortcut.
actions.ui.openFieldMenu: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Opens the field's right-click menu at the selected marchers using the keyboard. Only enabled when marchers are selected.
actions.ui.openSettings: Name of an action in the command palette and menus. Opens the app settings dialog. The ellipsis means a dialog opens next. Keep the ellipsis.
actions.ui.openView3d: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Opens the 3D View, a separate window showing the show in 3D, or brings it to the front if it is already open. "3D View" is a feature name used across the app.
actions.ui.openView3dKeywords: Search words for the Open 3D View action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (3d, three dimensional, stadium, venue, window).
actions.ui.showNextPaths: Tooltip of the next page paths toggle in its off state, so pressing it shows lines that preview where marchers go on the next page. Verb. A shortcut in square brackets is added after this text.
actions.ui.showShortcuts: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Opens a dialog listing every keyboard shortcut.
actions.ui.showStartFlagPositions: Tooltip of the start flag positions toggle, so pressing it shows the dots and paths of where marchers were at the start flag (the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins). Verb.
actions.ui.toggleNextPaths: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Turns on or off the lines previewing where marchers go on the next page.
actions.ui.togglePreview: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Switches into Preview, a watch-only mode where the show plays without being editable, and back out again. Verb phrase.
actions.ui.togglePreviewKeywords: Search words for the Preview action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (preview, cinematic, watch, present, presentation, fullscreen, play).
actions.ui.toggleStartFlagPositions: Name of an action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Pressing and holding the key peeks at the start flag positions (the dots and paths showing where marchers were at the start flag, the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins); a tap latches them on or off.
actions.ui.toggleStartFlagPositionsKeywo: Search words for the Toggle start flag positions action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Never shown; translate as words people might type to find it (previous paths, dots, where marchers were or came from, hold, peek, latch).
activities.drumCorps: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show. A drum and bugle corps is an independent competitive marching ensemble of brass, percussion and color guard, performing on a football field.
activities.indoorPercussion: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show. An indoor percussion ensemble performs marching percussion in a gym on a floor tarp.
activities.indoorWinds: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show. An indoor winds ensemble performs with wind instruments in a gym on a floor tarp.
activities.marchingBand: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show (it picks the default field). A marching band performs on a football field, usually with a high school or college.
activities.other: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show: any kind not listed.
activities.soundSport: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show. SoundSport is the name of a performance format run by Drum Corps International for smaller ensembles; it is a brand name and is usually left untranslated.
activities.winterGuard: Kind of ensemble a show is for, chosen when creating a new show. A winter guard is an indoor color guard (flags, rifles, dance) that performs in a gym on a floor tarp.
analyticsOptIn.description: First paragraph of the analytics consent dialog shown on first launch (and in the welcome flow). Explains what OpenMarch collects. `…` wraps the words that link to the privacy policy web page: keep the tags and translate only the words between them.
analyticsOptIn.optIn: Button in the analytics consent dialog (and the welcome flow): agree to share usage analytics. Sits next to the 'Opt Out' button; the app reloads after either choice. Verb phrase, short.
analyticsOptIn.optOut: Button in the analytics consent dialog (and the welcome flow): decline sharing usage analytics. Sits next to the 'Opt In' button. Verb phrase, short.
analyticsOptIn.settings: Sentence under the consent text saying the choice can be changed later. 'The app settings' is the Settings window, Privacy section.
analyticsOptIn.title: Title of the analytics consent dialog, and the name of the analytics step in the first-run welcome flow.
analyticsOptIn.whenYouOptIn: Lead-in label in the analytics consent dialog, shown above a green sample box that previews what Settings will say if the user agrees to share analytics. 'Opt in' means agree.
analyticsOptIn.whenYouOptOut: Lead-in label in the analytics consent dialog, shown above a red sample box that previews what Settings will say if the user declines analytics. 'Opt out' means decline.
app.codegenBanner: Yellow banner across the top of the window, seen only by developers who start OpenMarch in the mode that records clicks for automated tests (Playwright is the name of the testing tool; keep it). Regular users never see it.
app.releaseNotes: Button on the notification shown after an update. Opens the OpenMarch website's list of what changed in each version.
app.updated: Notification shown once after OpenMarch was updated to a new version. {version} is the version number, for example 0.1.8; the "v" before it is short for "version". OpenMarch is the product name; keep it as is.
audio.beats.create.error: Error toast shown when adding beats to the show's beat grid (the timing of every count in the music) fails.
audio.beats.create.success: Success toast after new beats (the beat grid that the show's counts follow) were created from the audio.
audio.beats.delete.error: Error toast shown when removing beats from the show's beat grid fails. Beats are the individual counts of the music.
audio.beats.flatten.error: Error toast shown when an internal clean-up that renumbers the order of beats in the show fails. Beats are the individual counts of the music.
audio.beats.replace.error: Error toast shown when replacing all the show's beats (the beat grid that the counts follow) with newly tapped or edited ones fails.
audio.beats.replace.success: Success toast after all the show's beats (the beat grid that the counts follow) were replaced with newly tapped or edited ones.
audio.beats.shift.error: Error toast shown when moving a run of beats earlier or later in the show's beat grid fails. Beats are the individual counts of the music.
audio.beats.update.error: Error toast shown when saving changes to beats (for example their length) in the show's beat grid fails. Beats are the individual counts of the music.
audio.context.error: Error toast shown when the app can't start its audio system (the browser's audio context), so music playback won't work.
audio.decode.error: Error toast shown when the chosen audio file can't be read as sound (damaged or an unsupported format).
audio.insert.databaseUnavailable: Error toast when the show file (a database) closed or became unreadable while a music file was being added to it.
audio.insert.noFileOpen: Error toast when the person tries to add a music file while no show is open.
audio.silentPlaceholder: Name shown in the audio file picker for the silent stand-in track the app plays when the show has no music added yet. It is not saved in the show.
auth.api.requestFailed: Error message shown (in a toast or under the upload button of the mobile app export) when a request to OpenMarch's online service couldn't be completed, for example with no internet connection. {reason} is a short technical description from the network library, in English (such as Network Error).
auth.api.requestFailedStatus: Error message shown (in a toast or under the upload button of the mobile app export) when a request to OpenMarch's online service fails and the service gave no explanation. {status} is the HTTP status number (such as 500) and {statusText} its short English description from the server (such as Internal Server Error), which may be empty; neither is translated.
auth.api.tokenRequired: Error message shown when the app tries to use OpenMarch's online service (such as uploading a show to the mobile app) but has no sign-in token to send: the user is signed out, or the sign-in couldn't be refreshed (usually because there's no internet connection).
auth.fullName: The signed-in user's full name, shown in the account menu and as the tooltip of the account button. {firstName} is the given name and {lastName} the family name; reorder them if your language puts the family name first.
auth.signIn: Button in the title bar for signing in to the user's OpenMarch online account (used for the mobile app and cloud features). Verb phrase. Visible text.
auth.signInAriaLabel: Screen-reader label of the title bar's sign-in button. Verb phrase; not shown.
auth.signOut: Menu item in the account menu that signs the user out of their OpenMarch online account. Verb phrase.
auth.signOutFailed: Error toast when signing out of the user's OpenMarch account failed (usually no internet connection); they are still signed in.
auth.userFallback: Name shown for a signed-in user in the account button and its tooltip when their account has neither a full name nor an email address. Noun, one word; its first letter is also used in the round avatar.
canvas.zoom.group: Screen-reader label of the zoom slider in the zoom controls at the bottom right of the field.
canvas.zoom.in: Tooltip of the + button in the zoom controls at the bottom right of the field. Zooms the field view in.
canvas.zoom.out: Tooltip of the − button in the zoom controls at the bottom right of the field. Zooms the field view out.
canvas.zoom.reset: Screen-reader label of the button showing the zoom level in the zoom controls at the bottom right of the field. {zoom} is the zoom level as a whole number (100 means the field fits the window). Clicking resets the zoom and centers the field.
canvas.zoom.resetAndCenter: Tooltip of the button showing the zoom level (for example 100%) in the zoom controls at the bottom right of the field. Clicking it resets the zoom and centers the field in the window.
colorPicker.discard: Button in the color picker popup. Throws away the color changes made in the popup and closes it. Verb.
colorPicker.removeSetting: Tooltip of a small button next to a color picker. Clears the chosen color so the default is used again. Verb phrase.
colorPicker.resetToDefault: Tooltip of the button next to a color swatch (for example a section's or tag's marcher color). Puts the color back to its default.
colorPicker.save: Button in the color picker popup. Applies the chosen color and closes the popup. Verb.
commandPalette.back: Hint in the footer of the command bar, next to a Backspace key cap: pressing Backspace goes back to the previous question. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.cancel: Hint in the footer of the command bar, next to an Escape key cap: pressing Escape cancels the action. The command bar asks follow-up questions (such as a number of counts) before running an action. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.close: Screen-reader label of the command palette's close button, and the hint in its footer next to an Escape key cap. Closes the palette. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.done: Hint in the footer of the command bar next to an Enter key cap, on the last question: pressing Enter finishes and runs the action. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.empty: Message in the command palette when the search text matches no commands.
commandPalette.navigate: Hint in the footer of the command palette, next to up and down arrow key caps: those keys move through the list. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.next: Hint in the footer of the command bar next to an Enter key cap, on every question but the last: pressing Enter goes on to the next question. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.notUnderstood: Message in the command bar's footer when the text typed for a question (such as a number of counts) can't be read. Asks the user to type it again.
commandPalette.offInPreview: Tooltip shown on a greyed-out command in the command palette while Preview (the watch-only mode) is on. Editing commands don't work in Preview, so the user must leave Preview first. "Preview" must match the name of that mode.
commandPalette.placeholder: Placeholder text and screen-reader label of the command palette's search box. The palette is a searchable list of every action in the app.
commandPalette.run: Hint in the footer of the command palette, next to an Enter key cap: pressing Enter runs the highlighted command. Short. Verb.
commandPalette.shape: Group label for the shape commands in the command palette, and the first part of their breadcrumb path (for example "Shape" then "Box"). Shapes are outlines such as a box or circle that marchers stand along.
commandPalette.stepOf: Progress text in the command bar's footer, shown while it asks several questions in a row for one action. {step} is the question number now being asked, such as 2, and {count} is the total number of questions, such as 3, for example "2 of 3".
commandPalette.suggested: Heading of the first group of commands in the command palette, the ones most likely to be wanted, shown before the user types anything.
commandPalette.title: Title of the command palette dialog (screen-reader only) and the label of its list. The command palette is a searchable list of every action in the app.
commandPalette.unavailable: Tooltip shown on a greyed-out command in the command palette that can't run right now, when no more specific reason is available (for example nothing is selected).
convertShow.backupError.busy: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: another program has the file locked. Shown in an error dialog.
convertShow.backupError.diskFull: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the disk is full. Shown in an error dialog. {folder} is the full path of the folder the show is in.
convertShow.backupError.nameTooLong: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the backup's file name (the show's name plus a suffix) is too long. Shown in an error dialog. {folder} is the full path of the folder the show is in.
convertShow.backupError.noFreeName: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: every numbered backup name next to the show is already taken. Shown in an error dialog. {folder} is the full path of the folder the show is in.
convertShow.backupError.noFreeNameRemove: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: every numbered backup name next to the show is already taken. Shown in an error dialog. {folder} is the full path of the folder the show is in; {suffix} is the part of a backup's file name that marks it as a backup ("pre-conversion"), kept untranslated because it is in the file names; {error} is a technical message.
convertShow.backupError.notWritable: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the folder can't be written to. Shown in an error dialog. {folder} is the full path of the folder the show is in.
convertShow.backupError.sourceMissing: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the show file is gone. Shown in an error dialog. {file} is the full path of the show file.
convertShow.backupError.stopped: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the background task making it ended unexpectedly. Shown in an error dialog. {reason} is a short technical cause, such as an exit code.
convertShow.backupError.unknown: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed, for an unexpected cause. Shown in an error dialog. {error} is a technical error message.
convertShow.backupError.unreadable: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the file couldn't be read as an OpenMarch show. Shown in an error dialog. {error} is a technical message from the database.
convertShow.backupError.verificationFail: Why the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed: the copy was checked against the original and differed. Shown in an error dialog. {error} is a technical message.
convertShow.backupFolder: Line in the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog under the backup file's name. {folder} is the folder path where the backup copy was put, for example '/Users/sam/Documents/Shows'. Reads like 'In /Users/sam/Documents/Shows'.
convertShow.backupIntro: Sentence in the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog introducing the backup file's name that follows. The 'copy' is an untouched copy of the show saved before converting; 'it' refers to the show.
convertShow.backupUse: Sentence at the end of the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog. 'Confirm' is the name of the button in the dialog. The saved copy stays usable in older OpenMarch versions that can't open converted shows.
convertShow.cancel: Button in the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog. Closes it without converting or opening the show. Verb.
convertShow.confirm: Button in the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog. Starts the conversion and then opens the show. Verb.
convertShow.convertingTitle: Title of the 'Convert this show' dialog while the conversion is running. {fileName} is the show file's name, for example 'Fall Show.dots'. The curly quotes surround the name. Present participle with an ellipsis.
convertShow.description: Body of the 'Convert this show to timelines?' dialog. {fileName} is the show file's name, for example 'Fall Show.dots'. Older OpenMarch versions stored each page's movement separately; this version stores movement as timelines (a different data layout), and a converted file can't be opened by older versions.
convertShow.openFailed.backupDetail: Detail text of the error dialog shown when the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed. {error} is a sentence explaining why the backup failed (already translated, or a technical message). Keep the blank line between the two parts.
convertShow.openFailed.backupMessage: Main text of the error dialog shown when the backup copy made before converting an older show to timelines failed. {fileName} is the show file's name. "Timelines" is how newer versions of OpenMarch store a show's movement.
convertShow.openFailed.backupTitle: Title of an error dialog shown when opening a show made with an older version of OpenMarch: before converting it to timelines, OpenMarch makes a backup copy of the file, and making that copy failed, so the file wasn't opened.
convertShow.openFailed.conversionStopped: Reason shown in the error dialog when converting an older show to timelines stopped partway (the background task ended unexpectedly). {reason} is a short technical cause, such as an exit code. "Rolled back" means every change was undone, so the file is as it was.
convertShow.openFailed.convertDetail: Detail text of the error dialog shown when converting an older show to timelines failed. {error} is why it failed (translated for known causes, otherwise a technical message). {backupPath} is the full path of the backup copy made before the conversion. Keep the line breaks: the path goes on its own line.
convertShow.openFailed.convertMessage: Main text of the error dialog shown when converting a show made with an older version of OpenMarch to timelines failed. {fileName} is the show file's name. "Timelines" is how newer versions of OpenMarch store a show's movement.
convertShow.openFailed.convertTitle: Title of an error dialog shown when opening a show made with an older version of OpenMarch: converting it to timelines failed, so the file wasn't opened.
convertShow.openFailed.noPages: Reason shown in the error dialog when an older show can't be converted to timelines because the file has no pages. Pages are how older versions of OpenMarch divided a show into sets of positions; "timelines" is how newer versions store movement.
convertShow.openFailed.ok: Button that closes the error dialogs shown when an older show couldn't be backed up or converted to timelines.
convertShow.progress.backingUp: Progress line in the convert dialog while the untouched backup copy of the show is being written. Present participle with an ellipsis.
convertShow.progress.converting: Progress line in the convert dialog while the show is being converted. {done} is the number of pages already converted and {total} the number of pages in the show, for example 3 and 12. A page is one section of the show between two page flags.
convertShow.title: Title of the dialog that asks before converting a show made with an older OpenMarch to this version's timeline format. A yes/no question.
coordinateRoundingSettings.custom: Option in a row of toggle buttons for rounding marcher coordinates to the nearest step size. Choosing it lets the user type their own step size instead of picking a preset. Short button label.
coordinateRoundingSettings.disableOffset: Small toggle button in the Coordinate Rounding popover, shown while the offset is on. Clicking it turns the offset (a custom reference point that rounding is measured from) off and resets it to 0. Verb phrase; keep short.
coordinateRoundingSettings.enableOffset: Small toggle button in the Coordinate Rounding popover, shown while the offset is off. Clicking it turns on the offset, a custom reference point that rounding is measured from instead of the field's own lines. Verb phrase; keep short.
coordinateRoundingSettings.groupNotice: Short gray note in the Coordinate Rounding popover. Rounding is applied when marchers are moved on the field; it doesn't work yet when marchers are moved together as a group.
coordinateRoundingSettings.nearestSteps: Label above a row of buttons in the Coordinate Rounding popover. Marcher positions snap to the nearest multiple of the chosen step size along one axis. {axis} is the axis letter, "X" (side to side) or "Y" (front to back); keep the letter as is. Example: "Nearest X-steps".
coordinateRoundingSettings.none: Option meaning no rounding: marchers keep their exact positions. Appears as a toggle button in the Coordinate Rounding popover and as the summary value on the toolbar when rounding is off. Keep short.
coordinateRoundingSettings.offset: Label next to the X and Y offset inputs in the Coordinate Rounding popover. The offset is a reference point, in steps, that rounding is measured from. Noun, short.
coordinateRoundingSettings.roundToHalf: Tooltip of the ½ option in the Coordinate Rounding pop-up. Marchers dragged on the field snap to the nearest half step on that axis. {axis} is the letter X (side to side) or Y (front to back). A step is the unit of distance on the field.
coordinateRoundingSettings.roundToQuarte: Tooltip of the ¼ option in the Coordinate Rounding pop-up. Marchers dragged on the field snap to the nearest quarter of a step on that axis. {axis} is the letter X (side to side) or Y (front to back). A step is the unit of distance on the field.
coordinateRoundingSettings.roundToSteps: Tooltip of a whole-number option (1 or 2) in the Coordinate Rounding pop-up. Marchers dragged on the field snap to the nearest multiple of {steps} steps on that axis. {axis} is the letter X (side to side) or Y (front to back). A step is the unit of distance on the field.
coordinateRoundingSettings.title: Title of the Coordinate Rounding popover and its toolbar button. The popover sets how marcher positions are rounded (snapped) to a step size when moved on the field. Short.
coordinateRoundingSettings.unit: Unit after the offset box and placeholder of the custom rounding box in the Coordinate Rounding pop-up: marching steps, the unit of distance on the field.
coordinateRoundingSettings.xStepDescript: Tooltip on the X-axis step-size buttons in the Coordinate Rounding popover. X is the side-to-side direction on the field. Left-click and right-click are mouse actions that step through the preset rounding sizes.
coordinateRoundingSettings.xStepValue: Short button in the toolbar next to Coordinate Rounding showing how X positions (side to side) are rounded. {value} is the rounding, such as ¼, ½, 1, 2 or the word None. Clicking cycles through the options.
coordinateRoundingSettings.yStepDescript: Tooltip on the Y-axis step-size buttons in the Coordinate Rounding popover. Y is the front-to-back direction on the field. Left-click and right-click are mouse actions that step through the preset rounding sizes.
coordinateRoundingSettings.yStepValue: Short button in the toolbar next to Coordinate Rounding showing how Y positions (front to back) are rounded. {value} is the rounding, such as ¼, ½, 1, 2 or the word None. Clicking cycles through the options.
coordinateSheet.countAbbreviation: Column header on both printable coordinate sheets (the full sheet, one page per marcher, and the quarter-page sheet; exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog), abbreviated to fit a narrow column. The column lists each page's number of counts (beats of music the marcher has to get to that position). English writes it without a period ("Ct"). Keep it very short.
coordinateSheet.countsColumnLabel: Screen-reader label for the abbreviated "Ct." column header in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog). The column lists how many counts (beats of music) lead to each page.
coordinateSheet.page: Header cell on a quarter-page coordinate sheet, part of the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog). A marcher with many pages gets several quarter sheets; this numbers them. {page} is the sheet's number, starting at 1.
coordinateSheet.pageAbbreviation: Column header on the full printable coordinate sheet (one page per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog), abbreviated to fit a narrow column. The column lists page names (each page is a numbered set position in the drill, e.g. 1, 2, 2A). English writes it without a period ("Pg"); the quarter-page sheet has its own key. Keep it very short.
coordinateSheet.pageColumnLabel: Screen-reader label for the abbreviated "Pg." column header in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog). The column lists page names (numbered set positions in the drill).
coordinateSheet.quarterPageAbbreviation: Column header on the quarter-page coordinate sheet (four small sheets per printed page, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog), abbreviated to fit a narrow column. The column lists page names (each page is a numbered set position in the drill, e.g. 1, 2, 2A). English writes it with a period ("Pg."), unlike the full sheet's "Pg" (coordinateSheet.pageAbbreviation). Keep it very short.
coordinateSheet.tableLabel: Screen-reader label for the table in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog). {drillNumber} is the marcher's drill number, such as B1 (a section letter and a number).
coordinateSheet.unnamedMarcherName: Name used for a marcher who has no name, in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog) and in the exported PDF's file name. {section} is the marcher's section (e.g. Trumpet) and {number} the number from their drill number (e.g. 3 for T3).
coordinateSheet.xHeader: Column header in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog) when the user chose X/Y headers. The column gives each position side to side (along the length of the field). Usually kept as the letter X.
coordinateSheet.yHeader: Column header in the printable coordinate sheet (one per marcher, exported as a PDF and previewed in the Export dialog) when the user chose X/Y headers. The column gives each position front to back (across the width of the field). Usually kept as the letter Y.
coordinates.full: A marcher's full drill coordinate: {x} is the side-to-side part (for example "S1: 3 inside 35 yard line") and {y} the front-to-back part (for example "4 behind front hash").
coordinates.terse.behind: Short front-to-back drill coordinate: {steps} steps behind (away from the audience from) the reference line {checkpoint}. "BE" abbreviates "behind"; keep it very short. {checkpoint} is the line's short name from the field's settings (for example "FSL" for front sideline). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.terse.inFrontOf: Short front-to-back drill coordinate: {steps} steps in front of (toward the audience from) the reference line {checkpoint}. "FR" abbreviates "in front of"; keep it very short. {checkpoint} is the line's short name from the field's settings (for example "FH" for front hash, "BSL" for back sideline). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.terse.inside: Short side-to-side drill coordinate, for compact readouts and printed coordinate sheets: {steps} steps inside (toward the center of the field from) the reference line {checkpoint}. "IN" abbreviates "inside"; keep it very short. {checkpoint} is the line's short name, usually the yard number (for example "35"). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.terse.onX: Short side-to-side drill coordinate of a marcher exactly on the reference line {checkpoint}, its short name, usually the yard number (for example "50"). Keep it very short.
coordinates.terse.onY: Short front-to-back drill coordinate of a marcher exactly on the reference line {checkpoint}, its short name from the field's settings (for example "FH" for front hash). Keep it very short.
coordinates.terse.outside: Short side-to-side drill coordinate: {steps} steps outside (away from the center of the field from) the reference line {checkpoint}. "OUT" abbreviates "outside"; keep it very short. {checkpoint} is the line's short name, usually the yard number (for example "40"). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.verbose.behind: Front-to-back drill coordinate, without the word "steps": the marcher stands {steps} steps farther from the audience than the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "front sideline"). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.verbose.behindSteps: Front-to-back drill coordinate: the marcher stands {steps} steps farther from the audience than the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "front sideline"). {steps} may have decimals (for example 2.5).
coordinates.verbose.inFrontOf: Front-to-back drill coordinate, without the word "steps": the marcher stands {steps} steps closer to the audience than the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "front hash" or "back sideline"). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.verbose.inFrontOfSteps: Front-to-back drill coordinate: the marcher stands {steps} steps closer to the audience than the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "front hash"). {steps} may have decimals (for example 2.5).
coordinates.verbose.inside: Side-to-side drill coordinate, without the word "steps": the marcher stands {steps} steps from the reference line {checkpoint}, toward the center of the field. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "35 yard line"). {steps} may have decimals. Shown in the inspector and on printed coordinate sheets.
coordinates.verbose.insideSteps: Side-to-side drill coordinate: the marcher stands {steps} steps from the reference line {checkpoint}, toward the center of the field. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "35 yard line"). {steps} may have decimals (for example 2.5). Shown in the inspector and on printed coordinate sheets.
coordinates.verbose.onX: Side-to-side drill coordinate of a marcher standing exactly on the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "50 yard line").
coordinates.verbose.onY: Front-to-back drill coordinate of a marcher standing exactly on the reference line {checkpoint}. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "front hash").
coordinates.verbose.outside: Side-to-side drill coordinate, without the word "steps": the marcher stands {steps} steps from the reference line {checkpoint}, away from the center of the field. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "40 yard line"). {steps} may have decimals.
coordinates.verbose.outsideSteps: Side-to-side drill coordinate: the marcher stands {steps} steps from the reference line {checkpoint}, away from the center of the field. {checkpoint} is the line's name from the field's settings, often in English (for example "40 yard line"). {steps} may have decimals (for example 2.5).
coordinates.withSide: A marcher's side-to-side drill coordinate with the side of the field in front. {side} is the side's short name from the field's settings (for example "S1" for side 1); {position} is the rest of the coordinate (for example "3 steps inside 35 yard line"). Shown in the inspector and on printed coordinate sheets.
ensembles.attachDialog.attach: Confirm button in the dialog for linking the open show file to a production of the OpenMarch cloud account. Verb.
ensembles.attachDialog.cancel: Button in the 'Attach to Production' dialog. Closes it without attaching. Verb.
ensembles.attachDialog.description: Body of the 'Attach to Production' dialog. A production is a show or season inside an ensemble (a group such as a band) on the user's OpenMarch online account. Attaching links the open .dots file to it, so its data can be uploaded to the mobile companion app named 'OpenMarch - On the Move' (keep that name as is).
ensembles.attachDialog.title: Title of the dialog for linking the open show file to a production (a show or season in an ensemble on the user's OpenMarch account).
ensembles.attachToProduction: Hover label shown at the right of a production's row in the ensemble list. Clicking the row links the open show file to that production. Verb phrase; small text.
ensembles.createDialog.cancel: Button in the 'Create Production' dialog. Closes it without creating anything. Verb.
ensembles.createDialog.create: Submit button of the 'Create Production' dialog. Creates a new production (a show or season) in an ensemble. Verb.
ensembles.createDialog.creating: Label of the submit button of the 'Create Production' dialog while the request is running. Present participle with an ellipsis.
ensembles.createDialog.description: Subtitle of the 'Create Production' dialog. {ensembleName} is the name of the ensemble (a group, such as a band, on the user's OpenMarch account), for example 'Lincoln High Marching Band'. A production is a show or season within it.
ensembles.createDialog.failed: Error toast shown when creating a production failed.
ensembles.createDialog.nameLabel: Label of the text field in the 'Create Production' dialog for the new production's name. A production is a show or season within an ensemble.
ensembles.createDialog.namePlaceholder: Placeholder text of the production-name field in the 'Create Production' dialog, for example 'Fall Show 2026'.
ensembles.createDialog.nameRequired: Error under the production-name field in the 'Create Production' dialog when it is left empty. Imperative.
ensembles.createDialog.title: Title of the dialog for creating a production (a show or season) inside an ensemble on the user's OpenMarch online account.
ensembles.createProduction: Small button in the ensemble list, next to a plus icon. Opens the dialog for adding a new production (a show or season) to that ensemble. Verb phrase.
ensembles.empty: Empty-state text in the ensemble list when the user's OpenMarch account has no ensembles. An ensemble is a group such as a marching band. 'Above' points to the create control placed above the list.
ensembles.loadError: Error shown in place of the ensembles list in the Export to Mobile panel when the list couldn't be loaded from OpenMarch On the Move (the mobile app's service). {error} is the reason, often from the server and possibly in English.
ensembles.loading: Loading text in the ensemble list while the user's ensembles (groups such as a band) are fetched from the OpenMarch account. Present participle with an ellipsis.
ensembles.viewDetails: Link below an ensemble's productions that opens the ensemble's page on the OpenMarch website in the browser. An ensemble is a group such as a marching band. An external-link icon follows the text.
errorBoundary.copyErrorMessage: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the clipboard icon button next to the technical error message on the full-screen error page. Copies that message so the user can send it to support.
errorBoundary.copySupportEmail: Button on the full-screen error page that copies the OpenMarch support email address to the clipboard.
errorBoundary.emailCopied: Alert box shown after the user clicks "Copy support email" on the full-screen error page: the support email address is now on the clipboard.
errorBoundary.errorCopied: Short confirmation that appears for two seconds next to the copy button on the full-screen error page, after the error message was copied to the clipboard.
errorBoundary.hearAboutThis: Heading on the full-screen error page asking the user to report the problem to the OpenMarch team.
errorBoundary.joinDiscord: Button on the full-screen error page that opens an invite to the OpenMarch community chat server on Discord (a chat app; keep the name Discord).
errorBoundary.reachOut: Paragraph on the full-screen error page, under "We want to hear about this!", encouraging the user to contact the team. OpenMarch is the product name; keep it as is.
errorBoundary.refreshApp: Main button at the bottom of the full-screen error page. Reloads the app window to recover from the error.
errorBoundary.reportIssue: Button on the full-screen error page that opens the OpenMarch website's guide on submitting feedback and bug reports.
errorBoundary.stoppedBecause: Line on the full-screen error page, directly above the technical error message (shown in English, as written by the program). OpenMarch is the product name; keep it as is.
errorBoundary.title: Heading of the full-screen error page shown when OpenMarch hits an unexpected error and stops working. The ":(" is a sad-face emoticon; keep it or use your language's equivalent.
exportCoordinates.abbreviateCoordinateDe: Checkbox label in the Coordinate Sheets tab of the Export dialog. When checked, the printed sheets use short coordinate descriptions (for example abbreviated yard line and side names) so they fit more easily.
exportCoordinates.addPagesToEnd: Button in a warning above the export options. Some moves run past the last page of the show. This button adds new pages to the end so those moves are included. Verb phrase; "page" is a section of the show between two page flags.
exportCoordinates.addPagesToEndTitle: Tooltip for the "Add pages to the end" button. It adds a new page every N counts after the last page, until the end of the last move. {counts} is the number of counts (beats of music) each new page lasts, for example 8. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
exportCoordinates.cancel: Button in the Export dialog that stops an export in progress, or closes the dialog. Verb, short.
exportCoordinates.cancelledByUser: Message when the user cancels an export while it is running. Shown as a status line or inside a failure toast.
exportCoordinates.checkFieldProperties: One line in a checklist shown when export is not available. {status} selects the mark: 'ok' when the field properties (the field's size and setup) are present, shown as a check mark ✓; 'other' when it is missing, shown as a cross ✗. Keep the select structure and the words 'ok' and 'other'; you may replace the marks with what your language uses for yes and no.
exportCoordinates.checkMarcher: One line in a checklist shown when export is not available. {status} selects the mark: 'ok' when at least one marcher (performer) exists, shown as a check mark ✓; 'other' when it is missing, shown as a cross ✗. Keep the select structure and the words 'ok' and 'other'; you may replace the marks with what your language uses for yes and no.
exportCoordinates.checkPage: One line in a checklist shown when export is not available. {status} selects the mark: 'ok' when the show has more than one page ("Page" is a section of the show between two page flags), shown as a check mark ✓; 'other' when it is missing, shown as a cross ✗. Keep the select structure and the words 'ok' and 'other'; you may replace the marks with what your language uses for yes and no.
exportCoordinates.coordinateSheets: Tab title in the Export dialog. A coordinate sheet is a printable table for one marcher listing their position (side to side and front to back) at every page of the show. Plural noun, short.
exportCoordinates.drillChartPreviewAlt: Alt text for the example image in the Drill Charts tab of the Export dialog. It shows what an exported drill chart (a printed picture of the field with every marcher's position on one page) looks like.
exportCoordinates.drillCharts: Tab title in the Export dialog. A drill chart is a printed picture of the field showing a marcher's (or everyone's) positions on each page of the show. Plural noun, short.
exportCoordinates.errorRendering: Placeholder shown in place of one marcher's sheet when it could not be built. {drillNumber} is the marcher's drill number (their ID in the show), for example "B1".
exportCoordinates.errorTitle: Heading shown in the coordinate sheet preview when it cannot be built because required show data is missing. A list of what is missing follows.
exportCoordinates.exampleMarcherName: Made-up marcher name used in the coordinate sheet preview as a sample, so the user can see how the sheet looks. A person's name or label such as "Example".
exportCoordinates.exampleMarcherSection: Made-up section name used in the coordinate sheet preview as a sample marcher's section. A section is a group of marchers who play the same instrument, e.g. "Baritone" (a brass instrument). Use the usual local name of an instrument section.
exportCoordinates.export: Button in the Export dialog that starts the export. Verb, short. Changes to the "Exporting... Please wait" text while it runs.
exportCoordinates.exportButton: Toolbar button (in the File tab) that opens the Export dialog. Verb, short.
exportCoordinates.exportComplete: Status text under the progress bar when an export has finished successfully.
exportCoordinates.exportFailed: Status text under the progress bar when an export did not finish because of an error.
exportCoordinates.exportFailedToast: Error notification when an export fails. {error} is the reason, usually a short message in English, for example "Unknown error".
exportCoordinates.exportNotAvailable: Heading shown instead of the export preview when the show is not ready to export, e.g. no pages or no marchers yet. Also used as a loading label in the video preview when the preview cannot be built.
exportCoordinates.exportNotAvailableDesc: Explanation shown below "Export Not Available". Lists what the show needs before it can be exported: field properties (the field's size and setup), at least one page other than the first, and at least one marcher.
exportCoordinates.exportPDFSuccess: Success notification after drill charts have been exported as PDF files. A button to open the export folder follows it.
exportCoordinates.exportVideoButton: Toolbar button (File tab) and dialog title in the web version of OpenMarch, which can only export video. Verb phrase.
exportCoordinates.exportedCount: Success notification after coordinate sheets are exported. {count} is the number of marchers whose sheets were exported, e.g. 24. A button to open the export folder follows it.
exportCoordinates.exporting: Label on the Export button while an export is running (the button is disabled). Keep the ellipsis.
exportCoordinates.fieldPropertiesNotLoad: Internal error message when an export starts before the field properties (the field's size and setup) have loaded. May appear in a failure toast.
exportCoordinates.fieldPropertiesRequire: Error notification when the user tries to export but the field properties (the field's size and setup) are missing.
exportCoordinates.frontToBackHeader: Column heading of a coordinate sheet: the marcher's position measured from front to back of the field (distance from the front sideline). Paired with "Side to Side". Printed on the sheet; keep short.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.0: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar while coordinate sheets are made. "8 to 5" is a marching term: eight steps for every five yards (the standard step size). Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.1: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar. "Cover down" is a marching term: line up directly behind the person in front of you, and "files" are the lines of marchers. Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.2: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar. "Cleaning drill" means polishing the show's movements until they are precise. Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.3: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar. "In step" means everyone marching on the same foot at the same time. Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.4: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar. Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.funPhrase.5: Playful message cycling under the export progress bar. Keep the emoji and the lighthearted tone.
exportCoordinates.generatingPDF: Status text under the export progress bar while a PDF is being made. {drillNumber} is a marcher's drill number (their ID in the show), for example "B1", or "MAIN" for the single overview chart.
exportCoordinates.includeMeasures: Checkbox label in the Coordinate Sheets tab of the Export dialog. When checked, the sheet includes a column with the music measure number for each page. A measure is a bar of music.
exportCoordinates.includeNotesAppendix: Checkbox label in the Drill Charts tab of the Export dialog. When checked, extra pages listing each page's notes are added at the end of the PDF.
exportCoordinates.includeNotesAppendixTo: Tooltip heading for the "Include notes appendix pages" checkbox. A "set" is one page (one formation) of the drill. Portrait means a tall page orientation.
Second paragraph of the tooltip for the notes appendix checkbox. Notes written on a page of the show are cut short when printed under the drill chart; the appendix has the full text.
