exportCoordinates.individualCharts: Checkbox label in the Drill Charts tab of the Export dialog. When checked, a separate drill chart PDF is made for each marcher.
exportCoordinates.individualChartsToolti: Tooltip for the "Individual Drill Charts" checkbox: each marcher gets their own personalized drill chart PDF.
Second line of the tooltip for "Individual Drill Charts", saying what happens when it is unchecked: a single overview chart PDF is made instead.
exportCoordinates.marcherPositionsMissin: Reason shown in an error toast when one marcher's drill chart is skipped because the marcher has no position on some pages. It is inserted as {error} into the "SVG export for {drillNumber} failed" message.
exportCoordinates.marchersNotLoaded: Internal error message when an export starts before the list of marchers has loaded. May appear in a failure toast.
exportCoordinates.marchersWithoutPositio: Warning notification when some marchers have no position at all, so their sheets are left out or empty. {drillNumbers} is a comma-separated list of the marchers' drill numbers (their IDs), for example "B1, B2".
exportCoordinates.measuresHeader: Column heading of a coordinate sheet: the music measure number (a measure is a bar of music) for each page. Printed on the sheet; keep short.
exportCoordinates.mobile: Tab title in the Export dialog for exporting the show to the OpenMarch "On the Move" phone app for marchers. Short.
exportCoordinates.mobilePreviewAlt: Screen-reader description of a picture on the Mobile tab that previews the On the Move phone app, where marchers see their positions.
exportCoordinates.movesPastEnd: Warning above the export options. Moves (a movement of marchers over time) can extend past the show's last page flag; those parts are not exported. {count} is the number of such moves, e.g. 3. {page} is the name of the last page, e.g. "12". "Pg" is short for page.
exportCoordinates.noFieldProperties: Line in the coordinate sheet preview error list: the field properties (the field's size and setup) are missing.
exportCoordinates.noMarcher: Line in the coordinate sheet preview error list: no marcher was provided to build the sheet for.
exportCoordinates.noMarcherPages: Line in the coordinate sheet preview error list: the marcher has no positions on any page.
exportCoordinates.noPages: Line in the coordinate sheet preview error list: the show has no pages.
exportCoordinates.openExportDirectory: Link-style button in a success notification that opens the folder or file that was just exported on the user's computer.
exportCoordinates.openExportDirectoryErr: Error notification when the exported folder could not be opened. {error} is the system's message, usually English, for example "Path not found".
exportCoordinates.organizeBySection: Checkbox label in the Coordinate Sheets tab of the Export dialog. When checked, the PDFs are grouped into folders by section (a group of marchers who play the same instrument).
exportCoordinates.organizeBySectionHint: Tooltip for the "Organize by Section" checkbox in the coordinate sheet export. Score order means the usual order of instruments on a music score. A coordinate sheet is a page listing one marcher's position on every page of the show.
exportCoordinates.pdfExportFailed: Error notification when making the drill chart PDF fails. {error} is the reason, usually a short English message.
exportCoordinates.preview: Heading above the preview image in the Export dialog, showing how the sheet or chart will look. Noun.
exportCoordinates.quarterPageLayout: Checkbox label in the Coordinate Sheets tab of the Export dialog. When checked, four coordinate sheets are printed on one page (each is a quarter of the page) to save paper.
exportCoordinates.rounding.eighth: Choice in the "Coordinate rounding" list of the coordinate sheet export: positions are rounded to the nearest eighth of a step (a step is the standard marching stride used to measure the field).
exportCoordinates.rounding.half: Choice in the "Coordinate rounding" list of the coordinate sheet export: positions are rounded to the nearest half step (a step is the standard marching stride used to measure the field).
exportCoordinates.rounding.quarter: Choice in the "Coordinate rounding" list of the coordinate sheet export: positions are rounded to the nearest quarter step (a step is the standard marching stride used to measure the field).
exportCoordinates.rounding.tenth: Choice in the "Coordinate rounding" list of the coordinate sheet export: positions are rounded to the nearest tenth of a step (a step is the standard marching stride used to measure the field).
exportCoordinates.rounding.whole: Choice in the "Coordinate rounding" list of the coordinate sheet export: marchers' positions on the printed sheets are rounded to the nearest whole step (a step is the standard marching stride used to measure the field).
exportCoordinates.roundingDenominator: Label for a dropdown in the Coordinate Sheets tab that sets how precisely printed coordinates are rounded (to the nearest whole step, half step, quarter step and so on). Ends with a colon.
exportCoordinates.saveDialog.chooseFolde: Title of the system's save dialog where the person picks the folder for exported coordinate sheets or drill charts (PDF files).
exportCoordinates.saveDialog.exportHere: Button in the system's save dialog that exports the coordinate sheets or drill charts (PDF files) into the chosen folder.
exportCoordinates.saveDialog.savePdfTitl: Title of the system's save dialog for saving exported coordinate sheets as one PDF file.
exportCoordinates.saveDialog.videoTitle: Title of the system's save dialog for choosing where to save the show exported as a video file.
exportCoordinates.sectionAppearancesNotL: Internal error message when an export starts before the marcher section colors and styles have loaded. May appear in a failure toast.
exportCoordinates.selectRoundingDenomina: Placeholder shown on the rounding dropdown in the Coordinate Sheets tab when nothing is selected. Short.
exportCoordinates.showChangedDuringExpor: Error shown when the show was edited while an export was running, so the export was stopped. Asks the user to try again.
exportCoordinates.sideToSideHeader: Column heading of a coordinate sheet: the marcher's position measured across the field from sideline to sideline (relative to the yard lines). Paired with "Front to Back". Printed on the sheet; keep short.
exportCoordinates.svgExportFailed: Error notification when one marcher's drill chart image fails. {drillNumber} is the marcher's drill number (their ID in the show), e.g. "B1". {error} is the reason, a short message.
exportCoordinates.svgGenerationFailed: Error notification when drawing the drill chart images fails. {error} is the reason, a short message.
exportCoordinates.title: Title of the Export dialog (it can export coordinate sheets, drill charts, video and the mobile app). Short.
exportCoordinates.unknownError: Fallback reason inserted into error messages when no specific error text is available.
exportCoordinates.unsortedSection: Name of the folder or group used in the export for marchers who have no section assigned. A section is a group of marchers who play the same instrument.
exportCoordinates.useXYHeaders: Checkbox label in the Coordinate Sheets tab of the Export dialog. When checked, the sheet's two coordinate columns are headed "X" and "Y" instead of "Side to Side" and "Front to Back".
exportCoordinates.video: Tab title in the Export dialog for exporting the show as a video of the marchers moving. Short noun.
exportCoordinates.webMobileUnavailable.d: Explanation under "Mobile upload isn't available here": uploading to the On the Move phone app needs an OpenMarch account, this test build can't sign in, so use the main web editor (keep the address editor.openmarch.com as is) or the desktop app.
exportCoordinates.webMobileUnavailable.o: Button that opens the main OpenMarch web editor in a new tab. Keep the address editor.openmarch.com unchanged.
exportCoordinates.webMobileUnavailable.t: Heading in the Mobile tab of the Export dialog, in test or development builds of the browser version of OpenMarch, where signing in (needed to upload to the phone app) doesn't work.
exportCoordinates.videoAudioNoData: Error shown in the "Video export failed" message of the Export dialog when the show's selected audio file is empty, so the video can't include the music.
exportCoordinates.videoAudioTrack: Line in the video export tab saying which music file the video will include. {name} is the audio file's name, for example "Opener - full band".
exportCoordinates.videoBackground: Label for a Light/Dark choice in the video export tab: whether the video's background is light or dark.
exportCoordinates.videoBranding: Branding drawn in the bottom-right corner of every exported video, next to the OpenMarch logo (the video export tab). {product} is the app's name, OpenMarch, which stays the same in every language. Keep it short: it sits in a small pill over the video.
exportCoordinates.videoExportFailed: Error notification when a video export fails. {error} is the reason, a short message.
exportCoordinates.videoExportSuccess: Success notification after a video was exported. A button to open the video file follows it.
exportCoordinates.videoFieldFraming: Subheading in the video export tab for sliders that control which part of the field is visible in the video (zoom and position).
exportCoordinates.videoFieldOffsetX: Label for a slider in the video export tab that moves the field left and right within the video frame.
exportCoordinates.videoFieldOffsetY: Label for a slider in the video export tab that moves the field up and down within the video frame.
exportCoordinates.videoFieldResetFraming: Button in the video export tab that resets the field zoom and position to their defaults.
exportCoordinates.videoFieldScale: Label for a slider in the video export tab that zooms the field in or out within the video frame.
exportCoordinates.videoFrameRate: Label for a dropdown in the video export tab: how many pictures per second the video has (for example 30 fps).
exportCoordinates.videoFrameRateValue: Option in the Frame rate menu of the Video tab in the Export dialog, and the menu's current value. {fps} is the number of video frames per second, such as 30 or 60. "fps" is the usual abbreviation for frames per second.
exportCoordinates.videoNoAudio: Line in the video export tab: no music file is attached to the show, so the exported video has no sound (a silent track).
exportCoordinates.videoNoCanvas: Error shown in the "Video export failed" message of the Export dialog when the computer or browser couldn't create the drawing surface the video frames are drawn on.
exportCoordinates.videoNoDuration: Error shown in the "Video export failed" message of the Export dialog when the show's pages add up to no time at all, so the video would be empty.
exportCoordinates.videoNoEncoder: Error shown in the "Video export failed" message of the Export dialog when the computer or browser has no video encoder the export can use, so it can't make a video file.
exportCoordinates.videoNoPages: Error shown in the "Video export failed" message of the Export dialog when the show has no pages (no set positions), so there is nothing to put in the video.
exportCoordinates.videoNoWebGL: Message in the video export tab (desktop app) when the computer can't make videos because WebGL graphics (keep the name) are unavailable. Suggests turning on hardware acceleration or updating graphics drivers, then reopening the Export window.
exportCoordinates.videoOpenFile: Link-style button in the success notification of a video export; opens the exported video file.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlay: Heading in the video export tab for the information drawn on top of the video: set and count, measure number, tempo, and elapsed time.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayClock: Checkbox label in the video export tab: show the elapsed time (like a clock from the start of the show) on the video.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayCount: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. Shows which count (beat of music) of the current move is playing out of how many. {count} and {total} are numbers, possibly padded with zeros or spaces so the box doesn't change width.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayMeasure: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. The current measure (bar) number of the music, abbreviated. {measure} is the number. Use the usual short form for "measure" or "bar" in sheet music.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayMeasureWit: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. The current rehearsal mark and measure (bar) number of the music. {mark} is the rehearsal mark (a letter or name from the score, such as A); {measure} is the measure number. Keep the brackets and the abbreviation style of "m. {measure}".
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayMeasures: Checkbox label in the video export tab: show the music measure numbers (a measure is a bar of music) and rehearsal marks (letters or numbers printed in the score) on the video.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayPreviewHin: Help text under the video preview. The user can drag the on-screen information box (side handle changes its width, corner changes its size), drag empty space to move the field, scroll to zoom, or use sliders for exact adjustments.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlaySet: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. Names the set (a numbered marching position, also called a page) the marchers stand on. {set} is the set's name, such as 4 or 2A.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlaySetCounts: Checkbox label in the video export tab: show the current set (a set is one page, one formation, of the drill) and the count within it on the video.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlaySetTransit: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. Shows the marchers moving from one set (a numbered marching position, also called a page) to the next. {from} and {to} are set names, such as 4 and 5. Keep the arrow.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayTempo: Checkbox label in the video export tab: show the current tempo (speed of the music in beats per minute) on the video.
exportCoordinates.videoOverlayTempoValue: Text drawn into the exported video (and its preview in the Video tab of the Export dialog), in the on-screen info box. The current tempo. {bpm} is the number of beats per minute; "bpm" is its usual abbreviation.
exportCoordinates.videoPreviewLoading: Placeholder over the video preview while the preview is being prepared. Keep the ellipsis.
exportCoordinates.videoRendering: Status text under the progress bar while the video is being created. It can take a long time.
exportCoordinates.videoResolution: Label for a dropdown in the video export tab: the picture size of the video, such as 720p or 1080p.
exportCoordinates.videoWebChecking: Status line in the web version's video export while the browser's ability to make videos is being checked. Keep the ellipsis.
exportCoordinates.videoWebInMemory: Warning in the web version's video export. The browser can't write the video to disk while it is made, so it all stays in memory. Long shows may run out of memory; suggests the lower 720p resolution or another browser.
exportCoordinates.videoWebKeepOpen: Tip in the web version's video export: keep the OpenMarch tab open and the device screen on until the video is done; switching apps or locking the screen may interrupt it.
exportCoordinates.videoWebReady: Message when a video made in the web version is finished. {name} is the video's file name, for example "Show.mp4".
exportCoordinates.videoWebReadySilent: Second line under "Your video is ready" in the web version, explaining the video has no sound because this browser can't add music to videos.
exportCoordinates.videoWebSave: Button in the web version that saves the finished video to the device (downloads it or opens the share sheet). Verb phrase.
exportCoordinates.videoWebSaveHintApple: Hint for iPhone and iPad users after a video is ready. The quoted names, “Save Video” and “Save to Files”, are options in Apple's share sheet; use the exact translated names shown in iOS/iPadOS.
exportCoordinates.videoWebSaveMissing: Error notification in the web version when the user taps Save but the finished video is no longer available; asks them to export again.
exportCoordinates.videoWebSaved: Success notification in the web version after the finished video was saved to the device.
exportCoordinates.videoWebSilent: Warning in the web version's video export: this browser can't add the show's music to a video, so the video will have no sound.
exportCoordinates.videoWebUnsupported: Error in the web version's video export: the browser can't make videos at all. Lists browsers that work: Safari 16.4 or later, Chrome, Edge. Keep the browser names and the version number.
field.benchmark.running: Small status badge over the field while the benchmark runs. {kind} is the name of the test now running, one of: play, scrub, zoom, pan, drag (currently inserted in English and not translated). Example: "Running: zoom…".
field.errors.contextLost: Error shown in the toast when a video export of the field stops because the graphics card reset or took back its drawing surface. WebGL is a web graphics technology name; keep it as is.
field.errors.noWebGL: Error when the computer can't draw the field in 3D graphics (WebGL, a web graphics technology; keep the name as is). Can appear in the error toast when a video export fails.
field.errors.offscreenTimeout: Error shown in the toast when a video export fails because the hidden copy of the field it draws frames from didn't load in time.
field.general.exportField: Button in the Field side panel. Saves the current field setup (size, yard lines, labels, colors) to a file that can be imported into other OpenMarch shows. Verb phrase.
field.general.exportField.tooltip: Tooltip for the Export Field button in the Field side panel. The field (its size, lines and labels) is saved as a file that can be loaded in other shows.
field.general.importField: Button in the Field side panel. Opens a file picker to load a custom field setup (size, yard lines, labels, colors) that was exported before. Verb phrase.
field.general.importField.tooltip: Tooltip for the Import Field button in the Field side panel. Loads a field setup from a file the user picks (a file made with Export Field).
field.gestureChip.equalSpacings: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor while a marcher or shape is dragged. It follows a modifier key symbol (such as ⇧) and tells what that held key is doing: keeping the spaces between marchers equal. Lowercase, very short; the key symbol is added before it.
field.gestureChip.fine: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor during a drag, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the key makes the drag move more finely and precisely (smaller increments). Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.freeRatio: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor while resizing a shape, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the key lets the width and height change independently, so the proportions are not kept. Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.fromCenter: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor while drawing or resizing a shape, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the shape grows outward from its center instead of from a corner. Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.keepDirection: Small chip near the pointer naming what a held modifier key does during a drag on the field. Text: "keep direction".
field.gestureChip.keepRatio: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor while resizing a shape, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the key keeps the width-to-height proportions fixed. Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.oneAxis: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor during a drag, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the movement is limited to one direction (straight horizontal or vertical). Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.snapOff: Chip text that follows the cursor during a drag when snapping (the pull toward grid lines and other marchers) is turned off. Not preceded by a key symbol. Sentence-style capital S, very short.
field.gestureChip.wholeDegrees: Word in a small chip that follows the cursor while rotating, after a held modifier key symbol. It means the rotation snaps to whole degrees. Lowercase, very short.
field.gestureChip.withKey: One part of a small hint shown next to the pointer while dragging on the field: a modifier key the user is holding, then what holding it does. <keys></keys> is replaced by the key drawn as a keyboard key (such as Shift or ⌥); keep the tag. {word} is the effect, such as "fine" (moves in smaller steps) or "one axis" (moves only straight across or straight up and down). Change the order if your language puts the key after the effect.
field.quality.dismiss: Button on a warning notification that closes it after the user has read it. Informal acknowledgement, like "OK". Short.
field.quality.gpuCrashed: Body of a warning notification. The graphics processor (GPU) stopped responding while drawing the field, so the app switched to a simpler, lower-quality field view until the app is restarted. Performance mode is a setting under Settings > Appearance; the menu names are written in this sentence, so match their translated names.
field.quality.software.desktop: Body of a warning notification in the desktop app. The computer has no usable hardware-accelerated graphics (it draws with the CPU, "in software"), so the field uses a simpler view. Suggests updating graphics drivers and restarting OpenMarch.
field.quality.software.web: Body of a warning notification in the web version of OpenMarch. The browser draws graphics with the CPU instead of the graphics card, so the field uses a simpler view. The quoted menu path matches the English wording of Chrome and Edge's setting "Use graphics acceleration when available"; use the browser's own translated names where they differ.
field.quality.title: Title of a warning notification. The field is being drawn with a simpler, lower-quality view (to stay smooth) because of limited graphics support. A short statement, not a button.
field.quality.unavailable.desktop: Message shown in the desktop app in place of the field when WebGL (the graphics technology that draws the field; keep the name) can't start. Advises updating graphics drivers and restarting; reassures the user their saved show is not lost.
field.quality.unavailable.retry: Button under the "field can't be drawn" message that tries to start the field graphics again. Verb phrase, short.
field.quality.unavailable.title: Heading shown in place of the field when it can't be drawn at all because graphics (WebGL) aren't available. Followed by an explanation and a Try again button.
field.quality.unavailable.web: Message shown in the web version of OpenMarch in place of the field when WebGL graphics (keep the name) are turned off or blocked in the browser. The quoted menu path is the English wording of Chrome and Edge's setting; use the browser's own translated names where they differ. Reassures the user their show is not lost.
field.title: Title of the Field side panel, which opens from the sidebar and holds the field's size, lines, labels, colors and image options. Noun, short.
fieldDisplay.label: Screen-reader label for the field display bar, a column of small buttons at the top right of the field that change what the field shows (marcher labels, shape outlines and so on).
fieldDisplay.valueLabel: Screen-reader label of a field display bar button that has a current choice. {label} is the button's name (such as "Labels") and {value} the choice in effect (such as "Drill numbers").
fieldProperties.applyFieldType: Button below the field template dropdown that switches the show to the chosen field template (size, lines, labels). Shown only after a different template is picked. Verb phrase.
fieldProperties.applyFieldTypeWarning: Warning shown with the Apply Field Type button. Changing the field template does not move marchers: they keep their positions on the screen, so their field coordinates may change. The user can switch back to the previous template at any time.
fieldProperties.buttons.newXCheckpoint: Button on the Checkpoints tab that adds a new X-checkpoint, a reference line running front to back at a given number of steps from the center of the field (a yard line, for example). Verb phrase.
fieldProperties.buttons.newYCheckpoint: Button on the Checkpoints tab that adds a new Y-checkpoint, a reference line running side to side at a given number of steps from the front of the field (a hash or sideline, for example). Verb phrase.
fieldProperties.buttons.resetTheme: Button at the bottom of the Theme tab that restores all field colors to the defaults.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.created: Success notification after a checkpoint was added. {axis} is "X" (a line running front to back, positioned side to side) or "Y" (a line running side to side, positioned front to back). {steps} is its position in steps, for example 0 or -8.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.delete: Button that deletes one checkpoint (a reference line on the field) on the Checkpoints tab. Verb, short.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.deleteTooltip: Tooltip for the checkpoint Delete button. A checkpoint is a named reference line on the field.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.deleted: Success notification after a checkpoint was deleted. {axis} is "X" or "Y". {steps} is its position in steps, for example 16. {name} is the name the user gave it, for example "45 Yard Line". The quotation marks around {name} are part of the text.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.fieldLabel: Label of a text field in a checkpoint's settings: the text drawn on the field at this line (such as a yard number, "45"). Checkpoint = a named reference line.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.fieldLabelToo: Tooltip for the checkpoint "Field label" text field: the label shown on the field, such as the yard marker numbers.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.minimumRequir: Error notification when the user tries to delete a checkpoint but only two remain on that axis. {axis} is "X" or "Y"; keep the letter as is.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.name: Label of a text field in a checkpoint's settings: the checkpoint's own name. Noun, short.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.nameTooltip: Tooltip for a checkpoint's Name field. The name is only for the user, to recognize which checkpoint (a reference line on the field) they are editing.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.newXCheckpoin: Default name given to a newly added X-checkpoint (a reference line running front to back). The user can rename it.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.newYCheckpoin: Default name given to a newly added Y-checkpoint (a reference line running side to side). The user can rename it.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.shortName: Label of a text field in a checkpoint's settings: the main name of the line, shown in coordinate descriptions such as "2 steps outside 45 Yard Line". Short noun phrase.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.shortNameTool: Tooltip for a checkpoint's Short Name field. The quoted example is a typical name for a yard line on a football field.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.stepsFromCent: Label of a number field for an X-checkpoint: how many steps (one marching step, usually 22.5 inches) the line is from the center of the field, to the left or right.

Tooltip for the "Steps from center" field of an X-checkpoint (a line across the field, such as a yard line). Describes how far the line is from the field's center line, side to side. Negative numbers go toward the left as seen from the audience (the front of the field), which is Side 1 on a standard field; positive numbers go to the right.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.stepsFromFron: Label of a number field for a Y-checkpoint: how many steps (one marching step) the line is from the front sideline of the field.
Tooltip for the "Steps from front" field of a Y-checkpoint. Describes the distance from the front sideline; negative numbers go toward the back.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.useAsReferenc: Label of a switch in a checkpoint's settings. When on, this line can be used as a reference for describing coordinates (for example "2 steps behind the 45 yard line").
Tooltip for the "Use as reference" switch of a checkpoint (a reference line on the field).
fieldProperties.checkpoint.visible: Label of a switch in a checkpoint's settings that shows or hides this line on the field.
fieldProperties.checkpoint.visibleToolti: Tooltip for the Visible switch of a checkpoint (a reference line on the field).
fieldProperties.customField: Heading of the custom field editor in the Field side panel, shown once the user chooses to customize the field. Followed by tabs for General, Checkpoints, Image and Theme.
fieldProperties.customFieldDocs: Button next to the custom field heading that opens the online guide about editing the field grid in the browser. Short.
fieldProperties.customFieldName: Name shown in the field template dropdown for the user's customized field. Adjective used as a name, short.
fieldProperties.customization: Heading in the Field side panel above the field template dropdown and the Customize button. Noun.
fieldProperties.customize: Button in the Field side panel that turns the field into a custom field so the user can edit its size, lines, labels and colors. Verb, short.
fieldProperties.errors.fieldsHaveErrors: First line of the problem list in the alert for an invalid field file (Import Field). {issues} is one line per problem: the name of an entry in the file (a code name, not translated) and what is wrong with it. "Fields" here means entries in the file, not football fields.
fieldProperties.errors.invalidColor: Error notification when a color entered for the field theme is not valid.
fieldProperties.errors.invalidFile: Alert shown when a field file chosen with Import Field (a .fieldots file holding a field's layout) is missing values or has wrong ones. {details} is a list of the problems, one per line, starting with "The following fields have errors:". "Fields" here means entries in the file, not football fields.
fieldProperties.errors.invalidJson: Alert shown when a field file chosen with Import Field (a .fieldots file holding a field's layout) can't be read because it isn't valid JSON text. JSON is a file format name; keep it as is.
fieldProperties.errors.noPropertiesToLoa: Error shown in the Field side panel when the field's settings could not be loaded. This is not expected to happen; asks the user to contact support.
fieldProperties.errors.notDefined: Error shown in the field template picker when the field's settings are missing. Not expected to happen; asks the user to contact support. "FieldProperties" is an internal name; keep as is.
fieldProperties.errors.unknownValidation: Shown in the alert for an invalid field file (Import Field) when the file was rejected but no specific problem was reported.
fieldProperties.fieldTemplate.custom: Group heading in the field template dropdown above the user's own customized field. Noun/adjective, short.
fieldProperties.fieldTemplate.football: Group heading in the field template dropdown for American football field templates (yard lines and hashes), for example high school and college fields.
fieldProperties.fieldTemplate.grid: Group heading in the field template dropdown for grid-based templates without football markings, such as indoor gym floors and SoundSport.
fieldProperties.fieldTemplate.label: Label for the dropdown where the user picks a field template (a predefined field size and set of lines).
fieldProperties.fieldType.label: Placeholder on a field settings picker (the field template, or the measurement system) when nothing is chosen yet. The field type is the kind of field the show is on, such as a football field or a grid.
fieldProperties.general: Heading in the Field side panel above the Import Field and Export Field buttons. General settings; noun.
fieldProperties.labels.background: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color behind the whole field.
fieldProperties.labels.backgroundImageOp: Label of a slider (and its screen-reader label) on the Image tab: how see-through the field's background image is, from 0% to 100%.
fieldProperties.labels.backgroundImageRa: Label above a read-only box on the Image tab showing the width-to-height ratio of the background image, for comparing it with the field's ratio.
fieldProperties.labels.bottom: Label of a switch in the External Labels section: show the labels placed outside the field along its bottom edge. One of Left, Right, Bottom, Top. Single word.
fieldProperties.labels.conformMethod: Label of the Fit/Fill dropdown on the Image tab: how the background image is resized to match the field (Fit or Fill).
fieldProperties.labels.conformingMethod: Screen-reader label of the Fit/Fill dropdown on the Image tab; says how the background image is made to match the field's size. Not shown visually.
fieldProperties.labels.directorsLeft: Label of a text field on the General tab: the name of the left side of the field as the director sees it, for example "Side 1" or "Audience Left". Appears in printed coordinate descriptions.
fieldProperties.labels.directorsRight: Label of a text field on the General tab: the name of the right side of the field as the director sees it, for example "Side 2" or "Audience Right". Appears in printed coordinate descriptions.
fieldProperties.labels.externalLabels: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the labels drawn outside the field (for example side names).
fieldProperties.labels.fieldLabels: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the labels drawn on the field, such as the yard numbers.
fieldProperties.labels.fieldName: Label of a text field on the General tab: the name of the field template, for example "High School Football Field".
fieldProperties.labels.fieldRatio: Label above a read-only box on the Image tab showing the field's width-to-height ratio.
fieldProperties.labels.gridLines: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the grid lines drawn across the field.
fieldProperties.labels.halfLineXInterval: Label of a number field on the General tab: spacing, in steps, of the extra half lines between the main lines along the X axis (side to side). Cosmetic only.
fieldProperties.labels.halfLineYInterval: Label of a number field on the General tab: spacing, in steps, of the extra half lines between the main lines along the Y axis (front to back). Cosmetic only.
fieldProperties.labels.height: Label above a read-only box on the Image tab showing the field's height (front to back) in steps and in real units.
fieldProperties.labels.left: Label of a switch in the External Labels section: show the labels placed outside the field along its left edge. One of Left, Right, Bottom, Top. Single word.
fieldProperties.labels.leftAbbreviation: Label of a text field on the General tab: a short form of the left side name, for example "S1". Used in compact coordinate descriptions.
fieldProperties.labels.marcherFill: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the inside color of marcher dots on the field. A marcher is a performer.
fieldProperties.labels.marcherOutline: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the outline color of marcher dots on the field.
fieldProperties.labels.marcherText: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the text drawn on marcher dots (their number or label).
fieldProperties.labels.measurementSystem: Label of a dropdown on the General tab: use Imperial (inches) or Metric (centimeters) units for step size.
fieldProperties.labels.nextPath: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the path showing where marchers go next, on the following page. A path is a line drawn between positions.
fieldProperties.labels.noBackgroundImage: Shown under Background Image Ratio in the field settings' Image tab when the field has no background image, so there is no ratio to show. "Not available"; keep it short.
fieldProperties.labels.previousPath: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the path showing where marchers came from, on the previous page. A path is a line drawn between positions.
fieldProperties.labels.primaryLines: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the main field lines, such as yard lines.
fieldProperties.labels.right: Label of a switch in the External Labels section: show the labels placed outside the field along its right edge. One of Left, Right, Bottom, Top. Single word.
fieldProperties.labels.rightAbbreviation: Label of a text field on the General tab: a short form of the right side name, for example "S2". Used in compact coordinate descriptions.
fieldProperties.labels.secondaryLines: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the lighter secondary lines, such as the in-between lines and hashes.
fieldProperties.labels.shapeType: Label of a dropdown on the Theme tab (also its screen-reader label) that chooses the default marcher dot shape: circle, square, triangle or X.
fieldProperties.labels.shapes: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color used for shapes drawn on the field.
fieldProperties.labels.showBackgroundIma: Label of a switch on the Image tab: show or hide the background image behind the field.
fieldProperties.labels.stepSize: Label of a number field on the General tab: the length of one marching step, in inches or centimeters (for example 22.5 inches).
fieldProperties.labels.stepSizeWarningRa: Label of the step size warning field in the General tab when a threshold is set; without one, the label is fieldProperties.labels.stepSizeWarningThreshold alone, so translate the start of both the same way. The field holds the longest step length allowed before a marcher's path is flagged as too fast. {steps} is the same limit written as the drill-writer ratio "steps per 5 yards", for example 4 or 6.5. Example: "Step Size Warning Threshold (4 to 5)".
fieldProperties.labels.stepSizeWarningTh: Label of a number field (General tab and New Show wizard): the longest step length allowed before a marcher's path is flagged as too fast, in inches or centimeters. 0 turns the warning off.
fieldProperties.labels.stepsFromFrontToA: Label of a number field on the General tab. Position of the "away" yard-line numbers (the ones on the back half of the field): steps from the front sideline to the outer (bottom) edge of those numbers.
Label of a number field on the General tab. Position of the "away" yard-line numbers (the ones on the back half of the field): steps from the front sideline to the inner (top) edge of those numbers.
fieldProperties.labels.stepsFromFrontToH: Label of a number field on the General tab. Position of the "home" yard-line numbers (the ones on the front half of the field): steps from the front sideline to the outer (bottom) edge of those numbers.
Label of a number field on the General tab. Position of the "home" yard-line numbers (the ones on the front half of the field): steps from the front sideline to the inner (top) edge of those numbers.
fieldProperties.labels.temporaryPath: Label of a color picker on the Theme tab: the color of the temporary path shown while a move is being drawn or previewed. A path is a line between positions.
fieldProperties.labels.top: Label of a switch in the External Labels section: show the labels placed outside the field along its top edge. One of Left, Right, Bottom, Top. Single word.
fieldProperties.labels.useHashes: Label of a switch on the Checkpoints tab: draw Y-checkpoints as hash marks, like a football field. Hash marks are short ticks. Off draws full lines.
fieldProperties.labels.width: Label above a read-only box on the Image tab showing the field's width (side to side) in steps and in real units.
fieldProperties.labels.widthHeight: Small label after the field's (or its background image's) width-to-height ratio in the field settings' Image tab: w/h means width divided by height. Keep it short, using your language's abbreviations for width and height.
fieldProperties.loading: Shown in place of the field template picker in the field settings while the show's field properties are being read.
fieldProperties.measurements.feet: The field's width or height in feet, shown in the Image tab of the field settings for a show that uses imperial measurements. {value} is the number, already written with two decimals in the app's language. Use your language's usual short form for feet.
fieldProperties.measurements.meters: The field's width or height in meters, shown in the Image tab of the field settings for a show that uses metric measurements. {value} is the number, already written with two decimals in the app's language. Use your language's usual short form for meters.
fieldProperties.measurements.steps: A distance measured in marching steps, shown in the field settings: the field's width or height in the Image tab, and how far a reference line (such as a yard line or hash) is from the field's center or front. {count} is the number of steps and may have decimals or be negative.
fieldProperties.messages.fieldRatio: Shape of the field, or of its background image, in the field settings' Image tab: width to height. {ratio} is a whole-number ratio such as 16:9 and {decimal} the same ratio as a decimal such as 1.778. Followed by a small w/h label.
fieldProperties.messages.measurementModi: Note at the bottom of the Image tab explaining that the field's measurements shown above can only be changed through the X and Y checkpoint positions, the step size and the background image.
fieldProperties.options.fill: Option in the background image Fit/Fill dropdown: the image is enlarged to cover the whole field, cropping what does not fit. Short.
fieldProperties.options.fit: Option in the background image Fit/Fill dropdown: the image is scaled so all of it fits inside the field, possibly leaving empty bands. Short.
fieldProperties.options.imperial: Option in the measurement system dropdown: units based on inches, used in the US. Short.
fieldProperties.options.metric: Option in the measurement system dropdown: units based on centimeters. Short.
fieldProperties.sections.externalLabels: Section heading on the General tab above the switches that show or hide labels outside the field on its sides.
fieldProperties.sections.fieldLabels: Section heading on the General tab above the fields that place the yard-line numbers on the field.
fieldProperties.sections.general: Section heading at the top of the General tab of the custom field editor.
fieldProperties.sections.imageRendering: Section heading on the Image tab above the settings for the field's background image (show, fit or fill, opacity).
fieldProperties.sections.measurements: Section heading on the Image tab above read-only readouts of the field's width, height and ratios.
fieldProperties.sections.sideDescription: Section heading on the General tab above the fields that name the left and right sides of the field and their short forms.
fieldProperties.sections.theme: Section heading at the top of the Theme tab, which holds the field's colors.
fieldProperties.sections.xCheckpoints: Section heading on the Checkpoints tab above the X-checkpoints: reference lines that run front to back and are positioned side to side from the field's center (for example yard lines).
fieldProperties.sections.yCheckpoints: Section heading on the Checkpoints tab above the Y-checkpoints: reference lines that run side to side and are positioned front to back from the front sideline (for example hashes).
fieldProperties.tabs.checkpoints: Tab title in the custom field editor, for the field's reference lines (checkpoints). Plural noun.
fieldProperties.tabs.general: Tab title in the custom field editor, for general settings such as name, step size and labels.
fieldProperties.tabs.image: Tab title in the custom field editor, for the background image settings and the field's measurements.
fieldProperties.tabs.theme: Tab title in the custom field editor, for the field's colors.
fieldProperties.themeSubsections.grid: Subheading on the Theme tab above the colors for the background and the field lines.
fieldProperties.themeSubsections.labels: Subheading on the Theme tab above the colors for the field labels (yard numbers and outside labels).
fieldProperties.themeSubsections.marcher: Subheading on the Theme tab above the colors and shape for marchers and shapes.
fieldProperties.themeSubsections.pathway: Subheading on the Theme tab above the colors for the paths marchers take between pages.
fieldProperties.tooltips.conformMethod: Tooltip for the Fit/Fill setting for the background image. Fit shows the whole image inside the field; Fill covers the field. The image's proportions are never distorted.
fieldProperties.tooltips.directorsLeft: Tooltip with example names for the left side of the field. Examples are common names a school or ensemble might use. Translate the examples naturally.
fieldProperties.tooltips.directorsRight: Tooltip with example names for the right side of the field. Examples are common names a school or ensemble might use. Translate the examples naturally.
fieldProperties.tooltips.fieldName: Tooltip for the Field Name text field: the name or title of this field template.
fieldProperties.tooltips.halfLineXInterv: Tooltip for the X half line interval. Half lines are extra lines drawn between the main lines. The interval is measured in steps from the center of the field. Empty means none. Cosmetic only; coordinates do not change.
fieldProperties.tooltips.halfLineYInterv: Tooltip for the Y half line interval. Half lines are extra lines drawn between the main lines. The interval is measured in steps from the front of the field. Empty means none. Cosmetic only; coordinates do not change.
fieldProperties.tooltips.leftAbbreviatio: Tooltip with example short names for the left side. Examples: S1 (Side 1), AL (Audience Left), SR (Stage Right). Translate the short forms to fit the translated full names.
fieldProperties.tooltips.measurementSyst: Tooltip for the measurement system dropdown (imperial or metric), used to define the step size. The user can switch back and forth.
fieldProperties.tooltips.resetTheme: Tooltip for the Reset Theme button: restore all field colors to their defaults.
fieldProperties.tooltips.resetToDefault: Tooltip for the small button next to the marcher shape dropdown that resets the shape to the default (circle).
fieldProperties.tooltips.rightAbbreviati: Tooltip with example short names for the right side. Examples: S2 (Side 2), AR (Audience Right), SL (Stage Left). Translate the short forms to fit the translated full names.
fieldProperties.tooltips.stepSize: Tooltip for the Step Size field: how long one step is, in inches or centimeters depending on the chosen measurement system.
fieldProperties.tooltips.stepSizeWarning: Tooltip for the step size warning threshold. When a marcher's step between two positions is longer than this length, its path is drawn in a warning color. 0 turns the warning off.
fieldProperties.tooltips.stepsFromFrontT: Tooltip for a number field. The "away" numbers are the yard-line numbers on the back half of the field. The field measures steps from the front sideline to the outside of those numbers (closer to the back sideline).

Tooltip for a number field. The "away" numbers are the yard-line numbers on the back half of the field. The field measures steps from the front sideline to the inside of those numbers (closer to the center of the field).

Tooltip for a number field. The "home" numbers are the yard-line numbers on the front half of the field. The field measures steps from the front sideline to the outside of those numbers (closer to the front sideline).

Tooltip for a number field. The "home" numbers are the yard-line numbers on the front half of the field. The field measures steps from the front sideline to the inside of those numbers (closer to the center of the field).
fieldProperties.tooltips.useHashes: Tooltip for the Use Hashes switch: draw Y-checkpoints as hash marks, like on a football field. When off, full lines are drawn.
fieldProperties.units.centimeters: Unit abbreviation for centimeters, written after a length number field when the show uses metric measurements: for example after the step size boxes in the field settings' General tab, and after the step size warning threshold in the new-show wizard. Use your language's usual short form.
fieldProperties.units.inches: Unit abbreviation for inches, written after a length number field when the show uses imperial measurements: for example after the step size boxes in the field settings' General tab, and after the step size warning threshold in the new-show wizard. Use your language's usual short form.
fieldProperties.warnings.xCheckpointsNot: Warning on the Checkpoints tab, shown when the leftmost and rightmost X-checkpoints (reference lines positioned side to side from the center) are not the same distance from the center. May cause drawing glitches. Starts with the word WARNING.
fieldProperties.warnings.yCheckpointsNeg: Warning on the Checkpoints tab. Y-checkpoints (reference lines positioned in steps from the front of the field) should all be negative numbers, i.e. behind the front of the field; otherwise graphics and coordinates may be wrong. Starts with the word WARNING.
fieldProperties.buttons.importImage: Button in the Field panel's Image tab that opens a file picker to choose an image shown under the field (for example a photo or drawing of the real field).
fieldProperties.tooltips.importImage: Tooltip for the Import Image button: the chosen image is drawn on the field behind the marchers.
fieldProperties.messages.refreshAfterImp: Note under the Import Image button in the Field panel's Image tab: after importing an image, the window may need a reload to show it. [Ctrl + R] is the reload shortcut; keep it as written.
fileAccessDialogError.closeButton: Button that closes the error dialog shown when a show file can't be opened. Verb.
fileAccessDialogError.default.descriptio: Body of the error dialog shown when a show file couldn't be opened for an unspecified reason.
fileAccessDialogError.default.title: Title of the error dialog shown when a show file couldn't be opened for an unspecified reason. A generic error title.
fileAccessDialogError.forbidden.descript: Body of the error dialog shown when the operating system refuses access to the chosen show file.
fileAccessDialogError.forbidden.title: Title of the error dialog shown when the operating system refuses access to the chosen show file.
fileAccessDialogError.guideLinkText: Text of a link to OpenMarch's online help article about file errors. It fills the <link></link> slot of 'Refer to the … for more information.', so it must work inside that sentence.
fileAccessDialogError.notFound.descripti: Body of the error dialog shown when the chosen show file isn't at the path OpenMarch looked in. The question hints that the file may have been moved or renamed.
fileAccessDialogError.notFound.title: Title of the error dialog shown when the chosen show file isn't at the path OpenMarch looked in.
fileAccessDialogError.referToGuide: Sentence at the end of the file error dialog pointing to a help article. <link></link> is a placeholder replaced by a clickable link whose text is 'OpenMarch File Error Guide'. Keep the tags in place.
fileAccessDialogError.renderFail.descrip: Fallback body of an error dialog, shown only if a different alert dialog could not be displayed. A developer-facing message.
fileAccessDialogError.renderFail.title: Fallback title of an error dialog, shown only if a different alert dialog could not be displayed. A developer-facing message.
fileAccessDialogError.server.description: Body of the error dialog shown when opening a show file failed because of an internal problem on OpenMarch's side (a server error code 500).
fileAccessDialogError.server.title: Title of the error dialog shown when opening a show file failed with an internal error (server error code 500).
fileAccessDialogError.tooNew.description: Body of the error dialog shown when the chosen show file was saved by a newer OpenMarch than the installed one. The file is left untouched. The user should update the app.
fileAccessDialogError.tooNew.title: Title of the error dialog shown when the chosen show file was saved by a newer OpenMarch than the installed one. Imperative.
fileDialog.filters.allFiles: File-type filter in the system's open dialogs that shows every file. Use the wording the operating system uses in this language.
fileDialog.filters.audioFile: File-type filter in the system's open dialog for choosing the show's music (mp3, wav, ogg and similar).
fileDialog.filters.openMarchFile: File-type filter in the system's open and save dialogs for OpenMarch show files (.dots). OpenMarch is the app's name; keep it as is.
fileDialog.filters.video: File-type filter in the system's save dialog when exporting the show as a video file.
fileDialog.newShow.button: Button in the system's save dialog that opens when starting a new show from a file: it creates the new show file at the chosen place.
fileDialog.openFailed.title: Title of an error dialog shown when a show file couldn't be opened. The show file is a database; the dialog's text is a technical error message from the app.
fileDialog.saveCopy.button: Button in the system's save dialog for Save As Copy: it saves a copy of the open show at the chosen place.
fileTab.exitFile: Button in the File tab of the toolbar. Closes the open show and returns to the start page. 'File' means a show file. Verb phrase.
fileTab.newFile: Button in the File tab of the toolbar. Starts creating a new show. 'File' means a show file. Verb phrase.
fileTab.openFile: Button in the File tab of the toolbar. Opens a file chooser to open another show file. Verb phrase.
fileTab.saveCopyDialogDescription: Body of the dialog opened by the 'Save Copy' button. OpenMarch saves changes to the open show automatically, so this command is only needed to make a separate, full copy of the show file.
fileTab.saveFile: Button in the File tab of the toolbar, and title and confirm button of the dialog it opens. Saves a copy of the open show as a new file. Verb phrase: 'Save' + noun 'Copy', not an unfinished save.
fileTab.saveFileCancel: Button in the 'Save Copy' dialog that closes it without making a copy. Verb.
fileTab.saveSpinnerText: Text next to a spinner in the 'Save Copy' dialog while the copy of the show file is being written. Present participle with an ellipsis.
fileTab.toasts.audioUploadFailed: Error toast shown when adding an audio file (the show's music) to the open show fails and no more specific reason is known.
fileTab.toasts.audioUploaded: Success toast shown after the user adds an audio file (the show's music) to the open show.
fileTab.toasts.error: Error toast shown when making a copy of the show file failed.
fileTab.toasts.errorWithDetails: Error toast shown when saving a copy of the open show file fails, followed by the technical reason. {error} is the error message from the system, usually in English.
fileTab.toasts.noFileOpen: Error toast shown when the user tries to add an audio file while no show file is open. A show is an OpenMarch drill file.
fileTab.toasts.success: Success toast shown after a copy of the show file was saved.
formButtons.discardChanges: Button of an edit form. Throws away the changes made in the form. Verb phrase.
formButtons.editButton: Default label of the button that switches a form (for example marcher or page details) from viewing into editing mode.
formButtons.saveChanges: Button that saves the edits made in a form.
formField.valueMissing: Validation message under a required form field that was left empty. Imperative.
infoTip.moreInfo: Default screen-reader label of a small round info button that opens a tooltip with extra explanation. Not shown visually.
inspector.marcher.addToTagCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector's tag row. Shown only on touch screens. The button adds the selected marchers to an existing tag (a named group of marchers). Keep it very short; it sits under a small icon.
inspector.marcher.alignHeading: Heading above the align and flip buttons in the marcher inspector, shown when several marchers are selected. The buttons line the selected marchers up in a row or column.
inspector.marcher.alignHorizontallyCapti: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector's align row, shown only on touch screens. The button lines the selected marchers up along a horizontal line (same vertical position on the field). One word; the sibling caption 'Vertical' is its counterpart.
inspector.marcher.alignVerticallyCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector's align row, shown only on touch screens. The button lines the selected marchers up along a vertical line (same horizontal position on the field). One word; the sibling caption 'Horizontal' is its counterpart.
inspector.marcher.coords.behind: One field of the selected marcher's front-to-back position in the marcher inspector, read together with a number of steps before it and a hash or sideline after it: the marcher is that many steps behind it (away from the audience).
inspector.marcher.coords.inFrontOf: One field of the selected marcher's front-to-back position in the marcher inspector, read together with a number of steps before it and a hash or sideline after it: the marcher is that many steps in front of it (toward the audience).
inspector.marcher.coords.inside: One field of the selected marcher's side-to-side position in the marcher inspector, read together with a number of steps before it and a yard line after it: the marcher is that many steps inside the yard line (toward the center of the field).
inspector.marcher.coords.on: One field of the selected marcher's position in the marcher inspector: the marcher stands exactly on the yard line, hash or sideline shown next to it.
inspector.marcher.coords.outside: One field of the selected marcher's side-to-side position in the marcher inspector, read together with a number of steps before it and a yard line after it: the marcher is that many steps outside the yard line (away from the center of the field).
inspector.marcher.coords.x: Label above the side-to-side position of the selected marcher in the marcher inspector (steps, inside/outside, the nearest yard line or other checkpoint, and the side of the field). The letter of the X axis.
inspector.marcher.coords.xCheckpoint: Fallback name of a side-to-side reference line (a checkpoint, such as a yard line) in the marcher inspector, used when the line has no name. {id} is its number.
inspector.marcher.coords.y: Label above the front-to-back position of the selected marcher in the marcher inspector (steps, in front of/behind, and the nearest hash or sideline). The letter of the Y axis.
inspector.marcher.coords.yCheckpoint: Fallback name of a front-to-back reference line (a checkpoint, such as a hash or sideline) in the marcher inspector, used when the line has no name. {id} is its number.
inspector.marcher.distributeHeading: Heading above the distribute buttons in the marcher inspector, shown when several marchers are selected. The buttons spread the selected marchers out evenly, side to side or front to back.
inspector.marcher.distributeStepsPlaceho: Placeholder in the small number box next to a Distribute button in the marcher inspector: how many steps apart to space the marchers. Left empty, they are spread evenly between the outermost two. A step is the unit of distance on the field.
inspector.marcher.drillNumber: Label for a read-only field in the marcher inspector showing the selected marcher's drill number: the short unique ID that identifies one marcher in the show, such as 'OT1' (section code plus number).
inspector.marcher.errorLoadingCoords: Red error text in the marcher inspector, shown instead of the coordinate fields when the selected marcher's position on the field could not be loaded.
inspector.marcher.flipHorizontalCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector, shown only on touch screens. The button mirrors the selected marchers' positions left-to-right (flips them across the field's vertical axis). The arrow shows the direction of the flip. Keep it very short.
inspector.marcher.flipVerticalCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector, shown only on touch screens. The button mirrors the selected marchers' positions top-to-bottom (flips them across the field's horizontal axis). The arrow shows the direction of the flip. Keep it very short.
inspector.marcher.itemsSelected: Note at the top of the marcher inspector when props (objects on the field that aren't people, such as a podium or a ramp) are selected along with, or instead of, marchers. {count} is the number of props selected, for example 3. Plural form. It tells the user props are edited in a different panel, the Props panel.
inspector.marcher.maxStepSize: Label in the marcher inspector when several marchers are selected, above the marcher with the largest step size on the current page. Step size is the distance a marcher covers in one count, written as a ratio such as '8 to 5' (8 steps per 5 yards).
inspector.marcher.minStepSize: Label in the marcher inspector when several marchers are selected, above the marcher with the smallest step size on the current page. Step size is the distance a marcher covers in one count, written as a ratio such as '8 to 5' (8 steps per 5 yards).
inspector.marcher.move.back: Caption under the up arrow of an on-screen nudge pad in the marcher inspector (touch screens only). The arrow moves the selected marchers toward the back sideline of the field, away from the audience. Sits under a small icon; keep it short.
inspector.marcher.move.fourSteps: Option in a small three-way toggle (1/4 step, 1 step, 4 steps) that sets how far each press of the on-screen nudge arrows moves the selected marchers. A step is one marching step, about 22.5 inches on a standard 8-to-5 field. Keep it short; it sits on a small toggle button.
inspector.marcher.move.front: Caption under the down arrow of an on-screen nudge pad in the marcher inspector (touch screens only). The arrow moves the selected marchers toward the front sideline of the field, the one nearest the audience. Keep it short.
inspector.marcher.move.oneStep: Option in a small three-way toggle (1/4 step, 1 step, 4 steps) that sets how far each press of the on-screen nudge arrows moves the selected marchers. A step is one marching step. Keep it short; it sits on a small toggle button.
inspector.marcher.move.quarterStep: Option in a small three-way toggle (1/4 step, 1 step, 4 steps) that sets how far each press of the on-screen nudge arrows moves the selected marchers. Means one quarter of a marching step. Keep it short; it sits on a small toggle button.
inspector.marcher.move.side1: Fallback name for the left end of the field (as the audience sees it), used as the left arrow's caption on the on-screen nudge pad when the field has no named sides (otherwise the field's own side name, such as 'Side 1' of a football field, is used). Short.
inspector.marcher.move.side2: Fallback name for the right end of the field (as the audience sees it), used as the right arrow's caption on the on-screen nudge pad when the field has no named sides (otherwise the field's own side name is used). Short.
inspector.marcher.move.stepSize: Accessible label (read by screen readers, not shown) for the three-way toggle that picks how far each press of the on-screen nudge arrows moves the marchers: 1/4 step, 1 step or 4 steps.
inspector.marcher.move.title: Small heading above the on-screen nudge pad (arrow buttons, touch screens only) in the marcher inspector. 'Move' is a verb here: it nudges the selected marchers a set distance. Not the same as a 'move' on the timeline, which is a marcher's path between two pages.
inspector.marcher.move.towardBack: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the up arrow on the on-screen nudge pad. Pressing it moves the selected marchers one nudge toward the back sideline of the field (away from the audience).
inspector.marcher.move.towardFront: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the down arrow on the on-screen nudge pad. Pressing it moves the selected marchers one nudge toward the front sideline of the field (nearest the audience).
inspector.marcher.move.towardSide: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the left and right arrows on the on-screen nudge pad, for a field whose ends have names. {side} is that name as the user or the field template wrote it, for example 'Side 1', 'Side 2' or a school name such as 'Home'; it is not translated. Pressing the arrow moves the selected marchers one nudge that way.
inspector.marcher.move.towardSide1: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the left arrow on the on-screen nudge pad when the field has no named sides. Side 1 is the left end of the field as the audience sees it; use the same words as inspector.marcher.move.side1. Pressing the arrow moves the selected marchers one nudge that way.
inspector.marcher.move.towardSide2: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the right arrow on the on-screen nudge pad when the field has no named sides. Side 2 is the right end of the field as the audience sees it; use the same words as inspector.marcher.move.side2. Pressing the arrow moves the selected marchers one nudge that way.
inspector.marcher.name: Label for a read-only field in the marcher inspector showing the selected marcher's name (the performer's own name, if one was entered; a dash is shown when empty).
inspector.marcher.newTagCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector's tag row, shown only on touch screens. The button creates a new tag (a named group of marchers) from the selected marchers. Keep it very short.
inspector.marcher.noPageSelected: Plain message in the marcher inspector when no page is selected, so there are no positions to show. A page is one section of the show between two page flags on the timeline.
inspector.marcher.playing: Note in the marcher inspector while the show is playing. The marcher details are hidden during playback; pausing brings them back. 'Pause' is a verb (stop playback).
inspector.marcher.removeFromTagCaption: Small caption under an icon-only button in the marcher inspector's tag row, shown only on touch screens. The button removes the selected marchers from a tag (a named group of marchers). Verb. Keep it very short.
inspector.marcher.rotation: Screen-reader label of the rotation box in the inspector's Transform section: type or drag a number of degrees to turn the selected marchers around the center of the selection.
inspector.marcher.section: Label for a read-only field in the marcher inspector showing the selected marcher's section: the instrument group they belong to, such as Trumpet, Color Guard or Drumline.
inspector.marcher.stepSize: Label in the marcher inspector for the selected marcher's step size on the current page: how far they travel per count to reach this page, written as a ratio such as '8 to 5' (8 steps per 5 yards). Noun.
inspector.marcher.stepSizeWarning: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a small red warning icon next to a marcher's step size in the marcher inspector. It appears when the step is too big to march comfortably (larger than the field's warning threshold).
inspector.marcher.swapMarchers: Button in the marcher inspector, shown only when exactly two marchers are selected. Swaps their positions with each other. Verb phrase. Appears as a full-width button.
inspector.marcher.timeline.goToHeldPage: Tooltip on a link in the marcher inspector that jumps the playhead to the page where the selected marchers' Held hold starts (they are held on purpose from that page up to this one, by a Held hold or by a shape placed on that page). {page} is the page name, for example '4' or '2A'. A page is one section of the show between two page flags.
inspector.marcher.timeline.goToPage: Tooltip on a link in the marcher inspector that jumps the playhead to the page where the selected marchers last moved. {page} is the page name, for example '4' or '2A'. A page is one section of the show between two page flags.
inspector.marcher.timeline.goToStart: Tooltip on a link in the marcher inspector that jumps the playhead to the very start of the show (the selected marchers have not moved since the beginning).
inspector.marcher.timeline.heldFromStart: Link in the marcher inspector: the selected marchers are held on purpose at their starting spots, from the very beginning of the show up to this page (the hold starts at the beginning), by a Held hold or by a shape (a formation such as a box or an arc) they start in. {held} is the hold state word (English 'Held', from timeline.terms.held). Clicking jumps to the start. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.timeline.heldSince: Link in the marcher inspector: the selected marchers are held on purpose from an earlier page (or this one) up to this page, by a Held hold or by a shape (a formation such as a box or an arc) placed on that page and carried on since. {held} is the hold state word (English 'Held', from timeline.terms.held). {page} is the page where that hold starts or the shape was placed, which may be later than where they last moved, for example '4' or '2A'. Clicking jumps to that page. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.timeline.holdFrom: Link in the marcher inspector saying where the selected marchers last moved: they have no move of their own after that page. {page} is the page name, for example '4' or '2A'. Clicking jumps to that page. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.timeline.holdFromStart: Link in the marcher inspector saying the selected marchers haven't moved since the very beginning of the show. Clicking jumps to the start. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.timeline.movesOnThisPa: Short statement in the marcher inspector: the selected marchers have their own movement on this page (they travel to a new position here) rather than standing still.
inspector.marcher.timeline.notDefinedFro: Link in the marcher inspector: nothing decides where the selected marchers are on this page, so they show their starting spots for now. {notDefined} is the state word (English 'Not defined', from timeline.terms.notDefined). Clicking jumps to the start. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.timeline.notDefinedSho: Link in the marcher inspector: nothing decides where the selected marchers are on this page, so they show the position from an earlier page for now. {notDefined} is the state word (English 'Not defined', from timeline.terms.notDefined). {page} is that earlier page, for example '4' or '2A'. Clicking jumps to that page. An arrow icon follows the text.
inspector.marcher.title: Title of the marcher inspector panel when several marchers are selected. {count} is the number selected, for example 12. Shown as a heading, so keep it short.
inspector.marcher.titleSingle: Title of the marcher inspector panel when one marcher is selected. {drillNumber} is that marcher's drill number, a short unique ID such as 'OT1'.
inspector.page.counts: Label in the page inspector for the number of counts (beats) in the selected page: how long the page lasts. The value shown beside it is a number such as 8 or 16. Noun.
inspector.page.measures: Label in the page inspector for the range of music measures the selected page covers. The value shown beside it is a range such as '1–2' or '3'.
inspector.page.notes: Heading and screen-reader label of the notes section in the page inspector, where the user writes free-form text notes about the selected page. Noun.
inspector.page.paused: Small help text in the page inspector, shown while the show is playing and the controls are disabled. 'Pause' is a verb. The page can be split into two pages, or marked as a subset, only when playback is paused.
inspector.page.split.error: Error toast shown when splitting a page fails. Splitting a page divides one page of the show (a stretch of counts between two page flags on the timeline) into two pages at a chosen count.
inspector.page.splitPage: Button in the page inspector. Splits the selected page into two pages at its middle count; the second half becomes a new subset page. Verb phrase. A page is one section of the show between two page flags on the timeline.
inspector.page.subset: Label of an on/off switch in the page inspector. A subset page is a page that splits a longer page into parts, named with a letter such as '3A' instead of getting its own number (so later pages are not renumbered). Noun; the switch is on when the page is a subset.
inspector.page.title: Title of the page inspector panel. {pageNumber} is the page's name, usually a number such as 4, but it may include a letter for subset pages, such as '4A'.
inspector.shape.alignmentTab: Tab label in the field toolbar for the group of alignment tools (align, distribute, flip the selected marchers). Tab names are one word and sit side by side with 'File', 'Shapes' and 'Select'.
inspector.shape.fileTab: Tab label in the field toolbar for the group of file tools: open, new and save file, undo and redo, close file and settings. Tab names are one word and sit side by side with 'Alignment', 'Shapes' and 'Select'.
inspector.shape.selectTab: Tab label in the field toolbar for the group of selection tools (select marchers by section, tag or drill prefix, or select all). Tab names are one word and sit side by side with 'File', 'Alignment' and 'Shapes'. 'Select' is a verb used as a tab name.
inspector.shape.shapesTab: Tab label in the field toolbar for the group of shape tools, used to arrange marchers into a shape (line, arc, circle and so on) on the field. Tab names are one word and sit side by side with 'File', 'Alignment' and 'Select'.
inspector.timeline.move.splitHelp: Help text in the move card shown when the 'Split at playhead' button is disabled because the playhead is outside the move. The playhead is the vertical line on the timeline showing the current count.
inspector.title: Title of the inspector, the side panel showing details of the current selection (marchers, page or move). Also appears written vertically on the panel's edge tab in touch mode. Noun.
languages.help.addYours: Line under the language picker in Settings and in the first-run setup, shown while the app is in English. Invites people whose language isn't in the list to help translate OpenMarch. <link> is a link that opens the OpenMarch website page explaining how to become a volunteer translator.
languages.help.madeWithAi: Line under the language picker in Settings and in the first-run setup, shown while the app is in any language other than English. Warns that this language's text was translated by AI and may contain mistakes, and asks native speakers to help review it. <link> is a link that opens the OpenMarch website page explaining how to become a volunteer translator. Translate 'this translation' as the translation of the app into the current language.
launchpage.files.clearAllRecentFiles: Small button above the Recent Files list on the start page. Removes every entry from the list of recently opened shows (the show files themselves are not deleted). Verb phrase; a tooltip explains it.
launchpage.files.clearAllRecentFilesTool: Tooltip of the 'Clear all' button above the Recent Files list on the start page. Removing an entry only forgets it in OpenMarch; the show file stays on the computer's disk.
launchpage.files.clearMissingRecentFiles: Small button above the Recent Files list on the start page. Removes only the entries whose show files can no longer be found (moved or deleted). Verb phrase; a tooltip explains it.

Tooltip of the 'Clear missing' button above the Recent Files list on the start page. Removes list entries whose show file was moved or deleted; files that still exist are untouched, and nothing is deleted from the disk.
launchpage.files.createNew: Button on the start page's left panel that begins creating a new show (opens the New show setup dialog). Verb phrase. In this app 'File' means an OpenMarch show file (.dots).
launchpage.files.failedToClearAllRecentF: Error toast on the start page when clearing the whole Recent Files list failed.
launchpage.files.failedToClearMissingRec: Error toast on the start page when removing the missing (moved or deleted) shows from the Recent Files list failed.
launchpage.files.failedToLoadRecent: Error toast on the start page when the list of recently opened shows could not be read.
launchpage.files.failedToOpen: Error toast on the start page when opening a show file (from the Recent Files list or an example show) failed.
launchpage.files.failedToRemoveRecent: Error toast on the start page when removing one show from the Recent Files list failed.
launchpage.files.fieldPreview: Alternative text (read by screen readers, not shown) for the small drawing of a show's field on a Recent Files card, and for the field preview in the New show setup. Noun phrase.
launchpage.files.loading: Screen-reader label of the spinning icon on the start page while the list of recently opened show files is loading.
launchpage.files.movedOrMissing: Red warning on a Recent Files card on the start page: the show's file is no longer at the place where OpenMarch last saw it (moved, renamed or deleted), so it can't be opened from here.
launchpage.files.openFile: Button on the start page's left panel that opens a file chooser to open an existing OpenMarch show file (.dots). Verb phrase.
launchpage.files.removeFile: Tooltip of the small button on a Recent Files card on the start page. Removes that show from the recent list only; the file stays on disk.
launchpage.files.title: Heading of the start page's list of recently opened shows, and the name of its tab in the left panel (the web version replaces the tab name with 'Your shows'). Noun phrase.
launchpage.learn.guides.customizeField.d: Description on the "Customize the Field" card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab: set the field's size and markings, and change its colors and look.
launchpage.learn.guides.customizeField.t: Title of a card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab. Opens the website's guide on setting up the field (the performance area drawn in the editor).
launchpage.learn.guides.gettingStarted.d: Description on the "Getting Started" card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab. A show is a drill design file.
launchpage.learn.guides.gettingStarted.t: Title of a card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab. Opens the website's beginner guide.
launchpage.learn.guides.music.descriptio: Description on the "Music" card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab. "Tap tempo" means tapping a key along with the music to mark its beats.
launchpage.learn.guides.music.title: Title of a card in the Guides section of the start page's Learn tab. Opens the website's guide on adding a show's music.
launchpage.learn.guides.title: Heading of the section on the start page's Learn tab that lists written guides (help articles) about using OpenMarch. Noun.
