launchpage.learn.title: Name of the Learn tab in the start page's left panel and heading of its content: tutorial videos, guides and troubleshooting tips for new users. A noun here, not the verb.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.cacheFo: List item in the Troubleshooting Tips on the start page's Learn tab, under "Clear the cache": where the cache folder is on one operating system. {system} is the system's name (Windows, macOS or Linux). <folder></folder> is replaced by the folder's path shown as code; keep the tag. Only adjust the punctuation if your language needs it.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.clearCa: Heading of a troubleshooting tip on the start page's Learn tab. Suggests deleting OpenMarch's cache and metadata folders to fix problems; a list of folder paths per operating system follows. Imperative.

Paragraph of a troubleshooting tip on the start page's Learn tab, under 'Clear the cache'. A warning that deleting the cache folders also resets the recent files list and the chosen theme. Followed by a list of folder paths.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.descrip: Intro sentence of the troubleshooting section on the start page's Learn tab. OpenMarch is still being built, so problems can happen and these tips may help.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.refresh: Heading of a troubleshooting tip on the start page's Learn tab. Suggests reloading the app window; the following paragraph gives the keyboard shortcut. Imperative.

Paragraph in the Troubleshooting Tips on the start page's Learn tab, under "Refresh the page". <keys></keys> is replaced by the reload keyboard shortcut drawn as keycaps (Ctrl + R, or ⌘ + R on a Mac); keep the tag. OpenMarch is the product name.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.title: Heading of the troubleshooting section on the start page's Learn tab, above a few tips for when something goes wrong. Noun phrase.
launchpage.learn.videoGuides.description: Sentence under the 'Video Guides' heading on the start page's Learn tab, above a list of tutorial videos.
launchpage.learn.videoGuides.title: Heading of the section on the start page's Learn tab that lists tutorial videos. Noun phrase.
launchpage.merch: Promotional link at the bottom of the start page's left panel. Opens the OpenMarch merchandise store (T-shirts and similar) in the browser. 'Merch' is short for merchandise. Fits one or two lines in a 350 px panel.
launchpage.newShow.back: Button in the New show setup dialog. Goes to the previous step. Verb.
launchpage.newShow.browse: Button in the New show setup dialog next to the save-location field. Opens a folder chooser so the user can pick where the show file is saved. Verb.
launchpage.newShow.client: Label of an optional text field in the New show setup, for the name of the organization the show is designed for (for example a school or band). Noun.
launchpage.newShow.create: Final button of the New show setup dialog. Creates the show with the choices made and opens it. Verb phrase.
launchpage.newShow.designer: Label of an optional text field in the New show setup for the name of the person who designs the show's drill. Noun.
launchpage.newShow.errors.audioNotSaved: Warning toast shown after a new show was created: the chosen music file may not have been stored in the show. The user can add music later from the editor.
launchpage.newShow.errors.createFailed: Error toast when creating a new show failed.
launchpage.newShow.errors.databaseNotRea: Error message shown in a notification when the new-show wizard is finished before its show file was created. "The project step" is the wizard's step where the show is named and its save location chosen.
launchpage.newShow.errors.filePathRequir: Error message shown in a notification when the new-show wizard is finished without a place to save the show file.
launchpage.newShow.errors.importFailed: Error toast when the user chose to start a new show from a previous show file (.dots) and reading that file failed. '.dots' is OpenMarch's file extension; do not translate it.
launchpage.newShow.errors.saveFailed: Error message shown in a notification when the new-show wizard couldn't save the new show file. {path} is the full file path on the computer, for example C:/Users/Ana/Documents/Opener.dots.
launchpage.newShow.errors.xmlNotImported: Warning toast shown after a new show was created: the chosen MusicXML file (sheet music exported from a notation program) may not have been imported. The user can import it later from the editor.
launchpage.newShow.exitConfirm.cancel: Button in the confirmation shown when the user tries to close the New show setup with unsaved choices. Cancels the closing so the user can continue filling in the setup. Verb phrase.
launchpage.newShow.exitConfirm.confirm: Red button in the confirmation shown when the user tries to close the New show setup with unsaved choices. Closes the setup and throws away the draft. Verb.
launchpage.newShow.exitConfirm.descripti: Body of the confirmation shown when the user tries to close the New show setup partway through. The 'draft' is the show being set up, which will be deleted.
launchpage.newShow.exitConfirm.title: Title of the confirmation shown when the user tries to close the New show setup partway through. A yes/no question.
launchpage.newShow.fileExistsWarning: Warning in the New show setup under the save-location field: a file with the chosen name already exists in the chosen folder, and creating the show will overwrite it.
launchpage.newShow.next: Button in the New show setup dialog. Goes to the next step. Verb.
launchpage.newShow.showName: Label and placeholder of the required text field in the New show setup where the user types the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. Noun.
launchpage.newShow.skip: Button in the New show setup dialog's footer that leaves out an optional step (audio, performers or tempo) and goes on to the next one. Verb.
launchpage.newShow.steps.audio.dbNotRead: Error text in the Audio step of the New show setup: the new show file hasn't been created yet, so music can't be added. The user should go back to the Project details step and continue again.
launchpage.newShow.steps.audio.descripti: Subtitle of the Audio step of the New show setup. The user may choose a music file now or add one later in the editor.
launchpage.newShow.steps.audio.optionalD: Note in the Audio step of the New show setup. Music is optional; it can be added later from the editor.
launchpage.newShow.steps.audio.title: Title of the Audio step of the New show setup, where the user chooses the music file for the show. Noun.
launchpage.newShow.steps.audio.waitingDb: Loading text in the Audio step of the New show setup while the new show file is being created. Present participle with an ellipsis.
launchpage.newShow.steps.ensemble.descri: Subtitle of the Activity step of the New show setup. The user chooses what kind of group the show is for (for example marching band, drum corps or color guard).
launchpage.newShow.steps.ensemble.title: Title of the Activity step of the New show setup. 'Activity' means the type of performing group, such as marching band or drum corps. Noun.
launchpage.newShow.steps.ensemble.typeLa: Label of the dropdown in the Activity step of the New show setup, listing types of performing group (marching band, drum corps, color guard and so on). Noun.
launchpage.newShow.steps.field.descripti: Subtitle of the Field setup step of the New show setup. A field template is a ready-made field layout (for example a football field with yard lines) that the show starts from.
launchpage.newShow.steps.field.title: Title of the Field setup step of the New show setup, where the user picks the field the show is on. Noun phrase.
launchpage.newShow.steps.performers.desc: Subtitle of the Performers step of the New show setup. Marchers are the performers on the field; they can be added now or later in the editor.
launchpage.newShow.steps.performers.none: Empty-state text in the Performers step of the New show setup, shown when no marchers have been added yet. 'Performers' means the marchers of the show.
launchpage.newShow.steps.performers.remo: Screen-reader label of the trash-can button next to a marcher in the Performers step of the new show dialog. Removes that marcher from the list of marchers the new show will start with. {marcher} is the marcher's drill number, such as B1 or T3.
launchpage.newShow.steps.performers.sect: Heading of a collapsible group in the performers step of the new-show wizard. {section} is a section (instrument group) name, for example Trumpet; {count} is the number of performers added in that section. Only change the punctuation if your language needs it.
launchpage.newShow.steps.performers.titl: Title of the Performers step of the New show setup, where the user adds the show's marchers (the people on the field), grouped by section. Noun.
launchpage.newShow.steps.project.descrip: Subtitle of the Project details step of the New show setup: give the show a name and pick the folder where its file is stored.
launchpage.newShow.steps.project.fileTyp: Name of the file type in the computer's own Save dialog, opened from Browse in the new-show wizard; it describes .dots files. OpenMarch is the product name; keep it as is.
launchpage.newShow.steps.project.title: Title of the first form step of the New show setup, with the show's name, save location and optional designer and client. 'Project' means the show file. Noun phrase.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.blank: Option title in the first step of the New show setup: create an empty show and choose the field and marchers in the following steps. Imperative.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.blankDesc: Description under the 'Start blank show' option in the New show setup. The field and the marchers (performers) are chosen in the steps that follow.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.descripti: Subtitle of the first step of the New show setup: pick between a blank show and a show based on an earlier one.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.importPre: Option title in the first step of the New show setup: start from an existing show file. '.dots' is OpenMarch's file extension; do not translate it. Imperative.

Description under the 'Import previous .dots file' option in the New show setup. The new show reuses the marchers (performers), the field and the marchers' positions on the last set (the final formation) of an existing show.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.importSum: Summary in the New show setup after the user picked a previous show file to start from. {fileName} is the file's name, for example 'Fall Show.dots'. {count} is the number of marchers (performers) that will be copied over, for example 48. Plural form.
launchpage.newShow.steps.start.title: Title of the first step of the New show setup, where the user chooses how to start the show. Noun phrase.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.dbNotRead: Error text in the Tempo data step of the New show setup: the new show file hasn't been created yet, so tempo can't be set. The user should go back to the Project details step and continue again.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.descripti: Subtitle of the Tempo data step of the New show setup. Timing can come from a single tempo (BPM, beats per minute) or from an imported MusicXML file (sheet music exported from notation software); it can also be skipped and edited later.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.method: Label of the dropdown in the Tempo data step of the New show setup that chooses where the show's timing comes from: a single tempo, a MusicXML file or nothing yet.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.methodHel: Helper text under the 'Tempo source' dropdown in the New show setup.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.musicXml: Option in the 'Tempo source' dropdown of the New show setup: get the timing (tempo and measures) from a MusicXML file (sheet music exported from notation software). Also shown as the dropdown's current value.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.skip: Option in the 'Tempo source' dropdown of the New show setup: set no tempo now. Also shown as the dropdown's current value. Short; 'for now' means it can be edited later.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.skipDescr: Note in the Tempo data step of the New show setup, shown when 'Skip for now' is chosen. Tempo is optional and can be edited later in the editor.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.tempoOnly: Option in the 'Tempo source' dropdown of the New show setup: use a single fixed tempo (beats per minute) and a time signature, without any music file. Also shown as the dropdown's current value.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.timeSigna: Label of the dropdown in the Tempo data step of the New show setup for the time signature (meter), for example 4/4 or 3/4. Music term.
Helper text under the 'Time signature' dropdown in the New show setup. 'Starter measures' are the empty measures (bars of music) the show starts with. 'Meter' means the time signature.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.title: Title of the Tempo data step of the New show setup, where the user chooses how the show's timing is set up. Noun phrase.
launchpage.newShow.steps.tempo.waitingDb: Loading text in the Tempo data step of the New show setup while the new show file is being created. Present participle with an ellipsis.
launchpage.newShow.success: Success toast shown after a new show was created.
launchpage.newShow.tempo: Label of the number field in the Tempo data step of the New show setup for the show's starting tempo in BPM (beats per minute), for example 120. BPM stays as is.
launchpage.newShow.title: Title of the New show setup dialog, a step-by-step wizard for creating a show. Noun phrase.
launchpage.settings.title: Name of the Settings tab in the start page's left panel and heading of its content. Noun.
launchpage.social.link: Screen-reader label of an icon-only link at the bottom of the start page's sidebar that opens OpenMarch's page on another website in the browser. {service} is the website's name, not translated: Discord (a chat community), GitHub (the source code) or Patreon (donations). OpenMarch is the app's name; don't translate it.
launchpage.title: Small caption at the top of the start page's left panel, above the New File and Open File buttons. Names the screen, 'Launch Page' (the start page shown when the app opens). Noun phrase.
layout.closeSettings: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the X button that closes the full-screen Settings sheet in the web editor (small screens). Short verb phrase.
layout.hideInspector: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a thin tab on the field's right edge that hides the Inspector, the side panel for editing the selected marchers. Shown while the Inspector is open.
layout.showInspector: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a thin tab on the field's right edge that shows the Inspector, the side panel for editing the selected marchers. Shown while the Inspector is hidden.
layout.windowTooSmall.body: Explanation on the full-screen notice shown when the app window is too small to use. {minWidth} and {minHeight} are the smallest window size in pixels (for example 744 and 500); the "×" between them reads "by". The Inspector is the side panel for the selected marchers.
layout.windowTooSmall.close: Screen-reader label of the window Close button (an X icon) on the "window too small" notice, which covers the title bar. Closes the whole app window, as in any window frame.
layout.windowTooSmall.current: Line on the "window too small" notice telling the user the window's current size. {width} and {height} are pixel counts (for example 600 and 420).
layout.windowTooSmall.hintDesktop: Hint under the "window too small" notice in the desktop app. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard shortcut that zooms out (shown as keycaps, for example Ctrl and -); keep the tag as is.
layout.windowTooSmall.hintWeb: Hint under the "window too small" notice in the web editor. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard shortcut that zooms the browser out (shown as keycaps); keep the tag as is. "Turn your tablet sideways" means switch to landscape; phones are not supported yet.
layout.windowTooSmall.hintZoomed: Hint under the "window too small" notice when the app is zoomed in, which is what made the window too small. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard shortcut that zooms out (shown as keycaps); keep the tag as is.
layout.windowTooSmall.maximize: Screen-reader label of the window Maximize button (a square icon) on the "window too small" notice. Makes the app window fill the screen.
layout.windowTooSmall.minimize: Screen-reader label of the window Minimize button (a dash icon) on the "window too small" notice. Hides the app window to the taskbar or dock.
layout.windowTooSmall.title: Heading of the full-screen notice shown when the app window is too small to fit the field, timeline and Inspector. An instruction: the user should enlarge the window.
marcherPages.errors.move: Error toast shown when saving marchers' new positions on the field fails for a reason other than a timeline rule.
marcherPages.errors.removePosition: Error toast shown when removing a marcher's set position on a page fails for a reason other than a timeline rule. A set position is a spot the marcher must reach on a page.
marcherPages.errors.updateSelected: Error toast shown when changing the coordinates of the selected marchers (for example by typing in the inspector) fails for a reason other than a timeline rule.
marcherPages.moveThemToo.action: Button inside a toast that appears after the user edits a marcher group's move. Pressing it also shifts the marchers' own later moves by the same amount. The toast says which marchers kept their spots. Short. Verb phrase.
marcherPages.moveThemToo.laterMoves: Toast shown after an edit when some marchers keep their positions because each has its own later moves on several pages. {names} is a list of marcher drill numbers, such as "OT1, OT2 and OT3". Followed by a Move them too button. A move is a marcher's travel between two sets.
marcherPages.moveThemToo.moveError: Error toast shown when the "Move them too" button (on the toast after an edit, offering to move marchers that have their own move on a later page by the same amount) fails for an unexpected reason.
marcherPages.moveThemToo.namesOthers: Last item of a shortened list of marcher names in the "Move them too" toast. The app joins it after the first two drill numbers as your language joins a list, giving "OT1, OT2 and 4 others". {count} is how many marchers are not named, at least 2.
marcherPages.moveThemToo.ownMove: Toast shown after an edit when some marchers keep their positions because each has its own move on one later page. {names} is a list of drill numbers already joined as a list in your language, such as "OT1", "OT1 and OT2" or "OT1, OT2 and 4 others"; treat it as a noun phrase. {count} is how many marchers it names, for the plural. {page} is a page name, such as "4". Followed by a Move them too button. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
marchers.addMarcher: Button in the header of the Marchers side panel. Opens the form for creating new marchers. Verb; short, sits next to 'Marcher Appearance'. A marcher is one performer on the field.
marchers.addMarchers: Title of the form (in the side panel) for creating new marchers, shown when not editing an existing one. Verb phrase; the form can create many marchers at once.
marchers.addMethod.manual: Tab label in the Add Marchers form for typing the marchers' details in by hand, as opposed to the 'Import from CSV' tab. Short.
marchers.backToList: Screen-reader label of the back-arrow button at the top of the Marchers side panel while adding or editing marchers. Returns to the list of all marchers in the show.
marchers.cancelDeleteButton: Button in the confirmation dialog for deleting marchers. Closes the dialog without deleting. Verb.
marchers.createButtonWithSection: Submit button of the Add Marchers form. {quantity} is how many marchers will be created, for example 12. {section} is the chosen section's display name, for example 'Flute' or 'Other'. Plural forms: 'Create Flute Marcher' for one, 'Create 12 Flute Marchers' for several. A section is an instrument group. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
marchers.createInfo: Small note under the submit button of the Add Marchers form: newly created marchers might not appear in the lists until the app is reloaded.
marchers.csv.chooseFile: Button in the Import from CSV form that opens a file chooser to pick a CSV file (a spreadsheet saved as comma-separated text) containing the marchers to import. Verb phrase.
marchers.csv.copySections: Small button in the Import from CSV form. Copies the list of section names and drill prefixes to the clipboard, so it can be pasted into a spreadsheet. Verb; briefly shows a check icon after being pressed.
marchers.csv.downloadExample: Button in the Import from CSV form that downloads a sample CSV file showing the expected columns. CSV is a spreadsheet saved as comma-separated text. Noun phrase used as a button label.
marchers.csv.error.ambiguousPrefix: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is the drill prefix found in the row, for example 'T'. Several sections share that prefix, so the file needs a column that names the section. A drill prefix is the letters at the start of a drill number (the 'F' in 'F12').
marchers.csv.error.duplicateInFile: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is a drill number, for example 'F12', that is listed in more than one row of the same file. Drill numbers must be unique.
marchers.csv.error.duplicateInShow: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is a drill number, for example 'F12', that belongs to a marcher already in the show.
marchers.csv.error.invalidDrillNumber: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is the text found in the drill number column. A valid drill number is a letter prefix followed by a number, such as F12. Straight quotes surround the value.
marchers.csv.error.missingDrillNumber: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file: the drill number cell is empty. A drill number is the marcher's unique ID, such as F12.
marchers.csv.error.missingSection: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file: the section cell is empty. A section is an instrument group, such as Flute.
marchers.csv.error.unknownPrefix: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is the drill prefix found in the row, for example 'Q'. No section in the show uses that prefix, so the file needs a column that names the section. A drill prefix is the letters at the start of a drill number (the 'F' in 'F12').
marchers.csv.error.unknownSection: Error for one row of an imported marcher CSV file. {value} is the section name found in the row, for example 'Kazoo'. It doesn't match any section in the show. Straight quotes surround the value.
marchers.csv.fileInput: Screen-reader label of the hidden file picker behind the "Choose CSV file" button when importing marchers from a CSV (spreadsheet text) file.
marchers.csv.ignoredColumns: Note in the Import from CSV form listing columns of the chosen file that OpenMarch doesn't use. {columns} is a comma-separated list of the column headings from the file, for example 'Age, Height'.
marchers.csv.importButton: Submit button of the Import from CSV form. {count} is the number of valid marchers found in the file, for example 24. Plural forms: with none, just 'Import' (disabled); with one, 'Import 1 marcher'; otherwise 'Import 24 marchers'. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
marchers.csv.info: Note under the Import button when importing marchers from a CSV (spreadsheet text) file. Keep <keys></keys>: it is replaced by the keyboard shortcut for Undo, shown as keycaps (for example Ctrl + Z).
marchers.csv.infoNoShortcut: Note under the Import button when importing marchers from a CSV (spreadsheet text) file, used instead of marchers.csv.info when the person has removed the keyboard shortcut for Undo. Says the import can be undone, without naming a shortcut.
marchers.csv.line: Start of an error line in the Import from CSV form, followed by a colon and the error text. {line} is the row number in the file, for example 5. Example: 'Line 5: Missing drill number'.
marchers.csv.missingColumns: Error in the Import from CSV form when the chosen file lacks the required column. {columns} is the column heading the file must have: either 'section' or 'drill_number' (literal heading text used in the CSV file, so leave it untranslated).
marchers.csv.mode.drillNumber.help: Help text under the 'By drill number' option in the Import from CSV form. Each CSV row names a marcher by drill number (a letter prefix and a number, such as F12). The marcher's section is worked out from the prefix, or from an optional section column.
marchers.csv.mode.drillNumber.title: Option in the Import from CSV form: the file lists marchers by their drill numbers, such as F12. A drill number is the marcher's unique ID.
marchers.csv.mode.section.help: Help text under the 'By section' option in the Import from CSV form. Each CSV row gives a section (an instrument group); OpenMarch makes up the drill numbers itself (F1, F2, … for Flute) and skips numbers already used in the show.
marchers.csv.mode.section.title: Option in the Import from CSV form: the file lists marchers by their section (instrument group); drill numbers are generated automatically.
marchers.csv.readError: Error in the Import from CSV form when the chosen file couldn't be read.
marchers.csv.result.empty: Error in the Import from CSV form when the chosen file has no marcher rows.
marchers.csv.result.failed: Error in the Import from CSV form when every row of the chosen file has a problem. A list of the problems follows below this sentence, with a colon at the end.
marchers.csv.result.partial: Warning in the Import from CSV form when only some rows are usable. {valid} is the number of good rows and {invalid} the number of rows with problems, for example 20 and 3. Plural forms in both halves. A list of the problems follows after the colon. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
marchers.csv.result.success: Success message in the Import from CSV form when every row of the chosen file is valid. {valid} is the number of marchers found, for example 24. Plural form. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
marchers.csv.sections: Heading of a collapsible section in the Import from CSV form. It opens a table of the show's sections (instrument groups) and the drill prefix each uses, which the user can refer to when filling in the CSV file.
marchers.csv.sectionsHelp: Help text in the collapsible 'Sections and drill prefixes' part of the Import from CSV form. A drill prefix is the letters starting a drill number: 'F' for Flute, so 'F12' is Flute marcher 12.
marchers.csv.title: Tab label and form title for importing marchers from a CSV file (a spreadsheet saved as comma-separated text). Shown next to a CSV file icon.
marchers.deleteButton: Red confirm button in the dialog for deleting marchers. Verb. Deletes the marchers listed in the dialog.
marchers.deleteTitle: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting marchers. A generic warning heading.
marchers.deleteWarningNoShortcut: Body of the confirmation dialog shown before saving the marcher list with marchers removed from it, used instead of marchers.deleteWarning when the person has removed the keyboard shortcut for Undo. {marchers} is the list of the removed marchers' drill numbers (such as B1, T3, F2), already joined as a list in the app's language.
marchers.deleteWarningWithShortcut: Body of the confirmation dialog shown before saving the marcher list with marchers removed from it. {marchers} is the list of the removed marchers' drill numbers (such as B1, T3, F2), already joined as a list in the app's language. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Undo shortcut drawn as keycaps (for example Ctrl + Z, or ⌘ Z on a Mac); keep the tag.
marchers.drillOrder: Label of the number field in the Add/Edit Marcher form for the marcher's drill number's numeric part, for example 12 in 'F12'. Together with the drill prefix it forms the marcher's unique ID.
marchers.drillOrderError.exists: Error under the drill number field in the Add/Edit Marcher form: another marcher already uses that prefix and number combination.
marchers.drillPrefix: Label of the text field in the Add/Edit Marcher form for the drill prefix: the letters at the start of the marcher's drill number, such as the 'F' in 'F12'. Also a column heading in the section/prefix table of the CSV import.
marchers.editMarcher: Title of the form (in the side panel) for changing an existing marcher. Verb phrase.
marchers.errors.create: Error toast shown when adding new marchers to the show fails for a reason other than a timeline rule.
marchers.errors.delete: Error toast shown when deleting marchers from the show fails for a reason other than a timeline rule.
marchers.errors.update: Error toast shown when saving changes to one or more marchers (name, section, drill number and so on) fails.
marchers.list.addSectionStyle: Button in the Section styles list of the Marcher Appearance panel. Adds a style (colors and dot shape) for a section (an instrument group). Verb phrase.
marchers.list.addTagAppearance: Button in the tag appearance list of the Marcher Appearance panel. Adds a style (colors and dot shape) for a tag (a named group of marchers). Verb phrase.
marchers.list.createTagsFirst: Hint in the tag appearance list when no tags exist yet. Tags (named groups of marchers) are created in the marcher inspector, the panel showing the selected marchers.
marchers.list.deleteButton: Item in the menu that opens from a marcher's row in the marcher list. Deletes that marcher (after a confirmation). Verb, shown with a trash icon.
marchers.list.dragToReorder: Screen-reader label of the drag handle on a row of the tag appearance list. Rows higher in the list have higher priority when a marcher belongs to several tags. Imperative.
marchers.list.drillNumberTitle: Column heading of the marcher list for the drill number (the marcher's unique ID, such as F12). The symbol '#' means 'number'; a very short heading.
marchers.list.editButton: Item in the menu that opens from a marcher's row in the marcher list. Opens the Edit Marcher form for that marcher. Verb, shown with a pencil icon.
marchers.list.fillColor: Label of a color picker in the appearance editor: the color that fills the marcher's dot on the field.
marchers.list.loadError: Shown in place of the marcher list in the Marchers panel when the show's marchers couldn't be read.
marchers.list.loading: Shown in place of the marcher list in the Marchers panel while the show's marchers are being read.
marchers.list.moreOptions: Screen-reader label of the ⋯ button on a marcher's row in the Marchers side panel. Opens a menu of actions for that marcher. {marcher} is the marcher's drill number, such as B1 or T3.
marchers.list.moveDown: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a button on a row of the tag appearance list. Moves the row down, lowering its priority: when a marcher belongs to several tags, the style higher in the list wins.
marchers.list.moveUp: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a button on a row of the tag appearance list. Moves the row up, raising its priority: when a marcher belongs to several tags, the style higher in the list wins.
marchers.list.nameTitle: Column heading of the marcher list for the marcher's name.
marchers.list.noMarchers: Empty-state message of the marcher list when the show has no marchers. A marcher is one performer on the field. The second sentence is a friendly nudge to add one.
marchers.list.noSectionStyles: Empty-state message in the Section styles list of the Marcher Appearance panel. A section style sets the colors and dot shape for all marchers of a section (instrument group).
marchers.list.none: Empty-state text in the tag appearance list of the Marcher Appearance panel, shown when there are no tag appearances to show.
marchers.list.outlineColor: Label of a color picker in the appearance editor: the color of the outline around the marcher's dot on the field.
marchers.list.sectionTitle: Column heading of the marcher list for the marcher's section: an instrument group, such as Flute.
marchers.list.shape: Label of the dropdown in the appearance editor for the shape of the marcher's dot on the field (such as circle or square). Not the same as a 'shape' formation of marchers.
marchers.list.unknown: Stand-in for a marcher's drill number in the list of marchers about to be deleted, when the drill number can't be found. A drill number is a marcher's code such as T12.
marchers.listTitle: Heading above the marcher list in the Marchers side panel. A noun naming the list.
marchers.marcherAppearance: Button label in the Marchers side panel and title of the panel it opens, where the user sets the colors and dot shapes of marchers by section or by tag. Noun phrase.
marchers.name: Label of the optional text field in the Add/Edit Marcher form for the marcher's name (the performer's own name), and a column heading in the CSV import preview.
marchers.nameInput: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the Name box when editing a marcher in the Marchers panel: the marcher's own name (for example the student's name).
marchers.notes: Label of the optional text area in the Add/Edit Marcher form for free-form notes about the marcher.
marchers.notesInput: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the Notes box when editing a marcher in the Marchers panel: free-text notes about this marcher.
marchers.notesPlaceholder: Placeholder text in the notes area of the Add/Edit Marcher form, shown while it is empty.
marchers.quantity: Label of the number field in the Add Marcher form for how many marchers to create at once, for example 12.
marchers.section: Label of the dropdown in the Add/Edit Marcher form for the marcher's section (instrument group, such as Flute). Also a column heading in the CSV import preview and section table. Noun; placeholder text of the dropdown too.
marchers.sectionAppearances.allTab: Tab in the "Add Section Style" menu listing every section (such as trumpets or color guard) OpenMarch knows, including ones with no marchers in this show.
marchers.sectionAppearances.createError: Error toast when adding a section style (the colors and shape that every marcher of one section, such as trumpets, gets on the field) fails.
marchers.sectionAppearances.inShowTab: Tab in the "Add Section Style" menu listing only the sections (such as trumpets or color guard) that have marchers in this show.
marchers.sectionError.chooseSection: Error under the section dropdown in the Add Marcher form, shown when the user submits without choosing a section. Polite imperative.
marchers.sectionText: Tab label in the Marcher Appearance panel. The tab sets the look of marchers by their section (instrument group, such as Flute). Sits next to the 'Tag' tab. One word.
marchers.tagAppearances.pageHeading: Heading above the tag appearances that start on one page, in the Marcher Appearance panel. {page} is a page name such as 3 or 2A.
marchers.tagAppearances.pageListLabel: Screen-reader label of the list of tag appearances that start on one page, in the Marcher Appearance panel. A tag appearance gives the marchers in a tag (a user-made group) their own colors and shape on the field from that page on. {page} is a page name such as 3 or 2A.
marchers.tagText: Tab label in the Marcher Appearance panel. The tab sets the look of marchers by their tag (a named group of marchers). Sits next to the 'Section' tab. One word.
marchers.title: Title of the Marchers side panel, which lists all marchers of the show and lets the user add or edit them. A marcher is one performer on the field. Plural noun.
marchers.updateButton: Submit button of the Edit Marcher form. Saves the changes to the marcher. Verb phrase.
marchers.year: Label of the optional text field in the Add/Edit Marcher form for the marcher's year, for example the performer's grade or year in school or in the group.
marchers.yearInput: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the Year box when editing a marcher in the Marchers panel: the marcher's school year or grade, free text.
measures.createFailed: Error toast shown when creating measures (bars of music) fails. {error} is the technical error message, such as "disk full".
measures.deleteFailed: Error toast shown when deleting measures (bars of music) fails. {error} is the technical error message, such as "disk full".
measures.updateFailed: Error toast shown when changing measures (bars of music) fails. {error} is the technical error message, such as "disk full".
menu.app.about: Item in the application menu (the menu named after the app, macOS only) that opens the About window. {appName} is the app's name, OpenMarch; keep it as is.
menu.app.hide: Item in the application menu (macOS only) that hides the app's windows. {appName} is the app's name, OpenMarch; keep it as is. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.app.hideOthers: Item in the application menu (macOS only) that hides every other app's windows. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.app.quit: Item in the application menu (macOS only) that quits the app. {appName} is the app's name, OpenMarch; keep it as is. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.app.services: Submenu in the application menu (macOS only) where macOS lists its system services. Use the name macOS uses in this language.
menu.app.showAll: Item in the application menu (macOS only) that shows the windows of every hidden app again. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.edit.copy: Item in the app's Edit menu, and in the right-click menu of a text field or selected text, that copies the selected text to the clipboard.
menu.edit.cut: Item in the app's Edit menu, and in the right-click menu of a text field, that cuts the selected text to the clipboard.
menu.edit.delete: Item in the app's Edit menu that deletes the selected text.
menu.edit.paste: Item in the app's Edit menu, and in the right-click menu of a text field, that pastes text from the clipboard.
menu.edit.pasteAndMatchStyle: Item in the app's Edit menu (macOS only) that pastes text without its formatting. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.edit.redo: Item in the right-click menu of a text field: redoes the last text change that Undo took back in the field (not in the show).
menu.edit.selectAll: Item in the app's Edit menu, and in the right-click menu of a text field or selected text, that selects all the text in the focused field.
menu.edit.speech: Submenu in the app's Edit menu (macOS only) with the system's read-aloud commands. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.edit.startSpeaking: Item in the Edit menu's Speech submenu (macOS only) that starts reading the selected text aloud.
menu.edit.stopSpeaking: Item in the Edit menu's Speech submenu (macOS only) that stops reading text aloud.
menu.edit.title: Name of the Edit menu in the app's menu bar (cut, copy, paste).
menu.edit.undo: Item in the right-click menu of a text field: undoes the last change to the text typed in the field (not to the show).
menu.file.closeFile: Item in the app's File menu that closes the open show and returns to the start screen.
menu.file.createNew: Item in the app's File menu that starts a new show.
menu.file.noDocument.message: Message of the error dialog shown when Save As Copy is chosen in the File menu while no window is focused, so there is no show to save.
menu.file.noDocument.title: Title of an error dialog shown when Save As Copy is chosen in the File menu while no window is focused.
menu.file.open: Item in the app's File menu that opens a show file from disk.
menu.file.saveAsCopy: Item in the app's File menu that saves a copy of the open show under a new name. OpenMarch saves changes automatically, so this only makes a copy.
menu.file.title: Name of the File menu in the app's menu bar (open, create, save and close show files).
menu.help.guides: Item in the app's Help menu that opens OpenMarch's documentation and guides in the browser.
menu.help.showShortcuts: Item in the app's Help menu that opens the list of keyboard shortcuts.
menu.help.title: Name of the Help menu in the app's menu bar.
menu.help.website: Item in the app's Help menu that opens the OpenMarch website in the browser.
menu.playback.playOn: Item in the app's Playback menu. Plays from the start flag (a marker on the timeline where playing begins) and keeps going past the selected range.
menu.playback.playPage: Item in the app's Playback menu. Plays from the playhead (the line marking the current time on the timeline), or pauses where it is.
menu.playback.playPause: Item in the app's Playback menu. Starts playing the show, or stops it and returns to where playing started.
menu.playback.title: Name of the Playback menu in the app's menu bar (play, pause, loop).
menu.playback.toggleLoop: Item in the app's Playback menu that turns looping of the selected range on the timeline on or off.
menu.view.forceReload: Item in the app's View menu that reloads the window, ignoring its cache.
menu.view.open3dView: Item in the app's View menu that opens the 3D View: a separate window that shows the show in 3D.
menu.view.reload: Item in the app's View menu that reloads the window.
menu.view.resetZoom: Item in the app's View menu that resets the interface zoom to 100%.
menu.view.title: Name of the View menu in the app's menu bar (3D View, zoom, full screen).
menu.view.toggleDevTools: Item in the app's View menu that shows or hides the developer tools panel.
menu.view.toggleFullScreen: Item in the app's View menu that switches the window into or out of full screen.
menu.view.zoomIn: Item in the app's View menu that makes the whole interface larger.
menu.view.zoomOut: Item in the app's View menu that makes the whole interface smaller.
menu.window.close: Item in the app's Window menu (Windows and Linux) that closes the window.
menu.window.front: Item in the app's Window menu (macOS only) that brings all the app's windows in front of other apps. Use the wording macOS uses in this language.
menu.window.minimize: Item in the app's Window menu that minimizes the window.
menu.window.title: Name of the Window menu in the app's menu bar (minimize, zoom, close).
menu.window.zoom: Item in the app's Window menu that maximizes the window or restores its size (the window, not the content). Use the wording the operating system uses.
menu.withShortcut: A menu item with its keyboard shortcut written after it, used on macOS for items whose shortcut the menu can't show in its own column. {label} is the item's name (for example Play / Stop) and {shortcut} is the key, such as Space, Shift+Space or ?. Keep both arguments and the brackets around the shortcut; change only the spacing or bracket style if your language writes them differently.
mobileExport.accessError.description: Error body in the Export to Mobile sidebar. The show file is linked to a production (the show's page in the On the Move phone app), but the signed-in account can't be confirmed to have access to it, or the production no longer exists.
mobileExport.accessError.hint: Advice under the access error. "Detach" unlinks this show file from its On the Move production (a button right below). The user can instead close the sidebar and sign in with an account that has access.
mobileExport.accessError.title: Heading of an error in the Export to Mobile sidebar: the app could not confirm that the signed-in account has access to the show's production in On the Move, the marchers' phone app.
mobileExport.audio.active: Small status tag next to the audio file that the phone app currently plays for the show. Adjective meaning "currently selected".
mobileExport.audio.add: Button in the Add Alternate Audio File dialog that uploads the chosen music file to the phone app. Verb, short.
mobileExport.audio.addAlternate: Button and dialog title for uploading an extra music file for the show to the phone app, in addition to the main one (for example a click track or a different edit). Verb phrase.
mobileExport.audio.addHelp: Help text in the Add Alternate Audio File dialog: once uploaded, the performers and instructors (the people using the phone app) can pick this music file in the app.
mobileExport.audio.cancel: Button that closes an audio dialog without saving or uploading. Verb, short.
mobileExport.audio.delete: Menu item in an audio file's options menu that deletes the file from the phone app production. Verb, short.
mobileExport.audio.duration: An audio file's length in the Audio Files list of the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app)'s settings. {minutes} and {seconds} are numbers; "m" and "s" abbreviate minutes and seconds.
mobileExport.audio.editNickname: Menu item in an audio file's options menu, and the title of the dialog that opens. A nickname is a friendly label chosen by the user for the audio file. Verb phrase.
mobileExport.audio.loadFailed: Error text shown when the list of audio files uploaded to the phone app could not be loaded. A Retry button follows.
mobileExport.audio.nicknameLabel: Label above a text field in the Add Alternate Audio File dialog for an optional nickname, a friendly name the user gives the audio file.
mobileExport.audio.nicknamePlaceholder: Placeholder (hint text) inside the nickname text field in the Add Alternate Audio File dialog. Shown in gray until the user types.
mobileExport.audio.nicknamePlaceholderSh: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the nickname text field in the audio dialogs. Shown in gray until the user types. Short.
mobileExport.audio.noData: Error shown when an audio file can't be uploaded with a revision in the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app) because the file in the show is empty. Appears inside "Revision uploaded, but audio sync failed".
mobileExport.audio.optionsAriaLabel: Screen-reader label of the three-dots button that opens the options menu (set as active, edit nickname, delete) for one audio file. Not shown visually.
mobileExport.audio.retry: Button that tries to load the list of audio files again after it failed. Verb, short.
mobileExport.audio.save: Button in the Edit Nickname dialog that saves the new nickname. Verb, short.
mobileExport.audio.saving: Label shown on the Save button in the Edit Nickname dialog while the change is being saved. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.audio.setActive: Menu item and checkbox label: make this audio file the one the phone app plays for the show. Verb phrase; "active" means the currently selected one.
mobileExport.audio.sizeMb: An audio file's size in megabytes in the Audio Files list of the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app)'s settings. {size} is a number with two decimals.
mobileExport.audio.title: Heading of the section in the mobile app settings that lists the music files uploaded to the phone app for this show. Plural noun.
mobileExport.audio.uploading: Label shown on the Add button while the audio file is being uploaded. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.close: Button that closes the Export to Mobile sidebar. Verb, short.
mobileExport.confirmPublish.cancel: Button in the Publish to mobile app confirmation that goes back without publishing. Verb, short.
mobileExport.confirmPublish.description: Warning in the confirmation shown before the first publish to the phone app. Publishing makes the show visible right away to everyone registered to the ensemble (the band or group) in On the Move.
mobileExport.confirmPublish.publish: Button in the confirmation that publishes the show to the phone app. Makes the show visible to the ensemble's members. Verb, short.
mobileExport.confirmPublish.title: Title of the confirmation shown before the show is published for the first time to the On the Move phone app.
mobileExport.date.dateTime: When a revision (an uploaded version of the show) was pushed, in the revisions list of the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app), for revisions a week old or more. {date} is the date and {time} the time of day, both already written in the app language's style.
mobileExport.date.daysAgo: Relative time on a revision in the list: how long ago it was published. {count} is a whole number of days, for example 3.
mobileExport.date.hoursAgo: Relative time on a revision in the list: how long ago it was published. {count} is a whole number of hours, for example 5.
mobileExport.date.justNow: Relative time on a revision in the list when it was published less than a minute ago.
mobileExport.date.minutesAgo: Relative time on a revision in the list: how long ago it was published. {count} is a whole number of minutes, for example 12.
mobileExport.detach.button: Button that unlinks this show file from its On the Move production (the show's page in the phone app). Verb phrase; the production itself is not deleted.
mobileExport.detach.cancel: Button in the detach confirmation that goes back without detaching. Verb, short.
mobileExport.detach.confirm: Confirmation text before detaching. After detaching, the user cannot upload new revisions (published versions of the show) to the phone app from this file until they attach it again. OTM Production = the show's page in the On the Move phone app.
mobileExport.detach.confirmButton: Button in the detach confirmation that carries it out. "Yes" confirms the question. Short.
mobileExport.detach.failed: Error notification when the show file could not be detached from its On the Move production.
mobileExport.loading.checkingSignIn: Status message in the Export to Mobile sidebar while the app checks whether the user is signed in. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.loading.validatingAccess: Status message in the Export to Mobile sidebar while the app confirms the signed-in account can access the show's On the Move production. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.logoAlt: Screen-reader description of the On the Move (OTM) logo image shown to signed-out users. OTM is the name of the marchers' phone app; keep the abbreviation.
mobileExport.pageLines.note: Quiet note in the Export to Mobile panel, shown when the show has moves the phone app can't play exactly (a move that starts or ends partway through a page, or a curved path). The phone app (OpenMarch On the Move) only knows each marcher's spot at the end of every page and draws a straight line from one page to the next.
mobileExport.revision.audioSyncFailed: Error notification: the revision was published, but its music file could not be set up in the phone app. {msg} is the error message, usually English, for example "Network error".
mobileExport.revision.backgroundSyncFail: Error notification: the revision was published, but the field background image could not be synced to the phone app. {msg} is the error message, usually English, for example "Network error".
mobileExport.revision.initialTitle: Automatic title given to the first revision (the first published version of the show) of a phone app production, so the user is not asked to type one.
mobileExport.revision.newTitleLabel: Label above a text field where the user names a new revision. A revision is one published version of the show uploaded to the phone app.
mobileExport.revision.noProductionLinked: Error shown in the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app) when uploading a revision but the show isn't attached to an On the Move (OTM) production, the show's entry in the mobile app.
mobileExport.revision.preparing: Label on the publish button while the app gets ready to upload (before and between upload steps). Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revision.publishButton: Main button for the first upload: publishes the show to the On the Move phone app for the first time. Verb phrase.
mobileExport.revision.publishing: Label on the publish button while the first upload is running. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revision.pushButton: Main button for later uploads: sends a new revision (updated version of the show) to the phone app. Verb phrase; "push" means send an update.
mobileExport.revision.pushing: Label on the push button while a new revision is uploading. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revision.titlePlaceholder: Placeholder (hint text) in the revision title text field, prompting the user to say what changed since the last revision.
mobileExport.revision.titleRequired: Validation error under the revision title field when the user tries to push a revision without giving it a title.
mobileExport.revision.uploadFailed: Error shown in the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app) when pushing a revision (an uploaded version of the show) fails. {error} is the reason, often from the server and possibly in English.
mobileExport.revision.uploadFailedGeneri: Fallback error message when a revision upload failed and the server returned an unreadable (web page) reply. The English asks the user to check the console, a developer tool.
mobileExport.revision.uploadFailedUnknow: Reason shown in "Upload failed: …" in the Export to Mobile panel (which publishes the show to the OpenMarch On the Move mobile app) when the server gave no reason for the failure.
mobileExport.revision.uploadSuccess: Success notification after a revision was uploaded to the phone app.
mobileExport.revision.uploadingAudio: Label on the publish button while the show's music file is being uploaded to the phone app. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revision.uploadingImage: Label on the publish button while the field background image is being uploaded to the phone app. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revision.validatingAudio: Label on the publish button while the show's music file is being checked before it is uploaded. Keep the ellipsis.
mobileExport.revisions.active: Small tag with a phone icon on the revision that marchers currently see in the phone app. Adjective meaning "currently live".
mobileExport.revisions.emptyMessage: Message shown instead of the revision list before anything has been published. Once the first revision is published, the user can push more revisions (updated versions) to keep the phone app current.
mobileExport.revisions.listHeading: Heading above the list of all revisions (published versions of the show) uploaded to the phone app.
mobileExport.settings.backgroundImage.al: Screen-reader description of the picture showing the field background image used by the production in the phone app.
mobileExport.settings.backgroundImage.em: Text shown when the production in the phone app has no background image.
mobileExport.settings.backgroundImage.he: Help text in the mobile app settings: the field's background image uploads automatically with each new revision. To change it, edit the background image in the field editor (the Field panel) and upload a new revision.
mobileExport.settings.backgroundImage.ti: Heading in the mobile app settings for the production's background image, the picture behind the field in the phone app.
mobileExport.settings.button: Button in the Export to Mobile sidebar that opens the mobile app settings dialog (audio files, background image, detach). Short noun.
mobileExport.settings.detach.title: Heading in the mobile app settings above the Detach File from Production button. Detach unlinks this show file from its On the Move production.
mobileExport.settings.noProduction: Text shown in the mobile app settings when this show file is not linked to any On the Move production (the show's page in the phone app).
mobileExport.settings.title: Title of the mobile app settings dialog, with settings for the On the Move phone app: audio files, background image, detaching the file.
mobileExport.signInRejected.description: Explanation in the Export to Mobile sidebar when OpenMarch's online service rejected the user's sign-in (it may have expired or been revoked). Tells them to sign out and sign in again.
mobileExport.signInRejected.signOut: Button under "Your sign-in wasn't accepted" in the Export to Mobile sidebar. Signs the user out so they can sign in again.
mobileExport.signInRejected.title: Heading in the Export to Mobile sidebar when OpenMarch's online service rejected the user's sign-in.
mobileExport.signedOut.createAccountProm: Text above the Set up your account button, shown to users who are not signed in in the Export to Mobile sidebar. "On the Move" is the marchers' phone app.
mobileExport.signedOut.setupAccount: Button that opens the sign-up page in the web browser to create an On the Move account. Verb phrase.
mobileExport.signedOut.signInPrompt: Text above the sign-in button for users who already have an account. "On The Move" is the name of the marchers' phone app; the phrase plays on the app name and means taking their show to the phone.
mobileExport.signedOut.errors.failed: Error under the Sign in button in the Export to Mobile sidebar when signing in to the user's OpenMarch account didn't work for an unknown reason. Short; ends by asking them to try again.
mobileExport.signedOut.errors.sessionExp: Message under the Sign in button in the Export to Mobile sidebar after the user's sign-in expired (they were signed out automatically). Uploading means uploading the show to the On the Move phone app.
mobileExport.signedOut.errors.unavailabl: Error under the Sign in button in the Export to Mobile sidebar when the sign-in service couldn't load, usually because there's no internet connection.
mobileExport.signedOut.signInPromptWeb: Text above the sign-in button in the browser version of OpenMarch (the web editor), for users who already have an account. Like mobileExport.signedOut.signInPrompt but without mentioning the desktop app. "On The Move" is the name of the marchers' phone app; the phrase plays on the app name and means taking their show to the phone.
mobileExport.title: Title of the Export to Mobile sidebar and its screen-reader label. It exports the show to the On the Move phone app for marchers.
mobileExport.unreachable.description: Explanation under the "Can't reach OpenMarch" heading in the Export to Mobile sidebar: the online service didn't answer or the sign-in couldn't be confirmed, and the user should check their internet connection and try again.
mobileExport.unreachable.retry: Button under the "Can't reach OpenMarch" message in the Export to Mobile sidebar. Tries loading the show's online production again.
mobileExport.unreachable.title: Heading in the Export to Mobile sidebar when the app couldn't reach OpenMarch's online service, or couldn't refresh the user's sign-in (usually no internet). Not an access problem: the account is fine. "OpenMarch" is the app's name.
music.accent: Label of an on/off switch in the Metronome dialog. When on, the metronome plays a stronger click on the first beat of every measure (bar). Reads like a setting name.
music.addAfterCaption: Short caption under a plus-icon button on a tempo group card, shown only in the touch layout (no hover tooltips). The button adds a new tempo group after this one. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter. Keep it very short.
music.addNewTempoGroupAfter: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the plus button on a tempo group card in the Music dialog: adds a new tempo group right after this one. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.addTempoGroup: Button at the bottom of the Music dialog's tempo group list. Opens the form for adding a tempo group at the end. While the form is open the same button reads Cancel. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.audio: Heading of the audio section in the Music dialog, above the chooser for the show's music file. Noun.
music.audioFile: Label of the dropdown in the Music dialog for choosing which imported audio file (the show's music) is in use. Noun.
music.beatPattern: Label of a dropdown in the tempo group form for mixed meter. The pattern groups the beats of a measure, such as "3+2+2" for seven beats. The trailing asterisk marks the field as required; keep it.
music.beatStyle: Label of a dropdown in the Metronome dialog that picks the sound of the click (Standard, Sharp or Smooth).
music.beatsPerMeasure: Label of a number box in the tempo group form: how many beats are in each measure (the top number of the time signature, such as 4). The trailing asterisk marks the field as required; keep it.
music.bpmUnit: Unit after a tempo number in the Music panel's list of tempo groups, in the tempo fields of the new/edit tempo group forms, and in the tempo field of the menu that opens on a beat in the timeline's music row. Abbreviation for beats per minute; keep it short.
music.cancel: Button that closes a form or confirmation without saving, in the Music dialog (the add tempo group toggle, the audio file delete confirmation and the tempo group delete confirmation). Verb. Short.
music.create: Submit button of the form for adding a new tempo group in the Music dialog. Creates the tempo group, with its measures and beats. Verb. Short.
music.custom: Heading on a tempo group card whose beats each have their own tempo (rather than one tempo for the whole group). Shown above the list of those individual beat tempos. Adjective used as a heading.
music.customization: Heading of the section of the Metronome dialog with the beat style (click sound) setting. Noun.
music.delete: Confirm button in the dialog that asks whether to delete an audio file. Permanently deletes the file from the show. Verb. Short.
music.deleteAllMeasures: Red confirm button in the dialog that asks before deleting a tempo group. Deletes every measure of the group together with the pages built on them. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.deleteAudioFile: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting an audio file, and the label of the button that opens it. Verb phrase.
music.deleteAudioFileDescription: Body text of the confirmation dialog for deleting an audio file from the show.
music.deleteSuccess: Success toast after an audio file was deleted. {fileName} is the name of that file, such as "halftime.mp3".
music.deleteTempoGroup: Screen-reader label of the trash button on a tempo group card, which starts deleting the tempo group. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.deleteTempoGroupAlert: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting a tempo group. Short question to make the user stop and read the warning below it.
music.deleteTempoGroupDescription: Warning text in the confirmation dialog for deleting a tempo group: the pages that belong to the group's measures are deleted too. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
music.editTempoGroup: Screen-reader label of the pencil button on a tempo group card, which opens the card for editing. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.endTempo: Label of a number box in the form for adding a tempo group: the tempo, in beats per minute, the group's tempo gradually moves toward, for a smooth speed change into the next group. Optional.
music.endTempoPlaceholder: Placeholder inside the optional End Tempo number box in the tempo group form. Means the field can be left empty.
music.endTempoTooltip: Tooltip on the End Tempo field in the form for adding a tempo group. Explains that the group's tempo changes gradually toward this value without quite reaching it, so the next tempo group can begin smoothly. The line break in the middle is intentional; keep it.
music.general: Heading of the section of the Metronome dialog with the on/off, accent and click-on-measure settings. Noun; means general settings.
music.import: Placeholder shown on the audio file dropdown in the Music dialog when no audio file is chosen yet. Invites the user to import one. Verb.
music.importAudioFile: Button in the Music dialog's audio file dropdown, with a plus icon. Opens a file picker to import an audio file (the show's music) into the show. Verb phrase.
music.importButton: Button label in the Music dialog that opens a file picker to import a MusicXML score file (a standard music notation format) so the show's measures and tempo follow the score. "MusicXML" is a file format name.
music.importChecksCount: Secondary line of a warning toast after a MusicXML import that needs the user's attention. {count} is the number of things to check in the score, such as 1 or 4 (plural form chosen by it). The # stands for the number.
music.importChecksIntro: Introductory paragraph of the dialog listing issues found while importing a MusicXML score file. {fileName} is the name of the imported file, such as "halftime.musicxml". The importer guessed at, or could not read, certain parts of the score, so the measure counts may differ from the music.
music.importChecksMeasure: A measure (bar) in the list of things to check after a MusicXML import (the "Check these in the score" dialog). {label} is the measure's number or label from the score, such as 12 or 12A; "m" abbreviates measure. Several of these are joined with commas.
music.importChecksMoreMeasures: Part of a line in the import checks dialog that lists the measures an issue concerns. {measures} is the first few measures already listed, such as "m4, m5, m6". {more} is how many further measures are not listed, such as 12. Reads like "m4, m5, m6 and 12 more".
music.importChecksShow: Button in a warning toast after a MusicXML import. Opens the dialog that lists what to check in the score. Verb. Short.
music.importChecksTitle: Title of the dialog listing issues found while importing a MusicXML score file, and the screen-reader label of that list. Tells the user to check these places against their score.
music.importDataMissing: Error toast when MusicXML import starts before the show's pages and beats have loaded, so the score can't be imported yet. MusicXML is a sheet-music file format.
music.importError: Error toast shown when importing a MusicXML score file fails. MusicXML is a standard music notation file format.
music.importLabel: Heading of the MusicXML import section in the Music dialog. MusicXML is a standard music notation file format; keep the name.
music.importSuccess: Success toast after a MusicXML score file was imported. {fileName} is the file's name, such as "halftime.musicxml". MusicXML is a music notation file format.
music.importing: Label of the MusicXML import button while the import is running. Present participle. Keep the three dots.
music.individualBeatTempos: Caption above a list of number boxes on a tempo group card that is being edited, one tempo (beats per minute) for each beat of the group. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.makeMixedMeter: Button in the form for adding a tempo group that switches it to mixed meter, where each measure's beats are grouped unevenly, such as 3+2+2. Verb phrase.
music.makeSimpleMeter: Button in the form for adding a tempo group that switches it back to regular (simple) meter, where each measure has evenly grouped beats, such as 4/4. Verb phrase.
music.metronome: Title of the Metronome dialog, where the user turns the metronome (an audible click on each beat during playback) on and sets its volume and sound.
music.mixedMeterTooManyBeats: Warning shown under the Beats per measure box of the form for adding a tempo group when mixed meter (uneven beat groupings such as 3+2+2) is chosen with too many beats. {maxBeats} is the largest allowed number, such as 30. {beatsPerMeasure} is the number the user typed, such as 40. Playful tone; asks the user to get in touch.
music.name: Label of the optional text box for a tempo group's name in the tempo group form and card. The name is typically a rehearsal letter.
music.nameDescription: Small help text beside the name box of a tempo group card being edited. A rehearsal letter is a letter such as "A" or "B" printed in the score to mark a place in the music.
music.namePlaceholder: Placeholder inside the optional name box of a tempo group card being edited. Means the name can be left empty.
music.numberOfMeasures: Label of a number box in the tempo group form: how many measures (bars) the group lasts. The trailing asterisk marks the field as required; keep it.
music.onOff: Label of the on/off switch in the Metronome dialog. Turns the metronome (an audible click on each beat during playback) on or off.
music.onlyClickOnMeasure: Label of an on/off switch in the Metronome dialog. When on, the metronome clicks only on the first beat of each measure (bar) instead of every beat.
music.phrases.errors.create: Error toast shown when adding a phrase fails. A phrase is a named stretch of the music (for example "Opener hit") marked on the timeline.
music.phrases.errors.delete: Error toast shown when deleting a phrase fails. A phrase is a named stretch of the music marked on the timeline.
music.phrases.errors.update: Error toast shown when saving changes to a phrase fails. A phrase is a named stretch of the music marked on the timeline.
music.rehearsalLetterOrIdentifier: Small help text beside the name box of the tempo group form. A rehearsal letter is a letter such as "A" or "B" printed in the score to mark a place in the music; the name can also be any other identifier.
music.repeatPlayNote: Note saved on a measure imported from MusicXML when it is a repeated pass of a written measure (it is played again because of a repeat). {label} is the written measure's label as in the score, such as "4". {time} is which pass it is, such as 2. Reads like "m4, time 2"; "m" abbreviates measure.
music.saveChanges: Button on a tempo group card being edited that saves the edits. Verb phrase. Short.
music.seeDocs: Link-style button in the Music dialog that opens the OpenMarch website's guide on tempo in the user's web browser. Short.
music.select: Placeholder on the beat style dropdown in the Metronome dialog, shown only when no style is chosen. Verb, as in choose one.
music.selectPattern: Placeholder option in the beat pattern dropdown of the tempo group form (the first, empty choice). Tells the user to choose a pattern of beat groupings, such as 3+2+2. Verb phrase.
music.sharp: Name of one metronome click sound in the beat style dropdown: a short, crisp click. Adjective.
music.smooth: Name of one metronome click sound in the beat style dropdown: a soft, rounded click. Adjective.
music.standard: Name of the default metronome click sound in the beat style dropdown. Adjective.
music.startTempo: Label of a number box in the form for adding a tempo group: the group's tempo, in beats per minute, at its first beat. The trailing asterisk marks the field as required; keep it.
music.tempo: Label of a number box on a tempo group card being edited: the group's tempo (speed). The trailing asterisk marks the field as required; keep it. The unit, beats per minute, is shown beside the box.
music.tempoBelowMinimum: Error toast shown when the user enters a tempo that is too slow. {min} is the lowest allowed tempo in beats per minute (BPM), such as 10.
music.tempoDescription: Small help text beside the Tempo box of a tempo group card being edited. Says the unit of the number: beats per minute.
music.tempoGroupCard.measure: The single measure (bar) a tempo group covers, shown in the Music panel's list of tempo groups. A tempo group is a run of measures with the same tempo and time signature. {measure} is the measure number; "m" abbreviates measure.
music.tempoGroupCard.measureRange: The measures (bars) a tempo group covers, shown in the Music panel's list of tempo groups. A tempo group is a run of measures with the same tempo and time signature. {start} and {end} are measure numbers; "m" abbreviates measures.
music.tempoGroupCard.measureRangeRepeats: The measures a tempo group covers plus how many times its measure repeats, shown in the Music panel's list of tempo groups. {range} is already written, such as "m 1-4"; {count} is the number of repeats (2 or more).
music.tempoGroupCreated: Success toast after a new tempo group was created. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.tempoGroupNamePlaceholder: Placeholder inside the optional name box of the form for adding a tempo group. Means the name can be left empty.
music.tempoGroupUpdated: Success toast after a tempo group was edited and saved. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
music.tempoGroups: Heading of the tempo group list in the Music dialog. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter. Noun, plural.
music.timeSignature: Help text under the Beats per measure box of the tempo group form. {timeSignature} is the resulting time signature, such as "4/4" or "7/8" (beats per measure over the note value). Keep the colon.
music.title: Title of the Music dialog, where the user manages the show's audio file, tempo groups and MusicXML import.. Noun.
music.undoWithShortcut: Note in the confirmation dialog for deleting a tempo group and its measures in the Music panel. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Undo shortcut drawn as keycaps (for example Ctrl + Z, or ⌘ Z on a Mac).
music.volume: Heading above the volume slider in the Metronome dialog. Next to it the app shows the percentage.
pages.createError: Error toast shown when creating a page fails. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation). {error} is the technical error message, such as "disk full".
pages.deleteWithMoves.changed: Last part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves: the pages whose marcher positions changed as a result. {pages} is a page name or a list of names and ranges (for example "3–5, 7"); {count} is how many pages that is. The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
pages.deleteWithMoves.changedBoth: Last part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves: the pages whose marcher positions changed, in two groups. {kept} lists pages that kept their names ({keptCount} of them); {renamed} lists pages the delete renumbered, by their old names ({renamedCount} of them). Names may be ranges like "3–5". The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
pages.deleteWithMoves.changedOld: Last part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves: the pages whose marcher positions changed. "old" because the delete renumbered them: {pages} lists their names from before the delete (for example "3–4"); {count} is how many pages that is. Starts lowercase in English because it follows a " · " separator; use your language's usual capitalization after such a separator. The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
pages.deleteWithMoves.deleted: First part of the toast after the user deletes one or more pages together with their moves on the timeline. {names} is the deleted page name, or several names separated by commas (for example "2, 4"); {count} is how many pages were deleted. A page is one section of the drill, ending at a set. The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
pages.deleteWithMoves.grown: Part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves: a page that took over the deleted page's time and is now longer. {page} is the page's name (for example "3" or "4A"); {counts} is its new length in counts (beats of the music). The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own.
pages.deleteWithMoves.grownOld: Part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves: a page that took over the deleted page's time and is now longer. "old" because the delete renumbered it: {page} is its name from before the delete, the one the user remembers. {counts} is its new length in counts (beats of the music). Starts lowercase in English because it follows a " · " separator; use your language's usual capitalization after such a separator. The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own.
pages.deleteWithMoves.noOtherChanged: Last part of the toast after deleting a page with its moves, when no remaining page's marcher positions changed. The toast is built from separate parts, each a complete statement on its own, joined with " · " in this order: deleted pages, then one part per page that grew, then which pages changed. No part's grammar depends on another, so translate each on its own.
pages.dotModeFailed: Error toast shown when changing how a page's marchers are drawn on the field (the page's dot mode) fails. A page is one section of the drill between two sets.
pages.durationFailed: Error toast shown when changing a page's length in counts fails. A page is one section of the drill.
