pages.durationNoBeat: Error toast shown when changing a page's length in counts fails because the show's beat grid has no beat where the page would need to end. A page is one section of the drill; beats are the counts of the music.
pages.noNextPage: Info toast shown when the user tries to go to the next page but the current page is the last one. A page is one section of the drill, ending at a set.
pages.noPreviousPage: Info toast shown when the user tries to go to the previous page but the current page is the first one. A page is one section of the drill, ending at a set.
pages.pushPastEnd: Error toast shown when lengthening a page would push the following pages later than the last beat of the show's music. "Push" means moving the later pages later in time.
pages.splitNoStartBeat: Error toast shown when splitting a page into two fails because the app can't find the count where the new second page should begin.
pages.splitTooShort: Error toast shown when the user tries to split a page into two, but the page is only one count long. A page is one section of the drill; a beat is one count of the music.
pages.undoDeleteUnavailable: Info toast shown when the user presses the Undo button on a "page deleted" toast but the show changed in between, so that exact undo is no longer possible. Points the user to the Undo button in the toolbar to step back through changes.
pages.updateError: Error toast shown when changing a page fails. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation). {error} is the technical error message, such as "disk full".
pages.yankEmptyPages: Error toast shown when the later pages can't be pulled earlier in time because one of them has no beats (counts) at all. "Yank" means pulling the later pages earlier in time.
pages.yankNegativeCounts: Error toast shown when shortening a page would pull the following pages back so far that a page would have fewer than zero counts. "Yank" means pulling the later pages earlier in time; a count is one beat of the music.
pages.yankOutOfBounds: Error toast shown when moving the later pages earlier or later in time would place a page before the first beat or after the last beat of the show's music.
props.back: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the back arrow in the Props panel's edit view. Returns to the list of props.
props.close: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the X button that closes the Props side panel.
props.color: Label of a prop's color in the Props panel, above or beside the color button. The prop is drawn in that color on the field and in the 3D View; with no color it keeps the default look.
props.colorMixed: Text on the color button for several selected props in the Props panel, when they have different colors. Picking a color gives all of them that color. Short.
props.colorNone: Text on a prop's color button in the Props panel when the prop has no color of its own (it is drawn in the default look). Clicking it opens a color picker. Short.
props.counts: Unit shown beside the Transition number when editing a prop. A count is one beat of the music; the number is how many counts the prop takes to change to its new outline. Lowercase, short.
props.delete: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the red trash button on a prop's row in the Props panel. Deletes that prop; the user can undo it. A prop is a piece of equipment or scenery on the field (for example a floor, a platform or an obstacle).
props.depth: Label of the number field for a prop's depth, its size front to back, measured in meters. Shown when editing a prop's outline.
props.draw.cancel: Button on the hint card shown while drawing a prop on the field. Stops drawing without making a prop.
props.draw.instructions.arc: Instruction on the card shown while drawing a prop with the Arc outline. The two ends are clicked first, then a third click sets how much the arc bends.
props.draw.instructions.circle: Instruction on the card shown while drawing a prop with the Circle outline. The user presses at the center and drags outward to set the radius.
props.draw.instructions.drag: Instruction on the card shown while drawing a prop with the Rectangle or Freehand outline. The playhead is the current position in the show's timeline; the prop appears on the field from that count (beat) onward.
props.draw.instructions.polygon: Instruction on the card shown while drawing a prop with the Polygon outline. The user clicks each corner, then double-clicks to close the shape.
props.draw.title: Small heading above the row of outline buttons (Rectangle, Circle, Polygon, Arc, Freehand) in the Props panel. Tells the user to pick an outline, then draw the prop on the field.
props.edit: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the pencil button on a prop's row in the Props panel. Opens that prop for editing. A prop is a piece of equipment or scenery on the field.
props.editTitle: Title of the Props panel while one prop is being edited (title case, as a window title).
props.empty: Message in the Props panel when the show has no props. "Above" refers to the row of outline buttons (Rectangle, Circle and so on) directly over this text; a prop is a piece of equipment or scenery on the field.
props.errors.create: Error toast shown when creating a prop fails. A prop is a piece of equipment or scenery on the field.
props.errors.delete: Error toast shown when deleting a prop fails.
props.errors.outline: Error toast shown when changing a prop's outline (its size, rotation or shape) fails.
props.errors.update: Error toast shown when changing a prop's other settings (name, surface type) fails.
props.height: Label of the number field for a prop's height, its vertical size, in meters.
props.hide: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the eye button on a prop's row. Shown while the prop is visible; pressing it hides the prop on the field (it is not deleted).
props.name: Label of the text field for a prop's name. Optional; when empty the prop shows its generated number.
props.offField: Notice shown instead of the outline fields when the prop is not on the field at the playhead's current count. A prop's outline can only be changed at a count where it is on the field.
props.outline.arc: Name of the Arc outline for drawing a prop: a curved line. Label of a button under "Draw a prop" and also shown as its tooltip.
props.outline.circle: Name of the Circle outline for drawing a prop. Label of a button under "Draw a prop" and also shown as its tooltip.
props.outline.freehand: Name of the Freehand outline for drawing a prop: the user draws any shape by dragging. Label of a button under "Draw a prop" and also shown as its tooltip.
props.outline.polygon: Name of the Polygon outline for drawing a prop: a shape with straight sides and as many corners as the user clicks. Label of a button under "Draw a prop" and also shown as its tooltip.
props.outline.rectangle: Name of the Rectangle outline for drawing a prop. Label of a button under "Draw a prop" and also shown as its tooltip.
props.outlineFrom: Heading above a prop's size fields while the playhead is at a count where the prop already has an outline. {count} is the count (beat number, a whole number such as 17) the outline starts from; edits apply from that count onward.
props.outlineTitle: Heading above a prop's size fields (width, depth, height, rotation, transition) when there is no specific count to name.
props.rollOut.back: Option in the Roll-out menu for a floor prop. The floor's artwork is revealed starting from the back edge (the edge farthest from the audience) as the outline grows, instead of being stretched.
props.rollOut.front: Option in the Roll-out menu for a floor prop. The floor's artwork is revealed starting from the front edge (the edge nearest the audience) as the outline grows, instead of being stretched.
props.rollOut.label: Label of the menu, shown only for floor props, for whether the floor's artwork is revealed from one edge (like a carpet unrolling) as its outline grows over the transition counts, rather than stretched.
props.rollOut.left: Option in the Roll-out menu for a floor prop. The floor's artwork is revealed starting from the left edge as the outline grows, instead of being stretched.
props.rollOut.none: Option in the Roll-out menu for a floor prop. The floor does not roll out: its artwork is stretched as the outline changes. Also shown as the menu's current value.
props.rollOut.right: Option in the Roll-out menu for a floor prop. The floor's artwork is revealed starting from the right edge as the outline grows, instead of being stretched.
props.rotation: Label of the number field for a prop's rotation, in degrees (the ° unit follows the number).
props.selectedCount: In the Props panel's list, shown when several props are selected on the field, beside a color button that colors all of them at once. # is how many props are selected.
props.show: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the eye button on a prop's row. Shown while the prop is hidden; pressing it shows the prop on the field again.
props.showNames: Label of a switch at the top of the Props list. Turns on or off the name labels drawn next to every prop on the field.
props.surface.floor: Surface type of a prop: flat, marched over, with artwork on top (for example a tarp or floor cover). Shown under the prop's name and as an option in the Surface menu.
props.surface.obstacle: Surface type of a prop: it has height and nothing can stand on it (for example large scenery). Shown under the prop's name and as an option in the Surface menu.
props.surface.platform: Surface type of a prop: it has height and performers whose dot is inside it stand on top (a raised stand). Shown under the prop's name and as an option in the Surface menu.
props.surfaceLabel: Label of the menu for a prop's surface type (Floor, Obstacle or Platform), which says whether it is flat, raised to stand on, or an obstacle.
props.title: Title of the Props side panel, which lists the show's props. A prop is a piece of equipment or scenery on the field.
props.transition: Label of the number field for how many counts a prop takes to change from its old outline to the new one. The unit "counts" follows the number.
props.units.meters: Unit abbreviation for meters, shown after the width, depth and height boxes of a prop's outline in the Props panel. A prop is a set piece or object placed on the field. Use your language's usual abbreviation.
props.width: Label of the number field for a prop's width, its size side to side, in meters.
section.appearances.errors.create: Error toast shown when adding a section appearance fails. A section appearance is the color and style used for every marcher of one section (for example all Trumpets).
section.appearances.errors.delete: Error toast shown when removing a section appearance fails. A section appearance is the color and style used for every marcher of one section (for example all Trumpets).
section.appearances.errors.update: Error toast shown when saving changes to a section appearance fails. A section appearance is the color and style used for every marcher of one section (for example all Trumpets).
section.drumMajor: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. The drum major, who conducts and leads the band.
section.family.battery: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. Battery means the marching drumline (snare, tenors, bass drums, cymbals).
section.family.brass: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. Brass instruments such as trumpets, trombones and tubas.
section.family.guard: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. The color guard: performers with flags, rifles and dancers.
section.family.other: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. A catch-all family for sections that fit no other group.
section.family.pit: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. The pit (front ensemble): the section of mallet and other percussion instruments, such as marimba and vibraphone.
section.family.woodwind: Name of an instrument family (a group of sections), used to group and order sections in lists and the Select tab. Woodwind instruments: flutes, clarinets, saxophones.
section.guard.colorGuard: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. General color guard performer.
section.guard.dancer: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A color guard dancer.
section.guard.flag: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A color guard member who spins a flag.
section.guard.rifle: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A color guard member who spins a rifle (a prop).
section.guard.twirler: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A baton twirler.
section.instrument.altoSax: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Alto saxophone.
section.instrument.bariSax: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Baritone saxophone, the lowest-pitched saxophone in the band.
section.instrument.baritone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Baritone horn, a brass instrument.
section.instrument.bassClarinet: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Bass clarinet.
section.instrument.bassDrum: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Bass drum in the drumline.
section.instrument.bassTrombone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Bass trombone.
section.instrument.clarinet: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Clarinet.
section.instrument.cymbals: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Marching cymbals in the drumline.
section.instrument.euphonium: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Euphonium, a brass instrument.
section.instrument.flubDrum: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Flub drum, a bass drum in the drumline (shown in the 3D View as a bass drum).
section.instrument.flute: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Flute.
section.instrument.mellophone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Mellophone, a marching brass instrument.
section.instrument.piccolo: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Piccolo, a small high-pitched flute.
section.instrument.snare: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Snare drum in the drumline.
section.instrument.sopranoSax: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Soprano saxophone.
section.instrument.tenorSax: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Tenor saxophone.
section.instrument.tenors: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Tenor drums, a drumline instrument (plural noun).
section.instrument.trombone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Trombone.
section.instrument.trumpet: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Trumpet.
section.instrument.tuba: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Tuba, the lowest-pitched brass instrument.
section.other: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A catch-all section for performers that fit no other section. Also the default section for a new marcher.
section.pit.auxPercussion: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Auxiliary percussion, a pit section for extra percussion instruments.
section.pit.marimba: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Marimba, a pit instrument.
section.pit.synthesizer: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Synthesizer (keyboard) in the pit.
section.pit.vibraphone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Vibraphone, a pit instrument.
section.pit.xylophone: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. Xylophone, a pit instrument.
section.soloist.soloist: Name of a section, the instrument or role that a marcher plays or performs; marchers are grouped by section. Appears in lists, filters and the CSV import table, and a typed name is also matched on import. A featured soloist performer.
settings.appearance: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for how the app looks: light or dark theme, showing the file path in the title bar, and performance mode.
settings.appearance.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Appearance' section title in Settings.
settings.database: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) with tools for the show file that is open. Here 'database' means the show's file on disk, not a server. Not in the web editor.
settings.database.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Database' section title in Settings. 'The file of the show that's open' is the show file currently loaded.
settings.database.noShowOpen: Message shown in the Database section of Settings when no show is open, so there is no file to repair.
settings.developer: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and heading of its collapsible panel) with tools for people who translate or debug OpenMarch. Not in the web editor.
settings.developer.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Developer Settings' section title in Settings. Translating here means working on the app's own translations.
settings.field: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for how the field looks: grid lines, marcher labels, step size warnings.
settings.field.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Field' section title in Settings.
settings.field.gridLines: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Field: show the grid lines on the field.
settings.field.halfLines: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Field: show the half lines, the lighter lines drawn halfway between the field's main lines.
settings.field.labelPosition: Label of a choice in Settings > Field: where each marcher's label (its name or number) is drawn relative to its dot. Choices: 'Above the dot' and 'Beside the dot'.
settings.field.labelPosition.above: Choice (pill button) for where marcher labels go: drawn above each marcher's dot on the field.
settings.field.labelPosition.beside: Choice (pill button) for where marcher labels go: drawn next to each marcher's dot on the field.
settings.field.labelSize: Label of a choice in Settings > Field: how large the marcher labels are drawn. Choices: Small, Normal, Large.
settings.field.labelSize.large: Choice (pill button) for marcher label size: large. Short adjective.
settings.field.labelSize.normal: Choice (pill button) for marcher label size: the default, medium size. Short adjective.
settings.field.labelSize.small: Choice (pill button) for marcher label size: small. Short adjective.
settings.field.stepSizeWarnings: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Field: mark moves whose step size is too large to march.
settings.field.stepSizeWarnings.descript: Help text under the 'Step size warnings' switch. Step size is the distance covered per count. A move is a marcher movement between two sets; its path is the line drawn for it on the field.
settings.general: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for app-wide preferences: language, updates, opening the 3D View.
settings.general.appearance: Label of the theme setting in Settings > Appearance. The two choices beside it are 'Light' and 'Dark'.
settings.general.appearance.dark: Dark theme choice (pill button with a moon icon) in Settings > Appearance. Adjective describing the color scheme.
settings.general.appearance.light: Light theme choice (pill button with a sun icon) in Settings > Appearance. Adjective describing the color scheme.
settings.general.automaticUpdates: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > General. When on, the desktop app downloads and installs new OpenMarch versions by itself. Not in the web editor.
settings.general.description: One-line subtitle under the 'General' section title in Settings. Editor mode means Basic or Expert, a choice made in Settings > Timeline.
settings.general.editorMode: Label above two cards in Settings > Timeline (and the welcome flow) for choosing the editor mode, 'Basic' or 'Expert'.
settings.general.editorMode.basic: Title of the Basic editor mode card (Settings > Timeline and the welcome flow). Basic works page by page, like a drill chart. A proper name for a mode; capitalize like the other mode, 'Expert'.
settings.general.editorMode.basic.descri: Description under the Basic mode card. A page is one drill set: marchers hold their positions until you move them again. 'Positions in the middle of a page' are positions between two sets, which Basic allows.
settings.general.editorMode.expert: Title of the Expert editor mode card (Settings > Timeline and the welcome flow). Expert is the full timeline. A proper name for a mode; capitalize like the other mode, 'Basic'.
settings.general.editorMode.expert.descr: Description under the Expert mode card. A move is one marcher movement on the timeline; the start flag marks where playback starts; loops repeat a section. Expert allows moves that cross page boundaries and overlap.
settings.general.editorMode.note: Small note under the editor mode cards. Switching modes never changes the show. 'Locked' is how Basic displays things made in Expert that Basic can't edit: they stay and play but can't be changed there.
settings.general.language: Label of the language picker in Settings > General.
settings.general.openView3dWithShow: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > General. When on, the 3D View window opens by itself each time a show is opened. Not in the web editor.
settings.general.performanceMode: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Appearance. A mode that draws the field more simply so it stays smooth on slower computers.
settings.general.performanceMode.descrip: Help text under the Performance mode switch. 'Graphics run in software' means the computer has no graphics acceleration; the app then turns the mode on automatically.
settings.general.showFullDatabasePath: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Appearance. When on, the window's title bar shows the full path of the open show file instead of just its name.
settings.general.showFullDatabasePath.de: Help text under the 'Show full file path' switch. The title bar is the top bar of the app window.
settings.input: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for choosing the tablet layout (fingers and pen) or the desktop layout (mouse and trackpad). Keep it short: it sits in a narrow sidebar.
settings.input.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Touch & Input' section title in Settings. 'Tablet' and 'desktop' name the two layouts; use the same words as the options 'Tablet' and 'Desktop'.
settings.input.interface: Label of the layout setting in Settings > Touch & Input. The choices beside it are 'Automatic', 'Tablet' and 'Desktop'.
settings.input.interface.auto: Choice (pill button with a magic wand icon) in Settings > Touch & Input: pick the layout automatically. Means 'decide for me', not a task running by itself.
settings.input.interface.description: Help text under the layout setting. Refers to the choices by name: 'Automatic' and 'Tablet' must match the choice labels exactly. 'Touch-screen laptop' is a laptop with a touch screen.
settings.input.interface.mouse: Choice (pill button with a cursor icon) in Settings > Touch & Input: the desktop layout, made for mouse and trackpad.
settings.input.interface.touch: Choice (pill button with a hand icon) in Settings > Touch & Input: the tablet layout, made for fingers and pen.
settings.mouse: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for how the mouse and trackpad zoom and pan the field. Keep it short: it sits in a narrow sidebar.
settings.mouse.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Mouse & Trackpad' section title in Settings. 'The field' is the on-screen drill field where marchers are shown.
settings.mouse.multiplier: Value shown next to a sensitivity slider in the Mouse settings (zoom sensitivity, trackpad pan sensitivity): how many times the normal speed it is. {value} is a number with one decimal, already formatted, for example 1.5. The "x" means "times"; use your language's usual way to write a multiplier.
settings.mouse.panSensitivity: Not shown on screen. Only matched against what the user types in the Settings search box, so searching 'pan' finds the Mouse & Trackpad section. Pan means sliding the field view; sensitivity is how far it moves for a given mouse or finger movement.
settings.mouse.trackpadMode: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Mouse & Trackpad. Trackpad mode changes how scrolling and pinching move and zoom the field, to suit a laptop trackpad.
settings.mouse.trackpadPanSensitivity: Label of a slider in Settings > Mouse & Trackpad, shown only when trackpad mode is on: how fast the field slides (pans) when scrolling with the trackpad. Also the slider's screen-reader label.
settings.mouse.zoomSensitivity: Label of a slider in Settings > Mouse & Trackpad: how much the field zooms for each scroll or pinch. Also the slider's screen-reader label.
settings.noResults: Message in the Settings sidebar when the search matches no setting.
settings.privacy: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) about what usage data OpenMarch shares. Not in the web editor.
settings.privacy.analytics: Heading of the collapsible panel in Settings > Privacy about analytics. Also matched by the Settings search.
settings.privacy.analytics.description: Explanation inside the analytics panel in Settings > Privacy. `…` wraps the words that link to the privacy policy web page: keep the tags and translate only the words between them.
settings.privacy.analytics.description.o: Friendly paragraph in Settings > Privacy asking users to keep analytics on, while saying they may opt out. OpenMarch is free software built by volunteers; Discord and Facebook are where users report bugs. ':)' is a smiley; keep it.
settings.privacy.analytics.disabled: Red message at the bottom of Settings > Privacy (and a preview in the analytics consent dialog) shown when analytics is off. `…` wraps the words that link to the feedback page: keep the tags and translate only the words between them.
settings.privacy.analytics.enabled: Green message at the bottom of Settings > Privacy (and a preview in the analytics consent dialog) shown when analytics is on. A thank-you.
settings.privacy.analytics.toggle: Label of the on/off switch in Settings > Privacy that turns usage analytics on or off. Also matched by the Settings search.
settings.privacy.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Privacy' section title in Settings.
settings.repairDotsFile: Label of the button in Settings > Database that opens the repair confirmation. DOTS is the OpenMarch show file format (.dots); do not translate it.
settings.repairDotsFile.cancel: Cancel button in the 'Repair DOTS file' confirmation dialog. Closes the dialog without repairing.
settings.repairDotsFile.confirm: Confirm button in the 'Repair DOTS file' dialog. Starts the repair. Verb, short.
settings.repairDotsFile.description: Body of the 'Repair DOTS file' confirmation dialog. The repair copies the show into a new file. '- FIXED' is a literal suffix added to the new file's name by the app; keep it as written. History is the undo/redo list.
settings.repairDotsFile.error: Error shown in the repair dialog and as an error toast when repairing failed. {error} is the technical error message, e.g. 'Permission denied'; do not translate it.
settings.repairDotsFile.noFileOpen: Reason shown in the error message of "Repair DOTS file" in Settings when no show file is open to repair. It is placed into the text "settings.repairDotsFile.error" as {error}. The database file is the open show's .dots file.
settings.repairDotsFile.reopenFailed: Error detail shown after repairing a show file, when the repaired copy was written but then failed to open. {path} is where the repaired file was saved; {status} is a numeric error code from the app.
settings.repairDotsFile.repairing: Text the confirm button shows while the repair runs. Keep the trailing '...'.
settings.repairDotsFile.success: Success toast after the repair finished. The app then reloads with the repaired copy, hence 'Reloading...'.
settings.repairDotsFile.title: Title of the repair confirmation dialog, and the label of the row in Settings > Database that holds the repair button. Also matched by the Settings search. DOTS is the OpenMarch show file format (.dots); do not translate it.
settings.repairDotsFile.unknownError: Reason shown in the error message of "Repair DOTS file" in Settings when the repair failed for a reason the app can't describe. It is placed into the text "settings.repairDotsFile.error" as {error}.
settings.search: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the search box at the top of the Settings sidebar. Typing filters sections by the settings they contain.
settings.shortcuts: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) where users view and change keyboard shortcuts.
settings.shortcuts.add: Screen-reader label of the small '+' button on a shortcut row that adds another key for that action. {action} is the action's name, e.g. 'Undo'.
settings.shortcuts.cancel: Cancel button in the conflict prompt on a shortcut row (shown when the pressed key is already used by another action). Keeps the existing shortcuts unchanged.
settings.shortcuts.category.alignment: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that line marchers up with each other (align, distribute).
settings.shortcuts.category.batchEdit: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that change many marchers or pages at once.
settings.shortcuts.category.cursor: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that switch the cursor mode (the tool used to click and drag on the field).
settings.shortcuts.category.edit: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for editing actions such as Undo, Redo, Copy and Paste. Not the verb 'to edit' as a button.
settings.shortcuts.category.file: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions on the show file: New, Open, Save, Export.
settings.shortcuts.category.movement: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that move selected marchers on the field (for example nudging them).
settings.shortcuts.category.navigation: Group name in the command palette for actions that move between pages and beats. In Settings > Keyboard shortcuts these are listed under 'Timeline'.
settings.shortcuts.category.playback: Group name in the command palette for actions that play, pause and stop the show. In Settings > Keyboard shortcuts these are listed under 'Timeline'.
settings.shortcuts.category.select: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that select marchers (select all, deselect).
settings.shortcuts.category.shape: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions about shapes (placing marchers in a line, box or curve).
settings.shortcuts.category.timeline: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts for timeline, navigation and playback actions together, and group name in the command palette for timeline actions. The timeline is the strip showing pages, moves and the music.
settings.shortcuts.category.ui: Group heading in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and group name in the command palette, for actions that change what the app shows (panels, zoom, view options).
settings.shortcuts.clearSearch: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the small 'x' button that empties a search box (shortcuts search and Settings sidebar search).
settings.shortcuts.conflictWith: Warning under a row in the Keyboard shortcuts settings when the shortcut just recorded already belongs to other actions. <keys></keys> is replaced by that shortcut drawn as keycaps (for example Ctrl + Z); keep the tag. {actions} is the list of the other actions' names, already joined with commas and "and" in your language. Buttons "Reassign" and "Cancel" follow.
settings.shortcuts.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Keyboard shortcuts' section title in Settings. 'Action' means any command in the app, such as Undo or Play.
settings.shortcuts.noResults: Message in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts when the search finds no shortcut.
settings.shortcuts.reassign: Button in the conflict prompt on a shortcut row. The pressed key already belongs to another action; this moves it to the current one. Verb, short.
settings.shortcuts.recordingHint: Shown in a row of the Keyboard shortcuts settings while it waits for the user to press the new shortcut. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key drawn as a keycap; keep the tag.
settings.shortcuts.remove: Screen-reader label of the small 'x' button next to a key on a shortcut row that removes that key. {binding} is the key combination as written on the keyboard, e.g. 'Ctrl+Z'.
settings.shortcuts.reset: Screen-reader label of the button that puts an action's shortcuts back to their original keys. {action} is the action's name, e.g. 'Undo'.
settings.shortcuts.resetAll: Button at the top of Settings > Keyboard shortcuts that restores every action's original keys. Shown only when something has been changed.
settings.shortcuts.search: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the search box in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts. Filters by action name or key.
settings.timeline: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for the timeline: Basic or Expert editor mode and the waveform style. The timeline is the strip showing pages, moves and the music.
settings.timeline.description: One-line subtitle under the 'Timeline' section title in Settings.
settings.timeline.waveformStyle: Label of a choice in Settings > Timeline: how the music's waveform (a picture of its loudness over time) is drawn on the timeline. Choices: Simplified, Precise, Hidden.
settings.timeline.waveformStyle.hidden: Waveform style choice (card with a small preview) in Settings > Timeline: don't draw a waveform. Adjective, short.
settings.timeline.waveformStyle.hidden.d: Help text shown under the waveform setting when 'Hidden' is chosen. The timeline is the strip showing pages, moves and the music.
settings.timeline.waveformStyle.precise: Waveform style choice (card with a small preview) in Settings > Timeline: an exact, beat-aligned waveform. Adjective, short.
Help text shown under the waveform setting when 'Precise' is chosen. Beats are the music's pulses; decibels measure loudness.
settings.timeline.waveformStyle.simplifi: Waveform style choice (card with a small preview) in Settings > Timeline: a smoother, rounded waveform. Adjective, short.
Help text shown under the waveform setting when 'Simplified' is chosen. Compares the look to a music player's waveform.
settings.title: Name of the app's Settings. Used as the Settings window's title (the operating system's title bar and window list), the heading of the Settings sheet in the web version, and the screen-reader name of the list of Settings sections.
settings.tolgeeApiKeyPlaceholder: Placeholder and screen-reader label of a text box in Settings > Developer Settings where a translator pastes their Tolgee API key. Tolgee is the translation tool OpenMarch uses; do not translate the name.
settings.tolgeeDevToolsToggle: Label of an on/off switch in Settings > Developer Settings. When on, translators can click text in the app to edit its translation in Tolgee, the translation tool OpenMarch uses; do not translate 'Tolgee'. Also matched by the Settings search.
settings.utilityUpdateFailed: Error toast shown when saving the show's internal timing settings (the length of the last page in counts and the default beat length) fails.
settings.view3d: Name of a Settings section (sidebar entry and page title) for how the 3D View draws on this computer. Must match the name 'the 3D View' is given elsewhere in the app.
settings.view3d.controls: Label of a choice in Settings > 3D View and in the 3D View's View settings panel: what dragging and scrolling do to the 3D camera. Choices: Orbit, Map, Trackpad.
settings.view3d.controls.input.drag: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names the input: dragging with the main (left) mouse button. Shown in muted text after the icon, before what the gesture does. Keep it short.
settings.view3d.controls.input.pinch: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names the input: a two-finger pinch on a trackpad. Shown in muted text after the icon, before what the gesture does. Keep it short.
settings.view3d.controls.input.rightDrag: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names the input: dragging with the right mouse button. Shown in muted text after the icon, before what the gesture does. Keep it short.
settings.view3d.controls.input.scroll: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names the input: turning a mouse's scroll wheel. Shown in muted text after the icon, before what the gesture does. Keep it short.
settings.view3d.controls.input.swipe: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names the input: sliding two fingers on a trackpad. Shown in muted text after the icon, before what the gesture does. Keep it short.
settings.view3d.controls.move.orbit: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names what the gesture does: circling the camera around a spot. Short noun or verb, one word if possible.
settings.view3d.controls.move.pan: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names what the gesture does: sliding the view across the field. Short noun or verb, one word if possible.
settings.view3d.controls.move.zoom: In the Controls choice of Settings > 3D View and the 3D View's View settings, each choice lists its gestures as an icon followed by what it does; this names what the gesture does: moving the camera closer or farther. Short noun or verb, one word if possible.
settings.view3d.controls.orbit: Choice (pill button) for the 3D View controls: dragging circles the camera around a spot, as in most 3D apps. Short name.
settings.view3d.controls.orbit.descripti: Help text shown under the Controls setting when 'Orbit' is chosen. Orbit means circling the camera around a spot; moving across the field means panning.
settings.view3d.controls.map: Choice (pill button) for the 3D View controls: dragging moves across the field, like dragging a map. Short name.
settings.view3d.controls.map.description: Help text shown under the Controls setting when 'Map' is chosen. Orbit means circling the camera around a spot. A modifier key is Ctrl, Option, Alt or Shift.
settings.view3d.controls.trackpad: Choice (pill button) for the 3D View controls: suited to a laptop trackpad, where two-finger scrolling turns the view. Short name.
settings.view3d.controls.trackpad.descri: Help text shown under the Controls setting when 'Trackpad' is chosen. Orbit means circling the camera around a spot; a pinch is the two-finger trackpad gesture.
settings.view3d.quality: Label of a choice in Settings > 3D View (and in the 3D View's View settings panel in the web editor): how detailed the 3D View is drawn. Choices: Automatic, High, Low.
settings.view3d.quality.auto: Choice (pill button) for 3D View quality: the app picks and may lower quality by itself. Short.
settings.view3d.quality.auto.description: Help text shown under the quality setting when 'Automatic' is chosen. 'High' and 'Low' are the names of the other two quality choices and must match them.
settings.view3d.quality.high: Choice (pill button) for 3D View quality: most detailed, with shadows and a full crowd. Short adjective.
settings.view3d.quality.high.description: Help text shown under the quality setting when 'High' is chosen. 'Low' is the name of the other quality choice and must match it. The crowd is the audience in the stands.
settings.view3d.quality.low: Choice (pill button) for 3D View quality: least detailed, no shadows. Short adjective.
settings.view3d.quality.low.description: Help text shown under the quality setting when 'Low' is chosen. The crowd is the audience in the stands.
settings.view3d.resolution: Label of a choice in Settings > 3D View (and in the 3D View's View settings panel in the web editor): how sharp the 3D picture is drawn. Choices: Sharp, Balanced, Fast.
settings.view3d.resolution.balanced: Choice (pill button) for 3D View resolution: a compromise between sharp and fast. Short adjective.
settings.view3d.resolution.balanced.desc: Help text shown under the resolution setting when 'Balanced' is chosen. The graphics card is the computer's graphics hardware.
settings.view3d.resolution.fast: Choice (pill button) for 3D View resolution: lowest detail, least work for the computer. Short adjective.
settings.view3d.resolution.fast.descript: Help text shown under the resolution setting when 'Fast' is chosen.
settings.view3d.resolution.sharp: Choice (pill button) for 3D View resolution: full detail. Short adjective.
settings.view3d.resolution.sharp.descrip: Help text shown under the resolution setting when 'Sharp' is chosen. High-resolution screens are very fine displays, such as Retina screens.
settings.view3d.summary: One-line subtitle under the '3D View' section title in Settings. 'Not saved in the show' means these choices belong to this computer, not to the show file.
shapes.box.left.closeUp: Action button on a toast. It appears after some marchers moved away from a shape, leaving empty spots in it. Pressing it lays the marchers that stayed out again so the shape has no empty spots (by the least walking). Short verb phrase.
shapes.box.left.hint: Second line of the toast that says marchers left a box. Their spots are the empty places the marchers left in the box; the Undo button of the toast restores the marchers' old positions.
shapes.box.left.many: Toast shown when several marchers that belonged to a box (a block of marchers placed with the shape tool) were moved away from it. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is how many marchers left, 2 or more; translate the forms your language needs (you may add a word for marchers). Followed by the buttons Close up and Re-split.
shapes.box.left.one: Toast shown when one marcher that belonged to a box (a block of marchers placed with the shape tool) was moved away from it. {name} is the marcher's name or drill number (for example "B12"). Followed by the buttons Close up and Re-split.
shapes.box.left.resplit: Action button on a toast shown after marchers left a box. Pressing it spreads the remaining marchers over the whole box again, inside the edges the box had, so its spots are all filled and the marchers are spaced evenly. Short.
shapes.box.params.fewerAcross: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the minus button beside a box's size in the shape editor. Removes one file (column) across the box's width. "Across" means side to side.
shapes.box.params.moreAcross: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the plus button beside a box's size in the shape editor. Adds one file (column) across the box's width. "Across" means side to side.
shapes.box.params.short: Small note beside a box's size in the shape editor when its Short back layout leaves the back rank incomplete. {count} is how many marchers short that rank is (for example "1 short"). Keep it very short.
shapes.box.params.size: Name of the box's size setting, shown in the command bar prompt and as the tooltip of the "6 × 2" number. Across means side to side (number of files), deep means front to back (number of ranks); the "×" reads "by".
shapes.box.params.spacingAcross: Name of the box's side-to-side spacing, shown as the tooltip and label of the number beside the ↔ symbol in the shape editor and in the command bar. The spacing is the distance between neighboring marchers, measured in steps.
shapes.box.params.spacingDeep: Name of the box's front-to-back spacing, shown as the tooltip and label of the number beside the ↕ symbol in the shape editor and in the command bar. The spacing is the distance between neighboring marchers, measured in steps.
shapes.command.fill: Prompt in the command bar while placing a shape: asks which way to fill the shape. {modes} is the list of choices, already joined with commas, for example "Grid, Outline, Spread". The user types the first letters of one.
shapes.command.layout: Prompt in the command bar while placing a box: asks which layout to use. {layouts} is the list of choices, already joined with commas, for example "Full, Stagger, Rounded, Short back, Notched". The user types the first letters of one.
shapes.distribute.blockName: A box shape's layout in the command bar when it isn't one of the picker's versions. {layout} is the layout's name (Full, Stagger, Rounded, Short back or Notched); {across} and {deep} are how many marchers wide and deep the block is.
shapes.distribute.hint.add: Hint in the shape editor's Layout menu, for a layout that cannot make the current number of marchers; it also ends the greyed-out layout's tooltip after a colon. Says how many marchers must be added to make it. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is a whole number, for example "add 2"; translate the forms your language needs (you may add a word for marchers). Lowercase in English, short.
shapes.distribute.hint.addOrRemove: Hint in the shape editor's Layout menu, for a layout that cannot make the current number of marchers; it also ends the greyed-out layout's tooltip after a colon. Says the two ways to make it: add {more} marchers, or remove {fewer} marchers (both whole numbers, shown as #), for example "add 1 / remove 2". The slash means 'or'. Translate the plural forms your language needs. Lowercase in English, short.
shapes.distribute.hint.remove: Hint in the shape editor's Layout menu, for a layout that cannot make the current number of marchers; it also ends the greyed-out layout's tooltip after a colon. Says how many marchers must be removed to make it. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is a whole number, for example "remove 1"; translate the forms your language needs. Lowercase in English, short.
shapes.distribute.layout.full: Name of a layout of a box, in the Layout menu of the shape editor and in the command bar. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box. Full: every rank is complete, a plain rectangle.
shapes.distribute.layout.notched: Name of a layout of a box, in the Layout menu of the shape editor and in the command bar. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box. Notched: the middle rank is shorter, leaving a notch in the sides.
shapes.distribute.layout.rounded: Name of a layout of a box, in the Layout menu of the shape editor and in the command bar. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box. Rounded: the first and last rank are shorter, so the corners look rounded.
shapes.distribute.layout.shortBack: Name of a layout of a box, in the Layout menu of the shape editor and in the command bar. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box. Short back: the back rank has fewer marchers than the others.
shapes.distribute.layout.stagger: Name of a layout of a box, in the Layout menu of the shape editor and in the command bar. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box. Stagger: every other rank has one marcher fewer and sits half an interval over, in a brick pattern.
shapes.distribute.version.frontToBack: Tooltip of a layout version in the shape editor's Layout menu. {counts} is the number of marchers in each line joined with slashes, for example "5 / 4 / 5". Here the counts go front to back (a line is a rank, side to side).
shapes.distribute.version.leftToRight: Tooltip of a layout version in the shape editor's Layout menu. {counts} is the number of marchers in each line joined with slashes, for example "5 / 4 / 5". Here the counts go left to right (a line is a file, front to back).
shapes.distribute.version.short: Name of a Short back layout version in the shape editor's Layout menu. {across} and {deep} are the box's size in files and ranks, {short} is how many marchers the back rank is short (for example "6 × 4, 1 short").
shapes.distribute.version.size: Label of a layout version (a thumbnail) in the shape editor's Layout menu: its size, {across} marchers side to side by {deep} front to back, for example "5 × 4". Keep the × sign unless your language writes sizes differently.
shapes.distribute.version.staggered: Name of a Rounded or Notched layout version in the Layout menu where the shorter line is half an interval in, between the files. {across} and {deep} are whole numbers (for example "5 × 3 staggered").
shapes.distribute.version.straight: Name of a Rounded or Notched layout version in the Layout menu where the shorter line stays lined up with the others. {across} and {deep} are whole numbers (for example "5 × 3 straight").
shapes.distribute.versionName: Full name of a box layout version, used as its button's label in the shape layout picker and in the command bar. {layout} is the layout's name (Full, Stagger, Rounded, Short back or Notched); {version} is the version's size, such as '6 × 4, 1 short' or '5 × 5 staggered'.
shapes.edit.aboutValue: Screen-reader label of a number in the shape editor that is not exactly on a half step. {label} is the number's name (for example "Side-to-side spacing, in steps"), {value} the displayed value (for example "3¾"). "About" means approximately.
shapes.edit.away.dismiss: Screen-reader label of the X button on the notice that a shape is still open at another moment. Discards the open shape; undo brings it back.
shapes.edit.away.dismissTip: Tooltip of the X button on the notice that a shape is still open at another moment. Discards the shape; the user can undo to get it back.
shapes.edit.away.goBack: Button on the notice at the top of the field shown when the user has moved the playhead away from a shape that is still open (not yet placed). Moves the playhead back to the moment the shape was drawn.
shapes.edit.away.text: Notice at the top of the field shown when the playhead has moved away from a shape that is still open (not yet placed). {moment} is the moment the shape was drawn at: the word "home" (the start of the show) or "count 12".
shapes.edit.closeUp.label: Label of the Close up button in the shape editor, shown with a placed shape that has empty spots. Pressing it lays the remaining marchers out again so the shape has no empty spots. Short verb phrase; the label is hidden on small bars.
shapes.edit.closeUp.title: Tooltip of the Close up button in the shape editor. {count} is the number of empty spots in the shape; the marchers that are left fill them.
shapes.edit.drawHintFor: Hint at the top of the field after choosing a shape tool and before drawing. {shape} selects the kind of shape: block (a box, a rectangular block of marchers), circle, line (a straight line of marchers), curve (a curved line), arc (part of a circle), or other (any other shape); translate each variant as the word fits this sentence, and keep the select structure and the words before the braces. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key drawn as a keycap ("Esc"); pressing it cancels. Keep the tag. The dot separates the two parts of the hint.
shapes.edit.drawPointsHintFor: Hint shown over the field while a line-like shape tool is armed in the Shapes tab. The user can drag to draw the shape, or click one point after another to place its corners or bend points. {shape} picks the shape's name: line (a straight line of marchers), curve (a curved line), arc (part of a circle); any other value reads "shape". <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key shown as a keycap; keep the tag.
shapes.edit.drawnOn: Small note in the shape editor of a placed shape that was placed at an earlier page than the playhead is now. {page} is that page's name, for example "Page 3". Reads "from Page 3".
shapes.edit.edge.label: Label of the Edge toggle in the shape editor, shown for a shape filled by Spread. When on, some marchers stand evenly along the outline of the shape and the rest spread inside. Noun.
shapes.edit.edge.tip: Tooltip of the Edge toggle in the shape editor when on or off. {edge} is the number of marchers standing on the outline, {inside} the number spread inside; both whole numbers (for example "Edge: 12 evenly along the outline, 8 spread inside").
shapes.edit.edge.tipEdgeOnly: Tooltip of the Edge toggle in the shape editor when there are too few marchers to put any inside the shape. {edge} is the total number of marchers, all of them standing on the outline.
shapes.edit.empty: Note beside a placed shape's size in the shape editor. {count} is how many spots in the shape are empty because marchers moved away (for example "2 empty"). Keep it very short.
shapes.edit.evenOut.already: Tooltip of the disabled Even out button in the shape editor. The marchers are already spread as evenly as the shape's size and shape allow, so pressing it would change nothing.
shapes.edit.evenOut.label: Label of the Even out button in the shape editor, which appears beside its icon when it can do something. Verb phrase.
shapes.edit.evenOut.tip: Tooltip of the Even out button in the shape editor. Spreads the marchers as evenly as the box allows.
shapes.edit.expand: Tooltip of the plus button in the shape editor that makes a shape larger. It grows the spacings by a half step each time while keeping the shape's proportions.
shapes.edit.flipAcross: Tooltip of the flip button in the shape editor. Mirrors the shape side to side (left becomes right) around its pivot.
shapes.edit.flipDeep: Tooltip of the flip button in the shape editor. Mirrors the shape front to back around its pivot.
shapes.edit.gap.menuLabel: Label of the Leftover menu button in the shape editor, used for a shape filled by Outline when the number of marchers leaves one spot over: names the side where that odd spot goes, for example "Leftover: Back". 'Leftover' is a noun. {side} selects the side, as the audience sees the field: back (farthest from the audience), front (nearest), left or other (right); translate each variant and keep the select structure and the words back, front, left and other before the braces.
shapes.edit.gap.side.back: Name of a side of a box, shown in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. The Leftover menu says where the odd spot of an outline goes. As the field is seen by the audience. Back: the edge farthest from the audience.
shapes.edit.gap.side.front: Name of a side of a box, shown in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. The Leftover menu says where the odd spot of an outline goes. As the field is seen by the audience. Front: the edge nearest the audience.
shapes.edit.gap.side.left: Name of a side of a box, shown in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. The Leftover menu says where the odd spot of an outline goes. As the field is seen by the audience. Left side.
shapes.edit.gap.side.right: Name of a side of a box, shown in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. The Leftover menu says where the odd spot of an outline goes. As the field is seen by the audience. Right side.
shapes.edit.gap.sideLabel: Label of the choice of side in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. Tells which side of the outline has the odd spot. Used both as a visible label and as a screen-reader label. Short.
shapes.edit.gap.spacing: A distance in steps, shown in the Leftover menu's note about the odd side. Plural message: {count} is the distance as a number (it can have a fraction, such as 3.75) and picks the plural form; it is not shown. {value} is the text shown for that number, with a leading "≈" when it is approximate (for example "4 steps" or "≈3¾ steps"). A step is one drill step.
shapes.edit.gap.spacingHint: Tooltip in the Leftover menu of the shape editor, about the outline's side that holds the odd spot. {side} selects the side, as the audience sees the field: back (farthest from the audience), front (nearest), left or other (right); translate each variant and keep the select structure and the words back, front, left and other before the braces. {spacing} is a distance with its unit (for example "4 steps"). That side has one marcher fewer, so its marchers spread wider than the other sides.
shapes.edit.gap.style.gap: Choice in the Leftover menu of the shape editor: the odd spot stays empty, leaving a visible gap in the side. Short.
shapes.edit.gap.style.spread: Choice in the Leftover menu of the shape editor: the marchers on that side are spread evenly with no gap. Short.
shapes.edit.gap.styleLabel: Label of the choice between leaving a gap and spreading evenly in the Leftover menu of the shape editor. "That side" refers to the side chosen above.
shapes.edit.gap.tip: Tooltip of the Leftover menu button in the shape editor: where an outline's odd spot goes and what that side does. {side} selects the side, as the audience sees the field: back (farthest from the audience), front (nearest), left or other (right); translate each variant and keep the select structure and the words back, front, left and other before the braces. {style} selects what the side does: gap (the odd spot stays empty, leaving a gap) or other (its marchers spread evenly); translate both and keep the select structure. Reads like "Leftover: Back, leaves a gap".
shapes.edit.gap.tipGap: Tip at the bottom of the Leftover menu of the shape editor, for a newly drawn shape. The user can click a marcher on the outline of the shape on the field to move the gap there. A corner cannot hold the gap.
shapes.edit.gap.tipSpread: Tip at the bottom of the Leftover menu of the shape editor, for a newly drawn shape. The user can click a marcher on another side on the field (not a corner) to spread that side instead.
shapes.edit.hideMarchers.hide: Tooltip of the eye button in the shape editor bar that hides the edited shape's own marchers (also hold or tap H). Text: "Hide the marchers".
shapes.edit.hideMarchers.show: Tooltip of the eye button in the shape editor bar that hides the edited shape's own marchers (also hold or tap H). Text: "Show the marchers".
shapes.edit.layout.aria: Screen-reader label of the Layout menu button in the shape editor. {label} is the current layout's name, for example "Short back".
shapes.edit.layout.cantMake: Tooltip of a layout in the shape editor's Layout menu that cannot make the current number of marchers at all. {label} is the layout's name (for example "Stagger"), {count} the number of marchers.
shapes.edit.layout.label: Tooltip of the Layout menu button in the shape editor. A layout is a pattern for how the marchers sit in a box. Noun.
shapes.edit.layout.needs: Tooltip of a greyed-out layout in the shape editor's Layout menu. {label} is the layout's name, {count} the number of marchers it needs instead; {hint} says how to get there, for example "add 2" or "remove 1".
shapes.edit.layout.needsEither: Tooltip of a greyed-out layout in the shape editor's Layout menu. {label} is the layout's name, {a} and {b} are the two numbers of marchers it could use instead; {hint} says how to get there, for example "add 1 / remove 2".
shapes.edit.layout.showVersions: Screen-reader label of the arrow beside a layout in the shape editor's Layout menu. Opens the list of that layout's versions (different sizes that make the same count). {label} is the layout's name.
shapes.edit.mode.current: Screen-reader label of the Fill menu button in the shape editor, which picks how the marchers are placed inside the shape. Starts with the menu's name (same as shapes.edit.mode.label), then the current choice: {mode} selects files (Grid: rows and columns), outline (Outline: only along the edge) or other (Spread: scattered evenly); use the same words as the menu's choices (shapes.edit.mode.files, .outline, .spread). Keep the select structure and the words files, outline and other before the braces.
shapes.edit.mode.files: Name of a way to fill a shape, in the Fill menu of the shape editor: the marchers sit in a regular grid of files and ranks (a file runs front to back, a rank side to side). Noun, short.
shapes.edit.mode.label: Tooltip and label of the Fill menu in the shape editor, which picks how the marchers are placed inside the shape (Grid, Outline or Spread). Noun or verb, short.
shapes.edit.mode.outline: Name of a way to fill a shape, in the Fill menu of the shape editor: the marchers stand around the edge of the shape and the middle stays empty.
shapes.edit.mode.spread: Name of a way to fill a shape, in the Fill menu of the shape editor: the marchers are spread evenly over the whole shape, with no rows.
shapes.edit.order.keep: In the shape editor, the Who goes where menu: how marchers are assigned to the spots of a shape they move into. Text: "Keep order".
shapes.edit.order.label: In the shape editor, the Who goes where menu: how marchers are assigned to the spots of a shape they move into. Text: "Who goes where".
shapes.edit.order.nearest: In the shape editor, the Who goes where menu: how marchers are assigned to the spots of a shape they move into. Text: "Least travel".
shapes.edit.order.reverse: In the shape editor, the Who goes where menu: how marchers are assigned to the spots of a shape they move into. Text: "Reverse order".
shapes.edit.pathways.hide: Tooltip of the pressed Pathways button in the shape editor. Hides the lines that show how each marcher walks from where they stand at the start flag to the shape. The start flag marks the beginning of the move being edited.
shapes.edit.pathways.show: Tooltip of the Pathways button in the shape editor. Shows the lines that show how each marcher walks from where they stand at the start flag to the shape. The start flag marks the beginning of the move being edited.
shapes.edit.pivot.aria: Screen-reader label of a pivot choice, and of the pivot menu button. The pivot is the point a shape turns, flips and scales around. {pivot} is a place name such as "back left" or "center".
shapes.edit.pivot.custom: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the pivot menu button when the pivot has been dragged to a free spot on the field rather than one of the nine named places. The pivot is the point a shape turns and flips around.
shapes.edit.pivot.label: Screen-reader label of the grid of nine pivot choices, and tooltip of the pivot menu. The pivot is the point (a corner, an edge's middle or the center) that a shape turns, flips and scales around. Noun.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.c: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The center of the shape.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.e: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The middle of the right edge.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.n: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The middle of the back edge (the edge farthest from the audience).
shapes.edit.pivot.names.ne: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The back right corner.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.nw: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The back left corner.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.s: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The middle of the front edge (the edge nearest the audience).
shapes.edit.pivot.names.se: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The front right corner.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.sw: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The front left corner.
shapes.edit.pivot.names.w: Name of a pivot place, used inside "Turn and flip around the …" and "Pivot: …". The pivot is a point on the shape. It is a lowercase noun phrase that must fit in those sentences. The middle of the left edge.
shapes.edit.pivot.tip: Tooltip of a cell in the pivot grid of the shape editor. {pivot} is a place name such as "back left" or "center" (lowercase). The shape will turn and flip around that point.
shapes.edit.place: Button label in the shape editor and the command bar. Puts the open shape on the field: the marchers are moved onto the shape's spots. Verb.
shapes.edit.quarterTurn: Tooltip of the turn button in the shape editor (a clockwise arrow). Adds a quarter turn to the shape each time it is pressed.
shapes.edit.guides.label: Menu button in the floating shape editor of an Arc shape. It opens a list of construction guides drawn on the field while the shape is edited, each checked on or off.
shapes.edit.guides.circle: Checkable item in the shape editor's Guides menu: show the whole circle (or oval) the arc of marchers is part of.
shapes.edit.guides.angles: Checkable item in the shape editor's Guides menu: show straight lines from the center of the arc's circle out through its two ends and beyond, so the angle the arc turns is easy to see.
shapes.edit.ratioLock.sizesLocked: Tooltip of the pressed chain-link button after an Arc shape's width × height in the shape editor. The two sizes are locked so changing one changes the other in the same proportion; pressing it unlocks them.
shapes.edit.ratioLock.sizesUnlocked: Tooltip of the chain-link button after an Arc shape's width × height in the shape editor. Pressing it locks the two sizes together so changing one changes the other in the same proportion.
shapes.edit.ratioLock.locked: Tooltip of the pressed chain-link button in the shape editor, shown beside the two spacings of a box. They are locked so that changing one changes the other in the same proportion. Pressing it unlocks them.
shapes.edit.ratioLock.unlocked: Tooltip of the chain-link button in the shape editor, shown beside the two spacings (side to side, front to back) of a box. Pressing it locks them together so that changing one changes the other in the same proportion.
shapes.edit.recalculate.already: Tooltip of the disabled Recalculate button in the shape editor. Who goes where means which marcher takes which spot of the shape. They are already assigned so that the total walking distance is the smallest possible, so recalculating would change nothing.
shapes.edit.recalculate.alreadyInOrder: Tooltip of the Recalculate button in the shape editor, which works out again who goes where. Text: "Who goes where is already in order along the line".
shapes.edit.recalculate.closeUpFirst: Tooltip of the disabled Recalculate button in the shape editor when the shape has empty spots. Who goes where means which marcher takes which spot. The user should close up the empty spots first (with Close up) before recalculating.
shapes.edit.recalculate.label: Label of the Recalculate button in the shape editor, shown next to its icon only when it can do something. Reassigns which marcher goes to which spot so the walking distance is smallest. Verb.
shapes.edit.recalculate.title: Tooltip of the Recalculate button in the shape editor. Who goes where means which marcher takes which spot of the shape. Pressing it reassigns them so the total travel is the least possible.
shapes.edit.recalculate.titleInOrder: Tooltip of the Recalculate button in the shape editor, which works out again who goes where. Text: "Recalculate who goes where, in order along the line".
shapes.edit.removePointHint: Hint shown in the shape editor while drawing a Line point by point. Text: "Right-click or <keys></keys> removes the last point · Double-click to finish · <esc></esc> to cancel". <keys></keys> is replaced by the remove-point key shortcut and <esc></esc> by the Escape key, each shown as a keycap.
shapes.edit.removePointHintClick: Hint shown in the shape editor while drawing a Line point by point. Text: "Right-click removes the last point · Double-click to finish · <esc></esc> to cancel". <esc></esc> is replaced by the Escape key shown as a keycap.
shapes.edit.reshuffle.label: Label of the Reshuffle button in the shape editor, shown for a shape filled by Spread. Pressing it makes a new random, even layout of the same marchers in the same shape. Verb.
shapes.edit.reshuffle.title: Tooltip of the Reshuffle button in the shape editor, shown for a shape filled by Spread. A new layout means a new random arrangement of the marchers in the same shape.
shapes.edit.scaleHint: Extra line in the tooltip of the shrink and expand buttons in the shape editor. Tells how they work: one click changes the size once, holding repeats, and dragging changes it continuously.
shapes.edit.scrubTip: Tooltip of a number in the shape editor. {label} is the number's name (for example "Turn, in degrees clockwise"). Clicking lets the user type a value; dragging sideways or up and down changes it.
shapes.edit.seed.copied: Tooltip text of the copy button in the Seed menu, shown after the seed has been copied to the clipboard. Very short confirmation.
shapes.edit.seed.copy: Tooltip of the copy button in the Seed menu of the Reshuffle control in the shape editor. Copies the seed number to the clipboard.
shapes.edit.seed.copyFailed: Tooltip text of the copy button in the Seed menu, shown when copying the seed to the clipboard failed. Very short.
shapes.edit.seed.count: Text beside the seed number in the Seed menu of the shape editor. {count} is the number of marchers in the shape. Reads "for 24 marchers".
shapes.edit.seed.hint: Help text in the Seed menu of the shape editor. A seed is a number that decides a random spread layout. The same seed with the same marcher count in the same shape always gives the same spread; the spacing only makes it bigger or smaller.
shapes.edit.seed.label: Label and screen-reader label of the number field in the shape editor's Seed menu. A seed is a number that decides a random-looking layout of a Spread: the same seed gives the same layout. Noun.
shapes.edit.shrink: Tooltip of the minus button in the shape editor that makes a shape smaller. It reduces the spacings by a half step each time while keeping the shape's proportions.
shapes.edit.shrinkFloor: Tooltip of the disabled shrink button in the shape editor. The shape cannot get smaller because no spacing may go under half a step (the closest two marchers may stand).
shapes.edit.snap.off: Tooltip of the pressed Snap button in the shape editor, when snapping is off. Snap makes drags land on the half-step grid and field lines. Pressing it turns snapping back on.
shapes.edit.snap.on: Tooltip of the Snap button in the shape editor, when snapping is on. Snap makes drags land on the half-step grid and field lines. Pressing it turns snapping off.
shapes.edit.snapLabel: Screen-reader label of a small "≈" button beside a number in the shape editor that is not on a half step. {label} is the number's name. Pressing it rounds the number to the nearest half step.
shapes.edit.snapTip: Tooltip of a small "≈" button beside a number in the shape editor that is not on a half step. Pressing it rounds the number to the nearest half step (half of a drill step).
shapes.edit.steps: Unit word after the spacings in the shape editor (for example "↔ 2 ↕ 2 steps"). A step is one drill step, the distance between marchers. Plural, lowercase.
shapes.edit.turn: Tooltip and label of the rotation number in the shape editor, which is measured in degrees clockwise (the ° unit is shown with the number). Typing or dragging it turns the shape.
shapes.edit.ungroup: Tooltip of the Ungroup button in the floating bar shown over a selected shape on the field. Clicking it turns the shape back into plain marchers who keep their spots.
shapes.field.stepLimit: The field's step size limit written as steps over five yards. {steps} is a number such as 8 or 6.7, so "8 to 5" means 8 steps for every 5 yards. It is inserted into a warning that marchers need steps longer than this limit.
shapes.frame.scale.apart: Readout of a shape's spacings. {spacings} holds the spacing symbols and values, for example "↔ 2 ↕ 2"; the full text reads "↔ 2 ↕ 2 apart" (steps apart between marchers).
shapes.frame.scale.size: Readout of a shape's overall size, in the shape editor's Transform section and by the pointer while dragging a handle. {sizes} holds the width and depth in steps joined with "×" (for example "10 × 4"), or a single number for a line. Plural message: {count} is the last number, which the word 'step' agrees with. Reads "10 × 4 steps".
shapes.groups.add: Inline interval chips in the Line shape's floating editor bar (a run of marchers at its own spacing). Text: "Add a group".
shapes.groups.addGroup: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Add group".
shapes.groups.all: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "All {count}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.at: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "at".
shapes.groups.count: Inline interval chips in the Line shape's floating editor bar (a run of marchers at its own spacing). Text: "Group {n} marchers". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them. {n} is the group's position in the list (1st, 2nd…), not a count.
