shapes.groups.countAt: One label drawn on the field for a whole interval group when its gaps are too small to label one by one, e.g. "4 at 2": {count} marchers at {interval} steps apart. Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.countDropped: Inline interval chips in the Line shape's floating editor bar (a run of marchers at its own spacing). Text: "Group {n} marchers: none left for it". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them. {n} is the group's position in the list (1st, 2nd…), not a count.
shapes.groups.countRest: Inline interval chips in the Line shape's floating editor bar (a run of marchers at its own spacing). Text: "Group {n}: the rest of the marchers. Type a count to fix it". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them. {n} is the group's position in the list (1st, 2nd…), not a count.
shapes.groups.first: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "First {count}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.grown: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Grew by {count} to take the marchers no group has". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.interval: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Group {n} spacing, in steps". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them. {n} is the group's position in the list (1st, 2nd…), not a count.
shapes.groups.last: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Last {count}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.list: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "All groups as a list: count * steps, + between groups".
shapes.groups.menuLabel: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Multiple intervals: {groups}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.menuName: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Interval groups".
shapes.groups.menuTip: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Groups of marchers at their own intervals".
shapes.groups.multiple: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Multiple intervals".
shapes.groups.next: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Next {count}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.groups.noMarchers: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "No marchers left".
shapes.groups.remove: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "Remove group {n}". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them. {n} is the group's position in the list (1st, 2nd…), not a count.
shapes.groups.restShort: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "rest".
shapes.groups.theRest: In the Line shape's floating editor, the Multiple intervals menu that lists the line's interval groups (runs of marchers at their own spacing). Text: "the rest,".
shapes.kinds.arc.hint.bend: Hover hint on an arc's middle handle on the field. Dragging it bends the arc more or less. Short.
shapes.kinds.arc.label: Name of the Arc shape kind: marchers in a curved line between two end points.
shapes.kinds.arc.validate.flat: Informational message about an arc shape. The arc has no bend, so it is the same as a straight line.
shapes.kinds.arc.validate.sameSpot: Error message about an arc shape. Both ends of the arc are at the same point, so there is no arc to make.
shapes.kinds.block.across: Label of a size field for a Box shape: its width, side to side, in steps. Short.
shapes.kinds.block.deep: Label of a size field for a Box shape: its depth, front to back, in steps. Short.
shapes.kinds.block.files: Label of a count field for a Box shape: how many files it has. A file is a line of marchers running front to back; the count is the number across the box. Plural noun.
shapes.kinds.block.hint.files: Hover hint on a Box's side handle on the field while its intervals are locked. Dragging it adds or removes files (lines of marchers running front to back). Plural noun.
shapes.kinds.block.hint.intervalAcross: Hover hint on a Box's side handle on the field. Dragging it changes the interval (the distance between marchers) side to side.
shapes.kinds.block.hint.intervalDeep: Hover hint on a Box's front or back handle on the field. Dragging it changes the interval (the distance between marchers) front to back.
shapes.kinds.block.hint.turn: Hover hint on a Box's rotation handle on the field. Dragging it turns the whole box. Verb, short.
shapes.kinds.block.keepIntervals.label: Label of a lock in the parameters of a Box shape. When locked, the interval (the distance between marchers) stays fixed while the box is resized. Verb phrase.
shapes.kinds.block.keepIntervals.locked: Help text for the Keep intervals lock when it is locked. Dragging a side then adds or removes files (lines of marchers running front to back); clicking the lock unlocks it so the intervals stretch instead.
shapes.kinds.block.keepIntervals.unlocke: Help text for the Keep intervals lock when it is unlocked. Dragging a side then stretches the intervals (the distance between marchers); clicking the lock locks it so files are added or removed instead.
shapes.kinds.block.label: Name of the Box shape kind: marchers in a block of ranks and files. Also used in shape names such as "Box 5 × 4" and in the toast "3 left the box" (lowercased there).
shapes.kinds.block.pattern: Heading of a group of settings of a Box shape: how its ranks (lines side to side) are arranged and where a short rank sits. Noun.
shapes.kinds.block.ranks.grid: Option for how a Box's ranks are arranged: every rank lines up exactly with the one behind it, in a square grid.
shapes.kinds.block.ranks.label: Label of the setting for how a Box's ranks (lines of marchers side to side) are arranged: in a grid or staggered. Plural noun.
shapes.kinds.block.ranks.staggered: Option for how a Box's ranks are arranged: every other rank is shifted by half an interval, so marchers sit between those behind them.
shapes.kinds.block.readout.interval: Label of a value in a Box shape's readout: the interval, the distance between neighboring marchers. The value beside it reads like "2 × 2 steps". Noun.
shapes.kinds.block.readout.intervalValue: Value of the Interval readout for a block shape (marchers in ranks and files) on the field: the spacing between marchers side to side ({across}) and front to back ({deep}), in marching steps. Both numbers have up to two decimals and are formatted for the app's language (keep the ", number" part of each argument).
shapes.kinds.block.readout.ranksFiles: Label of a value in a Box shape's readout: the number of ranks (lines side to side) times the number of files (lines front to back), for example "4 × 6". Keep the "×" order meaning.
shapes.kinds.block.readout.ranksFilesVal: Value next to the 'Ranks × files' readout of a box shape: {ranks} is the number of ranks (lines side to side) and {files} the number of files (lines front to back), for example "4 × 6". Keep the × sign unless your language writes sizes differently.
shapes.kinds.block.rotation: Label of the rotation angle setting of a Box shape, in degrees. Also the heading of its group. Noun.
shapes.kinds.block.shortRank.center: Option for where the short rank of a Box sits: in the center of the rank behind it.
shapes.kinds.block.shortRank.label: Label of the setting for where the last rank of a Box sits when it has fewer marchers than the others. A rank is a line of marchers side to side.
shapes.kinds.block.shortRank.left: Option for where the short rank of a Box sits: at the left end.
shapes.kinds.block.shortRank.right: Option for where the short rank of a Box sits: at the right end.
shapes.kinds.block.size: Heading of the group of size settings of a Box shape (files, width, depth). Noun.
shapes.kinds.block.validate.lastRankOne: Informational message about a Box shape. {files} is its number of files; the last rank (the line of marchers side to side) would have only one marcher.
shapes.kinds.block.validate.noFiles: Error message about a Box shape. A block is a rectangle of marchers; a file is a line of them running front to back. It needs at least one file.
shapes.kinds.circle.hint.radius: Hover hint on a Circle's handle on the field. Dragging it changes the radius, and it also marks where marcher 1 starts around the circle.
shapes.kinds.circle.label: Name of the Circle shape kind: marchers spaced around a circle.
shapes.kinds.circle.params.interval: Name of the Circle's spacing setting, shown as the tooltip and label of the number in the shape editor and in the command bar. It is the distance between neighboring marchers around the circle, in steps.
shapes.kinds.circle.readout.circumferenc: Label of a readout of a Circle shape: the length around the circle, measured in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.circle.validate.noRadius: Error message about a Circle shape. The radius is zero, so there is no circle.
shapes.kinds.circle.validate.overlap: Warning about a Circle shape. The spacings add up to the whole way around or more, so some marchers would stand on the same spot.
shapes.kinds.circle.validate.partFilled: Informational message about a Circle shape. {count} is the number of marchers, {run} is the length that they cover and {total} the circle's whole length, both in steps (for example "4 marchers at this interval fill 12 of the circle's 16 steps"). The size lock is a lock on the circle's radius; opening it lets the circle close up.
shapes.kinds.curve.hint.point: Hover hint on a Curve's point handle on the field. The point can be dragged, and double-clicking it removes it.
shapes.kinds.curve.label: Name of the Curve shape kind: marchers along a smooth line through several points.
shapes.kinds.curve.validate.points: Error message about a Curve shape. A curve goes through points, and it needs at least two that are not at the same place.
shapes.kinds.fill.edgeField: Label of a count field of a Filled shape: how many marchers stand on the shape's edge. 0 means the app picks the number. Keep "0 = auto".
shapes.kinds.fill.group: Heading of the group of settings of a Filled shape (a shape whose marchers are spread naturally over an area). Noun.
shapes.kinds.fill.hint.size: Hover hint on a Filled shape's corner handle on the field. Dragging it changes the shape's size. Noun.
shapes.kinds.fill.label: Name of the Filled shape kind: marchers spread naturally over an area, a box or circle.
shapes.kinds.fill.layout: Label of a number field of a Filled shape. It picks which spread to use (1, 2, 3 and so on); the same number always gives the same spread. Noun.
shapes.kinds.fill.readout.about: Label of a readout of a Filled shape. The value beside it tells about how far apart neighboring marchers are (for example "About 2 steps apart").
shapes.kinds.fill.readout.apart: Value of the About readout for a fill shape (marchers spread evenly inside an outline) on the field: roughly how far apart neighboring marchers stand, in marching steps. {steps} is the distance, to one decimal, written in the app's language.
shapes.kinds.fill.readout.edge: Label of a readout of a Filled shape. The value beside it is how many marchers stand on the shape's edge. Noun.
shapes.kinds.fill.readout.edgeAuto: Value of the Edge readout of a Filled shape when the app picked the number. {count} is the number of marchers on the edge (for example "6 (auto)").
shapes.kinds.fill.validate.noSize: Error message about a Filled shape. The shape's width or height is zero, so there is no area to fill.
shapes.kinds.group.label: Name of a kind of shape, shown on a placed shape's label and in its floating editor bar: a group of marchers kept as they stood, with no regular form such as a box or circle.
shapes.kinds.group.params.interval: Tooltip of the one number in a group's floating editor bar: the smallest distance between two neighboring marchers in the group, in steps. Changing it scales the whole group.
shapes.kinds.line.corners.label: In the Line shape editor: whether every corner of the line holds a marcher. Text: "Corners".
shapes.kinds.line.corners.off: In the Line shape editor: whether every corner of the line holds a marcher. Text: "Intervals run around corners".
shapes.kinds.line.corners.on: In the Line shape editor: whether every corner of the line holds a marcher. Text: "Marcher on every corner".
shapes.kinds.line.ends.closed: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Closed".
shapes.kinds.line.ends.label: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Open or closed".
shapes.kinds.line.ends.open: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Open".
shapes.kinds.line.label: Name of the Line shape kind: marchers in a straight line between two end points.
shapes.kinds.line.lock.locked: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Interval locked: dragging an end keeps it. Click to unlock".
shapes.kinds.line.lock.unlocked: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Lock the interval, so dragging an end keeps it".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.along: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Along the path".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.label: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Measured".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.noX: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "The line doesn't go side to side".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.noY: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "The line doesn't go front to back".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.offset: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Offset".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.offsetGroups: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Only with one interval for everyone".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.offsetPath: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Not with Interval on the path".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.offsetSegment: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Only on a one-segment line".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.squareX: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Part of the line runs straight front to back".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.squareY: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Part of the line runs straight side to side".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.straight: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "Straight across".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.turnsX: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "The line turns back side to side".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.turnsY: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "The line turns back front to back".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.x: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "↔ Side to side".
shapes.kinds.line.measured.y: In the Line shape editor's Measured menu: what a typed interval between marchers measures. Text: "↕ Front to back".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.add: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Add point here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.close: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Close line".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.closeFew: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "A line needs three points to close".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.corner: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Corner".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.cornerType: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Corner type".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.curved: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Curved".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.delete: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Delete point".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.fewestClosed: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "A closed line needs at least three points".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.fewestOpen: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "A line needs at least two points".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.lineKeeps: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Line keeps spacing even here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.linePuts: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Line puts a marcher here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.lineWouldKeep: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Line would keep spacing even here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.lineWouldPut: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Line would put a marcher here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcher: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Marcher on this point".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherAlways: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Marcher".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherEven: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Even spacing".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherFilled: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "A filled line's spots follow its fill".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherFollow: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Follow line's marchers".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherPath: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Interval on the path runs past every point".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.marcherTooFew: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Too few marchers for one on every point".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.noCurve: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "The line runs straight through here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.open: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Open here".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.roundness: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Roundness".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.smooth: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Smooth".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.straight: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Straight".
shapes.kinds.line.menu.swapHint: In the right-click menu on a point or segment of a Line shape on the field. Text: "Double-click a point to swap".
shapes.kinds.line.params.cornerOff: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "corner off its interval".
shapes.kinds.line.params.interval: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Spacing between neighbors, in steps".
shapes.kinds.line.params.offsetSide: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Side to side from each marcher to the next, in steps: right is more, left below 0".
shapes.kinds.line.params.offsetUp: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "Front to back from each marcher to the next, in steps: up the screen (toward the back) is more, down below 0".
shapes.kinds.line.params.offsetWaits: In the Line shape editor (a line of marchers drawn on the field). Text: "along the path until it's one segment (Offset)".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.fit: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Fit".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.keep: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Keep interval".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.label: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Spacing".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.pathCenter: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Interval on the path, centered".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.pathEnd: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Interval on the path, from the end".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.pathOffset: Reason shown on the disabled "Interval on the path" choice in the Line shape editor's Spacing menu. Text: "Offset sets the line's length".
shapes.kinds.line.spacing.pathStart: In the Line shape editor's Spacing menu: how the line's size and the interval between marchers relate. Text: "Interval on the path, from the start".
shapes.kinds.line.validate.sameSpot: Error message about a Line shape. Both ends of the line are at the same point, so there is no line to make.
shapes.kinds.measure.angle: Label of a number field of a shape: an angle, in degrees. Noun.
shapes.kinds.measure.depth: Label of a number field of a shape: its depth, front to back, in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.measure.radius: Label of a number field of a shape: the radius, from the center to the edge, in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.measure.sweep: Label of a number field of an arc shape: the sweep, how many degrees of a full circle the arc covers. Noun.
shapes.kinds.measure.width: Label of a number field of a shape: its width, side to side, in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.path.readout.interval: Label of a readout of a line, arc or curve shape: the distance between neighboring marchers, in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.path.readout.length: Label of a readout of a line, arc or curve shape: the whole length of the shape, in steps. Noun.
shapes.kinds.path.readout.run: Label of a readout of a line, arc or curve shape whose marchers are placed at a fixed interval: the length covered by the marchers, which can be shorter or longer than the shape. Noun.
shapes.kinds.path.readout.steps: Value of a readout on the shape tool for lines, arcs, curves and circles (its length, run or interval), in steps. A step is the drill unit of distance (one marching stride). {steps} is the number, possibly with two decimals (such as 2.5).
shapes.kinds.path.spacing: Label and heading of the spacing setting of a line, arc or curve shape: how the marchers are spaced along the shape. Noun.
shapes.placed.editError: Error toast shown when editing a placed shape (a shape already put on the field) fails.
shapes.placed.fillError: Error toast shown when filling empty spots of a placed shape, with Close up or Re-split, fails.
shapes.placed.groupError: Error toast when grouping the selected marchers into a shape fails.
shapes.placed.label: Label drawn on the field above a placed shape. {name} is the shape's name and size, for example "Box 5 × 4" or "Circle"; {interval} is the spacing between marchers, a number or two joined with "×" (for example "2" or "2 × 1½"). Plural message: {count} is the last spacing number, which the word 'step' agrees with. Reads "Box 5 × 4 · 2 steps". A step is one drill step.
shapes.placed.layoutSize: A placed box's size with its layout named first, in the label drawn on the field above it (for example "Stagger 3 × 3"). {layout} selects the layout, a pattern for how the marchers sit in the box: full, stagger, rounded, notched or other (Short back); use the same words as the Layout menu (shapes.distribute.layout.*) and keep the select structure and the words before the braces. {size} is the counts across × deep, such as "3 × 3".
shapes.placed.leftShape.many: Toast shown when several marchers that belonged to a placed shape moved away from it. Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is how many marchers left, 2 or more; translate the forms your language needs (you may add a word for marchers). {shape} selects the kind of shape: block (a box, a rectangular block of marchers), circle, or other (any other shape); translate each variant as the word fits this sentence, and keep the select structure and the words block, circle and other before the braces.
shapes.placed.leftShape.one: Toast shown when one marcher that belonged to a placed shape moved away from it. {name} is the marcher's name or drill number (for example "B12"). {shape} selects the kind of shape: block (a box, a rectangular block of marchers), circle, or other (any other shape); translate each variant as the word fits this sentence, and keep the select structure and the words block, circle and other before the braces.
shapes.placed.name: The name part of the label drawn on the field above a placed shape: {shape} is the shape's name as a stand-alone, capitalized label (for example "Box" or "Circle", as in the shape picker); {size} is its counts across × deep, for example "5 × 4", or with a layout first ("Stagger 3 × 3"). Reads "Box 5 × 4". Change the order if your language puts the numbers first.
shapes.placed.selectWholeShape: Button in the Inspector, shown when the selected marcher is part of a placed shape. Pressing it selects every marcher of that shape. {shape} selects the kind of shape: block (a box, a rectangular block of marchers), circle, or other (any other shape); translate each variant as the word fits this sentence, and keep the select structure and the words block, circle and other before the braces.
shapes.placed.summary.empty: Part of the summary line of a placed shape: how many of its spots are empty because marchers left it (for example "2 empty"). Plural message: {count} (shown as #) is that number; translate the forms your language needs. Joined to other parts with "·"; each part stands alone.
shapes.placed.summary.steps: Part of the summary line of a placed shape. {interval} is the spacing between marchers in steps, a number or two joined with "×" (for example "2" or "2 × 1½"). Plural message: {count} is the last spacing number, which the word 'step' agrees with. Joined to other parts with "·"; each part stands alone.
shapes.placed.ungroupError: Error toast when ungrouping a placed shape (turning it back into plain marchers) fails.
shapes.placed.ungroupIsolated: Error toast when Ungroup is used while one move on the timeline is isolated, on a shape that was made on an earlier page. The user has to leave isolation first.
shapes.spacing.empty: Error message under the spacing field when the user entered nothing. A spacing is the distance between marchers, in drill steps.
shapes.spacing.emptyGroup: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: "There's an empty group in the list. Type a group between each +: 2*3+4*2".
shapes.spacing.noGaps: Error message under the spacing field. The spacing was typed as steps x gaps (for example "4x3") and the number of gaps was less than 1. A gap is the space between two neighboring marchers.
shapes.spacing.noMarchers: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: "A group needs at least 1 marcher".
shapes.spacing.notCount: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: ""{count}" isn't a number of marchers. Type a whole count before the interval: 2*3". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.spacing.notInterval: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: ""{part}" isn't an interval. Type steps (2), or a count and steps for each group (2*3+4*2)". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.spacing.notPositive: Error message under the spacing field. The user typed zero or a negative number. A spacing is the distance between marchers, in drill steps.
shapes.spacing.repeating: Note under the spacing field. The user typed fewer spacings than there are gaps between marchers (a gap is the space between two neighboring marchers). {needed} is the number of gaps, {given} the number typed; the typed list repeats from its first number.
shapes.spacing.tooManyMarchers: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: "A group can have at most {max} marchers". Words in braces are filled in by the app; keep them.
shapes.spacing.twoRests: Error or note shown in the shape editor when the typed interval list for a shape can't be read. Text: "Only one group can go without a count (the rest). Type a count before the others: 2*3".
shapes.spacing.unused: Note under the spacing field. The user typed more spacings than there are gaps between marchers (a gap is the space between two neighboring marchers). {needed} is the number of gaps, {given} the number typed, {unused} how many are left over and ignored.
shapes.tool.moment.count: Name of a moment in the show, used in "Shape open at {moment}". {count} is the count (beat) number where the playhead was (for example "count 12"). A count is one beat of the music. Lowercase.
shapes.tool.moment.home: Name of a moment in the show, used in "Shape open at {moment}": the very start of the show, before the first count. Lowercase.
shapes.tool.placeError: Error toast shown when placing a shape on the field fails.
shapes.tool.ring.hint: Hint under the shape ring, a circular quick-pick menu of shapes that opens around the pointer. Shown when the ring stays open: the user can click a shape to pick it, or click anywhere else to close the ring.
shapes.tool.section.title: Heading of the Shapes section in the Inspector, with buttons to draw shapes. Plural noun.
shapes.tool.selectMarchersFirst: Reason shown when the shape tools are greyed out because no marchers are selected. Marchers are the performers shown as dots on the field. Short instruction.
shapes.tool.tab.greyed: Tooltip of a shape button in the Shapes tab that is greyed out. {name} is the shape's name (for example "Box"), {reason} is why (for example "Select marchers first").
shapes.tool.tab.kinds: Screen-reader label of the row of shape buttons (box, circle and so on) in the Shapes tab of the toolbar. Plural noun.
shapes.tool.tab.ringHintKeys: Hint at the end of the Shapes tab in the toolbar. The shape ring is a round menu of shape kinds (box, line, arc…) that opens around the pointer on the field while the user holds a key. Keep <keys></keys>: it is replaced by that key, shown as a keycap (for example R).
shapes.transform.title: Heading of the Inspector section for turning and flipping a selection of marchers (not a shape) around a pivot. Noun.
shapes.validate.noPosition: Error message about a shape. One of its spots has no valid position, so the shape cannot be placed.
shapes.validate.offField: Warning about a shape. {count} marchers would be placed outside the field's edges. Starts the sentence with the number.
shapes.validate.sameSpot: Error message about a shape. {count} marchers would be placed on exactly the same spot. Starts the sentence with the number.
shapes.validate.stepsTooLong: Warning about a shape. {count} is the number of marchers whose walk to their spot has steps longer than the field's step size limit. {limit} is the limit written as steps over five yards (for example "8 to 5"); {longest} is the longest step needed, written the same way. The "Field › Customize" settings page is where the limit is set; keep its names as in the app. "Orange" is the color of the walk lines on the field.
shapes.validate.tooClose: Warning about a shape. {count} marchers would be closer to each other than {min} step (the minimum distance, in drill steps). Starts the sentence with the number.
shortcut.gesture.click: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + click” (hold Shift while you click). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
shortcut.gesture.drag: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + drag” (hold Shift while you drag). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
shortcut.gesture.scroll: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + scroll” (hold Shift while you scroll). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
shortcutsDialog.group.alignment: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that line up or evenly space the selected marchers (performers).
shortcutsDialog.group.batchEdit: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that change many marchers (performers) at once, such as swapping or flipping them.
shortcutsDialog.group.cursor: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that switch the active editing tool.
shortcutsDialog.group.edit: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: editing shortcuts such as undo, redo, copy and paste.
shortcutsDialog.group.file: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts for opening, saving and exporting show files.
shortcutsDialog.group.movement: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that move the selected marchers (performers) on the field.
shortcutsDialog.group.navigation: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that go to the previous, next, first or last page. A page is one step of the drill, between two sets (fixed formations).
shortcutsDialog.group.other: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog for shortcuts that don't belong to any of the other groups.
shortcutsDialog.group.playback: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that play, pause and loop the show's music and animation.
shortcutsDialog.group.select: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that select or deselect marchers (performers on the field).
shortcutsDialog.group.shape: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts for the shape tool, which places marchers (performers) in a box, line or other drawn shape that moves as one.
shortcutsDialog.group.timeline: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts for the timeline, the strip at the bottom of the editor showing pages, counts and music over time.
shortcutsDialog.group.ui: Group heading in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: shortcuts that change what is shown on screen (panels, zoom, paths).
shortcutsDialog.movement.constrain: Row label in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog. Next to it, the key combination is shown (Ctrl or Cmd plus mouse drag). While dragging marchers on the field, holding the key keeps the move on a single axis (straight horizontally or vertically).
shortcutsDialog.movement.fineControl: Row label in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog. Next to it, the key combination is shown (Shift plus mouse drag). Holding Shift while dragging marchers on the field makes the movement finer and slower.
shortcutsDialog.movement.nudge: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Move marchers group: the W, A, S and D keys move the selected marchers (performers) a small step up, left, down or right on the field.
shortcutsDialog.shape.constrain: Row label in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog for the shape tools. Next to it, the key combination is shown (Ctrl or Cmd plus mouse drag). Holding the key while drawing or reshaping a shape of marchers constrains it: spacings become equal, movement stays on one axis, and proportional scaling flips (stays proportional instead of free, or the opposite). A shape here is a formation of marchers such as a line or circle.
shortcutsDialog.shape.fineControl: Row label in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog for the shape tools. Next to it, the key combination is shown (Shift plus mouse drag). Holding Shift while drawing a shape of marchers gives fine control, while still snapping to the field's yard lines and hash marks. A shape here is a formation of marchers such as a line or circle.
shortcutsDialog.shape.fromCenter: Row label in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog for the shape tools. Next to it, the key combination is shown (Alt plus mouse drag). Holding Alt while drawing or resizing a box of marchers makes it grow from its center instead of from a corner.
shortcutsDialog.timeline.dragWithoutSnap: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Timeline group: holding the key while dragging something on the timeline stops it from jumping to whole counts and page edges.
shortcutsDialog.timeline.drawRange: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Timeline group: holding the key and dragging across the timeline marks a range of time (counts).
shortcutsDialog.timeline.fitShow: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Timeline group: zooms the timeline (the strip at the bottom showing pages and counts over time) to fit the whole show, or, pressed again, back to the previous zoom.
shortcutsDialog.timeline.leaveIsolatedMo: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Timeline group. A move is the motion of marchers from one set (fixed formation) to the next; isolating one shows only that move on the timeline. This shortcut leaves that view.
shortcutsDialog.timeline.zoom: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog, Timeline group: holding the key while scrolling the mouse wheel zooms the timeline in or out.
shortcutsDialog.title: Title of the dialog that lists every keyboard shortcut in OpenMarch, grouped by area. Opened with the ? key or from the Help menu.
sidebar.appearance: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the Marcher Appearance panel (colors and dot shapes of marchers). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
sidebar.close: Screen-reader label of the X button in the top corner of a side panel (the tall panel beside the field that holds tools like Marchers, Music, Field or Assets). Closes the panel.
sidebar.field: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the Field panel (settings for the field the show is drawn on). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
sidebar.marchers: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the Marchers panel (list of the show's performers). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
sidebar.metronome: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the Metronome panel (a click track for the show's tempo). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
sidebar.mobile: Caption under the icon of the sidebar button that opens the panel for exporting the show to the OpenMarch mobile companion app. Shown only in touch mode; keep it short.
sidebar.music: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the Music panel (the show's audio file and related tools). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
sidebar.renderFail: Placeholder heading shown in the side panel only if the panel opens before its content is set, which should not normally happen. The side panel is the tall panel beside the field that holds tools like Marchers or Music.
sidebar.settings: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the sidebar button that opens the settings that belong to the open show (as opposed to the app-wide settings). In touch mode it is also the caption under the icon, so keep it short.
stepSize.hold: Step size shown in the marcher inspector when the marcher doesn't move at all on this page (they hold their position, marking time).
stepSize.tiny: Step size shown in the marcher inspector when the marcher's steps are extremely small (smaller than 64 steps per 5 yards), instead of a very large number.
stepSize.toFive: A marcher's step size in the marcher inspector, in the marching convention "N to 5": the marcher would take {steps} steps to cover 5 yards (for example "8 to 5" is a standard step; larger numbers are smaller steps). {steps} may have one decimal (for example 6.7). Keep "to 5" as the convention is written in your language's marching community.
stepSize.undefined: Step size shown in the marcher inspector when it can't be worked out because the page has no counts. Step size describes how big a marcher's steps are on the way to this page.
tags.addSelectedTo: Tooltip of a button in the marcher inspector, and the heading of the list of tags it opens. Picking a tag (a user-made group of marchers) adds the selected marchers to it.
tags.addSelectedToExisting: Screen-reader label of a button in the marcher inspector that opens a list of existing tags (user-made groups of marchers); picking one adds the selected marchers to it.
tags.cancel: Button in the pop-up for creating a new tag in the marcher inspector. Closes the pop-up without making the tag.
tags.create: Button in the pop-up for creating a new tag in the marcher inspector. Makes the tag (a user-made group of marchers) with the selected marchers.
tags.createWithSelected: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a button in the marcher inspector. Makes a new tag (a user-made group of marchers) containing the marchers currently selected on the field.
tags.delete: Menu item in a tag chip's menu in the marcher inspector. Deletes the tag (a user-made group of marchers); the marchers themselves stay.
tags.editAppearance: Menu item in a tag chip's menu in the marcher inspector. Opens the appearance panel where the tag's marchers get their own colors and shapes on the field. A tag is a user-made group of marchers.
tags.errors.createAppearances: Error toast shown when adding a tag appearance fails. A tag appearance is the color and style that marchers with a tag take on from a given page of the show.
tags.errors.createFromMarchers: Error toast shown when making a new tag from the selected marchers fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers. "Marcher ids" means the selected marchers.
tags.errors.createMarcherTags: Error toast shown when adding a tag to marchers fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers.
tags.errors.createTags: Error toast shown when creating one or more tags fails. A tag is a user-made label (like "Front rank") that groups marchers so they can be selected and styled together.
tags.errors.deleteAppearances: Error toast shown when removing a tag appearance fails. A tag appearance is the color and style that marchers with a tag take on from a given page of the show.
tags.errors.deleteMarcherTags: Error toast shown when removing a tag from marchers fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers.
tags.errors.deleteTags: Error toast shown when deleting one or more tags fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers.
tags.errors.updateAppearances: Error toast shown when saving changes to a tag appearance fails. A tag appearance is the color and style that marchers with a tag take on from a given page of the show.
tags.errors.updateMarcherTags: Error toast shown when changing which marchers have a tag fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers.
tags.errors.updateTags: Error toast shown when saving changes to one or more tags (for example a rename) fails. A tag is a user-made label that groups marchers.
tags.namePlaceholder: Placeholder in the text box for a tag's name, when renaming a tag or creating a new one in the marcher inspector. A tag is a user-made group of marchers.
tags.newTagNameLabel: Label above the name box in the small pop-up for creating a new tag (a user-made group of marchers) in the marcher inspector. The name can be left empty.
tags.removeSelectedFrom: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a button in the marcher inspector, and the heading of the list of tags it opens. Picking a tag (a user-made group of marchers) takes the selected marchers out of it.
tags.rename: Menu item, field label and screen-reader label for renaming a tag, in the menu that opens when a tag chip is clicked in the marcher inspector. A tag is a user-made group of marchers (for example "Front line").
tags.title: Heading of the Tags panel. A tag is a named group of marchers, such as 'Solo' or 'Front line', that can be selected together. Plural noun.
tags.unnamed: Name shown for a marcher tag that has no name of its own, in tag lists (the marcher inspector, tag appearances, and Select by tag on the toolbar). A tag is a user-made group of marchers. {id} is the tag's number. Keep it short; it reads like a placeholder name.
tempoGroup.createNewBeatsError: Error toast shown when creating the beats of a new tempo group fails. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter, such as 120 BPM in 4/4.
tempoGroup.deleteFailed: Error toast shown when deleting a tempo group fails. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
tempoGroup.deletedSuccessfully: Success toast after a tempo group was deleted. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
tempoGroup.differentBeatsError: Error shown when a tempo group has a different number of beats than expected after an edit. This should never happen, so it asks the user to contact the OpenMarch team. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo and meter.
tempoGroup.errorUpdatingTempoGroup: Error toast shown when updating a tempo group fails. A tempo group is a run of measures that share a tempo (speed in beats per minute) and meter.
tempoMode.band.action.addedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that adds a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.curve: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that bends a gradual tempo change (ramp) into a curve. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.endsOn: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging the end of a stretch of the tempo line up or down: the stretch ends on {tempo}, which is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120". Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.endsOnThen: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging the end of a stretch of the tempo line up or down: the stretch ends on {tempo}, then the music jumps to {next}. Both is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120". Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.gradual: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that turns a jump in tempo into a gradual change (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.held: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that sets how long a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) lasts. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {seconds} is a number of seconds; "s" is the unit. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.hold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that makes a count a hold or not. A hold (fermata) is a count held for a length of time in seconds instead of played at a tempo. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.holdDrill: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that ends a move one count early so the marchers stand still for a count (a breath), without changing the music. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.jump: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that turns a gradual tempo change (ramp) back into a sudden jump to the new tempo. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.measureNumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that renumbers measures by hand. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.movedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts) sideways to another count. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.rehearsalMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of an edit to a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C"). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.removedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that removes a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts); the tempo before it carries on. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.tempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of an edit to the tempo (speed of the counts). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.timeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that sets a time signature (such as 4/4 or 7/8). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.intro: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), explanation at the top of the box for adding counts (beats). The audio recording is never edited.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.keepMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when adding a count: the measure gets one more count in the same time, so its counts get faster. {measure} is a measure such as "m. 12". {count} is its new number of counts. {tempo} is the tempo before and after, such as "♩120 → ♩150".
tempoMode.band.ask.add.manyKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each keeps its length and its marchers stand still for the added counts at its end. {moves} is the number of moves (always 2 or more); {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.manyShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each gets longer. {moves} is the number of moves (always 2 or more); {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.noMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) is: the marchers simply stand still during the added counts.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.oneKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over the spot keeps its length, and its marchers stand still for the added counts at its end. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {moveCounts} is the move's length in counts; {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.oneShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over the spot gets longer. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {from} and {to} are its length in counts before and after.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.shift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when adding counts: the new counts add time, so everything after moves later against the music. Use it when the counts after were ahead of the music. {seconds} is the time added in seconds; "s" is the unit.
tempoMode.band.ask.addCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a count (beat), for when the music has a beat the counts miss. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.ask.addCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a count (beat), for when the music has a beat the counts miss. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.ask.addMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a measure. Shown when the music has a beat the counts miss. {count} is how many counts (beats) the measure has. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.ask.addedCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a count (beat). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.addedCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a count (beat). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.addedMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a measure. {count} is how many counts (beats) it has. {measure} is a measure number. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.many: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), what the "hold the drill" option does when several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each ends a count early and the marchers stand still for that count. Also shown alone as a toast once done. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.noCountAdded: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of the "hold the drill" option when adding a count: instead of adding a count, the move ends a count early so marchers stand still (a breath).
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.none: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), why the "hold the drill" option is unavailable: no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) runs over this spot, so there is nothing to end early.
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.one: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), what the "hold the drill" option does: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) gets one count shorter and the marchers stand still on its last count. Also shown alone as a toast once done. {move} names the move, such as "Page 11" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {from} and {to} are its length in counts before and after. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). It may end with ", before C" naming the next rehearsal mark.
tempoMode.band.ask.countsFewer: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), when counts are removed where no page is: how many fewer counts (beats) the show has. Shown as a sentence on its own.
tempoMode.band.ask.countsMore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), when counts are added where no page is: how many more counts (beats) the show gets. Shown as a sentence on its own.
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.fewer: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Button that removes fewer counts, leaving one count between the keyframe's end and the flag. {where} is the smaller range, like "m. 4 count 2 to m. 4 count 3".
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.fewerHint: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Under the remove-fewer-counts button.
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.fixHint: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Under the button that shortens the keyframe by one count and then removes the counts, as one step. {move} names the move whose set is kept, like "Page 2".
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.fixTooShort: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Why the shorten-the-keyframe button is unavailable: the keyframe has too few counts left.
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.marchersMore: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). A list of marchers cut short: {names} is the first few labels like "B1, B2, B3, B4", {count} how many more there are.
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.text: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Explains the problem under the title. {move} names the move whose set would be hidden, like "Page 2".
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.theMove: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Stands in for {move} when the move's name can't be read.
tempoMode.band.ask.hidden.title: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Shown instead of the usual choices when the removal would make a keyframe (a move on top of another for some marchers) end on the same count as the move under it, so those marchers would never stand on that move's set (their spot at its end). {marchers} is a list of marcher labels like "B1, B2, T3"; {move} names the move under it, like "Page 2".
tempoMode.band.ask.laterCountsStay: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence in an option when adding or removing counts: the counts after the change stay where they are against the music. Use it when they already line up with the music.
tempoMode.band.ask.noMoveHere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), very short reason the "hold the drill" option is unavailable: there is no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) here.
tempoMode.band.ask.pageCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), how a page's length in counts (beats) changes when counts are added or removed. {page} is the page's name, such as "11"; {from} is its count now and {to} after. Several may be listed, separated by ", ".
tempoMode.band.ask.pagesSentence: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), turns a list of page changes into a sentence in the explanation of adding or removing counts. {pages} is one or more items like "Page 11: 8 → 9 counts" separated by ", ", or a phrase like "1 count more". Only change the full stop if your language ends sentences differently.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.intro: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), explanation at the top of the box for removing counts (beats). The audio recording is never edited.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.keep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when removing counts: the remaining counts nearby stretch to fill the same time, so they get slower. {where} is the measure or span, such as "m. 12" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 12 count 4". {from} and {to} are the number of counts before and after. {tempo} is the tempo before and after, such as "♩120 → ♩90".
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.manyKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each keeps its length by ending later. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.manyShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each gets shorter. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.marksGo: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). A warning above the choices: the removed counts start measures with rehearsal marks (letters like A, B) that are deleted, because the measure left on the next count already has a mark. {marks} lists them, like "C" or "C, D".
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.noMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) is.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.oneKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over them keeps its length by ending later. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {moveCounts} is its length in counts; {count} is how many counts are removed.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.oneShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over them gets shorter. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {count} is how many counts are removed.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.shift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when removing counts: their time is removed too, so everything after moves earlier against the music. Use it when the counts after were behind the music.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.title: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to remove counts (beats), for when the music has fewer beats than counts. {where} is a count or span of counts such as "m. 12 count 3" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 11 count 4".
tempoMode.band.ask.removed: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after removing counts (beats). {where} is a count or span of counts such as "m. 12 count 3" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 11 count 4". Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.editor.holdHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for the length of a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time instead of played at a tempo). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.markHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for naming a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C"). Leaving the box empty removes the mark. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.editor.notATempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a tempo that can't be read. {value} is what was typed. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90 beats a minute; keep the numbers and the hyphen.
tempoMode.band.editor.renumberHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for giving a measure a number by hand; the measures after it are numbered on from there. Leaving it empty goes back to automatic numbering. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoFromToHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a small text box for typing the tempo (beats a minute) of a span of counts. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90; keep the examples as they are. {from} and {to} are places like "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoOfHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a small text box for typing the tempo (beats a minute) of one count. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90; keep the examples as they are. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoOutOfRange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a tempo outside the allowed range. {value} is what was typed.
tempoMode.band.editor.wholeStretch: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), link under the tempo text box: edit the tempo of the whole stretch (all the counts at this tempo) instead of just these counts. {range} is a span such as "m. 11 count 1 to m. 14 count 4". {tempo} is its tempo now, a number like "120" or "120-90" for a gradual change; ♩ is a quarter-note symbol.
tempoMode.band.label.beforeMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), where marchers hold, when a rehearsal mark starts right after it. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {mark} is a rehearsal mark: a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C".
tempoMode.band.label.count: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a place in the show before any measure starts, used inside other messages. {count} is the count (beat) number from the start of the show. A count is one beat of the drill.
tempoMode.band.label.measure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a measure, short form, used inside other messages and as a title. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.label.measureCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a place in the show, used inside many other messages. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number. {count} is the count (beat) within that measure, from 1.
tempoMode.band.label.measures: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a span of measures, short form, such as "m. 11–12". Used as a title and in the Play button's tooltip. {from} and {to} are the first and last measure numbers.
tempoMode.band.label.range: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a span of counts, used inside other messages. {from} and {to} are places like "m. 11 count 1" (first and last count of the span).
tempoMode.band.lane.clearSelection: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), screen-reader label of a small round × button at the end of the selected counts, which deselects them.
tempoMode.band.lane.clearSelectionTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip of a small round × button at the end of the selected counts, which deselects them. {key} is the keyboard key that does the same, such as "Esc".
tempoMode.band.lane.holdLabel: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), small label on the tempo lane over a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time): how long it is held. {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds). Keep it short.
tempoMode.band.lane.holdLabelShort: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the shortest label over a hold (fermata) on the tempo lane, when there is no room for "hold". {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds).
tempoMode.band.lane.markDrag: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label shown while dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) to another measure: where it would land. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is the measure number, or "?".
tempoMode.band.lane.markTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) in the marks lane. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.lane.renumberedTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a measure number that was set by hand. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.lane.shortMeasureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a measure number marked with an asterisk: the measure has fewer counts than its time signature. {measure} is a measure number. {count} is its number of counts (beats).
tempoMode.band.lane.tempoLabelTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a tempo label (such as "♩120") on the tempo lane. Clicking the label opens a small box to type a new tempo. {range} is where that tempo applies, such as "m. 5–8".
tempoMode.band.lane.timeSignatureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a time signature chip in the measures lane. {meter} is the time signature, such as "4/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)".
tempoMode.band.menu.addChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that adds a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo can start) at this count, without changing any tempo yet.
tempoMode.band.menu.addCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a count (beat) after this one, for when the music has a beat the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.addCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a count (beat) before this one, for when the music has a beat the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.addMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to put a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) on this measure.
tempoMode.band.menu.addMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a measure before this one, for when the music has beats the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.cancel: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that closes the menu without doing anything.
tempoMode.band.menu.clearSelection: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that deselects the selected counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.countTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for one count (beat). "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. {count} is the count within that measure, from 1.
tempoMode.band.menu.countTitleNoMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for a count (beat) before any measure. {count} is its number from the start of the show.
tempoMode.band.menu.editMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to rename or remove this measure's rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section).
tempoMode.band.menu.gradual: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item (unavailable here) that would make the tempo change gradually (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando) to the tempo after it.
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the "Gradual change to …" menu item. Holds (fermatas) outside the stretch don't change. {tempo} is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualNothingHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the unavailable "Gradual change" menu item: why there is no gradual change to make.
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualTo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the tempo change gradually (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando) to the tempo after this stretch. {tempo} is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.menu.holdLength: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to type how long a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) lasts.
tempoMode.band.menu.holdSubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the menu title of a count that is a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time): how long it is held. {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds).
tempoMode.band.menu.makeHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the count a hold: held for a length of time in seconds instead of played at a tempo (a fermata in music).
tempoMode.band.menu.markMoveHere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item: move a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) from another measure to this one. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is the measure it is on now.
tempoMode.band.menu.markTaken: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a small menu after naming a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) with a name another measure already has. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.markUseAgain: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item: give this measure the same rehearsal mark (section letter or name) as another measure. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.measureSubtitleMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside a measure's menu title: its time signature and rehearsal mark. {meter} is a time signature such as "4/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)". {mark} is the rehearsal mark (section letter or name), such as "C".
tempoMode.band.menu.measureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for a measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.notAHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that turns a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) back into an ordinary count.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that removes the tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts) at this count; the tempo before it carries on.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove this count (beat), for when the music has fewer beats than counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove the selected counts (beats).
