tempoMode.band.menu.removeMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove this measure's counts, for when the music has fewer beats than counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.renumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to number this measure by hand; the measures after are numbered on from it.
tempoMode.band.menu.seconds: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet value at the right of a menu item: a length in seconds. "s" is the unit.
tempoMode.band.menu.selectionCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the title of the right-click menu for selected counts: how many counts (beats) are selected.
tempoMode.band.menu.setTempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to type the tempo (beats a minute) of the counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.timeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item on a measure that opens a menu of time signatures (such as 4/4 or 7/8).
tempoMode.band.menu.toMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text at the right of the "Set tempo…" menu item: the tempo would be set up to this measure. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.counted: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item choosing a time signature with how its eighth notes are grouped into counts. {meter} is a time signature such as "7/8"; {grouping} is the grouping such as "2+2+3".
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.fromSubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the time signature menu title: the choice lasts until the next time signature.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.fromTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the time signature menu: the choice applies from this measure. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.justThisMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that switches on or off (with a check mark) whether the chosen time signature applies to this measure only.
In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the "Just this measure" menu item.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.onlySubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the time signature menu title when "Just this measure" is on: the measures after keep their time signatures.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.onlyTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the time signature menu when "Just this measure" is on. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.other: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that opens a box to type any time signature with its grouping of eighth notes. Keep the example as it is.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.otherHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above the text box for typing a time signature and how its eighth notes are grouped into counts. Keep the examples as they are.
tempoMode.band.move.from: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), names a move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel between positions) that starts on no page, by where it starts. Used as the subject of a sentence, as {move} in other messages. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.move.its: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the subject of a sentence about the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) of the page just named, as {move} in other messages. "Its" is the page.
tempoMode.band.move.page: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), names a move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel between positions) by the page it starts on. Used as the subject of a sentence, as {move} in other messages. {page} is the page's name, such as "11" or "11A".
tempoMode.band.move.pagesMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel) that starts on a page, as the subject of a sentence ({move} in other messages). {page} is the page's name, such as "11".
tempoMode.band.tip.outlier: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip over a red dot on the tempo line, marking a count much faster or slower than the counts either side, so it may not sit on the music. "Set tempo…" is an item in the right-click menu (tempoMode.band.menu.setTempo); translate it the same way. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {direction} chooses "faster" or "slower". {tempo}, {before} and {after} are tempos such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.toast.changedFirst: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when an edit made while the previous edit was still saving (or just after an undo or redo) is not applied, because it was worked out from the show as it was before. {action} names the edit (such as "Tempo" or "Time signature").
tempoMode.band.toast.failed: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when an edit fails. {action} names the edit (such as "Tempo" or "Time signature"); {error} is the reason, already translated.
tempoMode.band.toast.holdInvalid: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a hold length that isn't a number of seconds between 0.05 and 600. A hold is a fermata: a count held for a length of time.
tempoMode.band.toast.holdMade: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after making a count a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time instead of played at a tempo). It explains how to set its length: "Hold length…" is an item in the right-click menu (tempoMode.band.menu.holdLength); translate it the same way. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.toast.markAlreadyThere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) onto a measure that has one. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. {mark} is that measure's mark, such as "C".
tempoMode.band.toast.markMoved: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) to another measure. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {from} and {to} are measure numbers.
tempoMode.band.toast.meterSetFrom: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after setting a time signature from a measure until the next time signature. {meter} is the time signature, such as "7/8 (2+2+3)". {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {count} is how many counts (beats) each measure now has. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterSetOnly: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after setting a time signature for one measure only. {meter} is the time signature, such as "2/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterShiftNote: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence added to the toast after setting a time signature for one measure: the measures after it move. {count} is by how many counts (beats); {direction} chooses "earlier" or "later".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterShortNote: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence added to the toast after setting a time signature: the counts didn't divide evenly, so the last measure has fewer counts; it is marked with an asterisk (*) in the measures lane. {count} is its number of counts.
tempoMode.band.toast.movesCouldNotKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding or removing counts: how many moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) had to get longer or shorter. Shown after the edit's name, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.movesKept: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding or removing counts: how many moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) kept their number of counts. Shown after the edit's name, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.movesKeptHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding counts that fit into the same stretch of music: the moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) over the spot kept their length, so the marchers stand still for the added counts at the end. {kept} is the number of moves; {count} is the number of counts added.
tempoMode.band.toast.notATimeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a time signature that can't be read. {text} is what was typed. "7/8 2+2+3" is a time signature followed by how its eighth notes are grouped into counts; keep the examples as they are.
tempoMode.band.toast.notMeasureNumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing something that isn't a whole number when renumbering a measure. {value} is what was typed.
tempoMode.band.toast.tooFastOrSlow: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when a tempo edit can't be made because a count would go faster than 400 or slower than 20 beats a minute. {action} names the edit (such as "Tempo" or "Ends on ♩120").
tempoMode.button.hint: Second line of the Edit music button's tooltip while the mode is off: what the mode is for. Time signatures are e.g. 4/4 or 3/4; rehearsal marks are the letters (A, B, C…) printed in sheet music to name sections. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.button.hintOn: Second line of the tempo mode button's tooltip while the mode is on. <escape></escape> is replaced by a keycap showing the Escape key and <toggle></toggle> by a keycap showing Shift+T; either key leaves tempo mode. Keep the tags, each with nothing between them. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.button.label: Name of the button in the timeline's transport bar that turns Edit music on and off; shown as its tooltip title and read by screen readers. Imperative: edit the music. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.button.labelOn: Tooltip title of the Edit music button while the mode is on. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.button.text: Short visible text on the Edit music button in the timeline's transport bar (next to a music-notes icon). Keep it short. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.errors.cantRemoveLastCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast when trying to remove the show's last count (beat).
tempoMode.errors.moveOneCountLong: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast after "Hold the drill: " when a move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) can't end a count early because it is only one count long.
tempoMode.errors.wouldHideSet: Error toast in Edit music when removing counts is refused because a keyframe (a move on top of another for some marchers) would end on the same count as the move under it, so that move's set would never show.
tempoMode.errors.wouldRemovePage: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast when removing counts would remove the start of a page (a section of the drill).
tempoMode.help.doubleClickLane.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Add a tempo change", saying how to do it. A tempo change is a point where the tempo changes; it shows as a dot on the tempo line. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.doubleClickLane.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. A tempo change is a point where the tempo changes; it shows as a dot on the tempo line. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragChangeDot.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Move a tempo change", saying how to do it. A tempo change shows as a dot on the tempo line. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragChangeDot.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. A tempo change shows as a dot on the tempo line. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragEndDot.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Set where a rit. ends", saying how to do it. rit. is ritardando (slowing down); a tempo is the musical term for going back to the earlier tempo. A stretch is the part of the tempo line between two tempo changes. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragEndDot.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. rit. is ritardando (slowing down); a tempo is the musical term for going back to the earlier tempo. A stretch is the part of the tempo line between two tempo changes. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragLine.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Set a tempo", saying how to do it. The tempo line is the line on the tempo lane whose height is the tempo. 'Set tempo…' is a right-click menu item. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragLine.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. The tempo line is the line on the tempo lane whose height is the tempo. 'Set tempo…' is a right-click menu item. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragMeasures.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Select counts", saying how to do it. Measures is the name of a lane in the timeline; the music is the lane showing the audio's waveform. Counts are the beats of the show. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragMeasures.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. Measures is the name of a lane in the timeline; the music is the lane showing the audio's waveform. Counts are the beats of the show. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragRoundHandle.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Change tempo gradually", saying how to do it. A stretch is the part of the tempo line between two tempo changes. A gradual change is an accelerando or ritardando; a jump is a sudden change. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.dragRoundHandle.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. A stretch is the part of the tempo line between two tempo changes. A gradual change is an accelerando or ritardando; a jump is a sudden change. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.keys.escape: Help card, keyboard list: what the Escape key does in Edit music, in order of priority: clear selected counts, else cancel a drag in progress, else close tempo mode.
tempoMode.help.keys.metronome: Help card in Edit music, list of keyboard shortcuts: what the key shown at its left (⌘M or Ctrl+M) does. It turns the metronome (a click on every count) on or off. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.keys.play: Help card, keyboard list: what the Space key does in Edit music. The playhead is the vertical line marking the current time on the timeline.
tempoMode.help.keys.tap: Help card, keyboard list: what the T key does. Tap tempo is a tool where you tap a key in time with the music and it shows the speed in beats per minute.
tempoMode.help.keys.toggle: Help card, keyboard list: what Shift+T does: turns tempo mode on or off.
tempoMode.help.label: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the '?' button in Edit music's header row. It opens a card explaining how tempo mode works. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.musicFile.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Change the music", saying how to do it. The header is the bar at the top of the timeline while Edit music is on; the music file's name is a button there. The music offset is how many seconds after count 1 the music starts. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.musicFile.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. The header is the bar at the top of the timeline while Edit music is on; the music file's name is a button there. The music offset is how many seconds after count 1 the music starts. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.rightClick.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Holds and counts", saying how to do it. A hold is a fermata: a count held longer than the tempo says. Counts are the beats of the show. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.rightClick.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. A hold is a fermata: a count held longer than the tempo says. Counts are the beats of the show. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.rightClickMeasure.text: Help card in Edit music: one sentence, under the bold title "Measures and rehearsal marks", saying how to do it. A rehearsal mark is a letter (A, B, C…) naming a section of the music. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.rightClickMeasure.title: Help card in Edit music: a short bold title for one thing you can do; a sentence under it says how. A rehearsal mark is a letter (A, B, C…) naming a section of the music. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.help.title: Heading of the help card that opens from the '?' button in Edit music's header: the mode's purpose, getting the drill's counts to line up with the beats of the recorded music. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count). Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.import.audio: Item in the Edit music Import menu: opens a file picker for the show's music recording (mp3, wav…). The ellipsis means a file picker follows. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.import.button: Text of a menu button in the Edit music header; its menu imports an audio file or a MusicXML score. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.import.hint: Second line of the Import menu button's tooltip. A score is sheet music in MusicXML format. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.import.score: Item in the Edit music Import menu: takes the timing from a MusicXML score (sheet music file). Keep "MusicXML" as is. The ellipsis means a dialog follows. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.importScore.choose: Primary button of the dialog that confirms importing a MusicXML score's timing: opens the system file picker. The ellipsis means a file picker follows.
tempoMode.importScore.keeps: Second paragraph of the dialog before importing a MusicXML score's timing: what is NOT changed. Pages, drill (the marchers' movements), cues and props stay attached to the same count numbers, so they now play at the score's tempos. Undo reverses the whole import.
tempoMode.importScore.replaces: First paragraph of the dialog before importing a MusicXML score's timing: what the import overwrites, including any edits the user made in Edit music.
tempoMode.importScore.title: Title of the dialog shown before importing a MusicXML score's timing in Edit music. A question; the dialog explains what is replaced and what stays.
tempoMode.lanes.marks.name: Name of a row (lane) in Edit music, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows rehearsal marks (letters A, B, C… naming sections of the music). Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.lanes.marks.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in Edit music, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows rehearsal marks (letters A, B, C… naming sections of the music). Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.lanes.measures.name: Name of a row (lane) in Edit music, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows measures (bars of music) and their numbers and time signatures. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.lanes.measures.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in Edit music, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows measures (bars of music) and their numbers and time signatures. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording. A time signature is e.g. 4/4 or 3/4.
tempoMode.lanes.music.name: Name of a row (lane) in Edit music, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows the music's waveform. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.lanes.music.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in Edit music, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows the music's waveform. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording. The playhead is the line marking the current time. Count 1 is the first count of the show: right-clicking a spot offers to move the music so that spot is heard on count 1.
tempoMode.lanes.tempo.name: Name of a row (lane) in Edit music, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows the tempo line, a graph of the speed in beats per minute. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.lanes.tempo.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in Edit music, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows the tempo line, a graph of the speed in beats per minute. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording. A tempo change is a point where the speed changes (a dot); a round handle on a stretch between changes makes the change gradual. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count). Double-clicking only adds a change; "Set tempo…" is an item in the right-click menu (tempoMode.band.menu.setTempo) for typing a tempo.
tempoMode.music.add: Button in the Edit music header, next to the mode's name when the show has no audio file yet: opens a file picker for the music recording. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.delete: Item in the music file menu: asks to delete the selected audio file from the show. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.importAnother: Item in the music file menu: opens a file picker for another music recording, which becomes the show's music. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.menuLabel: Screen-reader name of the button in the Edit music header that shows the audio file's name and opens a menu to switch, import or delete audio files. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.offset: Item in the music file menu (in the Edit music header): opens a box to type the audio offset, how many seconds after count 1 the music starts. The ellipsis means a dialog follows. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.offsetHelp: Explanation in the Music offset box: how many seconds after count 1 (the first count of the show) the music starts; a negative number starts count 1 partway into the music. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.offsetSet: Button that applies the typed audio offset in the Music offset box.
tempoMode.music.offsetTitle: Title of the box for typing the audio offset (also the input's screen-reader name): how many seconds after count 1 the music starts. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.music.seconds: Unit shown after the number field in the Music offset box.
tempoMode.music.offsetValue: The current audio offset shown at the right of the Music offset menu item; {seconds} is a number, s = seconds (abbreviated).
tempoMode.music.pick: Shown on the music file button when the show has audio files but none is selected. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.blocked.canc: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Closes the box without changing anything.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.blocked.fix: In Edit music's box for removing counts (the beats of the music grid). Main button when the removal would hide a set: shortens the keyframe by one count, then removes the counts, as one undo step.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.footer: Small print at the bottom of the box that opens when adding or removing counts in Edit music, explaining its choice cards. <enter></enter> is replaced by a keycap showing the Enter key and <escape></escape> by one showing the Escape key; keep the tags, each with nothing between them. 'The one marked' is the card showing the Enter keycap, which is the choice made last time. 'Undo' is the app's Undo command.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.hold: Title of a choice card in the box that opens when adding a count in Edit music: instead of adding a count, make the drill (the marchers' movement) pause in place here. Clicking the card does it.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.holdIntro: Question shown above the last choice card in the box that opens when adding a count in Edit music: the music has no extra beat here, but maybe the marchers need extra time (a pause) before the next part of the drill.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.keep: Title of a choice card in a box that opens when adding or removing counts in Edit music: the counts after the change stay where they are against the music. Clicking the card does it. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.shift: Title of a choice card in a box that opens when adding or removing counts in Edit music: everything after the change moves later or earlier by the time added or removed. Clicking the card does it.
tempoMode.popovers.measureGlyph: A tiny icon in Edit music's right-click menu showing a measure number, e.g. 'm34' for measure 34. {number} is the measure number. Use your language's usual one- or two-letter abbreviation for 'measure' (bar), with no space.
tempoMode.tap.average: Shown in the Tap tempo panel under the measured tempo. {bpm} is the average tempo in beats per minute with one decimal, e.g. 120.4. If you stop tapping for 2 seconds, the next tap starts a new measurement. 's' is the abbreviation for seconds.
tempoMode.tap.count: In the corner of the Tap tempo panel: how many taps have been made so far. {count} is that number.
tempoMode.tap.hint: Second line of the Tap tempo button's tooltip, explaining the tool: tap in time with the music to measure its approximate tempo (speed in beats per minute).
tempoMode.tap.instructions: Instruction in the Tap tempo panel before any taps. <key></key> is replaced by a keycap showing the T key; keep the tag, with nothing between. 'The button' is the large Tap button below it. Each beat = each beat of the music.
tempoMode.tap.name: Name of the Tap tempo tool in Edit music's header row: on its button, as the button's tooltip and screen-reader label, and as the heading of its panel. Tap tempo: you tap a key or button in time with the music and it shows how fast the music is, in beats per minute.
tempoMode.tap.reset: Button in the Tap tempo panel that clears the taps so far and starts over.
tempoMode.tap.selectFirst: Tooltip on the disabled Use button of the Tap tempo panel when there are no counts to apply the tempo to: the user needs to select counts first. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.tap.setTarget: Tooltip on the Use button of the Tap tempo panel. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol followed by beats per minute, e.g. ♩120, or ♩– when nothing has been tapped. Keep '♩' as it is. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.tap.tap: The large button in the Tap tempo panel that you press in time with the music; also its screen-reader label. 'Tap' as a verb (press briefly).
tempoMode.tap.use: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel, before anything is tapped and with no counts to apply it to. Use = apply the tapped tempo.
tempoMode.tap.useBpm: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel, with no counts to apply it to. ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol followed by beats per minute, e.g. ♩120. Keep '♩'. Use = apply the tapped tempo.
tempoMode.tap.useBpmOn: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel. ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol and beats per minute, e.g. ♩120; keep '♩'. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). Text inside <muted></muted> is shown in lighter text; keep the tags around the matching part. Use = apply the tapped tempo to those counts.
tempoMode.tap.useHint: Second line of the Use button's tooltip in the Tap tempo panel: Use sets a steady, unchanging tempo on the selected counts, or if none are selected, on the stretch under the playhead (the vertical line marking the current time). A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes.
tempoMode.tap.useOn: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel before anything is tapped. Text inside <muted></muted> is shown in lighter text; keep the tags around the matching part. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). Use = apply the tapped tempo to those counts.
tempoMode.timeline.playFromPlayhead: Tooltip on the timeline's Play button while tempo mode is on and no measures are selected: plays the music from the playhead (the vertical line marking the current time) onward.
tempoMode.timeline.playLoop: Tooltip on the timeline's Play button while tempo mode is on and some measures are selected: plays those measures over and over. {measures} names them, e.g. 'm. 11–12' (measures 11 to 12). 'Loop' is a verb here.
tempoMode.timeline.stopHere: Tooltip on the timeline's Stop button while playing in Edit music: stops playback and leaves the playhead (current time) where it stopped, instead of jumping back.
tempoMode.toolbar.done: Button at the right of Edit music's header row (and its screen-reader label) that closes tempo mode and returns to the normal timeline.
tempoMode.toolbar.doneLabel: Tooltip title of the Done button in the Edit music header: it leaves the mode. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronome: Button in Edit music's header row (and its screen-reader label) that turns the metronome on and off: a click sound on every count, to hear whether the counts line up with the music.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeHint: Second line of the Metronome button's tooltip in Edit music: what the metronome is for. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count). 'Sit on the music' = line up with the beats of the music.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeOff: Tooltip title of the Metronome button in Edit music's header while the metronome is off. The metronome plays a click on every count.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeOn: Tooltip title of the Metronome button in Edit music's header while the metronome is on. The metronome plays a click on every count.
tempoMode.toolbar.title: Title at the left of the timeline's header row while Edit music is on, naming the mode. Edit music is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for the show's music: its audio file, and lining the show's counts up with the recording.
timeline.appendAtPlayhead.label: Label of a button that appears at the playhead (the current position on the timeline) when it is past the last page: adds a new page from the last page flag to the playhead. {counts} is the new page's length in counts (beats), such as 8. Reads like "Add 8-Count Page". Short.
timeline.appendAtPlayhead.subsetLabel: Label of the add page button at the playhead past the last page when the user holds Shift, which switches it to adding a subset page (a short page inside a larger one that keeps later page numbers). {counts} is its length in counts (beats), such as 4. Reads like "Add 4-Count Subset". Short.
timeline.appendAtPlayhead.subsetTitle: Tooltip of the add subset page button at the playhead. {counts} is the number of counts (beats) in the new page, such as 4 (plural form chosen by it). A subset is a short page that keeps the later pages' numbers. The page runs from the last page flag to the playhead.
timeline.appendAtPlayhead.title: Tooltip of the add page button at the playhead past the last page. {counts} is the number of counts (beats) in the new page, such as 8 (plural form chosen by it). The page runs from the last page flag to the playhead.
timeline.appendCounts.pagesAdded: Success toast after pages were added to the end of the show. {pages} is how many pages were added, such as 1 or 3 (plural form chosen by it). A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
timeline.basic.expertMark.letter: A one-letter badge on a page box in the timeline (Basic mode). It stands for "Expert": some marchers on this page use Expert moves (edited in the Expert timeline), so Basic mode can't edit them there. Use the first letter of your translation of "Expert", or a very short abbreviation.
timeline.basic.expertMark.tooltip: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the "E" badge on a page box in the timeline, in Basic mode. Basic and Expert are the app's two editing modes; Expert moves are moves made in Expert mode, which Basic mode can't change. {count} is how many marchers on the page use them; {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.basic.locked: Warning toast in Basic mode when dragged marchers include some Basic can't edit on this page, because they use Expert moves (moves made in the Expert editing mode). Nothing was moved. {count} is how many marchers. The toast has a Switch to Expert button. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.basic.lockedNotMoved: Warning toast in Basic mode after a drag: the other marchers moved, but these use Expert moves (moves made in the Expert editing mode) on this page, so Basic left them where they were. {count} is how many marchers. The toast has a Switch to Expert button. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.basic.point.label: Screen-reader label of a thin tick on a page box in the timeline (Basic mode). The tick marks a position the selected marchers have partway through a page (a mid-page position). {count} is the count (beat) within the page where it is, starting at 1; {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". Clicking it moves the playhead there.
timeline.basic.point.remove: Item in the right-click menu of a mid-page position tick on a page box in the timeline (Basic mode). Removes the selected marchers' position at that count, so they move straight from the page's start to its end again.
timeline.basic.point.tooltip: Tooltip of a thin tick on a page box in the timeline (Basic mode). The tick marks a position the selected marchers have partway through a page. {count} is the count (beat) within the page, starting at 1; {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A".
timeline.basic.switchToExpert: Button on the Basic mode warning toast about marchers Basic can't edit. Switches the editor to Expert mode, which can edit every move. Basic and Expert are the app's two editing modes.
timeline.clip.descriptionWithKeys: Screen-reader description of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: a note about the move, then its keys. {description} is a note such as "Overridden by Move 4 on Page 3, counts 1–4"; {keys} is the list of keyboard keys. Usually keep as is.
timeline.clip.fallbackName: Screen-reader name of a bar (clip) on the timeline that has no better description. {label} is its name, such as "Move 2"; {from} and {to} are the first and last beats it covers, counted from the start of the show.
timeline.clip.keys: Screen-reader description of the keyboard keys for a move's bar (clip) on the timeline that isn't selected. Enter, F2, Shift+F10 and Delete are keys; translate key names only if your language's keyboards label them differently.
timeline.clip.keysSelected: Screen-reader description of the keyboard keys for the selected move's bar (clip) on the timeline. Enter, F2, Shift+F10 and Delete are keys; translate key names only if your language's keyboards label them differently.
timeline.clip.options: Tooltip of the "⋯" button on the selected move's bar (clip) on the timeline, which opens the move's menu (edit, rename, split, delete). A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.clip.optionsLabel: Screen-reader label of the "⋯" button on the selected move's bar (clip) on the timeline, which opens the move's menu. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2".
timeline.clip.renameField: Screen-reader label of the text field that opens over a move's bar (clip) on the timeline to rename it. {label} is the move's current name, such as "Move 2".
timeline.clip.selectedName: Screen-reader name of the selected move's bar (clip) on the timeline. {name} is the clip's name, such as "Move 2, move, Page 3, counts 1–4".
timeline.clipResize.change: Tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the move's length before the drag and if dropped here, in counts (beats). {before} and {after} are whole numbers.
timeline.clipResize.changeNamed: Tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the move's name and its length before the drag and if dropped here, in counts (beats). {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 3"; {before} and {after} are whole numbers.
timeline.clipResize.member: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline, saying why the edge stops: a marcher joins or leaves the move at this beat. Lowercase because it follows other text after a middle dot.
timeline.clipResize.minimum: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the move can't be shorter than one count (beat).
timeline.clipResize.stopsAt: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline, saying why the edge stops: another move is in the way. {name} is that move's name, such as "Move 3" or "Page 2's move". Lowercase because it follows other text after a middle dot.
timeline.clipResize.taken: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the edge can't land here because another move already covers exactly these counts (beats). {name} is that move's name, such as "Move 3" or "Page 2's move".
timeline.clipResize.takenMerge: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the edge can't land here because a page's own move already covers exactly these counts, so the user should merge this move into it instead. {name} is that move's name, such as "Page 2's move".
timeline.clipResize.throughFlags: Note in the tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the move would now pass this many page flags it didn't before. {count} is how many page flags, a number such as 1 or 3 (the # in the text). A page flag is the marker where a page ends. Lowercase because it follows other text after a middle dot.
timeline.clipResize.withNote: Tag shown while dragging an edge of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline: the length change, then a note after a middle dot. {change} is such as "Move 3: 4 → 6 counts"; {note} is such as "1 count minimum". Usually keep as is.
timeline.compact.label: Screen-reader label, and tooltip while off, of a toggle button on the timeline that shrinks it to a thin strip (compact) or shows it full size.
timeline.compact.onTooltip: Tooltip of the Compact timeline toggle while it is on, so the timeline is a thin strip. Clicking shows the full timeline again.
timeline.edit.inShapeOrFollowTheLeader: Warning toast after a timeline command that left some marchers' moves as they were, while it did the rest. It names why, by group: marchers in a shape, marchers that follow the leader (walk one after another along one path), and marchers whose curved move shares a follow-the-leader order. {shapeCount}, {leaderCount} and {orderCount} are how many marchers are in each group (0 leaves that part out), and {shapeNames}, {leaderNames} and {orderNames} their drill numbers, already joined as a list in your language. {count} is how many marchers in all, for "it keeps its" or "they keep their". The ", and " pieces join the groups that are there. Add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) if it needs them.
timeline.edit.notSimple: Warning toast in Basic mode: some dragged marchers use Expert moves (moves made in the Expert editing mode) on this page, which Basic can't change. The toast has a Switch to Expert button.
timeline.edit.passThrough.catchUp: Toast shown after a drag on the timeline changed what other moves do. {caughtUp} is a name for a move or a list of moves, such as "Page 3" or "Move 2 (Page 4, counts 1–4)". The dragged marchers now reach the set (formation) at the end of that move. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets.
timeline.edit.passThrough.keepStops.page: Label of a button in a toast after a drag made marchers move straight through pages. Pressing it makes those pages hold a stored marcher position (keyframe) again. {count} is how many pages. {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "3" and "5" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.edit.passThrough.keepStops.unna: Label of a button in a toast after a drag made marchers move straight through some pages whose names aren't available. Pressing it makes marchers stop at those pages again. A keyframe is a stored marcher position at a page.
timeline.edit.passThrough.keepStopsError: Error toast shown when the "Keep … as keyframes" button (on the toast after an edit made the marchers pass through pages that were keyframes) fails for an unexpected reason. A keyframe is a position stored for a marcher at a page; the button would have stored them again.
timeline.edit.passThrough.noLongerStop.p: Toast shown after a drag on the timeline made marchers move straight through pages, so those pages no longer hold a stored marcher position (keyframe). {count} is how many pages. {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "3" and "5" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.edit.passThrough.noLongerStop.u: Toast shown after a drag on the timeline made marchers move straight through pages whose names aren't available, so those pages no longer hold a stored marcher position (keyframe).
timeline.edit.passThrough.through: Toast shown after a drag on the timeline made marchers move straight through other moves. {through} is a name or list of names of those moves, such as "Page 3" or "Move 2 (Page 4, counts 1–4)". A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.edit.passThrough.throughAndCatc: Toast shown after a drag on the timeline. {through} is a name or list of names of moves the marchers now go straight through, such as "Page 3". {caughtUp} names the move whose end set (formation) they then reach, such as "Page 4". A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets.
timeline.edit.pastLastPage: Toast in Basic mode when marchers are dragged while the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) is past the show's last page. "Create page at playhead" is an item in the playhead's right-click menu, and F is its keyboard shortcut; use the same item name as its translation. A set is the marchers' formation at the end of a page.
timeline.edit.selectTimeline: Toast when marchers are dragged on the field but no point on the timeline is chosen, so the app doesn't know when they should arrive at the new spot. Clicking the timeline picks that moment.
timeline.errors.assignmentDoesNotFit: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A transition is the part of a move that takes marchers from one formation to another; a slot is one marcher's place in it. The marcher's move must stay inside the transition's range of counts and use a slot the transition has.
timeline.errors.assignmentOutsideTransit: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A transition is the part of a move that takes marchers from one formation to another. A marcher's move must stay within the counts of its transition, so the user should change either range.
timeline.errors.assignmentOverlap: Error toast from the Expert timeline. Layers let one marcher have overlapping moves; two moves of the same marcher can't overlap on the same layer. Tells the user to put one on another layer or move it. A beat is one count of the music.
timeline.errors.blockTooSmall: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A block is a grid of places (rows and columns) that marchers fill; each slot (a marcher's place in a transition) needs its own place in it. Tells the user to add rows or columns or use fewer slots.
timeline.errors.database: Error toast shown when saving a timeline change fails in the show file's database. Nothing was changed. Asks the user to try again and to report the problem if it keeps happening.
timeline.errors.destinationInvalid: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A destination is the point on the field where a marcher ends up at the end of a transition. Destinations must be real, finite positions on the field, not blank or infinite.
timeline.errors.destinationShapeUnsuitab: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A transition takes marchers from one formation to another. Its destination is a shape for the marchers to end on. A follow-the-leader transition (marchers following one another's path) can't end on a block (a grid of places), and a block needs at least as many places as the transition has slots (marcher places).
timeline.errors.followLeaderBlock: Error toast from the Expert timeline. In a follow-the-leader transition marchers follow one another along a path; it can't end on a block (a grid of places). Tells the user to choose a line, curve, circle or box shape instead.
timeline.errors.followLeaderNeedsShape: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A follow-the-leader transition makes marchers follow one another along a path, so it needs a shape (line, curve and so on) to follow.
timeline.errors.heldConflict: Error toast when an edit would put a move inside a hold. {names} is the marchers' drill numbers, already joined as a list in your language; {count} is how many. {pages} names the pages, such as "Page 3" or "Pages 3 and 4". {held} is the state word "Held" and {clearThisPage} the command "Clear this page", both filled in by the app; keep them as placeholders. Dragging inside the hold moves it instead. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now). The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.errors.heldHoldsOverlap: Error toast: an edit would give one marcher two holds over the same counts. {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.errors.heldPages: The pages a hold message names, inside another sentence: "Page 3" or "Pages 3 and 4". {pages} is one page name or several, already joined as a list in your language; {count} is how many pages. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.errors.legacyConvertedTimeline: Error toast shown when the user edits a show file that an earlier development version of OpenMarch converted to the timeline format incorrectly, so it can't be edited. Tells them to convert it again from the backup copy that was saved next to the file before the conversion.
timeline.errors.moveInHeldHold: Error toast when an edit would put a move inside a hold (a stretch where a marcher stays where the previous page left it). {held} is the state word "Held" and {clearThisPage} the command "Clear this page", both filled in by the app; keep them as placeholders. Dragging inside the hold moves it instead. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.errors.notJoined.marcherCount: Stands in for the marchers' names in the "couldn't join their moves" toast when their names aren't known: "3 marchers". {count} is how many. Add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) if it needs them.
timeline.errors.notJoined.message: Toast after "Remove keyframe" when some marchers' moves before and after the count couldn't be joined into one move, so they stand still and then walk. {names} is the marchers' names (or "3 marchers"), already joined as a list in your language. {reason} is why, one of the timeline.errors.notJoined reasons (a lowercase clause).
timeline.errors.notJoined.overlap: Reason in the "couldn't join their moves" toast, inserted as {reason}: a lowercase clause. Layers let one marcher have overlapping moves; the joined move would overlap another of the same marchers' moves on its layer.
timeline.errors.notJoined.partway: Reason in the "couldn't join their moves" toast, inserted as {reason}: a lowercase clause. A marcher enters or leaves the next move partway through it, so the two moves can't become one.
timeline.errors.notJoined.secondMove: Reason in the "couldn't join their moves" toast, inserted as {reason}: a lowercase clause. Joining would give the marchers two moves over exactly the same counts.
timeline.errors.notReady: Error toast shown when the user tries to edit the timeline before it has finished loading. Asks them to try again in a moment.
timeline.errors.numberOutOfRange: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A number is invalid or too large or small: beats (counts), layers, slot counts (the number of marcher places in a transition) and positions must be whole or finite numbers within the allowed limits.
timeline.errors.pathParamsInvalid: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A path setting is invalid. An arc is a curved path between two points; its bulge can be at most half the distance between its ends. Waypoints (points a path passes through) must be positions on the field.
timeline.errors.shapeInvalid: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A shape (the formation that marchers move to) isn't valid. Its points must be on the field, a line needs two different end points, a freehand path needs some length, and a circle, box or block needs a positive size.
timeline.errors.shapeOrDestinations: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A transition takes marchers from one formation to another. It needs either one shape or an individual destination (end position) for every slot (marcher place), never both and never too few.
timeline.errors.slotOutOfRange: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A slot is one marcher's place in a transition (the part of a move that takes marchers from one formation to another). Slots are numbered from 0 up to one less than the slot count, and the chosen number is outside that.
timeline.errors.transitionSpansTimeline: Error toast from the Expert timeline. A transition (the part of a move that takes marchers from one formation to another) must start and end exactly where its timeline starts and ends. Tells the user to change the timeline's range instead, and its transitions move with it.
timeline.errors.unknown: Generic error toast shown when a timeline change was refused for a reason with no more specific message.
timeline.fit.hint: Second line of the tooltip on the timeline's Fit the show button (which zooms the timeline to show the whole show). Says that pressing it again returns to the previous zoom, and how else to zoom: pinch on a trackpad, or scroll while holding a key. <keys></keys> is replaced by that key and the word for scrolling, shown as a key (Command + scroll on a Mac, Ctrl + scroll elsewhere).
timeline.fit.label: Tooltip name of the Fit button in the timeline's transport bar: zooms the timeline so the whole show fits in view.
timeline.goTo.label: Screen-reader label of the go-to box in the timeline's transport bar. Typing a page name, a measure (bar of music) or a rehearsal mark (a letter or number printed in the music, such as "C") jumps the timeline there.
timeline.goTo.placeholder: Placeholder in the go-to box of the timeline's transport bar: examples of what to type. A page name, "m23" for measure 23, or "C" for rehearsal mark C. The box only understands an "m" before a measure number, so keep "m23" as written; translate "Page" and "or".
timeline.goTo.readoutLabel: Screen-reader label of the position readout button in the timeline's transport bar. {position} is the playhead's position spelled out, such as "Page 3, count 4 of 8, measure 12 beat 2". Clicking the button opens the go-to box.
timeline.goTo.readoutTooltip: Tooltip of the position readout button in the timeline's transport bar. {position} is the playhead's position spelled out, such as "Page 3, count 4 of 8". {key} and {modKey} are keyboard shortcuts written as text ("G", and "Ctrl+G", or "⌘G" on a Mac). A rehearsal mark is a letter or number printed in the music.
timeline.heldBar.detail: Second part of a hold bar's label on the timeline, when several marchers are selected: how many of them the hold is for. {held} is that number and {total} how many are selected (here {held} is a number, not the state word).
timeline.heldBar.title: Label of a hold bar on the timeline, which marks where the selected marchers stay where the previous page left them. {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app; {page} is the page's name, such as "3". The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdEdge.endLabel: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a small handle at the end of a hold bar on the timeline. A hold bar shows where a selected marcher stays still on purpose ({held}, the state word "Held", filled in by the app). Dragging the handle makes the hold end earlier (the marcher leaves earlier) or later. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdEdge.readoutEnd: Shown next to the pointer while dragging the end of a hold bar on the timeline: the last count the marcher stays still. {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app; {page} is a page's name, such as "3"; {count} is a count within that page, such as "5". The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdEdge.blocked.minimum: Shown under the readout while dragging an end of a hold bar on the timeline (a stretch where a marcher stays still), when the drag can't go further: the hold can't be shorter than one count.
timeline.holdEdge.blocked.nextMove: Shown under the readout while dragging the end of a hold bar on the timeline (a stretch where a marcher stays still), when the drag can't go further: the marcher's next move starts there.
timeline.holdEdge.blocked.showEnd: Shown under the readout while dragging the end of a hold bar on the timeline (a stretch where a marcher stays still), when the drag can't go further: the show ends there.
timeline.holdEdge.changeError: Error toast shown when dragging (or stepping with the arrow keys) the end of a hold bar on the timeline fails for an unexpected reason. A hold bar is a stretch where a selected marcher stays still on purpose; the drag makes the hold end at another count.
timeline.holdEdge.splitError: Error toast shown when "Split hold here" fails for an unexpected reason. "Split hold here" is a right-click menu command on a hold bar on the timeline (a stretch where a selected marcher stays still on purpose) that cuts the hold in two at the count under the pointer.
timeline.heldBar.titleRange: Label of a hold bar on the timeline that spans several pages. {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app; {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "4" and "6" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.heldBar.titleWithDetail: A hold bar's full label on the timeline: its title ("Held · Page 3") then how many of the selected marchers it is for ("2 of 3 selected"). {title} and {detail} are those two texts, already translated.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.arrivalFollowL: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names (or "3 marchers"), already joined as a list in your language; {page} names the page, such as "Page 3". The move that brings them onto the page is a follow-the-leader move (marchers walk one after another along one path), so there's no single spot to hold.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.arrivalShape: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names (or "3 marchers"), already joined as a list in your language; {page} names the page, such as "Page 3". The move before the page ends in a shape, so the marchers' spots belong to the shape.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.count: Stands in for marchers' names in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast when their names aren't known: "3 marchers". {count} is how many. Add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) if it needs them.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.crossesFlag: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. A move runs across one of the page's flags (the markers where a page starts and ends on the timeline).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.done: Title of the toast after "Hold from last keyframe": who is now held on the page. {names} is their names (or "3 marchers"), already joined as a list in your language; {page} names the page, such as "Page 3", or the pages when the hold reaches back over earlier pages, such as "Pages 3–5". {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.expertMoves: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They use Expert moves on this page (moves made in the Expert editing mode), which Basic mode can't change.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.followLeader: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They follow the leader on this page (walk one after another along one path).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.held: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it didn't change. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app: they already stay where the previous page left them. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.homeShape: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. A shape sets where they stand at the start of the show; ungrouping that shape there lets each be held on its own.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.endsWithoutArr: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language; {page} names the page, such as "Page 3". One of their moves ends at that page, but they don't arrive there with it (another move of theirs decides where they stand at that count, or the move is part of a longer one that carries on), so there's no spot to hold.
timeline.holdFromPrevious.none: Title of the toast after "Hold from last keyframe" when it held no one. {page} names the page, such as "Page 3". {held} is the state word "Held", filled in by the app. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.notHeldReasons: Body of the toast after "Hold from last keyframe": who it couldn't hold, and why. {heldLower} is the lowercase state word "held", filled in by the app. {reasons} is one or more reasons, each a translated clause such as "OT1: in a shape on this page", separated by semicolons. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.holdFromPrevious.shape: One reason in the "Hold from last keyframe" toast for marchers it couldn't hold. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They are in a shape on this page.
timeline.isolation.done: Button in the isolation bar that ends isolation (shows the whole timeline again). <keys></keys> is replaced by the Esc key shown as a key cap, which does the same. Keep the tags.
timeline.isolation.ghostKey: Key (legend) in the isolation bar, next to a small dotted gray line: the dotted gray paths on the field show where this move would have taken marchers who were removed from it. Visible text; screen readers hear the full sentence instead.
timeline.isolation.ghostKeySpoken: Screen-reader version of the key (legend) in the isolation bar: explains that the dotted gray paths on the field show where the isolated move would have taken marchers who were removed from it.
timeline.isolation.nothingToIsolate: Toast after double-clicking a stretch of the timeline that has no move yet. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts; dragging marchers on the field while a stretch is selected makes one. Isolating a move shows only it and replays it so it can be worked on alone.
timeline.isolation.summary: In the isolation bar over the field: which move is isolated and how many marchers are in it. {name} is the move's name or stretch, such as "Page 2's move" or "Page 2, counts 1–8"; {count} is the number of marchers.
timeline.isolation.title: Label at the start of the isolation bar over the field. Isolating a move shows only that move's marchers and keeps replaying it, so it can be worked on alone. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.keep.errors.keep: Error toast shown when Keep fails for an unexpected reason. Keep holds the selected marchers in place on a page of the timeline, instead of following (holding the position an earlier page left them in).
timeline.keep.errors.readKept: Error toast shown when the K shortcut (Keep) can't read which marchers are kept in place on which pages from the show file. A kept spot is a page where a marcher is held in place instead of following an earlier page.
timeline.keep.followed.hadNoPositions: Toast shown after an edit that also changed later pages, because those pages had no positions of their own for the edited marchers and showed this page's. {count} is how many pages. {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "4" and "6" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. Followed by a button that undoes the change on those pages. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.keep.followed.keepAsBefore: Label of the action button in a toast after an edit also changed later pages that were holding the same formation. Pressing it puts those pages back as they were. {count} is how many pages. {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "3" and "5" (the dash marks a range); with one page only {first} is used. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.keep.followed.keepError: Error toast shown when the "Keep Page … as before" button (on the toast after an edit changed later pages that were holding the edited form) fails for an unexpected reason. The button would have kept those later pages as they were before the edit.
timeline.keep.names.others: Last item of a shortened list of marcher names in the timeline's keep texts (inspector tooltips). The app joins it after the first two drill numbers as your language joins a list, giving "OT1, OT2 and 4 others". {count} is how many marchers are not named, at least 2.
timeline.keyframes.detail: Second line of a keyframe diamond's tooltip on the timeline when several marchers are selected. {set} is how many of them have this keyframe, such as 2. {total} is how many are selected, such as 3. A keyframe is a stored marcher position at a count.
timeline.keyframes.detailNames: Second line of a keyframe diamond's tooltip on the timeline when several marchers are selected. {set} is how many of them have this keyframe, such as 2. {total} is how many are selected, such as 3. {names} lists the drill numbers of those that have it, such as "B1 and B4".
timeline.keyframes.removeError: Error toast shown when removing the selected marchers' keyframes fails. A keyframe is a position stored for a marcher at a certain count, shown as a diamond on the timeline.
timeline.keyframes.removeLocked: Toast shown in Basic mode when Remove keyframe skipped some marchers because they use Expert moves on this page, which can only be edited in Expert mode. {count} is how many marchers were skipped, such as 1 or 3 (plural form chosen by it). Basic and Expert are the two editing modes; match their names. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.keyframes.removeLockedAll: Toast shown in Basic mode when Remove keyframe did nothing because all selected marchers use Expert moves on this page, which can only be edited in Expert mode. {count} is how many marchers, such as 1 or 3 (plural form chosen by it). Basic and Expert are the two editing modes; match their names. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.keyframes.spoken: Screen-reader name of a keyframe diamond on the timeline when several marchers are selected: its title, then who has the keyframe. {title} is such as "Keyframe · Page 2, count 8"; {detail} is such as "2 of 3 selected: B1 and B4". A keyframe is a position a marcher is set to reach at that count. Usually keep as is.
timeline.keyframes.title: Tooltip of a keyframe diamond on the timeline, and the first part of its screen-reader label. A keyframe is a position stored for a marcher at a certain count. {page} is the page name, such as "2". {count} is the count number within that page, such as 8. Keep the dot.
timeline.label: Screen-reader label of the timeline's scrolling area, which holds the page boxes, the moves and the playhead.
timeline.loop.endHandle: Screen-reader label of the handle at the right end of the loop bar on the timeline's ruler. The loop bar marks the stretch of the show that plays over and over. {beat} is the beat number (from the start of the show) where the loop ends; arrow keys move it.
timeline.loop.handleTooltip: Tooltip of either end handle of the loop bar on the timeline's ruler (the bar marking the stretch that plays over and over).
timeline.loop.hintIsolated: Second line in the Loop button's tooltip while a move is isolated. A move is one group of marchers traveling between two positions over some counts; isolating it hides everything else on the timeline and keeps playing that move over and over, so looping can't be turned off.
timeline.loop.hintOff: Second line in the Loop button's tooltip while looping is off: turning it on loops the page being edited. A page is one section of the show, from one formation (set) to the next.
