timeline.loop.hintOn: Second line in the Loop button's tooltip while looping is on. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Play shortcut (the Space key) shown as a key cap. "The bar on the ruler" is the colored bar across the top of the timeline that marks the stretch that loops; dragging its ends changes the stretch. Keep the tags.
timeline.loop.label: Screen-reader label of the Loop button in the timeline's transport bar. Looping plays a stretch of the show (the loop region, a bar on the timeline's ruler) over and over.
timeline.loop.off: Tooltip of the Loop button in the timeline's transport bar while looping is off. Looping plays a stretch of the show over and over.
timeline.loop.on: Tooltip of the Loop button in the timeline's transport bar while looping is on. Looping plays a stretch of the show over and over.
timeline.loop.startHandle: Screen-reader label of the handle at the left end of the loop bar on the timeline's ruler. The loop bar marks the stretch of the show that plays over and over. {beat} is the beat number (from the start of the show) where the loop starts; arrow keys move it.
timeline.merge.done: Toast shown after merging one move into another on the timeline. {source} and {target} are names of moves or pages, such as "Move 6" and "Page 3". A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.merge.inBoth: Reason shown on a disabled Merge entry in the timeline menu. {count} is the number of marchers that are in both moves, such as 1 or 4 (plural form chosen by it). Merging would give them two moves at once, which isn't allowed. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.merge.menuInto: Menu item in the timeline's right-click menu for a move: merges the selected or clicked move into another. {target} is the name of the other move or page, such as "Move 6" or "Page 3". Verb phrase.
timeline.merge.menuIntoFit: Menu item in the timeline's right-click menu for a move: merges it into another one, and the merged move is resized to the other move's counts. {target} is the name of the other move or page, such as "Move 6" or "Page 3". Keep the dot. Verb phrase.
timeline.merge.menuPair: Menu item for merging one move into another. {source} and {target} are names of moves or pages, such as "Move 6" and "Page 3". Verb phrase.
timeline.merge.menuPairFit: Menu item for merging one move into another, resizing it to the other move's counts. {source} and {target} are names of moves or pages, such as "Move 6" and "Page 3". Keep the dot. Verb phrase.
timeline.merge.noPageMove: Reason shown on a disabled Merge entry. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". That page has no move of its own to merge into. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.merge.noPageMoveUnnamed: Reason shown on a disabled Merge entry, for a page whose name isn't known. That page has no move of its own to merge into. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.merge.page: Words used to name a page inside merge texts. {name} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation). Reads like "Merge into Page 3".
timeline.merge.pickTwo: Reason shown on a disabled Merge entry when fewer than two different moves are chosen. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.merge.thisMove: Words used to name a move inside a message when the move has no name. Lowercase, used mid-sentence, like "Split this move". A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.merge.thisPage: Words used to name a page inside a message when the page has no name. Lowercase, used mid-sentence. A page is one section of the show that ends in a set (formation).
timeline.move.nameField: Screen-reader label of the text field for naming a move on the timeline. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts, drawn as a bar (clip).
timeline.move.nameLimit: Small note above a move's name field on the timeline, shown when the typed name reaches the longest allowed. {count} is the maximum number of characters.
timeline.moveClip.accessibleName: Screen-reader name of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2"; "move" says what kind of item it is; {where} is its stretch of the timeline, such as "Page 3, counts 1–4".
timeline.moveClip.anotherMove: Used inside "Overridden by … on …" when the other move has no name to show. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts, drawn as a bar (clip) on the timeline. Lowercase because it continues a sentence.
timeline.moveClip.overriddenBy: Description of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline, and in the Move card in the inspector, explaining why part of it is drawn dashed: another move takes over all its marchers there. {move} is the other move's name, such as "Move 4"; {where} is the stretch of the timeline, such as "Page 3, counts 1–4".
timeline.moveClip.overriddenSeparator: Separator between several "Overridden by … on …" notes in one move's description. Keep any spaces your language needs.
timeline.moveClip.unnamed: Label of a move's bar (clip) on the timeline when the stored move has no name and isn't numbered as a move, a rare case (a page's own move drawn as a bar). {id} is the move's internal number, such as 12. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions.
timeline.moveDeleted.message: Toast shown after a move was deleted from the timeline. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2" or "Page 3". Followed by an Undo button. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.moveDeleted.withPages: Toast shown after a move was deleted and pages now look different, because marchers that held their positions after the move fell back. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2". {count} is how many pages changed. {pages} is the page names, already written as runs: one name such as "4", a range such as "4–5", or runs joined with commas such as "2, 4–6". Keep the dot. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.moveMenu.delete: Item in a move's menu on the timeline, shown in red. Deletes the move, so its marchers stop traveling along it. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.moveMenu.edit: Item in a move's menu on the timeline (right-click a move's bar, or its ⋯ button). Isolates the move: only its marchers' paths show, and dragging them on the field changes where they end up. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.moveMenu.paused: Reason shown behind a ? next to the unavailable Edit move and Delete move items in a move's menu on the timeline: they can't run while the show is playing.
timeline.moveMenu.rename: Item in a move's menu on the timeline (right-click a move's bar, or its ⋯ button). Opens a text field to rename the move. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.moveMenu.splitAtPlayhead: Item in a move's menu on the timeline. Cuts the move into two moves where the playhead is (the vertical line marking the current moment). A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.moveName.unnamed: A move's label when it has no name and no number to show: in the move's card in the inspector (the side panel) as the name field's placeholder, and inside toasts and menu items that name the move. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. A noun.
timeline.moveSplit.changed: Second sentence of the toast after splitting a move, shown when marchers' paths were redrawn. {count} is how many marchers, such as 3. Their path is now straight before the split point ("it") and starts again after it.
timeline.moveSplit.isolatedOutside: Error toast for Split at playhead (from the command palette) while a move is isolated (shown alone): the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) isn't inside that move, so there is nothing to split.
timeline.moveSplit.message: Toast shown after a move was split in two at one point on the timeline. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2". {where} is the split point, such as "Page 3 count 4" (text made elsewhere). A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.moveSplit.messageAtPlayhead: Toast after Split at playhead cut a move in two, when the playhead's moment has no page name to say it by. The playhead is the timeline's current-time marker. {label} is the move's name, such as "Move 2" or a name the user gave it.
timeline.moveSplit.noneAt: Error toast for Split at playhead (from the command palette) when no move passes the playhead. {where} is the playhead's spot, such as "Page 2 count 8" or "count 3 after Page 4". A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.moveSplit.noneAtPlayhead: Error toast for Split at playhead (from the command palette) when no move passes the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) and its spot has no page name.
timeline.moveSplit.paused: Reason shown on a disabled Split entry while the show is playing: the user must pause first. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.moveSplit.restarted: Second sentence of the toast after splitting a move, when marchers' curved paths keep their curve before the split point and start again after it ("it"). {count} is how many marchers, such as 3. Add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) if it needs them.
timeline.moveSplit.severalAt: Error toast for Split at playhead (from the command palette) when more than one move passes the playhead, so the app can't tell which to split. {where} is the playhead's spot, such as "Page 2 count 8". Right-clicking a move's bar on the timeline offers Split at playhead for that one.
timeline.moveSplit.severalAtPlayhead: Error toast for Split at playhead (from the command palette) when more than one move passes the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment), so the app can't tell which to split. Right-clicking a move's bar offers Split at playhead for that one.
timeline.moveSplit.withNote: Toast after splitting a move when some marchers' paths had to be redrawn: the split message, then a note after a middle dot. {message} is such as "Split Move 2 at Page 3 count 4"; {note} is such as "3 marchers' paths are redrawn: straight before it, restarted after". Usually keep as is.
timeline.page.contextMenu.subsetToggle: Switch item in a page box's right-click menu on the timeline. Marks the page as a subset: a page that splits a longer page into parts, usually named with a letter such as "2A", instead of getting its own number.
timeline.page.homeTooltip: Tooltip of the first box on the timeline's ruler (home). Home is the start of the show, where the marchers stand in the first page's set (formation) before anything moves. {page} is the first page's name, such as "0" or "1".
timeline.page.label: Screen-reader label of a page's box on the timeline's ruler, and in other places that name a page. A page is a section of the show ending in a set (formation). {pageName} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A".
timeline.pageFlag.gripLabel: Screen-reader label of the grip on a page flag on the timeline's ruler. A page flag is the marker where a page ends and the marchers reach that page's set (formation). {page} is the page's name, such as "3"; {counts} is the page's length in counts (beats).
timeline.pageFlag.gripTooltip: Tooltip of the grip on a page flag on the timeline's ruler. A page flag is the marker where a page ends. Dragging it makes this page longer and the next page shorter by the same number of counts (or the reverse); other page flags don't move. {page} is the page's name, such as "3".
timeline.pageFlag.readoutLine: One line of the readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline: how a page's length in counts (beats) changes. {page} is the page's name, such as "3"; {before} is its counts before the drag, {after} its counts if the flag is dropped here. A page flag is the marker where a page ends; moving it lengthens one page and shortens the next.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.home: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, naming what stops it: the start of the show (home, where marchers stand before the first move). A page flag is the marker where a page ends.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.inTheWay: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, saying why it can't go further: a move blocks it. The select picks how the move is named: "page" = a page's own move, {page} is the page's name such as "3"; "named" = a move with its own name, {name}, shown in quotes; "other" = a move without a name to show. Translate each branch; keep the {who, select, …} structure.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.sharesCounts: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, saying why it can't go further: a move already uses those counts (beats). The select picks how the move is named: "page" = a page's own move, {page} is the page's name such as "3"; "named" = a move with its own name, {name} such as "Opener", shown in quotes; "other" = a move without a name to show. Translate each branch; keep the {who, select, …} structure.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.showEnd: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, naming what stops it from going further right: the end of the show. A page flag is the marker on the timeline where a page ends.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.showStart: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, naming what stops it from going further left: the start of the show. A page flag is the marker on the timeline where a page ends.
timeline.pageFlagBlock.startsOrEnds: Readout shown while dragging a page flag on the timeline, saying why it can't move: a move begins or ends exactly on this flag. The select picks how the move is named: "page" = a page's own move, {page} is the page's name such as "3"; "named" = a move with its own name, {name}, shown in quotes; "other" = a move without a name to show. Translate each branch; keep the {who, select, …} structure.
timeline.pagesText.one: One page, named inside a longer sentence (for example in the reason "Every selected marcher is already set on Page 3, …" or the inspector's keyframe hints). {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A".
timeline.pagesText.range: A run of pages, named inside a longer sentence (for example in the inspector's hint "… and Pages 3–5 follow back to the keyframe before it"). {first} and {last} are the first and last pages' names, such as "3" and "5".
timeline.percent: A percentage shown next to a slider or on a zoom button on the timeline (music volume, or how far the beat editor is zoomed). {percent} is a whole number from 0 up, such as 80. Change only the percent sign's form or position if your language writes it differently (for example a space before it).
timeline.playbackSpeed.current: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the playback speed button in the timeline's transport bar (and the 3D View's). {speed} is the speed playing now, written like "1×", "0.5×" or "2×" (times normal speed).
timeline.playbackSpeed.hintClick: Hint line in the tooltip of the playback speed button. A click steps to the next speed in a fixed list (0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×); a right-click opens a small panel with a slider and more speeds.
timeline.playbackSpeed.hintFaster: Hint line in the tooltip of the playback speed button. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard key shown as a key cap (the ] key); while it is held, playback runs twice as fast. Keep the tags.
timeline.playbackSpeed.hintSlower: Hint line in the tooltip of the playback speed button. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard key shown as a key cap (the [ key); while it is held, playback runs at half speed. Keep the tags.
timeline.playbackSpeed.holdKeys: Footer line of the playback speed panel (opened by right-clicking the speed button). <faster></faster> and <slower></slower> are replaced by key caps for the ] and [ keys: holding the first plays twice as fast, holding the second at half speed. Keep the tags.
timeline.playbackSpeed.title: Heading of the playback speed panel (opened by right-clicking the speed button in the transport bar), and the screen-reader label of its slider. The speed is how fast the show and music play, as a multiple of normal speed.
timeline.playbackSpeed.value: A playback speed, shown on the speed button next to the timeline's play controls and in its menu of speeds, like a video player's (1× is normal speed, 0.5× half speed, 2× double). {speed} is the number, written in the app's language. Keep it short; change the × sign only if your language writes speeds differently.
timeline.playhead.label: Screen-reader label of the playhead, the vertical line on the timeline marking the current moment. {position} is its position spelled out, such as "Page 3, count 4 of 8, measure 12 beat 2". Arrow keys move it.
timeline.playheadChip.label: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a small chip at the edge of the timeline when the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) has scrolled out of view. Clicking it scrolls back to the playhead.
timeline.playheadChip.text: Text of a small chip at the edge of the timeline, with an arrow, when the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) is out of view. Clicking it scrolls back to the playhead. Keep it short.
timeline.rangeMenu.deletePage: Item in a page box's right-click menu on the timeline, shown in red. Deletes the page (its flag) while every later page keeps its look. A page is a section of the show ending in a set (formation).
timeline.rangeMenu.deleteWithMoves: Item in a page box's right-click menu on the timeline, shown in red. Deletes the page together with its moves (the marchers' travel into that page), so later pages that held its positions change.
timeline.rangeMenu.holdFromPrevious: Item in a page box's right-click menu on the timeline: the "Hold from last keyframe" command. {holdFromPrevious} is the command's name, filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder. It makes the selected marchers stay on this page where the previous page left them (Held).
timeline.rangeMenu.holdFromPreviousNone: Why "Hold from last keyframe" is unavailable, shown next to the disabled menu item. {page} is a page name such as "Page 3". {heldLower} is the lowercase state word "held", filled in by the app. "Partway through a move" means the marcher is in the middle of a move there. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.rangeMenu.setAsShown: Menu item in a page's right-click menu on the timeline: the "Define as shown" command. {defineAsShown} is the command's name, filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder. It gives the selected marchers their current on-field positions as their own on that page (Defined), so they stop showing an earlier page's position. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.rangeMenu.splitHold: Menu item in the right-click menu of a hold bar on the timeline: the "Split hold here" command. {splitHold} is the command's name, filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder. It ends the selected marchers' hold at the count that was right-clicked; after it they are Not defined, so an edit there starts a new move. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.rangeMenu.setAsShownError: Error toast shown when "Set as shown" fails for an unexpected reason. "Set as shown" is a menu command on a page of the timeline that stores the selected marchers' current on-field positions as fixed (set) positions on that page.
timeline.rangeMenu.setAsShownNone: Why "Define as shown" is unavailable, shown next to the disabled menu item. {page} is a page name such as "Page 3". {definedLower} and {heldLower} are the lowercase state words "defined" and "held", filled in by the app. "Partway through a move" means the marcher is in the middle of a move there. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.rangeName.afterPage: Name of a stretch of the timeline past the show's last page flag, where a new page would be written. {page} is the last page's name; {from} and {to} are counts after that page's flag, starting at 1. Shown in the line over the field and the isolation bar.
timeline.rangeName.beat: Name of a spot on the timeline that isn't inside any page, by its beat number from the start of the show. {beat} is a whole number. Shown in the line over the field and the isolation bar.
timeline.rangeName.beats: Name of a stretch of the timeline that isn't inside named pages, by beat numbers from the start of the show. {from} and {to} are whole numbers.
timeline.rangeName.flag: Name of a spot on the timeline: exactly on a page's flag. A page flag is the marker on the timeline where a page ends and the marchers reach that page's set (formation). {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". Shown in the line over the field, in the isolation bar and in move details, often inside another sentence such as "Editing …".
timeline.rangeName.pageCount: Name of a spot or a one-count stretch on the timeline: one count (beat) inside a page. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A"; {count} is the count within that page, starting at 1. Shown in the line over the field, the isolation bar and move details, often inside another sentence.
timeline.rangeName.pageCounts: Name of a stretch of the timeline inside one page. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A"; {from} and {to} are the first and last counts (beats) of the stretch within that page, starting at 1.
timeline.rangeName.pageMove: Name of a stretch of the timeline that is exactly one page: that page's move, where the marchers travel from the previous page's set (formation) to this page's set. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". Shown in the line over the field, the isolation bar and move details, often inside another sentence.
timeline.rangeName.pageToPage: Name of a stretch of the timeline that crosses a page flag (from inside one page into the next). {fromPage} and {toPage} are page names, such as "2" and "3"; {from} and {to} are counts within those pages, starting at 1.
timeline.rangeName.pages: Name of a stretch of the timeline covering several whole pages. {from} and {to} are the first and last pages' names, such as "2" and "4". Shown in the line over the field, the isolation bar and move details.
timeline.readout.home: Position readout in the timeline's transport bar when the playhead is at home: the start of the show, where marchers stand before the first move. Keep it very short.
timeline.readout.measure: Short readout in the timeline's transport bar: the music's measure and beat under the playhead. "m" abbreviates measure (bar of music). {measure} is the measure number; {beat} the beat within that measure.
timeline.readout.pageCount: Very short position readout in the timeline's transport bar: the page and count under the playhead. "Pg" abbreviates page and "ct" abbreviates count (a beat within the page). {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A"; {count} is the count within the page. Use short abbreviations; it sits in a narrow box.
timeline.readout.pageCountOf: Very short position readout in the timeline's transport bar: the page and count under the playhead. "Pg" abbreviates page and "ct" abbreviates count (a beat within the page). {page} is the page's name; {count} is the count within the page and {total} the page's length in counts. Use short abbreviations; it sits in a narrow box.
timeline.readout.pastEnd: Very short position readout in the timeline's transport bar when the playhead is past the end of the show's last page. {count} is how many counts (beats) past the end. Keep it about this short; it sits in a narrow box.
timeline.readout.spoken.home: Screen-reader version of the playhead position when it is at home (the start of the show, before the first move). {page} is the name of the first page, such as "0" or "1".
timeline.readout.spoken.pageCount: Screen-reader version of the playhead position: the page and the count (beat within that page). {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A"; {count} the count within it.
timeline.readout.spoken.pageCountOf: Screen-reader version of the playhead position: the page, the count (beat within that page) and the page's length. {page} is the page's name; {count} the count within it; {total} the page's length in counts.
timeline.readout.spoken.pastEnd: Screen-reader version of the playhead position when it is past the end of the show's last page. {count} is how many counts (beats) past the end.
timeline.readout.spoken.withMeasure: Screen-reader version of the playhead position with the music's measure. {where} is the page part, such as "Page 3, count 4 of 8"; {measure} is the measure (bar of music) number and {beat} the beat within that measure.
timeline.readout.withMeasure: The playhead's position in one line, joining the page part (such as "Pg 3 · ct 4/8") and the measure part (such as "m12 beat 2") with a middle dot. Usually keep as is.
timeline.refusals.casting.alreadyIn: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when some selected marchers are already in the transition. {count} is how many of them are. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.casting.alreadyInSlot: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when the user moves a marcher to the slot it already has. {slot} is the slot's number.
timeline.refusals.casting.alreadyNearest: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when recasting by nearest slot would change nothing.
timeline.refusals.casting.followTheLeade: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when the user asks to recast a follow-the-leader transition (marchers walking one behind another along a path) by nearest slot.
timeline.refusals.casting.noMarchers: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when the user asks to recast a transition that has no marchers.
timeline.refusals.casting.notEnoughSlots: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when there are fewer empty slots than marchers to cast. {vacant} is the number of empty slots; {marchers} is the number of marchers.
timeline.refusals.casting.selectToCast: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when the user asks to cast marchers into a transition but none are selected.
timeline.refusals.casting.tooManySlots: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Casting decides which slot (place in a formation) each marcher takes in a transition (one group's travel to a formation within a move). Shown when a transition has too many slots for automatic casting. {slots} is its number of slots; {max} is the most automatic casting handles.
timeline.refusals.changesNothing: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when an edit to a marcher's move (its layer, start or end) would leave it exactly as it is.
timeline.refusals.defineAsShown.wholePag: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. {defineAsShown} is the command's name ("Define as shown"), filled in by the app; the sentence starts with it. Shown when the selected counts aren't exactly one page. {counts} names the selected counts, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4", "the counts from Page 2 count 5 to Page 3 count 4" or "these counts".
timeline.refusals.holdFromPrevious.whole: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. {holdFromPrevious} is the command's name ("Hold from last keyframe"), filled in by the app; the sentence starts with it. Shown when the selected counts aren't exactly one page. {counts} names the selected counts, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4", "the counts from Page 2 count 5 to Page 3 count 4" or "these counts".
timeline.refusals.holdEdge.outside: Error message shown in a toast when dragging an end of a hold bar on the timeline is refused. A hold is a stretch where a marcher stays still on purpose (Held). Shown when the dragged end would land past where it may go: the marcher's next move, the end of the show, or less than one count from the hold's other end. Rare: the drag normally stops there by itself.
timeline.refusals.keep.wholePage: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Keep is a command that holds the selected marchers in place for a page (it starts with the command's name, "Keep"). Shown when the selected counts aren't exactly one page. {counts} names the selected counts, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4", "the counts from Page 2 count 5 to Page 3 count 4" or "these counts".
timeline.refusals.members.alreadyIn: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user adds marchers to a move (here called a timeline: a stretch of counts in which marchers travel) and every selected marcher is already in it. {count} is how many of the selected marchers are already in it. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.members.joinPartway: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when adding a marcher to a stretch of counts would make it join another move partway through. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {move} names the other move, such as "Page 2's move" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". {counts} is the stretch being added to, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4". {start} is where the other move starts, such as "Page 2 count 8".
timeline.refusals.members.joinPartwayNoS: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Like the message above, for when the other move's start has no page name to say it by. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {move} names the other move, such as "Page 2's move". {counts} is the stretch being added to, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4".
timeline.refusals.members.notIn: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user removes marchers from a move (here called a timeline: a stretch of counts in which marchers travel) and none of them is in it. {count} is how many marchers were selected. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.members.offField: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when adding a marcher to a move (a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions) would put it further from the field than a show can store (a rare case, far beyond the field's edges). {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {at} says where on the timeline, such as "Page 2 count 8" or "count 3 after Page 4".
timeline.refusals.members.offFieldNoWher: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when adding a marcher to a move (a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions) would put it further from the field than a show can store (a rare case, far beyond the field's edges), at a count that has no page name to show. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3".
timeline.refusals.members.selectToAdd: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user asks to add marchers to a move on the timeline but no marchers are selected.
timeline.refusals.members.selectToRemove: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user asks to remove marchers from a move on the timeline but no marchers are selected.
timeline.refusals.members.wouldReplace: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when adding a marcher to a stretch of counts would swallow a shorter move the marcher is already in. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {move} names that move, such as "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". {counts} is the stretch being added to, such as "Page 2, counts 1–8".
timeline.refusals.merge.fitCollides: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when fitting the source to the target's counts would overlap another move of the same marchers. {source} and {target} name the two moves, such as "Page 2", "Move 3" or "this move". {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3". {other} names the move they would run into. Resize means dragging the move's edges on the timeline.
timeline.refusals.merge.inBoth: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when some marchers are in both moves. {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3" or "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more"; {count} is how many marchers it names. {source} and {target} name the two moves, such as "Page 2", "Move 3" or "this move". The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.merge.itself: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when the source and the target are the same move.
timeline.refusals.merge.pageMove: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when the move being merged away is the move that fills a whole page, which has to stay. {source} and {target} name the two moves, such as "Page 2", "Move 3" or "this move".
timeline.refusals.merge.partway: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when fitting the source to the target's counts would cut off marchers who start or stop partway through the source. {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3" or "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more"; {count} is how many marchers it names. {source} and {target} name the two moves, such as "Page 2", "Move 3" or "this move". Resize means dragging the move's edges on the timeline. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.merge.sameCounts: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Merge moves every marcher of one move (the source) into another (the target) and deletes the emptied one; a move with other counts is first stretched or shrunk (fitted) to the target's counts. Shown when some marchers already have another move over exactly the target's counts. {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3" or "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more"; {count} is how many marchers it names. {other} names that other move and {target} the move being merged into, such as "Move 3" or "Page 2". The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.moveTimeline.tooEarly: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user drags a move (here called a timeline: a stretch of counts in which marchers travel) earlier than the start of the show. {start} is the beat number the move starts on, counted from the start of the show; {count} is how many beats earlier it was dragged.
timeline.refusals.moveTimeline.tooLate: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user drags a move (here called a timeline: a stretch of counts in which marchers travel) past the latest beat a show can have. {max} is that beat number.
timeline.refusals.pageTakeover: Error message on the timeline when the user drags or resizes a move so it would cover exactly the same counts as a page. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels; each page also has its own move. Instead, the user should merge the move into that page's move.
timeline.refusals.positions.fromOtherMov: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user moves a marcher on the field at the end of a move, but another move decides where the marcher is at that moment. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {end} is a moment, worded like "Page 2 count 8". {move} names the other move, such as "Page 3's move" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". The start flag and the playhead are the two markers on the timeline that bound what is being edited.
timeline.refusals.positions.leftMove: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user asks to make a page a stop again for some marchers, but they have already left the long move that passed through it. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions.
timeline.refusals.positions.noMoveEndsAt: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user moves a marcher on the field at the end of a page, but no move of that marcher ends there, so there is no end position to change. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {page} names the page, such as "Page 2" or "this page".
timeline.refusals.positions.notInMove: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user moves a marcher on the field while editing a move (here called a timeline: a stretch of counts in which marchers travel) that the marcher isn't part of. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3".
timeline.refusals.positions.severalMoves: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user moves a marcher on the field while editing a move (here called a timeline) in which the marcher has several moves, so it is unclear which to change. The inspector is the side panel with the selection's details. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3".
timeline.refusals.positions.stopsEarly: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user moves a marcher on the field at the end of a move, but that marcher's part of the move ends earlier. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {stop} and {end} are moments, each worded like "Page 2 count 8" or "home". The inspector is the side panel with the selection's details.
timeline.refusals.resize.memberChange: Shown when resizing a move on the timeline would pass the count where one of its marchers joins or leaves it. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels; a count is one beat of the music.
timeline.refusals.resize.minimum: Shown when the user tries to resize a move on the timeline to zero length. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels; a count is one beat of the music.
timeline.refusals.resize.moveInTheWay: Shown when resizing a move on the timeline would overlap another move of some of the same marchers, so the edge stops at that move. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels.
timeline.refusals.resize.pastShow: Shown when the user tries to resize a move on the timeline past the start or end of the show. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels.
timeline.refusals.resize.sameCounts: Shown when resizing a move on the timeline would make it cover exactly the same counts as another move that shares marchers with it. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels; a count is one beat of the music.
timeline.refusals.resize.wholeCounts: Shown when the user tries to resize a move on the timeline so an edge would land between counts. A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels; a count is one beat of the music.
timeline.refusals.ripple.noCounts: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when an edit to the pages (adding, deleting or moving a page flag) would shift the moves around it so far that one breaks. Here the move would be squeezed to no counts at all. {what} names the move or the marcher's part of it, such as "Page 2's move", "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)" or "marcher T3's part of Page 2's move".
timeline.refusals.ripple.outsideShow: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when an edit to the pages (adding, deleting or moving a page flag) would shift the moves around it so far that one breaks. Here the move would be pushed before the start or past the end of the show. {what} names the move or the marcher's part of it, such as "Page 2's move", "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)" or "marcher T3's part of Page 2's move".
timeline.refusals.shapes.selectToMove: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Shown when the user asks to move marchers into a shape (a line, arc or other formation drawn on the field) but none are selected.
timeline.refusals.split.allSelected: Reason shown on the disabled "Split into new move" item when every marcher of the move is selected, which would only rename the move. {move} is the move's name, for example "Move 3" or "Page 2". A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels.
timeline.refusals.split.followTogether: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split moves some selected marchers out of a move into a new move over the same counts. Shown when the selected marchers march follow-the-leader (one behind another along a path) together with marchers who stay, so they can't be separated. {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3" or "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more"; {count} is how many marchers it names. {others} lists the marchers who would stay, in the same way. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.split.noneSelected: Reason shown on the disabled "Split into new move" item (menus, the Move card and the command palette) when none of the selected marchers is in the move. {move} is the move's name, for example "Move 3" or "Page 2". A move is a block on the timeline in which a group of marchers travels.
timeline.refusals.split.selectToSplit: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split moves some selected marchers out of a move into a new move over the same counts. Shown when no marchers are selected.
timeline.refusals.split.sharedShape: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split moves some selected marchers out of a move into a new move over the same counts. Shown when the selected marchers fill one shape (a line, arc or other formation) together with marchers who stay, so they can't be separated. {marchers} is a list of marcher labels, such as "T1, T2 and T3" or "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more"; {count} is how many marchers it names. {others} lists the marchers who would stay, in the same way. The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.refusals.splitAt.halfTaken: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split at playhead cuts one move into two at the playhead (the timeline's current-time marker). Shown when one of the two halves would have exactly the same counts as an existing move, which isn't allowed. {move} names the move, such as "Page 2" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". Here it is the existing move. {counts} is the stretch of counts, such as "Page 2, counts 1–4".
timeline.refusals.splitAt.nothingAfter: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split at playhead cuts one move into two at the playhead (the timeline's current-time marker). Shown when no marcher in the move travels after the playhead, so the second half would be empty. {move} names the move, such as "Page 2" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". {where} is the playhead's moment, such as "Page 2 count 8".
timeline.refusals.splitAt.nothingBefore: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split at playhead cuts one move into two at the playhead (the timeline's current-time marker). Shown when no marcher in the move travels before the playhead, so the first half would be empty. {move} names the move, such as "Page 2" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". {where} is the playhead's moment, such as "Page 2 count 8".
timeline.refusals.splitAt.outside: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. Split at playhead cuts one move into two at the playhead (the timeline's current-time marker). Shown when the playhead isn't inside the move being split. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. {where} is the playhead's moment, such as "Page 2 count 8". {move} names the move, such as "Page 2" or "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)".
timeline.refusals.tooFarPastEnd: Error message shown in a toast when the timeline refuses an edit. The show's counts go on past its last page (endless counts), and an edit there first stores the counts it needs. Shown when one edit would need too many new counts at once. {count} is how many counts past the show's end the edit reaches; {max} is the most one edit may add.
timeline.rehearsalMark: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a rehearsal mark tab in the timeline's measure row. A rehearsal mark is a letter or number printed in the sheet music so a group can start from that spot; {mark} is it, such as "C"; {measure} is the measure (bar) number it is on. Clicking it moves the playhead there.
timeline.selection.end: Screen-reader label of the handle at the end of the selected stretch of the timeline.
timeline.selection.endTooltip: Tooltip of the handle at the end of the selected stretch of the timeline. {beat} is the beat boundary (the line between two beats, counted from the start of the show) where the selection ends.
timeline.sound.metronomeOff: Toggle button in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar, while the metronome is off. The metronome is the click track that counts the beats; clicking turns it on.
timeline.sound.metronomeOn: Toggle button in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar, while the metronome is on. The metronome is the click track that counts the beats; clicking turns it off.
timeline.sound.mute: Screen-reader label of the mute toggle in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar.
timeline.sound.muteTooltip: Tooltip of the mute toggle in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar, while the music plays. The metronome (the click track that counts beats) keeps clicking while the music is muted.
timeline.sound.muted: Short status shown in place of the volume percentage in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar while the music is muted. Keep it very short.
timeline.sound.stateMetronomeOff: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the Sound button in the timeline's transport bar. {volume} is the music volume, 0 to 100. The metronome is the click track that counts the beats.
timeline.sound.stateMetronomeOn: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the Sound button in the timeline's transport bar. {volume} is the music volume, 0 to 100. The metronome is the click track that counts the beats.
timeline.sound.stateMutedMetronomeOff: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the Sound button in the timeline's transport bar while the music is muted and the metronome (the click track that counts the beats) is off.
timeline.sound.stateMutedMetronomeOn: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the Sound button in the timeline's transport bar while the music is muted but the metronome (the click track that counts the beats) is on.
timeline.sound.unmuteTooltip: Tooltip of the mute toggle in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar, while the music is muted.
timeline.sound.volume: Screen-reader label of the volume slider in the Sound popup of the timeline's transport bar. It sets the volume of the music and the metronome.
timeline.split.done: Toast shown after marchers were split off into a new move. {count} is how many marchers, such as 1 or 8 (plural form chosen by it). {label} is the new move's name, such as "Move 6". A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.split.drag: Tag shown next to the pointer while dragging vertically on a move to split marchers off it into a new move. {count} is how many marchers would be split off, such as 1 or 8 (plural form chosen by it).
timeline.split.menu: Menu item in a move's right-click menu: takes the selected marchers out of the move and into a new move of their own. {count} is how many of the selected marchers are in this move, such as 3 (English uses the same words for one and many; use your language's plural forms). A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets.
timeline.split.menuNone: Menu item in a move's right-click menu (shown when no count applies, or disabled): takes the selected marchers out of the move and into a new move of their own. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.split.nothingOnPage: Reason shown on a disabled Split entry in a page's menu: no marcher has a move on this page yet. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.split.pageSplitOff: Why splitting is unavailable on a page's box on the timeline: the page has no move of its own, only moves that run across it. A clip is a move's bar on the timeline; splitting a move happens from its clip.
timeline.split.paused: Reason shown on disabled Split and Merge entries while the show is playing: the user must pause first. A move is a marcher group's travel between two sets (formations).
timeline.splitter.label: Screen-reader label of the horizontal divider above the timeline panel. Dragging it (or using arrow keys on it) makes the timeline taller or shorter.
timeline.startFlag.dragTooltip: Tooltip of the start flag on the timeline. The start flag is a marker (a small pennant on a line) at the start of the stretch being edited: when marchers are dragged on the field, their new paths begin at the start flag and end at the playhead.
timeline.startFlag.label: Screen-reader label of the start flag on the timeline: the marker where the stretch being edited begins (where dragged marchers leave from, and where Play starts). {beat} is its beat number from the start of the show; arrow keys move it.
timeline.startFlag.markTooltip: Tooltip of the start flag mark on the timeline when it can't be dragged: Play starts playback from this marker.
timeline.startFlagPositions.always: Heading and option name in the start flag positions popover. The settings under it are used all the time, as opposed to only while the hold key is pressed. Adverb. Keep it short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.buttonLabel: Screen-reader label of the start flag positions button in the field display bar. Starts with the button's name (same as timeline.startFlagPositions.label); {state} is a full summary line of what it shows now, such as "Always · Dots: All · Paths: Selected".
timeline.startFlagPositions.dots: Label of one of two rows in the start flag positions popover (the other is Paths): how many dots to draw for the positions at the start flag (the marker where the editing window begins). Noun, plural. Short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.hold: Name of the start flag positions state that applies while the user holds a key down, used as plain text (a screen-reader label and the block's accessible name in the start flag positions menu). {key} is that key as text, for example N or Shift + N. The start flag is the marker on the timeline where playback starts.
timeline.startFlagPositions.holdHeading: Heading of the second block in the start flag positions menu: the settings that apply while the user holds a key down. Keep <keys></keys>: it is replaced by that key, shown as a keycap (for example P). The start flag is the marker on the timeline where playback starts; this menu chooses which marchers show dots and paths from their positions there.
timeline.startFlagPositions.holdNoKey: Heading and option name in the start flag positions popover when the hold key has been unassigned, so there's no key to name. The settings under it apply only while the hold key is pressed. Verb.
timeline.startFlagPositions.label: Tooltip title, screen-reader label and popover label of the start flag positions button on the field display bar. The start flag is the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins; this button controls dots and paths drawn on the field to show where marchers were at it.
timeline.startFlagPositions.level.all: Option in the start flag positions popover for dots or paths: show them for all marchers. Short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.level.off: Option in the start flag positions popover for dots or paths: show none. Short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.level.select: Option in the start flag positions popover for dots or paths: show them only for the selected marchers. Short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.partLabel: Screen-reader label of an Off/Selected/All switch in the start flag positions menu. {block} is the block's name (which marchers it is about) and {part} is what the switch controls: Dots or Paths.
timeline.startFlagPositions.paths: Label of one of two rows in the start flag positions popover (the other is Dots): how many paths to draw, lines drawn on the field for the positions at the start flag. Also the caption of the button on the field display bar. Noun, plural. Short.
timeline.startFlagPositions.stateLine: Summary line in the tooltip of the start flag positions button on the field display bar, also part of its screen-reader label, for the settings used all the time (Always). The start flag is the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins; this button shows dots and paths for marchers' positions there. {dots} and {paths} select which marchers show dots (positions) and paths: 'all' (All marchers), 'selected' (only the selected marchers) or 'other' (Off, none); translate the variants and keep the select structure and the words all, selected and other before the braces. Keep the dots between the parts. Reads like "Always · Dots: Selected · Paths: Off".
timeline.startFlagPositions.stateLineHol: Second line of the tooltip on the start flag positions button in the field display bar, while the user holds its key down. The start flag is the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins; this button shows dots and paths for marchers' positions there. Keep <keys></keys>: it is replaced by the key being held, shown as a keycap (for example N). {dots} and {paths} select which marchers show dots (positions) and paths: 'all' (All marchers), 'selected' (only the selected marchers) or 'other' (Off, none); translate the variants and keep the select structure and the words all, selected and other before the braces. Keep the dots between the parts.

Summary line in the tooltip of the start flag positions button, also part of its screen-reader label, while the hold settings apply but the hold key has been unassigned, so there's no key to name. The start flag is the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins; this button shows dots and paths for marchers' positions there. {dots} and {paths} select which marchers show dots (positions) and paths: 'all' (All marchers), 'selected' (only the selected marchers) or 'other' (Off, none); translate the variants and keep the select structure and the words all, selected and other before the braces. Keep the dots between the parts. Same start as timeline.startFlagPositions.holdNoKey.

Screen-reader text summarizing the start flag positions button while the user holds its key down: the settings that apply while held. The start flag is the marker on the timeline where the editing window begins; this button shows dots and paths for marchers' positions there. {key} is that key as plain text, for example N or Shift + N. {dots} and {paths} select which marchers show dots (positions) and paths: 'all' (All marchers), 'selected' (only the selected marchers) or 'other' (Off, none); translate the variants and keep the select structure and the words all, selected and other before the braces. Keep the dots between the parts. Reads like "Hold N · Dots: All · Paths: Selected".
timeline.terms.clearThisPage: The name of the "Clear this page" command: it takes the selected marchers' positions off the current page, so they have no position of their own there. One shared word, filled into menus, buttons and messages that name the command; keep it short. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.terms.defineAsShown: The name of the "Define as shown" command: it gives the selected marchers their current on-field position as their own on this page (Defined). One shared word, filled into menus, buttons and messages that name the command. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.terms.defined: State word for a marcher on a page, title case: it has its own position on this page. Shown on its own (a menu item, a bar title) and filled into sentences as an adjective ("is Defined on Page 3"), so it must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.definedLower: The lowercase form of the state word "Defined", for use inside sentences ("make them defined here"). Must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.held: State word for a marcher on a page, title case: it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose. Shown on its own (a bar title, a menu item) and filled into sentences as an adjective ("is Held on Page 3"), so it must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.heldLower: The lowercase form of the state word "Held", for use inside sentences ("Not held:", "already held on Page 3"). Must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.holdFromPrevious: The name of the "Hold from last keyframe" command: it makes the selected marchers stay on this page where their last keyframe left them (Held), and fills any Not defined pages back to that keyframe. One shared word, filled into menus, buttons and messages that name the command. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.terms.notDefined: State word for a marcher on a page, title case: nothing is decided for it on this page yet, so it shows its last position for now. Shown on its own and filled into sentences as an adjective ("is Not defined"), so it must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.notDefinedLower: The lowercase form of the state word "Not defined", for use inside sentences. Must read as an adjective. The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.terms.removeKeyframe: The name of the "Remove keyframe" command: it deletes the selected marchers' keyframe (a position stored on a count), so they go back to the keyframe before it. One shared word, filled into menus, buttons and messages that name the command. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.terms.splitHold: The name of the "Split hold here" command: it ends the selected marchers' hold (a stretch where they stay still on purpose, Held) at the count that was right-clicked on the hold bar, so after that count they are Not defined. One shared word, filled into menus and messages that name the command. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.transport.label: Screen-reader label of the timeline's transport bar: the row of playback controls (play, previous, next, the clock and the position readout), as in audio and video software.
timeline.transport.more: Screen-reader label of the "⋯" button in the timeline's transport bar, shown when the panel is narrow. It opens the controls that didn't fit.
timeline.transport.moreTooltip: Tooltip of the "⋯" button in the timeline's transport bar on a narrow panel. Lists the controls it opens: the sound button, the clock, the Fit button (zooms to show the whole show) and the view controls.
timeline.transport.nextBeat: Name of the Next button while Shift is held, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead forward one beat (count).
timeline.transport.nextPage: Name of the Next button in the timeline's transport bar, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead to the next page. A page is a section of the show ending in a set (formation).
timeline.transport.pauseHere: Name of the Stop button while Shift is held during playback, and a row of its tooltip guide: stops playback and leaves the playhead where it is.
timeline.transport.playFromPlayheadAndCo: Name of the Play button while Shift is held (Shift+Space), and a row of its tooltip guide. Plays from the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment) and keeps going.

Row in the Play button's tooltip guide, same meaning as "Play from playhead and continue". <playhead></playhead> is replaced by a small picture of the playhead; put it right after the word "playhead". Keep the tags.
timeline.transport.playFromStartAndConti: Name of the Play button (or of Alt+Play in Expert mode), and a row of its tooltip guide. Plays from the start flag (the marker where the edited stretch begins) and keeps playing past the playhead.

Row in the Play button's tooltip guide, same meaning as "Play from start flag and continue". <start></start> is replaced by a small picture of the start flag; put it right after the words "start flag". Keep the tags.
timeline.transport.playFromStartAndStop: Name of the Play button in Expert mode, and a row of its tooltip guide. Plays from the start flag (the marker where the edited stretch begins) and stops at the playhead (the vertical line marking the current moment).
timeline.transport.playFromStartAndStopM: Row in the Play button's tooltip guide, same meaning as "Play from start flag and stop at playhead". <start></start> is replaced by a small picture of the start flag and <playhead></playhead> by a small picture of the playhead; put each right after the word it illustrates. Keep the tags.
timeline.transport.playLoop: Name of the Play button while looping is on, and a row of its tooltip guide: plays the loop (the stretch marked by the loop bar) over and over.
timeline.transport.playLoopOnce: Name of the Play button while Shift is held and looping is on, and a row of its tooltip guide: plays the loop's stretch one time.
timeline.transport.previousBeat: Name of the Previous button while Shift is held, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead back one beat (count).
timeline.transport.previousPage: Name of the Previous button in the timeline's transport bar, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead back to the previous page. A page is a section of the show ending in a set (formation).
timeline.transport.showEnd: Name of the Next button while Alt (Option on a Mac) is held, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead to the end of the show.
timeline.transport.showStart: Name of the Previous button while Alt (Option on a Mac) is held, and a row in its tooltip guide: moves the playhead to the start of the show.
timeline.transport.stopAndGoBack: Name of the Stop button (the Play button while playing), and a row of its tooltip guide: stops playback and returns the playhead to where Play was pressed.
timeline.waveform.label: Screen-reader label of the music's waveform (the picture of the music's loudness over time) drawn along the timeline.
timeline.where.aMove: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a move that can't be named otherwise. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.afterPageCount: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a stretch of one count past the show's last page flag, as "after Page 4, count 3". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.afterPageCounts: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a stretch of counts past the show's last page flag, as "after Page 4, counts 1–4". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". {from} and {to} are count numbers after the last page. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.anotherMove: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a move that has no name and no page to say it by. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.beat: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a moment by its beat number, used only where the moment has no page to say it by. {beat} is the beat number counted from the start of the show. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.countAfterPage: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names one moment past the show's last page flag: count {count} after the last page, as "count 3 after Page 4". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.countToCount: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a stretch of counts that crosses a page flag, as "Page 2 count 5 to Page 3 count 4". {from} and {to} are moments, each worded like "Page 2 count 5" or "count 3 after Page 4".
timeline.where.countsFromTo: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. The object of a sentence for a stretch of counts that crosses a page flag, as in "… only partly overlaps the counts from Page 2 count 5 to Page 3 count 4". {from} and {to} are moments, each worded like "Page 2 count 5". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.home: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names the very start of the show, before the first page's counts: where every marcher stands at the beginning (their home positions). Lowercase because it is used inside sentences, as in "stops at home".
timeline.where.inPageCount: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a stretch of one count inside one page, as "Page 2, count 3". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". {count} is the count number within the page.
timeline.where.inPageCounts: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a stretch of counts inside one page, as "Page 2, counts 1–4". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". {from} and {to} are the first and last count numbers within the page.
timeline.where.marcher: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a marcher that has no label to say it by, by its number. {marcher} is the marcher's number. Used inside lists and sentences.
timeline.where.marcherPart: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names one marcher's share of a move, as "marcher T3's part of Page 2's move". {marcher} is the marcher's label, such as "T3". {move} names the move, such as "Page 2's move" or "a move".
timeline.where.moreMarchers: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. The last item of a shortened list of marchers, as in "T1, T2, T3 and 4 more". {count} is how many marchers the list leaves out.
timeline.where.moveAfter: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names an unnamed move past the show's last page flag, as "the move after Page 4, counts 1–4". {where} is the stretch of counts and starts with "after", such as "after Page 4, counts 1–4". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.moveFromTo: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names an unnamed move that crosses a page flag, as "the move from Page 2 count 13 to Page 3 count 4". {from} and {to} are moments, each worded like "Page 2 count 13". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.moveOn: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names an unnamed move inside one page, as "the move on Page 2, counts 9–12". {where} is the stretch of counts, such as "Page 2, counts 9–12". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.movesAt: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a move by its name, with where it is in brackets, as "Move 2 (Page 2, counts 1–4)". {names} is the move's name ("Move 2" or a name the user gave it), or several names joined as a list when moves share the range. {where} is a stretch of counts such as "Page 2, counts 1–4".
timeline.where.page: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a page, or the move that fills exactly one page, as "Page 2". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". It is inserted into other messages, so keep it a short noun phrase.
timeline.where.pageCount: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names one moment: the end of count {count} of a page, as "Page 2 count 8". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". {count} is the count number within the page (counts are the music's beats as marchers step them).
timeline.where.pageMove: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names the move that fills exactly one page (its 'page move'), inside a sentence such as "T3 is in Page 2's move". {page} is a page's name, such as "2" or "2A". A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions.
timeline.where.theseCounts: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. The object of a sentence for a stretch of counts that has no page name to say it by, as in "… inside these counts". Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.thisMove: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names a move that has no name to say it by. A move is a stretch of counts in which marchers travel to new positions. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.where.thisPage: Part of a message on the timeline (a refusal, toast or readout) that says where something is, in pages and counts. Names the page being edited when it has no name to say it by. Lowercase because it is used inside sentences.
timeline.windowCount.length: Small label on the timeline next to the selected stretch, giving its length in counts (beats) when it isn't inside one page (for example past the show's last page).
timeline.windowCount.one: Small label on the timeline next to the selected stretch, when it is one count inside a page. {count} is that count (beat) within the page, starting at 1.
timeline.windowCount.range: Small label on the timeline next to the selected stretch, when it lies inside one page. {from} and {to} are its first and last counts (beats) within that page, starting at 1.
timeline.windowLine.addPageHere: Line over the field in Basic mode when the playhead is past the show's last page, so dragging marchers can't edit anything there. The playhead is the vertical line on the timeline marking the current moment; its right-click menu can add a page.
timeline.windowLine.afterPaused: Screen-reader sentence for the line over the field after playback paused on another page. {paused} is a note such as "Paused on page 3"; {rest} is what a drag edits now, such as "Editing Page 3's move".
timeline.windowLine.countOfPage: Used inside "Editing …" in the line over the field (Basic mode): a position partway through a page. {count} is the count (beat) within the page, starting at 1; {page} is the page's name. Lowercase because it continues the sentence.
timeline.windowLine.editing: Line over the field saying what dragging marchers on the field changes now. {name} is a stretch or spot of the timeline, such as "Page 2's move", "page 3", "count 4 of page 2" or "home positions".
timeline.windowLine.editingThrough: Screen-reader sentence for the line over the field when the edited stretch passes page flags. {editing} is the sentence such as "Editing Pages 2–4"; {sets} is a list such as "set 3" or "sets 3 and 4" (sets are formations at page ends).
timeline.windowLine.home: Used inside "Editing …" in the line over the field: the marchers' home positions, where they stand before the show's first move. Lowercase because it continues the sentence.
timeline.windowLine.loops: Badge at the end of the line over the field while looping is on somewhere other than what is being edited. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Play key (Space) shown as a key cap; {loop} is the looping stretch of the timeline, such as "Page 2's move". Keep the tags.
timeline.windowLine.moveAt: Used inside "Editing …" in the line over the field: a move and where it is. {move} is the move's name, such as "Move 2"; {where} is its stretch of the timeline, such as "Page 2, counts 1–8". A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
timeline.windowLine.page: Used inside "Editing …" in the line over the field (Basic mode): a whole page. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A". Lowercase because it continues the sentence.
timeline.windowLine.passedSets: Used as {sets} inside "through …" texts in the line over the field (see timeline.windowLine.through and timeline.windowLine.editingThrough): the sets the edited stretch passes through. A set is the formation the marchers reach at the end of a page. {count} is how many sets. {names} is their page names, already joined as a list in your language, such as "3", "3 and 4" or "3, 4 and 5". Lowercase because it continues the sentence; a noun phrase, so the surrounding text can stay one sentence.
