The "=1" branch is the wording for exactly one and "other" is for every other number; add your language's own plural forms (one, few, many) only if it needs them for numbers other than 1.
timeline.windowLine.pausedAfterLast: Note in the line over the field after playback was paused past the show's last page, where no page exists yet.
timeline.windowLine.pausedOnPage: Note in the line over the field after playback was paused on a different page than it started on, so the user knows a drag now edits that page. {page} is the page's name, such as "3" or "2A".
timeline.windowLine.pausedPrefix: Bold start of the line over the field after playback paused on another page. {paused} is a short note such as "Paused on page 3"; the middle dot separates it from the rest of the line (what dragging marchers edits).
timeline.windowLine.through: Part of the line over the field when the edited stretch of the timeline passes page flags, so a drag changes the marchers' paths through those sets too. {sets} is a list such as "set 3" or "sets 3 and 4". The middle dot separates it from the text before it.
timeline.windowLine.withLoop: Screen-reader sentence for the line over the field while looping is on somewhere other than what is being edited. {rest} is the sentence before it, such as "Editing Page 3's move"; {key} is the name of the Play key ("Space"); {loop} is the looping stretch, such as "Page 2's move".
timeline.zoom.hint: Second line of the tooltip on the timeline's Zoom in and Zoom out buttons: the other ways to zoom, pinching on a trackpad or scrolling while holding a key. <keys></keys> is replaced by that key and the word for scrolling, shown as a key (Command + scroll on a Mac, Ctrl + scroll elsewhere).
timeline.zoom.in: Tooltip name of a magnifying-glass button in the timeline's transport bar (shown in tempo mode): zooms the timeline in one step, so each count is drawn wider.
timeline.zoom.out: Tooltip name of a magnifying-glass button in the timeline's transport bar (shown in tempo mode): zooms the timeline out one step, so more of the show fits in view.
titlebar.bugReport: Title bar button, tooltip and screen-reader label that opens the form (in the web browser) for reporting a bug or sending feedback about OpenMarch. On narrow windows only an icon is shown. Verb phrase.
titlebar.databasePathError: Title of an error dialog shown in the title bar when OpenMarch couldn't find the path of the open show file (a .dots file, which is a database).
titlebar.databasePathError.description: Body of the error dialog shown when OpenMarch couldn't find the path of the open show file. '.dots' is OpenMarch's file extension; do not translate it. Contains blank lines (\n\n) between three short paragraphs: what failed, what to do first (fully quit and reopen the app), and when to contact support.
titlebar.databasePathError.dismiss: Button that closes the database path error dialog. Verb.
titlebar.databasePathUnavailable: Shown in the middle of the window's title bar, where the open show's file name normally appears, when OpenMarch can't find out which file is open. ".dots" is the OpenMarch show file format; keep it as is.
titlebar.menu: Screen-reader label of the title bar's menu button (the hamburger icon) that opens the application menu. Noun.
titlebar.reload: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the title bar button that reloads the app window, which is a troubleshooting step. Verb.
titlebar.webBadge: Small badge next to the version number in the title bar of the web (browser) version of OpenMarch. Clicking it opens a dialog explaining how the web version differs from the desktop app. One short word.
titlebar.window.close: Screen-reader label of the window's close button (an icon of an X) at the right end of the title bar, on Windows and Linux. Closes the window.
titlebar.window.maximize: Screen-reader label of the window's maximize button (an icon of a square) at the right end of the title bar, on Windows and Linux. It also restores a maximized window to its earlier size.
titlebar.window.minimize: Screen-reader label of the window's minimize button (an icon of a dash) at the right end of the title bar, on Windows and Linux.
toolbar.alignment.clearThisPage: Menu item under "Place selected marchers" or "Place all marchers": the "Clear this page" command, which takes the marchers' positions off this page. {clearThisPage} is the command's name, filled in by the app; keep it as a placeholder.
toolbar.alignment.lockMarchersAriaLabel: Screen-reader label of the toolbar group that holds the Lock X, Lock Y and Snap toggle buttons, which control how dragged marchers move and snap on the field.
toolbar.alignment.lockXCaption: Short caption under the Lock X toolbar button's icon, shown only in the touch layout (no hover tooltips). Locks marchers' side-to-side (X) movement. Keep it very short.
toolbar.alignment.lockYCaption: Short caption under the Lock Y toolbar button's icon, shown only in the touch layout (no hover tooltips). Locks marchers' up-down (Y) movement. Keep it very short.
toolbar.alignment.placeAllMarchers: Label of a dropdown button in the Alignment toolbar tab. Its menu offers copying every marcher's position from the previous or next page onto the current page. Verb phrase.
toolbar.alignment.placeSelectedMarchers: Button that opens a menu in the marcher inspector and the alignment toolbar. Its menu items finish the phrase ("...to previous page positions", "...to next page's spots"): it moves the selected marchers to where they stand on another page.
toolbar.alignment.setMarcherPositionsAri: Screen-reader label of the toolbar section holding the "Place all marchers" menu, which moves every marcher to where they stand on the previous or next page.
toolbar.alignment.snapCaption: Short caption under the Snap to grid toolbar button's icon, shown only in the touch layout (no hover tooltips). Rounds the selected marchers' positions to the nearest grid step. Keep it short.
toolbar.alignment.snapToggleCaption: Short caption under the Snap toggle button's icon, shown only in the touch layout (no hover tooltips). Snap makes dragged marchers jump to grid steps and guides. Noun. Keep it very short.
toolbar.alignment.toNextPageSpots: Menu item under "Place selected marchers" or "Place all marchers", continuing that phrase (the leading dots show that). Moves the marchers to the spots they stand on at the next page; a spot is a marcher's position on the field.
toolbar.collisions.collisionsToolbar: Screen-reader label for the Collisions toolbar section, which lists marchers who are too close together on the current page.
toolbar.collisions.distance: Distance between two colliding marchers, in one row of the collisions list. {distance} is a number with one decimal place, measured in steps (a marching step is the unit of distance on the field).
toolbar.collisions.found: Heading in the Collisions toolbar section. {count} is how many pairs of marchers are too close together (colliding) on the selected page.
toolbar.collisions.foundOnNextPage: Line under the heading of the pop-up listing colliding marchers (pairs of marchers too close together). {count} is how many pairs there are.
toolbar.collisions.position: Where on the field two marchers collide, in one row of the collisions list. {x} and {y} are field coordinates in steps (a marching step is the unit of distance), each with one decimal place.
toolbar.collisions.review: Button in the Collisions toolbar section that opens a list of the pairs of marchers who are too close together (colliding).
toolbar.collisions.tab: Name of a toolbar tab that only appears when marchers are too close together (colliding) on the selected page. Opens the Collisions toolbar section.
toolbar.collisions.title: Heading of the pop-up listing colliding marchers (pairs of marchers too close together). {count} is how many pairs there are.
toolbar.collisions.zoomToReview: Button in the pop-up listing colliding marchers. Zooms and pans the field to show where the collisions are.
toolbar.select.drillPrefixesLabel: Screen-reader label of the list of drill prefixes the user can select by. A drill prefix is the letters at the start of a marcher's drill number (for example "OT" in "OT1"). Selecting one selects all marchers with it.
toolbar.select.familiesLabel: Screen-reader label of the row of chips in the Select toolbar tab that select every marcher in an instrument family (for example brass or woodwinds) at once.
toolbar.select.loading: Shown in the Select toolbar tab while the show's marchers are being read.
toolbar.select.noDrillPrefixesToSelect: Message in the Select tab when there are no drill prefixes to select by (no marcher has one). A drill prefix is the letters at the start of a marcher's drill number, such as "OT" in "OT1".
toolbar.select.noResultsFound: Message in the Select tab's list when the typed search text matches no items (sections, tags or drill prefixes).
toolbar.select.noSectionsToSelect: Message in the Select tab when there are no sections to select by. A section is a group of marchers who play the same instrument or do the same job, such as trumpets.
toolbar.select.noTagsToSelect: Message in the Select tab when there are no tags to select by. A tag is a custom label the user puts on marchers so they can be selected together.
toolbar.select.recent: Label in the Select tab before the most recently used items (sections, tags or prefixes), shown as a quick-pick row. A dash is added after it. Adjective used as a heading.
toolbar.select.searchPlaceholder: Placeholder text of the search box in the Select tab, where the user filters sections, tags or drill prefixes by typing.
toolbar.select.sectionsLabel: Screen-reader label of the list of sections the user can select marchers by. A section is a group of marchers who play the same instrument or do the same job, such as trumpets.
toolbar.select.selectBy.drillPrefix: Option in the Select tab's "Select by" dropdown (also its current value). Selects marchers by drill prefix, the letters at the start of a drill number such as "OT" in "OT1". Short.
toolbar.select.selectBy.family: Option in the Select tab's "Select by" dropdown (also its current value). Selects marchers by instrument family, such as brass, woodwinds or percussion. Short.
toolbar.select.selectBy.section: Option in the Select tab's "Select by" dropdown (also its current value). Selects marchers by section, a group that plays the same instrument or does the same job, such as trumpets. Short.
toolbar.select.selectBy.tag: Option in the Select tab's "Select by" dropdown (also its current value). Selects marchers by tag, a custom label the user puts on marchers. Short.
toolbar.select.selectByText: Label before a dropdown in the Select tab. The dropdown chooses how to select marchers: by section, tag, family or drill prefix. Reads like "Select by: Section".
toolbar.select.tagsLabel: Screen-reader label of the list of tags the user can select marchers by. A tag is a custom label the user puts on marchers so they can be selected together.
toolbar.select.tapMode.add: Option in a two-way switch in the Select tab (touch layout) meaning that choosing a group adds its marchers to the current selection. The other option is Replace. Verb. Keep it short.
toolbar.select.tapMode.ariaLabel: Screen-reader label of the Replace/Add switch in the Select tab (touch layout), which decides what tapping a group (a section, tag or prefix) does to the current selection.
toolbar.select.tapMode.replace: Option in a two-way switch in the Select tab (touch layout) meaning that choosing a group replaces the current selection with that group's marchers. The other option is Add. Verb. Keep it short.
toolbar.settings: Label of a button in the File toolbar tab that opens the app's settings dialog. "App Settings" means the settings of the application, not of the current show.
toolbar.view.labels: Label of the field display bar's marcher-labels button and popover heading. It chooses what text is drawn on each marcher on the field: drill numbers, plain numbers, automatic, or nothing. Noun (plural).
toolbar.view.labelsAuto: Option in the marcher labels choice on the field display bar. The app picks what to show and uses smaller text when marchers are crowded together.
toolbar.view.labelsNames: Option in the marcher labels choice on the field display bar. Shows each marcher's full drill number, such as "OT1" (the section prefix and number). Despite the key name these are not personal names.
toolbar.view.labelsNumbers: Option in the marcher labels choice on the field display bar. Shows only the number part of each marcher's drill number (for example "1" instead of "OT1").
toolbar.view.labelsOff: Option in the marcher labels choice on the field display bar. Draws no text on the marchers. Short.
toolbar.view.nextPaths: Label of a switch in the start flag positions popover. When on, lines on the field preview where the marchers go on the next page. A keyboard shortcut cap may follow it.
toolbar.view.shapes: Label of the field display bar's shapes button and popover heading. It chooses when the outlines of placed shapes (boxes, circles and so on that marchers stand along) are drawn on the field. Noun (plural).
toolbar.view.shapesAlways: Option in the shape outlines choice on the field display bar: always draw the outlines of placed shapes. Short.
toolbar.view.shapesOff: Option in the shape outlines choice on the field display bar: never draw the outlines of placed shapes. Short.
toolbar.view.shapesSelected: Option in the shape outlines choice on the field display bar: draw a placed shape's outline only while that shape is selected. Short.
touch.modifiers.add: Short label (with an icon) of a toggle button on the tablet modifier bar; the screen-reader label is the same text. While on, tapping marchers adds them to the selection instead of replacing it. Verb, a few characters wide.
touch.modifiers.addHint: Tooltip of the Add toggle on the tablet modifier bar. "Hold" means keep a finger on the button while another finger or the Apple Pencil works; "tap to keep on" latches it on until tapped again. Marchers are the dots on the field.
touch.modifiers.constrain: Short label of a toggle button on the tablet modifier bar. While on, drags are constrained: equal spacing, movement along one axis only. The label is the English word "equal" (the keyboard Shift role); keep it short.
touch.modifiers.constrainHint: Tooltip of the Equal toggle on the tablet modifier bar. "Hold" means keep a finger on the button while another finger or the Apple Pencil works; "tap to keep on" latches it on. Describes what it changes: spacings come out equal, a move stays on one axis, and scaling a shape flips between proportional and free.
touch.modifiers.explain.add: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the Add toggle on the tablet modifier bar. Marchers are the dots on the field.
touch.modifiers.explain.constrain: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the Equal toggle on the tablet modifier bar. Describes what it does: spacings come out equal, moving stays on one axis, and it flips whether scaling keeps proportions.
touch.modifiers.explain.fine: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the Fine toggle on the tablet modifier bar. Half steps are the grid marchers normally snap to; "leave the half steps but still catch lines" means shapes move freely yet still snap to yard lines; turns then go by 1 degree instead of larger jumps.
touch.modifiers.explain.fromCenter: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the From center toggle on the tablet modifier bar. A box is a shape of marchers drawn by dragging.
touch.modifiers.explain.grip: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the grip (dotted handle) on the tablet modifier bar. The bar can be dragged to another spot on the screen.
touch.modifiers.explain.help: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the question-mark button on the tablet modifier bar. Very short: the button opens a list of gestures.
touch.modifiers.explain.snap: Explanation shown in a small bubble when the user long-presses the Snap off button on the tablet modifier bar. Snap makes marchers and shapes land on whole and half steps and field lines; the button switches that on or off.
touch.modifiers.fine: Short label (with an icon) of a toggle button on the tablet modifier bar; the screen-reader label is the same text. While on, drags are fine: slower and not tied to the step grid. Adjective, a few characters wide.
touch.modifiers.fineHint: Tooltip of the Fine toggle on the tablet modifier bar. "Hold" means keep a finger on the button while another finger or the Apple Pencil works; "tap to keep on" latches it on. Half steps are the grid marchers normally snap to; turns normally go in larger jumps.
touch.modifiers.fromCenter: Short label (with an icon) of a toggle button on the tablet modifier bar; the screen-reader label is the same text. While on, boxes are drawn and resized outward from their center instead of from a corner.
touch.modifiers.fromCenterHint: Tooltip of the From center toggle on the tablet modifier bar. "Hold" means keep a finger on the button while another finger or the Apple Pencil works; "tap to keep on" latches it on. A box is a shape of marchers drawn by dragging.
touch.modifiers.grip: Screen-reader label of the dotted handle at the left of the tablet modifier bar. The user drags the handle to move the whole bar to another place.
touch.modifiers.gripTitle: Tooltip of the dotted handle at the left of the tablet modifier bar (hover or long press). Tells the user to drag it to move the bar.
touch.modifiers.help: Screen-reader label of the question-mark button at the end of the tablet modifier bar. Opens a short list explaining each button.
touch.modifiers.helpList.add: One line of the help list opened by the question-mark button on the tablet modifier bar. … marks bold text: keep the tags and put each button name inside them. "Snap off" and "Add" are the names of two buttons on the bar; snapping makes marchers land on step positions.
touch.modifiers.helpList.fine: One line of the help list opened by the question-mark button on the tablet modifier bar. … marks bold text: keep the tags and put each button name inside them. "Fine" and "Equal" are the names of two buttons on the bar; Fine gives exact, unsnapped drags and turns, Equal gives equal spacings.
touch.modifiers.helpList.fromCenter: One line of the help list opened by the question-mark button on the tablet modifier bar. … marks bold text: keep the tags and put the button name inside them. "From center" is the name of a button on the bar; boxes then grow from their middle.
touch.modifiers.helpList.toggles: First line of the help list opened by the question-mark button on the tablet modifier bar. … marks bold text: keep the tags around the two verbs. Explains the two ways to use a toggle button: tap it to keep it on, or hold it with one finger while dragging with another.
touch.modifiers.noSnap: Label (with a magnet icon) of the toggle button on the tablet modifier bar that turns snapping off. Snapping makes marchers land on whole and half steps and field lines. The button reads "Snap off" and appears pressed while snapping is off; the screen-reader label is the same text.
versionCheck.error.fetchFailed: Error text in the update dialog when checking for the latest version of OpenMarch failed.
versionCheck.error.message: Red error line in the update dialog (which shows the newest OpenMarch release and its notes) when the newest release can't be looked up. {message} is the reason, already translated, for example that the release information couldn't be fetched.
versionCheck.error.noVersion: Error text in the update dialog when no information about the latest version of OpenMarch could be found.
versionCheck.installLinux: Download button in the update dialog for the Linux installer of the new OpenMarch version. 'Linux' stays as is.
versionCheck.installMacArm: Download button in the update dialog for the macOS installer for Macs with Apple chips (M1 and later). 'Apple Silicon' is Apple's name for those chips.
versionCheck.installMacIntel: Download button in the update dialog for the macOS installer for Macs with Intel processors. 'Intel' stays as is.
versionCheck.installWindows: Download button in the update dialog for the Windows installer of the new OpenMarch version. 'Windows' stays as is.
versionCheck.skipVersion: Button in the update dialog. Hides the update notice for this particular version, until an even newer version is released. Verb phrase.
versionCheck.title: Title of the dialog that tells the user a newer OpenMarch version can be downloaded.
versionCheck.trigger: Small clickable text in the title bar that appears when a newer OpenMarch version exists. Opens the update dialog. The exclamation mark draws attention. Keep it short.
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.description: Second line of the 3D View's "open on launch" question card. Settings › General is the app settings section where the answer can be changed later.
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.no: Button answering no to the 3D View's "open on launch" question: the 3D View won't open by itself (it stays open for now).
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.title: Question in a card at the bottom right of the 3D View window, shown each time the window opens until answered: should the 3D View open by itself whenever a show is opened?
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.yes: Button answering yes to the 3D View's "open on launch" question: the 3D View will open by itself with every show.
view3d.camera.blimp: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A high aerial view from the back-left, as if from a blimp above the stadium. Short; the menu truncates long names.
view3d.camera.corner: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the indoor gym venue: a high view from a corner of the room looking down at the floor. In the indoor arena venue: a seat in a corner of the lower level of seating.
view3d.camera.endZone: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A view from a seat behind one end of the field, looking along the field. 'End zone' is the football field area behind the goal line.
view3d.camera.floor: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the indoor gym venue: a view from floor level, at a performer's eye height, looking across the performance floor. Also used in the indoor arena venue.
view3d.camera.frontRow: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A view from a seat in the first row of the stands, closest to the field.
view3d.camera.geJudge: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the indoor gym venue: a view from where a General Effect (GE) judge sits in the bleachers. GE judges score a show's overall impact in competition In the indoor arena venue, the seat is high in the lower level of seating on the front side.
view3d.camera.lowerBowl: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the pro dome venue: a view from a seat in the lower level of the stadium bowl (the ring of seating).
view3d.camera.podium: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A view from a podium, a raised platform near the field, looking out over it.
view3d.camera.pressBox: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A view from the press box, the enclosed booth high in the stands on one side of the field.
view3d.camera.sideline: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the pro dome venue: a view from near the field's sideline at standing height.
view3d.camera.topDown: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. A view looking straight down at the field from above, like the 2D field.
view3d.camera.upperDeck: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the pro dome venue: a view from a seat in the stadium's upper level. In the indoor arena venue: a seat in the upper level of seating on the front side.
view3d.cameras.addView: Button at the bottom of the Cameras panel. Adds a new camera at the current view, i.e. where the 3D camera is now. Its tooltip is 'Save where the view is now as a new camera'.
view3d.cameras.addViewTooltip: Tooltip of the 'Add current view' button in the Cameras panel.
view3d.cameras.alreadyDefaults: Tooltip of the disabled 'Reset to defaults' button in the Cameras panel when the cameras already are the venue's built-in ones. A venue is the 3D setting, such as a stadium or gym.
view3d.cameras.cancel: Cancel button in the Cameras panel's name field (saving a camera profile) and in its confirmation prompts (delete, replace). Closes without changing anything.
view3d.cameras.close: Screen-reader label of the 'x' button that closes the Cameras panel.
view3d.cameras.edit: Menu item in the 3D View's Camera menu that opens the Cameras panel for editing cameras. The ellipsis means it opens a panel.
view3d.cameras.empty: Empty-state message in the Cameras panel when the list has no cameras. 'Move the view' means orbit or pan the 3D picture.
view3d.cameras.full: Tooltip of the disabled 'Add current view' button when the camera limit is reached. {max} is the most cameras a venue can have, e.g. 30. A venue is the 3D setting, such as a stadium.
view3d.cameras.goTo: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the numbered button on each camera row; clicking it flies the view to that camera. {name} is the camera's name, e.g. 'Sideline'.
view3d.cameras.hint: Small help text under the camera list in the Cameras panel. The number on each row is the number key (1 to 9) that jumps to that camera; the view starts on the first camera.
view3d.cameras.moveDown: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the down-arrow button on a camera row. Moves the camera lower in the list, which changes its number key.
view3d.cameras.moveUp: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the up-arrow button on a camera row. Moves the camera higher in the list, which changes its number key.
view3d.cameras.name: Screen-reader label of the text box holding a camera's name on its row in the Cameras panel.
view3d.cameras.newName: Default name for a new saved camera view in the 3D View's Cameras panel, made by 'Add view'. {n} is the smallest number that no camera already uses, so views read Camera 1, Camera 2 and so on. The name is saved with the show and can be renamed.
view3d.cameras.none: Shown in the 3D View's Camera menu when the venue has no cameras.
view3d.cameras.remove: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the trash-can button on a camera row. Removes that camera from the list; an Undo link appears afterwards. Verb.
view3d.cameras.removed: Message shown in the Cameras panel after a camera was removed, next to an 'Undo' link. {name} is the removed camera's name; it appears between curly quotes.
view3d.cameras.replace: Confirm button in the Cameras panel prompt that asks before replacing the current cameras with a profile or the defaults. Verb.
view3d.cameras.reset: Button in the Cameras panel that puts the cameras back to the venue's built-in set. Its tooltip explains it. A venue is the 3D setting, such as a stadium.
view3d.cameras.resetConfirm: Confirmation question before putting the cameras back to the venue's built-in ones. {count} is how many built-in cameras there are, e.g. 6. Plural forms, # is the number.
view3d.cameras.resetTooltip: Tooltip of the 'Reset to defaults' button in the Cameras panel.
view3d.cameras.saveFailed: Error toast shown when saving the show's list of cameras for the 3D View fails. The 3D View is OpenMarch's window that shows the drill in 3D; cameras are saved viewpoints in it.
view3d.cameras.setView: Screen-reader label of the crosshair button on a camera row. Moves that camera to where the 3D view is now. Its tooltip is 'Move this camera to where the view is now'.
view3d.cameras.setViewTooltip: Tooltip of the crosshair button on a camera row in the Cameras panel.
view3d.cameras.title: Title of the Cameras panel, and its screen-reader label. A camera is a saved 3D viewpoint.
view3d.cameras.undo: Link-style button shown briefly after a camera was removed in the Cameras panel. Brings the camera back. Verb.
view3d.keyNames.pair: In the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel, next to the matching 'view3d.keys' text. Two shortcuts that do a pair of opposite things, such as Q (previous page) and E (next page), or Alt+Q (first page) and Alt+E (last page). <first></first> and <second></second> are replaced by the keys shown as keys; keep both tags and their order (the description names the first one's action first). Change the slash if your language separates alternatives differently.
view3d.keys.cameras: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. The number keys jump to the venue's cameras in the order they appear in the Camera menu.
view3d.keys.crowd: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Toggles the crowd (the audience in the stands).
view3d.keys.escape: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Escape cancels picking a seat, closes the settings panel, or leaves fullscreen. A seat pick is the mode where clicking a stand seat moves the camera there.
view3d.keys.firstLast: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Jumps to the first page or the last page of the show.
view3d.keys.fullscreen: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Toggles fullscreen. Noun used as an action label.
view3d.keys.orbit: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Orbit means turning the view around the field, as if circling it. Dragging does this.
view3d.keys.orbitOrRight: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Orbit means circling the camera around a spot.
view3d.keys.panPlain: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Pan means sliding the view across the field.
view3d.keys.zoomOrPinch: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. A pinch is the two-finger trackpad gesture.
view3d.keys.pan: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Pan means sliding the view sideways, which Shift+drag does; dragging with the right mouse button does the same.
view3d.keys.playPause: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. The space bar plays the show or pauses it.
view3d.keys.previousNext: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Moves to the previous page or the next page. A page is one drill set.
view3d.keys.zoom: Explains what the matching key or gesture in the 'Keyboard and mouse' list of the 3D View's View settings panel does. Sits to the right of the key; keep it short. Scrolling zooms the view in and out. Noun used as an action label.
view3d.kit.bighs: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. A larger high school stadium than 'High school'.
view3d.kit.blank: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. Just the field, with no stands or crowd around it.
view3d.kit.college: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. A college football stadium, with a large ring (bowl) of seating.
view3d.kit.gym: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. An indoor gym with a floor and bleachers, for indoor guard and percussion shows.
view3d.kit.hs: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. A typical high school football stadium.
view3d.kit.pro: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. A professional domed stadium, with a roof and two levels of seating.
view3d.lighting.day: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. Daylight. Short.
view3d.lighting.dusk: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. The light at sunset, in between day and night. Short.
view3d.lighting.house: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. Indoor gym only: the house lights, the ordinary bright lights of an arena or gym before the show lights come on.
view3d.lighting.night: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. Night, with stadium lights on. Short.
view3d.lighting.roofClosed: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. Pro dome only: the stadium's roof is closed and it is lit indoors.
view3d.lighting.show: Lighting preset button in the 3D View's View settings panel; the set of presets depends on the venue. Indoor gym only: show lighting, the dimmed room with stage-style lights used while a show is performed.
view3d.open: Small button at the top of the editor that opens the 3D View in its own window. The 3D View shows the show as a 3D scene with marchers and a venue.
view3d.overlay.cameras: Screen-reader label and group label of the Camera menu button in the 3D View. Singular noun; the button itself shows the current camera's name.
view3d.overlay.crowd: Label of an on/off switch in the 3D View's View settings panel, and its screen-reader label, to show the crowd (the audience in the stands).
view3d.overlay.enterFullscreen: Screen-reader label of the fullscreen button in the 3D View, and the action name in its tooltip (the tooltip adds the shortcut, the F key, through actions.tooltipWithShortcut). Makes the 3D View fill the screen.
view3d.overlay.exitFullscreen: Screen-reader label of the fullscreen button while the 3D View is already fullscreen, and the action name in its tooltip (the tooltip adds the shortcut, the F key, through actions.tooltipWithShortcut).
view3d.overlay.freeCamera: Shown on the 3D View's Camera menu button when the viewer has moved the view away from every saved camera, so no camera is selected. 'Free' as in not locked to a camera.
view3d.overlay.lighting: Row label and screen-reader label for the lighting presets (Day, Dusk, Night…) in the 3D View's View settings panel.
view3d.overlay.pickSeat: Screen-reader label of the seat-picking icon button in the 3D View's camera bar. A seat is a place in the stands. Verb phrase.
view3d.overlay.pickSeatTooltip: Tooltip of the seat-picking button in the 3D View. Clicking the button then a stand seat moves the camera to sit there and look at the field.
view3d.overlay.venue: Row label and screen-reader label for the venue picker in the 3D View's View settings panel. A venue is the 3D setting, such as a stadium or gym.
view3d.playback.label: Screen-reader label of the group of playback controls (Previous, Play, Next, speed) at the bottom of the 3D View window.
view3d.quality.autoLowered.panel: Explanation in the 3D View's quality notice when Automatic quality dropped to Low because the view stuttered. 'View settings' (the panel title) and 'Quality' (a row in it) must match those labels; 'High' matches the quality choice.
view3d.quality.autoLowered.settings: Explanation in the 3D View's quality notice when Automatic quality dropped to Low because the view stuttered. 'Settings' and '3D View' name the Settings window and its 3D View section and must match those labels; 'High' matches the quality choice.
view3d.quality.autoLoweredHint: Short line under the Quality choices in the 3D View's View settings panel after Automatic quality dropped to Low. 'High' matches the quality choice.
view3d.quality.dismiss: Button on the 3D View's quality notice card that closes the card. Informal acknowledgement, short.
view3d.quality.software.desktop: Explanation in the 3D View's quality notice in the desktop app: the computer draws graphics in software, with no graphics hardware, so the 3D View stays at low quality and is slow.
view3d.quality.software.web: Explanation in the 3D View's quality notice in a web browser when the browser draws graphics in software. The quoted words 'Settings, System, "Use graphics acceleration when available"' are the menu path in Chrome or Edge; use those browsers' own wording in your language.
view3d.quality.softwareHint: Short line under the Quality choices in the 3D View's View settings panel when graphics run in software and the view stays on Low.
view3d.quality.title: Title of the quality notice card shown at the bottom right of the 3D View window when the view is in low-quality mode.
view3d.readout.count: Readout in the 3D View of the current beat step within the page. {count} is the current count and {total} how many counts the page has, e.g. 'Count 3 of 16'. A count is one beat of a page.
view3d.readout.noPages: Readout in the 3D View when the show has no pages yet. A page is one drill set.
view3d.readout.page: Readout in the 3D View naming the current page. {page} is the page's name, e.g. '4' or '4A'.
view3d.readout.pastEnd: Readout in the 3D View when playback is past the last page of the show. 'END' marks the end of the show and {count} is how many counts past it, e.g. 'END +8'. Keep it very short; shown in a monospace font.
view3d.readout.showTime: Screen-reader label of the elapsed show time clock in the 3D View's readout (minutes:seconds.milliseconds, e.g. 1:23.456).
view3d.settings.awayColor: Label of a color swatch in the 3D View's View settings panel: the crowd color for the visiting team's side of the stands. Next to 'Home'.
view3d.settings.close: Screen-reader label of the 'x' button that closes the 3D View's View settings panel.
view3d.settings.crowdColors: Row label in the 3D View's View settings panel for the two color swatches that set the colors of the crowd (the audience in the stands), 'Home' and 'Visitors'.
view3d.settings.endZoneColor: Label and screen-reader label of a color swatch in the 3D View's View settings panel: the color of the end zones' paint. Single word.
view3d.settings.endZoneText: Screen-reader label of the text box in the 3D View's View settings panel for the lettering painted in the end zones, such as a team or school name.
view3d.settings.endZoneTextPlaceholder: Placeholder of the end-zone lettering text box in the 3D View's View settings panel, shown when it is empty.
view3d.settings.endZones: Row label in the 3D View's View settings panel for the end zones' lettering and color. The end zones are the areas behind the goal lines at each end of a football field.
view3d.settings.graphicsHint: Help text under the 'This computer' heading in the 3D View's View settings panel. It sits above the Quality and Resolution choices.
view3d.settings.graphicsSection: Section heading in the 3D View's View settings panel (web editor) for graphics choices that belong to this computer. Uppercase in the UI; keep it short.
view3d.settings.brassFinish: Row label and screen-reader label for a two-option picker in the 3D View's View settings panel that chooses the metal finish of the brass instruments the band carries (trumpets, mellophones, baritones, tubas and so on).
view3d.settings.tuba: Row label and screen-reader label for a two-option picker in the 3D View's View settings panel that chooses which instrument the Tuba section carries. Plural: the tuba players as a group.
view3d.brassFinish.brass: Option in the 3D View's brass finish picker (a pill button): gold-colored clear lacquer over brass, the usual yellow finish of a brass instrument. Keep it short.
view3d.brassFinish.silver: Option in the 3D View's brass finish picker (a pill button): silver-plated instruments. Keep it short.
view3d.tuba.contra: Option in the 3D View's tubas picker (a pill button): a marching tuba (also called a contra), carried on the left shoulder with the bell pointing forward. Keep it short.
view3d.tuba.sousaphone: Option in the 3D View's tubas picker (a pill button): a sousaphone, the circular tuba worn around the body with a large bell above the head.
view3d.settings.guardUniforms: Row label and screen-reader label for the guard uniform picker in the 3D View's View settings panel. The guard is the color guard, performers who spin flags and equipment.
view3d.settings.homeColor: Label of a color swatch in the 3D View's View settings panel: the crowd color for the home team's side of the stands. Next to 'Visitors'.
view3d.settings.keysSection: Section heading in the 3D View's View settings panel above the list of keyboard and mouse controls. Uppercase in the UI; keep it short.
view3d.settings.title: Title of the 3D View's View settings panel and its screen-reader label, also the tooltip of the button that opens it. Other messages refer to it by this name.
view3d.settings.uniforms: Row label and screen-reader label for the band uniform picker in the 3D View's View settings panel.
view3d.settings.venueHint: Help text under the 'This show' heading in the 3D View's View settings panel. Changes are saved into the show file, and the editor's Undo reverses them.
view3d.settings.venueSection: Section heading in the 3D View's View settings panel for choices saved in the show (venue, lighting, uniforms, crowd). Uppercase in the UI; keep it short.
view3d.uniformPreset.fade: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. A jacket that fades from near-black at the waist to purple at the chest.
view3d.uniformPreset.military: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. Corps-style military look in midnight blue with purple cross belts and silver buttons; 'night watch' as in a guard on night duty.
view3d.uniformPreset.plastron: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. A lilac bib (plastron, the front panel of a jacket) on a purple jacket.
view3d.uniformPreset.prism: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. A jacket split on a diagonal into purple and lavender, like light through a prism.
view3d.uniformPreset.sash: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. A midnight jacket with a purple sash edged in gold; the default guard uniform.
view3d.uniformPreset.signature: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. OpenMarch's own signature look: a purple jacket and shako (a tall military-style hat) with silver trim.
view3d.uniformPreset.westPoint: Name of a built-in uniform design in the 3D View's band uniform and guard uniform pickers (a pill button, two per row). It's a design name in OpenMarch's purple palette, so it may stay in English or be adapted as a name. Academy full dress, styled after the West Point cadet uniform; the default band uniform.
view3d.venue.updateFailed: Error toast shown when changing the venue (stadium, gym or field surroundings) used by the 3D View fails. The 3D View is OpenMarch's window that shows the drill in 3D.
view3d.window.graphicsUnavailable: Message shown in the 3D View window instead of the scene when the computer can't run WebGL, the graphics technology the 3D View needs.
view3d.window.title: Title of the 3D View window (a separate window that shows the show in 3D), shown in the operating system's title bar, taskbar and window list. {showName} is the open show's name, e.g. 'Spring Show 2026'. The long dash separates the two parts.
workspace.editor: Segment of the workspace switch: the normal 2D editor where the user designs formations and movement on the field. Short.
workspace.label: Screen-reader label of the two-way switch at the top of the app that chooses the workspace: Editor or Preview.
workspace.preview: Segment of the workspace switch: a watch-only mode that plays the show without editing it. Short, one word.
web.actionFailed: Error toast in the browser version of OpenMarch when an action on a saved show (rename, duplicate, delete, restore a version) fails. {message} is the technical error text from the browser, in English, for example 'QuotaExceededError'.
web.backUp: Menu item, button and toast action in the browser version of OpenMarch. Saves a copy of the show as a .dots file outside the browser (on iPad it opens the share sheet) so the work is safe elsewhere. Verb phrase; 'Back up' is two words as a verb, not the noun 'backup'.
web.backUpDone: Success toast in the browser version after a show was backed up (saved as a .dots file outside the browser). {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. The curly quotes surround the name.
web.backUpFailed: Error toast in the browser version when backing up a show failed. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'; {message} is the technical error text from the browser, in English. The curly quotes surround the name.
web.backUpNow: Button in the save-status popover in the title bar of the browser version. Starts a backup of the open show: it saves a copy as a .dots file outside the browser (on iPad, via the share sheet). Verb phrase.
web.backUpReady: Toast in the browser version shown when a backup file is prepared but the browser needs a fresh tap before it may open the share sheet or save it. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. A button 'Save backup' appears next to this text.
web.backUpSave: Button inside a toast in the browser version, shown after '“{name}” is ready to back up'. Tapping it saves the backup file (a .dots file) to the device or opens the share sheet. Verb phrase.
web.backedUpAgo: Second line of the save-status button in the browser version's title bar, telling when the open show was last copied to a file outside the browser. {ago} is a relative time produced by the browser in the user's language, such as '3 hours ago' or 'yesterday'.
web.backupReminder: Toast in the browser version, shown at most once a day, reminding the user to back up a show they have been editing for several days. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'; the curly quotes surround it. A 'Back up' button sits next to the text.
web.cantKeepForReload: Alert in the browser version, shown when OpenMarch must reload the page to open a file but the browser refuses to hold the open show for the moment of the reload (typical in Private Browsing). A 'normal window' means a non-private browser window.
web.close: Button that closes the Versions dialog in the browser version. Verb.
web.fileMenu: Tooltip and screen-reader label for the File menu button in the title bar of the browser version. Noun, the menu's name.
web.fileNotOpened: Alert in the browser version when opening a chosen .dots file failed. The show that was already open is left as it was. {message} is the technical error text, in English.
web.gotIt: Button that closes an introduction dialog in the browser version (the welcome dialog or the iPad Home Screen tip). Means 'I understand, dismiss this'.
web.homeScreen.howTitle: Heading in the iPad welcome dialog, above numbered steps that explain how to add OpenMarch to the iPad Home Screen (a Safari feature that puts an app icon on the home screen). 'It' is OpenMarch.
web.homeScreen.note: Note in the iPad welcome dialog. Shows made in an ordinary Safari tab live separately from those in the Home Screen app, so the user should first back them up (Share → Save to Files, the iPad's own menu names) and then open the files in the Home Screen app. Keep 'Share' and 'Save to Files' matching the iPad's wording in the user's language.
web.homeScreen.step1: Step 1 of the instructions for adding OpenMarch to the iPad Home Screen. The Share button is Safari's share icon in its toolbar. A small Share icon image is placed right after the text.
web.homeScreen.step2: Step 2 of the instructions for adding OpenMarch to the iPad Home Screen. “Add to Home Screen” and 'Add' are the labels of Safari's menu item and its confirm button; use the same wording iPadOS shows in the user's language.
web.homeScreen.step3: Step 3 of the instructions for adding OpenMarch to the iPad Home Screen: afterwards use the new Home Screen icon to open the app.
web.homeScreen.title: Title of the welcome dialog that appears when OpenMarch is opened in Safari on an iPad, asking the user to add it to the Home Screen first.
web.homeScreen.why: Intro sentence of the iPad welcome dialog, before three bullet reasons. Explains that adding OpenMarch to the Home Screen is how the user's shows are kept safe on the iPad.
web.homeScreen.why1: Bullet in the iPad welcome dialog explaining why to add OpenMarch to the Home Screen: shows are stored on the iPad itself, not on a server.
web.homeScreen.why2: Bullet in the iPad welcome dialog: Safari may delete a website's stored data, including the user's shows, when the site hasn't been visited for about a week. The Home Screen app is exempt from this.
web.homeScreen.why3: Bullet in the iPad welcome dialog: opened from the Home Screen, OpenMarch fills the screen without Safari's toolbars, like any other app.
web.homeScreen.whyTitle: Heading in the iPad welcome dialog, above three bullet reasons to add OpenMarch to the Home Screen.
web.keptHereNote: Note in the save-status popover and the show list of the browser version. Shows are stored inside the browser itself, not on a server; the user can back up to get a copy elsewhere. Followed on the same line by another sentence (the 'browser may remove shows…' or 'has agreed to keep…' note).
web.leave.memory: Text of a browser confirmation dialog (OK / Cancel) in the browser version, shown when the user is about to close the open show or replace it (for example by opening another file) while it has changes that were never downloaded and the browser can't store it. Two paragraphs separated by a blank line: a warning, then the question. 'Download' means save a copy as a .dots file.
web.leave.noAnswer: Text of a browser confirmation dialog (OK / Cancel) in the browser version, shown when the user is about to close the open show or replace it (for example by opening another file) but the browser's storage gave no reply, so the latest changes may not be stored. Two paragraphs separated by a blank line: a warning, then the question. Same message as web.leave.unsaved, for when there is no error text to show.
web.leave.unsaved: Text of a browser confirmation dialog (OK / Cancel) in the browser version, shown when the user is about to close the open show or replace it (for example by opening another file) but the latest changes could not be stored in the browser. {error} is the reason, a technical error message from the browser in English, for example 'QuotaExceededError'. Two paragraphs separated by a blank line: a warning, then the question.
web.library.backedUpAgo: Line on a show's card in the browser version's show list telling when it was last backed up (copied to a file outside the browser). {ago} is a relative time in the user's language, for example '3 days ago' or 'yesterday'.
web.library.cancel: Button in the Delete and Rename dialogs of the browser version's show list. Closes the dialog without changing anything. Verb.
web.library.copyName: Name given to a duplicated show in the browser version's show list. {name} is the original show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026', so the copy becomes 'Fall Show 2026 copy'. The word 'copy' is a noun; word order may differ.
web.library.delete: Menu item on a show's card in the browser version's show list, opening a confirmation. Verb. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
web.library.deleteConfirm: Red button in the confirmation dialog for deleting a show in the browser version. Permanently deletes the show and its saved versions. Verb.
web.library.deleteDescription: Body of the delete confirmation dialog in the browser version's show list. 'It' is the show named in the dialog title; its 'versions' are the automatic snapshots kept while editing. 'Back it up' means save a copy as a .dots file outside the browser.
web.library.deleteTitle: Title of the delete confirmation dialog in the browser version's show list. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. The curly quotes surround the name.
web.library.duplicate: Menu item on a show's card in the browser version's show list. Makes a copy of the show. Verb.
web.library.edited: Line on a show's card in the browser version's show list telling when the show was last changed. {ago} is a relative time in the user's language, for example '2 hours ago' or 'yesterday'.
web.library.empty: Message in the browser version's show list when no shows are stored yet. A .dots file is OpenMarch's show file format; do not translate '.dots'.
web.library.more: Screen-reader label of the '…' more-actions button on a show's card in the browser version's show list. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. The button opens a menu with Rename, Duplicate, Versions and Delete.
web.library.nameLabel: Label of the text field in the Rename dialog of the browser version's show list, where the user types the show's new name. Noun.
web.library.newerFormat: Warning shown above the browser version's show list when the stored shows were saved by a newer OpenMarch than the one currently loaded. The older version does not touch them. 'The newer version' means the up-to-date OpenMarch the user should open instead.
web.library.notKept: Warning shown above the browser version's show list when the browser refuses to store anything (typical in Private Browsing). The user's work is lost on closing the tab unless they download (back up) it.
web.library.open: Screen-reader label of a show's card in the browser version's show list. Opens that show for editing. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. The curly quotes surround the name.
web.library.openFailed: Error toast when a show in the browser version's show list failed to open. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. 'Back it up' means save a copy as a .dots file outside the browser.
web.library.otherTab: Warning shown above the browser version's show list when another browser tab already has OpenMarch open. Only one tab can manage the stored shows at a time, so the user should use the other tab or close it.
web.library.rename: Menu item on a show's card in the browser version's show list, opening a dialog to type a new name. Verb. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
web.library.renameTitle: Title of the dialog in the browser version's show list where the user changes a show's name. Verb phrase.
web.library.save: Button in the Rename dialog of the browser version's show list. Applies the new show name. Verb.
web.library.tab: Name of the 'files' tab on the start page of the browser version, listing shows stored in the browser. Replaces the desktop app's 'Files' tab. Sits in a narrow side list.
web.library.titleBrowser: Heading above the list of stored shows on the start page of the browser version, used on computers. The shows are stored inside the web browser itself.
web.library.titleIpad: Heading above the list of stored shows on the start page of the browser version when running on an iPad. The shows are stored on the iPad itself.
web.memoryNote: Detail text in the save-status popover of the browser version when the browser doesn't keep shows (private window, or another tab has OpenMarch open). The user must download (back up) the show before closing the tab.
web.neverBackedUp: Second line of the save-status button in the browser version's title bar, and on a show's card in the show list: this show has never been copied to a file outside the browser.
web.notAudioFile: Error shown in the browser version when the file chosen as the show's music isn't an audio file. {name} is the chosen file's name, for example 'notes.txt'. MP3, WAV and M4A are audio file formats; keep them as they are. Straight quotes surround the name.
web.notKept: Short status in the browser version's title bar (next to a warning icon) when the browser doesn't keep shows between visits. Means the open show is not being stored. Small space; keep it short.
web.notPersistedNote: Sentence in the save-status popover of the browser version, shown after 'Your shows are saved here as you work…'. The browser has not promised to keep shows, so it may erase them if disk space runs low or the site goes unused. 'Back up' is a verb: save a copy as a .dots file.
web.notSaved: Short status in the browser version's title bar (next to a warning icon) when saving the show into the browser's storage failed. Small space; keep it short.
web.notSavedFull: Detail text in the save-status popover of the browser version when saving failed because the browser's storage space allotted to OpenMarch is full. 'Back up' means save a copy as a .dots file outside the browser.
web.notSavedOther: Detail text in the save-status popover of the browser version when saving failed for some other reason. {message} is the technical error text from the browser, in English. 'Back up now' refers to the button of that name in the same popover.
web.notShowFile: Error shown in the browser version when the file the user chose isn't an OpenMarch show file. {name} is the chosen file's name, for example 'photo.jpg'. '.dots' is OpenMarch's file extension; do not translate it. Straight quotes surround the name.
web.noticeDismiss: Screen-reader label of the × button that closes a notice bar along the bottom of the page in the browser version of OpenMarch.
web.persistedNote: Sentence in the save-status popover of the browser version, shown after 'Your shows are saved here as you work…'. The browser has promised to keep the stored shows even when disk space runs low.
web.reopenFailed: Notice in the browser version shown after the page reloaded when OpenMarch couldn't open the show that was open before the reload. Reloading the page tries again.
web.repairUnavailable: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside the "Error repairing database: …" message, when the user asks to repair a show file: the repair tool only exists in the desktop app so far.
web.restore: Button next to a saved version in the Versions dialog of the browser version. Brings the show back to that earlier version; the current state is kept as a version too. Verb.
web.restored: Success toast in the browser version after restoring an earlier version of a show. {when} is the version's date, time and relative age, for example 'Nov 1, 2026, 3:45 PM (5 minutes ago)'. 'Versions' refers to the Versions dialog.
web.saveStatusLabel: Screen-reader label for the save status button in the title bar of the web editor. {status} says whether the show is saved (e.g. "Saved in this browser"); {backup} says when it was last backed up (e.g. "Backed up 2 days ago"). Both are full phrases already translated.
web.savedInBrowser: Status in the title bar of the browser version, with a green check, when the show is saved. The show is stored inside the web browser (used on computers; on iPad see 'Saved on this iPad'). Small space; keep it short.
web.savedOnIpad: Status in the title bar of the browser version, with a green check, when the show is saved on an iPad. Small space; keep it short.
web.saving: Status in the title bar of the browser version, with a spinning icon, while the show is being stored into the browser. Present continuous; small space, keep it short.
web.showStaysOpen: Alert in the browser version when closing the current show failed (for example, before opening another file), so it simply stays open. {message} is the technical error text, in English.
web.startFailed: Text that fills the page when the browser version of OpenMarch fails to start. {error} is the technical reason, usually in English, such as "SecurityError: The operation is insecure." OpenMarch is the product name; keep it as is.
web.statusDetailsLabel: Screen-reader label of the popover that opens from the save-status button in the title bar of the browser version. It lists whether the show is saved, when it was last backed up, and the Back up and Versions buttons.
web.storageNotice.lost: Notice bar shown in the browser version of OpenMarch when the browser stops letting it store the open show while the user works (often because the device is out of space). The show is then kept only in this browser tab, and is lost when the tab is closed or reloaded unless the user downloads it.
web.storageNotice.newerFormat: Notice shown when the browser version starts and finds stored shows made by a newer OpenMarch. This older version leaves them untouched, and anything done in this tab is kept only until the tab is closed. 'The newer version' means the up-to-date OpenMarch the user should open instead.
web.storageNotice.notKept: Notice shown when the browser version starts and the browser refuses to store anything (typical in Private Browsing). Work is lost when the tab closes unless downloaded. The suggestion: use a normal Safari tab, or add OpenMarch to the iPad Home Screen, where shows are kept.
web.storageNotice.otherTab: Notice shown when the browser version starts and another tab already has OpenMarch open, so this tab can't store shows. Work here is kept only until the tab is closed or reloaded, unless downloaded.
web.variants.label: Screen-reader label of a switch at the bottom left of the page, shown only in test builds that compare versions of a feature. Testers pick which version of the app to try; the versions' names come from the test.
web.variants.name: Short label before the switch at the bottom left of the page, shown only in test builds that compare versions of a feature; the buttons after it name the versions to try.
web.versionReason.beforeRestore: Label under a saved version in the Versions dialog: this snapshot was made automatically right before an earlier version was restored.
web.versionReason.edit: Label under a saved version in the Versions dialog: this snapshot was made automatically during editing.
web.versionReason.opened: Label under a saved version in the Versions dialog: this snapshot was made automatically at the moment the show was opened.
web.versionsDescription: Explanation at the top of the Versions dialog in the browser version. A version is an automatic snapshot of a show. 'Restoring' brings an older snapshot back; the state before restoring becomes a snapshot too.
web.versionsEmpty: Message in the Versions dialog when a show has no saved versions yet. A version is an automatic snapshot of the show.
web.versionsMenu: Menu item and button in the browser version that opens the Versions dialog for a show (the list of automatic snapshots it can be restored to). Noun used as a label; the ellipsis means a dialog follows.
web.versionsTitle: Title of the Versions dialog in the browser version. {name} is the show's name, for example 'Fall Show 2026'. The curly quotes surround the name.
web.versionsWhen: When a saved version of the show was made, in the Versions dialog of the web editor. {date} is the date and time already written in the app language's style; {ago} is how long ago, such as "3 hours ago".
web.welcome.backUpBody: Paragraph in the welcome dialog of the web (browser) version of OpenMarch, under "Back up regularly". "File → Back up" names the Back up item in the File menu; translate both names the same way as that menu. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard shortcut drawn as keycaps (Ctrl + S, or ⌘ + S on a Mac); keep the tag. A show is a drill design file.
web.welcome.backUpTitle: Heading in the browser version's welcome dialog, above a paragraph explaining that the user should save a copy (back up) of their shows regularly. Verb phrase.
web.welcome.desktopBody: Paragraph in the browser version's welcome dialog. Some features exist only in the desktop (installed) app. Export to PDF and some file tools are missing; export to video works.
web.welcome.desktopTitle: Heading in the browser version's welcome dialog, above a paragraph about features available only in the installed desktop app.
web.welcome.intro: First paragraph of the browser version's welcome dialog. OpenMarch runs locally inside the browser on this device; no sign-in and no data sent to a server.
web.welcome.labIntro: Extra paragraph in the welcome dialog of the web (browser) version of OpenMarch, shown only on the lab site where unfinished features are tried out by testers. A show is a drill design file.
web.welcome.savedBody: Paragraph in the browser version's welcome dialog. Changes are saved automatically; for each show, the most recent 20 snapshots (versions) are kept. 'The start page' is the screen listing all shows.
web.welcome.savedTitle: Heading in the browser version's welcome dialog, above a paragraph explaining that shows are stored on this device.
web.workerError.midChange: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside another message (such as "That didn't work: …" or a question before leaving the page), when the show can't be stored right now because an edit is still being written.
web.workerError.noFileOpen: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch when adding an audio file while no show is open.
web.workerError.noLibrary: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside another message (such as "That didn't work: …"), when the user acts on the list of stored shows in a tab that can't store shows (another tab has them, or the browser refuses to store anything).
web.workerError.noShow: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside another message (such as "Couldn't back up …: …"), when the user backs up a show from the list of stored shows that has since been deleted (for example in another tab).
web.workerError.notSaved: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside another message (such as a question before leaving the page), when the latest changes to the open show couldn't be stored in the browser.
web.workerError.readOnly: Error in the browser version of OpenMarch, shown inside another message (such as "That didn't work: …"), when the user tries to change the stored shows (rename, delete, copy) but they were saved by a newer OpenMarch, which this older version leaves untouched. OpenMarch is the product name.
welcome.description: Text on the start page's empty-state welcome card, shown when the user has no recent shows. Suggests creating a show, looking at the guides, and customizing theme and navigation in the app's Settings.
welcome.examples: Heading above a list of example shows on the start page's welcome card. The user can open an example to try OpenMarch. The 'Or' follows the suggestion to create a new show.
welcome.title: Heading of the start page's welcome card, and title of the browser version's welcome dialog.
welcomeFlow.back: Button in the first-run setup dialog (language, mode, theme). Goes to the previous step. Verb.
welcomeFlow.changeLater: Reassurance line under the choices in the first-run setup dialog (language, working mode, theme). 'Settings' is the name of OpenMarch's settings screen.
welcomeFlow.continue: Button in the first-run setup dialog. Goes to the next step. Verb.
welcomeFlow.dialogLabel: Screen-reader label for the whole first-run setup dialog that appears the first time OpenMarch is opened (choose language, working mode and theme). Imperative.
welcomeFlow.finish: Button on the last step of the first-run setup dialog. Closes it and starts using OpenMarch. Verb.
welcomeFlow.getStarted: Button on the first screen of the first-run setup dialog. Begins the setup. Imperative.
welcomeFlow.language.title: Heading of the language step in the first-run setup dialog. Imperative.
welcomeFlow.mode.title: Heading of the working-mode step in the first-run setup dialog. The choices below are two cards: Basic (simpler) and Expert (all tools). A question.
welcomeFlow.step: Small progress label in the first-run setup dialog. {current} is the number of the step being shown, for example 2, and {total} how many steps there are, for example 4.
welcomeFlow.theme.title: Heading of the theme step in the first-run setup dialog, where the user picks a light or dark appearance for the app. A question.
welcomeFlow.welcome.description: Sentence under the title on the first screen of the first-run setup dialog. Friendly marketing tone; 'the future of design' refers to drill design (planning marching band formations).
welcomeFlow.welcome.title: Title on the first screen of the first-run setup dialog.
welcomeFlow.welcomeBack.description: Sentence under the 'Welcome back' title on the first screen of the setup for people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch. Says that what changed in the app comes next: a short walkthrough of the new features follows (after the language and theme steps, when they are asked), then the last setup question. 'it' is OpenMarch.
welcomeFlow.welcomeBack.title: Large title on the first screen of the setup for people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, greeting them on their return.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.carousel: Screen-reader description of the kind of element for the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. A noun for a set of slides you step through.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.guides: Link on the last slide of the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. Opens the OpenMarch documentation website (step-by-step guides) in the web browser.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.next: Button in the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. Goes to the next slide. Verb.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.position: Screen-reader label for one slide in the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. {current} is the slide's number, for example 2, and {total} how many slides there are, for example 4.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.skip: Button on every slide of the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. Leaves the walkthrough and goes on to the remaining setup questions. Verb.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slide: Screen-reader description of the kind of element for one slide in the optional 'What's new' walkthrough shown to people who used an earlier version of OpenMarch, one new feature per slide with a short looping video. A noun.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.pathways.med: Screen-reader description of the placeholder picture on the 'Pathways' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough, shown before its video exists.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.pathways.tex: Sentence under the title on the 'Pathways' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. The 'Path pen' is the name of a drawing tool; 'corners' are the points where the path turns; a 'marcher' is a band member, who then walks along the path instead of straight to their next spot.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.pathways.tit: Title of the 'Pathways' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough: drawing the route a marcher walks between two formations.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.props.media: Screen-reader description of the video on the 'Props' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. A riser is a raised platform on the field.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.props.text: Two short sentences under the title on the 'Props' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Props' are objects placed on the field (set pieces, platforms); the 'timeline' is the strip under the field showing the show over time. The second sentence says that, in this version, props appear in the 3D View only as plain boxes without detail. 'The 3D View' is the name of a window; keep it as the app names it.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.props.title: Title of the 'Props' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Props' are objects placed on the field such as set pieces and platforms.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.shapes.media: Screen-reader description of the video on the 'Shapes' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Marchers' are band members; a 'section' is a group of them; the field's lines are the yard lines and hash marks.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.shapes.text: Sentence under the title on the 'Shapes' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. You draw a shape on the field and the marchers you selected are placed along or inside it; while drawing, its points jump to the nearest half step (a step is the marching distance unit), the yard lines and the hash marks. 'Box' is a rectangular block formation; an 'arc' is part of a circle.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.shapes.title: Title of the 'Shapes' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough: drawing formations (lines, arcs, circles, boxes) on the field.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.tempo.media: Screen-reader description of the video on the 'Edit music' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Beats a minute' is the tempo (118, 81); a 'gradual' change is a slowing down over several measures (a ritardando), drawn as a sloping tempo line; a 'time signature' is the measure's meter (2/4, 4/4). The 'playhead' is the line that marks where the music is playing.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.tempo.text: Sentence under the title on the 'Edit music' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Counts' are beats of the drill; 'drag the tempo' means dragging the tempo line up or down to make the counts faster or slower, until they sit on the beats of the recorded music; 'holds' are counts held longer (fermatas).
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.tempo.title: Title of the 'Edit music' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough: the timeline's mode for lining the counts up with the recorded music. It is also the name of the button that turns the mode on; use the same words as that button (key tempoMode.button.text).
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.timeline.med: Screen-reader description of the video on 'The timeline' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'Expert mode' is one of the app's two working modes; a 'section' is a group of band members (trumpets, flutes); 'page flags' are the markers on the timeline where pages start.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.timeline.tex: Sentence under the title on 'The timeline' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. The 'timeline' is a strip below the field showing the show over time. 'Pages' are sections of the show between set formations, 'moves' are the marchers' paths between formations, 'counts' are beats of the music. 'Expert' is the name of one of the app's two working modes (keep it as the app names it).
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.timeline.tit: Title of 'The timeline' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough: the strip under the field that shows the show over time.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.view3d.media: Screen-reader description of the video on 'The 3D View' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. A 'set' is a formation the band stands in; the 'press box' is the booth at the top of the stands; a 'color guard' is the section of the band that performs with flags.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.view3d.text: Sentence under the title on 'The 3D View' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'From the stands' means as the audience sees it from the seats; 'marchers' are the band members.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.view3d.title: Title of 'The 3D View' slide of the 'What's new' walkthrough. 'The 3D View' is the name of a window that shows the show in 3D; keep it as the app names it.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.title: Heading of the 'What's new' step of the first-run setup, shown to everyone after the language and theme steps: a short walkthrough of the features new in OpenMarch version 0.2, one per slide. Also its screen-reader label. '0.2' is the version number; keep it as is.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.timeline.lab: Short name of the 'The timeline' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.shapes.label: Short name of the 'Shapes' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words.
