welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.view3d.label: Short name of the 'The 3D View' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words. 'The 3D View' is the name of a window; keep it as the app names it.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.props.label: Short name of the 'Props' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.tempo.label: Short name of the 'Edit music' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.slides.pathways.lab: Short name of the 'Pathways' slide in the row of clickable step names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; the current one is highlighted. Keep it to one or two words.
welcomeFlow.whatsNew.steps: Screen-reader label for the row of clickable feature names above the video in the 'What's new' walkthrough; each name jumps to that feature's slide.
workspaceSettings.audioOffsetSeconds: Label of a number field, in the Show settings dialog and in the Music dialog: how many seconds the music is shifted against the timeline's start. Can be negative or fractional. The unit 'seconds' appears beside the field.
workspaceSettings.cancel: Cancel button in the Show settings dialog. Discards unsaved changes to the settings and closes the dialog.
workspaceSettings.close: Screen-reader label of the 'x' button that closes the Show settings dialog.
workspaceSettings.defaultBeatsPerMeasure: Label of a number field in the Show settings dialog: the default number of beats in each measure (e.g. 4) for new tempo sections. The unit 'beats' appears beside the field.
workspaceSettings.defaultNewPageCounts: Label of a number field in the Show settings dialog: how many counts a newly added page lasts by default (e.g. 16). A page is one drill set; a count is one beat step. The unit 'counts' appears beside the field.
workspaceSettings.defaultTempo: Label of a number field in the Show settings dialog: the default tempo for new tempo sections, in beats per minute. The unit 'BPM' appears beside the field.
workspaceSettings.loadingSettings: Message shown while the Show settings dialog loads. Keep the trailing '...'.
workspaceSettings.measurementOffset: Label of a whole-number field in the Show settings dialog: an offset applied to measure numbering for the show. Can be negative. Keep the wording close to the English: it names the setting, 'Measure' meaning a musical measure (bar).
workspaceSettings.noSettingsFound: Message in the Show settings dialog when no settings could be loaded for the open show.
workspaceSettings.pageNumberOffset: Label of a whole-number field in the Show settings dialog: an offset applied to page numbering, which shifts the number given to the first page. Can be negative. A page is one drill set.
workspaceSettings.resetToDefaults: Button in the Show settings dialog that puts every field back to OpenMarch's original values. Does not save until the user saves.
workspaceSettings.saveChanges: Button in the Show settings dialog that saves the edited settings to the show.
workspaceSettings.saved: Success toast after the Show settings were saved.
workspaceSettings.title: Title of the Show settings dialog (opened from the sidebar). These settings belong to the open show, such as default tempo, page length and numbering offsets.
workspaceSettings.units.beats: Unit shown beside the 'beats per measure' number field in the Show settings dialog. Lowercase, plural noun.
workspaceSettings.units.bpm: Unit shown beside the tempo number field in the Show settings dialog. BPM means beats per minute; use the abbreviation musicians use in your language.
workspaceSettings.units.counts: Unit shown beside the 'new page counts' number field in the Show settings dialog. A count is one beat step in a drill. Lowercase, plural noun.
workspaceSettings.units.seconds: Unit shown beside the audio offset number field in the Show settings dialog. Lowercase, plural noun.
workspaceSettings.unsavedChanges: Small warning at the bottom of the Show settings dialog while some edits are not saved yet.
workspaceSettings.updateFailed: Error toast shown when saving the show settings (default tempo, page counts, number offsets and so on) fails.
workspaceSettings.showInfo.client: Label in the Show settings panel (sidebar settings) for an optional text field. The band or school the show was written for, shown on the 3D View's video boards as "For <client>".
workspaceSettings.showInfo.designer: Label in the Show settings panel (sidebar settings) for an optional text field. The person who designed (wrote) the drill, shown on the 3D View's video boards as "Designed by <name>".
workspaceSettings.showInfo.optional: Grey placeholder in an empty optional text field in the Show settings panel.
workspaceSettings.showInfo.projectName: Label in the Show settings panel (sidebar settings) for an optional text field. The show's display name, shown on the 3D View's video boards; when blank the file name is used.
workspaceSettings.showInfo.projectNamePl: Grey placeholder in the empty Show name field: when no name is typed, the show's file name is used instead.
toolbar.alignment.toPreviousPagePosition: Menu item under "Place selected marchers" in the marcher inspector, continuing that phrase (the leading dots show that). Puts the selected marchers back where they stood on the previous page, for the current page.
timeline.moveMenu.selectMarchers: Item in a move's menu on the timeline (right-click a move's bar, or its ⋯ button). Selects the marchers (performers) in the move on the field. A move is a group of marchers traveling together over some counts.
actions.shape.arc: Name of a shape action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Text: "Shape: Arc".
shapes.kinds.arc.params.bend: Tooltip for the Arc shape's number in the floating shape editor: how many degrees the arc of marchers turns through (its sweep), e.g. 90° for a quarter circle.
shapes.kinds.arc.ends.label: Tooltip for the Arc shape's menu that picks whether the arc of marchers is left open or closed into a shape.
shapes.kinds.arc.ends.open: Menu option for an Arc shape: leave the arc open (its two ends are not joined).
shapes.kinds.arc.ends.chord: Menu option for an Arc shape: close the arc by joining its two ends with a straight line, making a half-moon shape that can be filled with marchers.
shapes.kinds.arc.ends.circle: Menu option for an Arc shape: continue the arc all the way around so it becomes a full circle of marchers.
shapes.kinds.arc.ends.round: Menu option for an Arc shape that runs on an ellipse (an oval): continue the arc all the way around so it becomes a whole ellipse of marchers.
shapes.kinds.arc.params.width: Tooltip for a number in the floating editor of an Arc shape: how far the arc of marchers reaches from side to side on the field (for arcs up to a half circle, the distance between its two end marchers), in marching steps.
shapes.kinds.arc.params.height: Tooltip for a number in the floating editor of an Arc shape: how tall the arc of marchers is (front to back on the field), measured from the line between its two ends to its farthest edge, in marching steps.
shapes.kinds.arc.params.stretch: Tooltip for a number in the floating editor of an Arc shape, shown while the arc lies on an ellipse (oval): how many times deeper than wide it is, or wider than deep, e.g. "1.3× deep".
shapes.kinds.arc.size.tall: Word after the stretch number in an Arc shape's floating editor: "1.3× tall" means the oval the arc is on is 1.3 times as tall (front to back on the field) as it is wide. Also accepted when typing the number.
shapes.kinds.arc.size.wide: Word after the stretch number in an Arc shape's floating editor: "1.3× wide" means the oval the arc is on is 1.3 times as wide (side to side) as it is tall. Also accepted when typing the number.
shapes.kinds.arc.size.round: Word after the stretch number in an Arc shape's floating editor while it's dragged onto exactly 1×: "1× circle", meaning the oval has become a circle.
shapes.kinds.arc.size.steps: Unit after the depth number in an Arc shape's floating editor, ending the phrase "60 × 30 steps" (width × depth of the arc): marching steps (8 to 5).
actions.batchEdit.holdOverWindow: Name of the "Hold from start flag to playhead" action in the command palette, shortcut settings and menus. {holdOverWindow} is the command's name, filled in by the app from one shared word list; keep it as a placeholder. In Expert, it holds the selected marchers still (Held) from the start flag to the playhead, removing their moves in between.
timeline.terms.holdOverWindow: The name of the "Hold from start flag to playhead" command (Expert): it makes the selected marchers stay still (Held) from the start flag to the playhead, the two lines on the timeline. One shared word, filled into menus and messages that name the command. Imperative verb phrase.
timeline.expertHolds.held: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They are already Held ({heldLower}, the hold state word) over the whole stretch.
timeline.expertHolds.shape: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They are in a shape between the start flag and the playhead, which this command doesn't take marchers out of yet.
timeline.expertHolds.followLeader: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They follow the leader between the start flag and the playhead, which this command doesn't take marchers out of yet.
timeline.expertHolds.followLeaderOrder: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. They share a curved move with marchers whose follow-the-leader order depends on it, so they can't be taken out of it.
timeline.expertHolds.arrivalShape: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. The move their hold would start from ends in a shape, which the hold can't edit.
timeline.expertHolds.arrivalFollowLeader: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. The move their hold would start from is a follow-the-leader move, which the hold can't edit.
timeline.expertHolds.homeShape: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. A shape sets where they start the show; ungrouping it at the start of the show lets them be held one by one.
timeline.expertHolds.endsWithoutArriving: One reason in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, for marchers it left alone. {names} is their names, already joined as a list in your language. The last move before the start flag is cut short (it's part of a longer move, or another move takes over), so the marcher never arrives at the spot the hold would keep.
timeline.expertHolds.count: How many marchers, used in the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead when their names aren't known. # is the number.
timeline.expertHolds.notHeld: Title of the toast after "Hold from start flag to playhead" (Expert): holds the selected marchers from the start flag to the playhead, when some marchers were left alone. # is how many; {heldLower} is the hold state word in lowercase (English 'held').
inspector.marcher.timeline.heldOfSelecte: Line in the marcher inspector when only some selected marchers are Held at the playhead. {count} is how many are Held, {total} how many are selected; {held} is the hold state word (English 'Held').
timeline.heldBar.shape: Added to a hold bar's label on the timeline when the bar is drawn as Held because a shape (a formation such as a box or an arc) placed on an earlier page carries on over these pages, with no Held hold stored. Says the shape is what keeps the marchers there.
timeline.notDefinedBar.title: Label of a dashed hold bar on the timeline, which marks counts where the selected marchers have no position of their own yet and show the last one. {notDefined} is the state word "Not defined", filled in by the app; {page} is the page's name, such as "3". The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.notDefinedBar.titleRange: Label of a dashed hold bar on the timeline that spans several pages. {notDefined} is the state word "Not defined", filled in by the app; {first} and {last} are the first and last page names, such as "4" and "6" (the dash marks a range). The holds words, shared by the whole app: "Defined" (the marcher has its own position on this page), "Held" (it stays where the previous page left it, on purpose) and "Not defined" (nothing decided yet; it shows the last position for now).
timeline.departure.title: Label of a small tick on the timeline where a selected marcher stops holding still and its next move starts. {page} is the page's name, such as "4", and {count} the count within that page where it starts moving, such as "1".
view3d.camera.judgesTable: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the indoor arena venue: a view from a seat at the judges' table on the arena floor, in front of the audience, at a seated person's eye height. 'Judges' are the people who score the show.
view3d.camera.tunnel: Name of a built-in camera (a saved viewpoint) in the 3D View's Camera menu and Cameras panel; also the label for its number key. In the indoor arena venue: a view from the mouth of the tunnel the performers walk through to enter the arena floor, at standing eye height.
view3d.kit.arena: Name of a venue (the 3D setting the show is shown in) in the 3D View's venue picker; also used as the heading above a venue's camera profiles and inside default profile names such as '{venue} cameras'. A large indoor basketball arena with seating on all four sides, where indoor guard and percussion championships are held. Different from 'Indoor gym', which is a smaller school gym.
view3d.board.designedBy: Line on the video boards (scoreboards) of the 3D View's stadium and arena venues, under the show's name. {name} is the drill designer from Show settings, e.g. 'Designed by Sam Rivera'. Keep it short: it's painted on a board in large type.
view3d.board.forClient: Line on the video boards (scoreboards) of the 3D View's stadium and arena venues, under the designer line. {name} is the client the show is for (usually a school or band), from Show settings, e.g. 'For Lincoln High School'. Keep it short.
view3d.board.nowPerforming: Small heading above the show's name on the video boards (scoreboards) of the 3D View's stadium and arena venues, like an announcer's 'now performing' card. Painted in capital letters with wide letter spacing, so keep it very short.
view3d.board.untitled: Shown in large type on the 3D View's video boards in place of the show's name when the show has no name. Keep it short.
view3d.keys.pausedPose: Row in the 3D View's keyboard shortcut list (View settings panel) for the S key, which switches how marchers stand while playback is paused: the closed position (feet together on their dots) or the actual mid-step pose at that moment.
view3d.pausedPose.label: Screen-reader name of an on/off toggle button (footprints icon) in the 3D View's playback bar. When on, paused marchers show their actual mid-step pose at that moment; when off (default), they stand in the closed position, feet together on their dots.
view3d.pausedPose.tooltip: Tooltip of the 3D View's paused-pose toggle (footprints icon) in the playback bar. 'Closed' is the marching-band term for standing with feet together; 'dots' are the marchers' drill positions.
